Consider a self-similar L\'evy process in dimension $d$ and let $n\ge 2$.
We prove here that the Hausdorff and fractal dimensions of the
level sets of the path at time $0$ behave very differently as a
function of the level when $n$ is far smaller than $d$. More
precisely, we construct a function $A :(1, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}_+$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exp_level_sets}
A(n)\le \mathrm{dim}_H(S_n)\le A(n)+\frac{1}{n}\;\;\; \text{ and}\;\;\;
\frac{1}{n}\le \mathrm{dim}_F(S_n)\le A(n)+1,
\end{equation}
where
$\mathrm{dim}_H(S_n)$ and~$\mathrm{dim}_F(S_n)$ are the Hausdorff
dimension and the fractal dimension of $S_n$.

Our proofs are based on probabilistic and analytic techniques,
exploiting the fractal nature of the paths in addition to the self
similarity property.

This work provides an answer to the question posed by Le Gall (see
arXiv:math/0508062), of whether there is a process which looks like a
Brownian motion from a time-scale of one, but which is "wild" on any other
time-scale.

Games have long been seen as a form of entertainment, but new studies suggest that they can also be a valuable tool for learning. Researchers have found that games can help people absorb information in a fun and engaging way, making it easier to retain knowledge.

One study published in the Journal of Educational Psychology found that students who played a game designed to teach them about the human body were better able to recall information than those who were simply taught through traditional methods like lectures or worksheets.

The study's author, Dr. Mark Lepper, said: "The results suggest that games can help people learn and play at the same time. When people are intrinsically motivated to play a game, they're not thinking about the fact that they're learning. It feels like pure fun."

Other studies have found that games can be particularly effective in teaching complex or abstract concepts, such as algebraic equations or scientific principles. By allowing players to experiment with different scenarios and try out different approaches, games can help people understand difficult concepts in a hands-on way.

As technology continues to advance, there are now more interactive and immersive games available than ever before. Whether it's through virtual reality or motion sensors, these games can create a more realistic and engaging experience for players, making it even easier to learn and play at the same time.

Though games may not replace traditional teaching methods altogether, they can certainly be a valuable addition to the classroom. Teachers are starting to recognize the benefits of incorporating games into their lessons, using them as a way to engage students and help them absorb information in a fun and dynamic way.

Overall, the idea that games are just a form of entertainment may be a thing of the past. With their ability to teach, engage, and inspire, games show great promise as a tool for learning and growth.

Zuleika Dobson is a stunningly attractive young woman of the Edwardian era, a true femme fatale, who is a prestidigitator by profession, formerly a governess. Zuleika's current occupation (though, more importantly, perhaps, her enrapturing beauty) has made her something of a small-time celebrity and she manages to gain entrance to the privileged, all-male domain of Oxford University because her grandfather is the Warden of Judas College (based on Merton College, Oxford, Beerbohm's alma mater). There, she falls in love for the first time in her life with the present Duke of Dorset, a snobbish, emotionally detached student who—frustrated with the lack of control over his feelings when he sees her—is forced to admit that she too is his first love, impulsively proposing to her. As she feels that she cannot love anyone unless he is impervious to her charms, however, she rejects all her suitors, doing the same with the astonished Duke. The Duke quickly discovers that Noaks, another Oxford student, also claims to have fallen in love her, without ever having even interacted with her. Apparently, men immediately fall in love with her upon seeing her. As the first to have his love reciprocated by her (for however brief a time) the Duke decides that he will commit suicide to symbolise his passion for Zuleika and in hopes that he will raise awareness in her of the terrible power of her bewitching beauty, as she innocently goes on crushing men's affections. Zuleika is able to interrupt the Duke's first suicide attempt from a river boat, but seems to have a romanticised view of men dying for her, and does not oppose the notion of his suicide altogether. The Duke, instead pledging to kill himself the next day—which Zuleika more or less permits—has dinner that night with his social club where the other members also affirm their love for Zuleika. Upon telling them of his plan to die, the others unexpectedly agree to also commit suicide for Zuleika. This idea soon reaches the minds of all Oxford undergraduates, who inevitably fall in love with Zuleika upon first sight. The Duke eventually decides that the only way he can stop all the undergraduates from killing themselves is by not committing suicide himself, hoping they will follow his example. By an ancient tradition, on the eve of the death of a Duke of Dorset, two black owls come and perch on the battlements of Tankerton Hall, the family seat; the owls remain there hooting through the night and at dawn they fly away to an unknown place. After debating whether to follow through with his suicide, while seeming to decide at last to embrace his life as just as valuable as Zuleika's, the Duke receives a telegram from his butler at Tankerton, reporting the portentous return of the owls. The Duke promptly interprets the omen as a sign that the gods have decreed his doom. He proudly tells Zuleika that he will still die, but no longer for her; she agrees as long as he makes it appear that he is dying for her by shouting her name as he jumps into the river. Later the same day, a thunderstorm overwhelms the May Week boat races while the Duke drowns himself in the River Isis, wearing the robes of a Knight of the Garter. Every fellow undergraduate, except one, promptly follows suit. All of the Oxford undergraduates now dead, including, with some delay, the cowardly Noaks, Zuleika discusses the ordeal with her grandfather, who reveals that he too was enamoured by all when he was her age. While Oxford's academic staff barely notice that all of their undergraduates have vanished, Zuleika decides to order a special train for the next morning... bound for Cambridge.

He is on lookout one night when Michael and his dog Stella Artois are washed overboard, near Papua New Guinea. They awake to discover that they are stranded on a desert island that is shaped like an elongated peanut in the Pacific Ocean. While Michael is struggling to survive on the island, food is regularly left for him. To his surprise, he learns that an elderly Japanese man called Kensuke is also living on the island. Kensuke helps Michael to survive. He sets guidelines that Michael thinks are just annoyances, until Kensuke saves him from a jellyfish after warning him never to go in the water. Michael teaches Kensuke English, and Kensuke teaches Michael how to paint, how to fish and where to find the best food and water. He is eventually revealed to be a doctor and survivor of World War II, and he believes that his family died in Nagasaki after the atomic bomb was dropped there on August 9, 1945. Over time Kensuke begins to understand how Michael feels and how he misses his family. Together they build a beacon that can be lit to signal to ships, but for a long time they see no sign of any ships. Later, however, Michael witnesses a Chinese junk and he consults Kensuke as to whether or not he should light the beacon. Kensuke recognizes the ship as that of poachers, and he and Michael rush to gather all the orangutans into the cave to protect them from the threat that lies in the ship. They nearly succeed but cannot find one particular orangutan, the one Kensuke calls Kikanbo his. The ship arrives and they hear gunshots. When the ship leaves, they discover that some gibbon monkeys have been killed but that Kikanbo is still alive. The next time they see a ship it is not the poachers, and they both light the fire. The crew on the ship see the fire and change direction, heading towards the island. When the boat is closer, Michael sees that the boat is the Peggy Sue, with his parents on board. Kensuke decides at that point, despite thinking otherwise earlier, that he will not be sailing home with Michael; he says "This is my place. This Kensuke's Kingdom. Kensuke tells him to keep everything a secret until ten years have passed, when Kensuke will be dead. Michael runs out to the beach where the ship had landed and is reunited with his parents. Four years after Michael's secret log is published, he receives a letter from Kensuke's son (who is still alive). Michael goes to Japan to visit him a month later.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that facilitates a phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor.  The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the enzyme ITP3K is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase.  In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the  LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they are not expressed in yeast or plants.

An increasing number of works tackle relational data in the context of clustering, where each data point is represented as a graph. This comes with the challenge of appropriately defining and measuring similarity between graphs, which is usually done by considering only the subgraphs that are induced by a common set of vertices, called the kernel. In this paper, we propose a new framework where, instead of considering a fixed kernel, the kernel is learned from the data following a criterion based on the optimization of a cost function. This allows to account for the richest information in the graphs, and therefore, we show that it can improve clustering accuracy. We derive a new family of cost functions with theoretical guarantees on the convergence of the solution, and we propose an efficient algorithm to learn the optimal kernel. We conduct experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, where we show the advantage of our approach compared to state-of-the-art graph clustering methods.

(makes about 3 cups)
1/2 cup (120g) heavy cream
2 teaspoons (6g) confectioners sugar

Diced fresh strawberries
Put the strawberries, water, and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and puree with an immersion blender. Ladle out about 3/4 cup of the strawberry puree into a small heatproof bowl. Sprinkle the gelatin over the surface and let sit for about 1 minute. Microwave for 45 seconds or heat gently in a saucepan until melted. Stir the gelatin into the rest of the strawberries and pour into a half-size hotel pan. Let cool to room temperature. Cover with plastic wrap and freeze overnight. Line a perforated hotel pan with several layers of cheesecloth and turn the frozen puree out into it. Wash the hotel pan, set the perforated pan into it, and refrigerate to drain for 2 days. Discard the solids. Load the strawberry water into a soda siphon and charge with a CO2 charger. Shake vigorously for 1 minute. Refrigerate until youre ready to serve or for up to 3 days. Put the cream in a chilled bowl with the sugar and birch beer extract and whip to soft peaks. Put a few diced strawberries in the bottom of each glass and fill with the soda. Top with a dollop of the birch beer cream.

500 g skinless chicken breasts
vegetable oil (for deep frying)
MARINADE
4 cups water
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon msg
COATING
1 egg, beaten
1 cup milk
2 cups plain flour
3 teaspoons salt
1 teaspoon pepper
1 1/2 tablespoons paprika
1 tablespoon Mexican chili powder
1 teaspoon msg (isn't really important it just adds extra flavour)
Trim any excess skin or fat from the chicken breasts. Slice the chicken breasts into nice size strips (approximately 1/2 inch x 3-4 inches). Combine the water, salt and MSG for the marinade in a large bowl and let it sit and marinate for 20 minutes. Turn the strips once while they are marinating. Combine the beaten egg and milk and a bit of pepper in a medium size bowl. In a small plastic bag combine the remaining ingredients (flour, salt, pepper, paprika, Mexican chili and MSG) and shake. At this time you can start to preheat the oil in a deep-fryer to 220°C. When the chicken has been marinating for 20 minutes, transfer each piece to paper towels so that excess liquid can drain off. Using about ten strips at once, place the chicken in the bag with the flouer and shake the bag until the strips of chicken are coated. Place them on a plate. Once they have been coated with the flour mixture dip them in the egg and milk mixture individually and them back into the bag for another shake. Be sure to try and get as much coating on each strip. If you wish you can coat them again if you want a thicker coating. Drop the strips, 5-6 at a time into the hot oil. They should only take a couple of minutes depending on how you like your chicken. Be sure to stir when frying so the strips don't stick together. Remove the chicken from the oil and allow them to drain on paper towels for a couple of minutes. Enjoy your homemade takeaway!

Twenty-eight naked young women bathed by the shore
Or near the bank of a woodland lake
Twenty-eight girls and all of them comely
Worthy of Mack Sennett's camera and Florenz Ziegfield's
Foolish Follies.
They splashed and swam with the wondrous unconsciousness
Of their youth and beauty
In the full spontaneity and summer of the fieshes of
awareness
Heightened, intensified and softened
By the soft and the silk of the waters
Blooded made ready by the energy set afire by the
nakedness of the body,
Electrified: deified: undenied.
A young man of thirty years beholds them from a distance.
He lives in the dungeon of ten million dollars.
He is rich, handsome and empty standing behind the linen curtains
Beholding them.
Which girl does he think most desirable, most beautiful?
They are all equally beautiful and desirable from the gold distance.
For if poverty darkens discrimination and makes
perception too vivid,
The gold of wealth is also a form of blindness.
For has not a Frenchman said, Although this is America...
What he has said is not entirely relevant,
That a naked woman is a proof of the existence of God.
Where is he going?
Is he going to be among them to splash and to laugh with them?
They did not see him although he saw them and was there among them.
He saw them as he would not have seen them had they been conscious
Of him or conscious of men in complete depravation:
This is his enchantment and impoverishment
As he possesses them in gaze only.
. . .He felt the wood secrecy, he knew the June softness
The warmth surrounding him crackled
Held in by the mansard roof mansion
He glimpsed the shadowy light on last year's brittle leaves fallen,
Looked over and overlooked, glimpsed by the fall of death,
Winter's mourning and the May's renewal.

White matter hyperintensity (WMH) is commonly found in elder individuals and
appears to be associated with brain diseases. U-net is a convolutional network
that has been widely used for biomedical image segmentation. Recently, U-net
has been successfully applied to WMH segmentation. Random initialization is
usally used to initialize the model weights in the U-net. However, the model
may coverage to different local optima with different randomly initialized
weights. We find a combination of thresholding and averaging the outputs of
U-nets with different random initializations can largely improve the WMH
segmentation accuracy. Based on this observation, we propose a post-processing
technique concerning the way how averaging and thresholding are conducted.
Specifically, we first transfer the score maps from three U-nets to binary
masks via thresholding and then average those binary masks to obtain the final
WMH segmentation. Both quantitative analysis (via the Dice similarity
coefficient) and qualitative analysis (via visual examinations) reveal the
superior performance of the proposed method. This post-processing technique is
independent of the model used. As such, it can also be applied to situations
where other deep learning models are employed, especially when random
initialization is adopted and pre-training is unavailable.

In mem'ry of my sister, gone too soon,
I hold dear thoughts of you, within my heart's boon.
Though miles and years now stretch between us far,
Your laughter echoes still, like morning dew on tar.

The mem'ries we made, in days long past,
With joy they spring to life, forever vast.
In gardens bright, where wildflowers bloom,
We danced with glee, beneath sun's gentle broom.

As children wild, we chased each other 'round,
Our footsteps traced in circles on hallowed ground.
You were my guide, through thickets dark and deep,
My constant friend, in slumber or waking sleep.

In winter's snow, our cheeks rosy red,
We built great forts and snowmen towering overhead.
And when night fell, by fire's warm embrace,
We whispered secrets, face to face.

Oh, how I miss your presence now, so true,
Yet know that in spirit, it remains anew.
For though apart, my love for you persists,
With grace divine, enshrined like tender mist.

While time continues its relentless flow,
Somewhere beyond this world, I know
That you still dwell, free from earthly pains,
In haven of peace, where love sustains.

Therefore, sweet sister, rest assured, in faith,
That here with me upon this mortal stage,
Until we meet again, you will always be,
A cherished thought, entwined with destiny.

A fundamental issue in Quantum Computing revolves around approximating matrices in $SU(2)$ through the use of limited "generators." A specific topological framework for $SU(2)$ is introduced to define a concept called a covering exponent, which compares the number of steps needed to cover $SU(2)$ with $\varepsilon$-balls versus the volume covered by those same $\varepsilon$-balls under the Haar measure. An optimal subset of $PSU(2)$ is created using Pauli matrices, based on the covering exponent's metric. Subsequent manipulation of the relationship between $SU(2)$ and $S^3$ enables correlation of angles among points on $S^3$, yielding an educated guess regarding the greatest possible angle between points within a lattice structure. This approach demonstrates how such a conjecture may be applied to calculate the covering exponent and allows its extension to more general subsets of $SU(2)$.

> The narrator and main character is Professor Duff, the chair of Mathematics at an unnamed university. As a small boy in Ireland many years before, he had visited the world of his friend Professor Honey, one dimension lower than his own (a line). Now, as a man, at the invitation of Professor Xanadu, who is an inhabitant of another world, this time eight dimensions higher than his own (and an infinite number of dimensions in general), he becomes a professor in Flatterland. The narrator, Professor Duff, teaches Flatlanders at different stages of their education, from beginners to those at the end of their first term (recalling the earlier 20th-century tradition of mathematical tutoring).
>
> Throughout the story, the narrator's progress in Flatterland is narrated from different perspectives. The reader is presented with the character's reactions to the new world, which is described using terms familiar to two dimensional objects. These reactions are often humorous, sometimes bemused, and occasionally downright confused. This confusion is intended to provide a view of the difficulty that a person might face trying to understand multiple dimensions from a perspective which, at best, views only three dimensions.
>
> As Professor Duff's understanding of the higher-order world increases, the reader is presented with a new perspective, that of a higher dimensional being looking down at the world that Professor Duff inhabits.
>
> At the end of the novel, Professor Duff travels back to the three-dimensional world from the eighth-dimensional world, where he is promptly captured and taken to a prison on Earth. There, he tells his story to the professor, who relates it to the reader.

"Flatterland", by Ian Stewart and Jack Cohen, 2001, Prometheus Books.

Let's Get Skase is a 2001 Australian comedy starring Lachy Hulme, Alex Dimitriades, Craig McLachlan, Alex Menglet, and Bill Kerr. It is based on the life of failed Australian businessman Christopher Skase, who after the collapse of his Qintex business, fled to Majorca, Spain. Skase died at around the time of the film's release. It was filmed in Melbourne and Perth. Plot
After the collapse of his massive Qintex business empire, Christopher Skase flees to the Spanish Island of Majorca, leaving angry creditors high and dry. Enter Peter Dellasandro, a fast-talking con man and failed entrepreneur who sees the "Chase For Skase" as a potential gold mine.
Dellasandro convinces the Creditors Board that he's the only man with the ability and recklessness to undertake the task demanded by his country: the kidnapping of Christopher Skase.
But not everyone is convinced, especially Danny D'Amato, the fiery son of the Creditors Chairman. Suspicious of Dellasandro, the two form an uneasy alliance as Dellasandro sets out to recruit the ego-centric TV host Eric Carney into his scheme, until seasoned mercenary Mitch Vendieks warns Dellasandro that Carney is planning a kidnap plot of his own.
Determined to beat Carney to the punch, Dellasandro and Danny join forces with Mitch to form their own team, recruiting the inept Sean Knight, mendacious getaway driver Dave Phibbs and cynical intelligence ace Rupert Wingate, who soon discovers that Skase is devising a deadly scheme to resurrect his business empire across Europe.
With time running out, Dellasandro and the boys head for Majorca and track Skase to his sprawling mansion, confronting the devious businessman.
The team is outnumbered by Skase's Security Guards and thus cannot manage to kidnap him. However, they make out with several computer discs which contain sensitive documents revealing Skase's plan to "bust out" Qintex. The information at hand is enough evidence for the Australian Government to make compensation payments to the Qintex Creditors Boardmembers.

The MD-MS Program is an instructor-led initiative where students receive guidance from experts in the latest medical advancements within the healthcare sector. Designed for those aiming to engage in clinical practice and enhance their research capabilities in a corresponding field of engineering, this degree equips students with knowledge of the technologies used by practicing physicians. This degree aims to foster research publishing through a funded research experience, coupled with training in engineering design and analysis. The curriculum is structured around mentorship, allowing students to learn under the supervision of experienced medical professionals affiliated with recommended medical centers. Most courses are conducted online, facilitating flexible learning without requiring students to leave their employment.

Some individuals, particularly those with mixed black and white heritage, often assert that they "look Spanish." However, my experience reveals that for me, the term conjures images of Spain, where the majority of the population is white and has little African ancestry. In essence, equating oneself with Spain overlooks the historical context, much like how a person of European descent might incorrectly identify with African identity based on the legacy of colonial settlers in South Africa. As someone of English Caribbean origin, I've encountered numerous instances where people mistakenly assume that mixed individuals hail from Spanish colonies. Furthermore, I've noticed that some Dominicans refuse to acknowledge their African roots despite appearing identical to African Americans, instead insisting on identifying as "Spanish," a label that doesn't accurately reflect their heritage. It's essential to recognize that not everyone of mixed background comes from former Spanish colonies, and not all Latin American countries boast significant numbers of mixed individuals. For instance, regions like Belize and the Honduran coastline in Central America exhibit substantial African populations, whereas other areas, such as Costa Rica, feature predominantly white populations. Let us reject the attempts by monoracial individuals to categorize us according to their narrow understanding of what constitutes "race."

The state-of-the-art method for automatically segmenting white matter bundles
in diffusion-weighted MRI is tractography in conjunction with streamline
cluster selection. This process involves long chains of processing steps which
are not only computationally expensive but also complex to setup and tedious
with respect to quality control. Direct bundle segmentation methods treat the
task as a traditional image segmentation problem. While they so far did not
deliver competitive results, they can potentially mitigate many of the
mentioned issues. We present a novel supervised approach for direct tract
segmentation that shows major performance gains. It builds upon a stacked U-Net
architecture which is trained on manual bundle segmentations from Human
Connectome Project subjects. We evaluate our approach \textit{in vivo} as well
as \textit{in silico} using the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge phantom
dataset. We achieve human segmentation performance and a major performance gain
over previous pipelines. We show how the learned spatial priors efficiently
guide the segmentation even at lower image qualities with little quality loss.

As the story opens, Irene Bobs, the unconventional and whip-smart protagonist, sits at her desk in the newsroom of the local newspaper where she works as a reporter. Her life is turned upside-down when she receives a phone call from her son, Billy, who is in trouble at his boarding school and needs her immediate help. Despite the risks and dangers involved in going to him, Irene sets out on a journey to her son's school, not knowing what she will find.

Along the way, she reflects on her troubled relationship with Billy, who has always been a sensitive and introverted child. Irene has always struggled to connect with him and fears that she has failed as a mother. As she drives through the night, she recalls the moments when she could have done things differently and wonders if she has the strength to help her son overcome his difficulties.

When Irene finally arrives at the school, she is shocked to discover that Billy has been involved in a violent incident and is now in police custody. As she sits in the waiting room, she realizes that she must confront her own past and confront the truth about her own childhood in order to help her son.

The plot summary of this novel, "Reading in the Dark," follows Irene Bobs as she embarks on a journey to help her son and comes to terms with her own past. Along the way, she discovers the strength and resilience within herself and learns that the power of love and understanding can overcome even the darkest of circumstances.

At the age of nine, Chiyo Sakamoto is taken from her poverty-stricken fishing village of Yoroido on the coast of the Sea of Japan with her older sister Satsu and sold to an okiya (geisha boarding house) in Gion, the most prominent geisha district in Kyoto. Satsu is not sold into the okiya with her and is instead forced into becoming a prostitute in Kyoto's pleasure district. Chiyo lives in the okiya alongside another young girl named Pumpkin, elderly and grumbling Granny, money-obsessed Mother and Auntie, a failed geisha. Also living in the okiya is the famous ill-mannered geisha Hatsumomo who promptly takes to disliking Chiyo, who she sees as a possible rival. Despite Pumpkin and Auntie's warnings, Chiyo plans to leave the okiya and escape the city with Satsu, but is caught when she falls off the roof and breaks her arm. Enraged at her for dishonoring the okiya, Mother stops investing in Chiyo and makes her pay off her increasing debts as a slave. Several years later, a downtrodden Chiyo is given money and a handkerchief in the street by a strange but kind man known at this point only as the Chairman. She donates the money to the Yasaka Shrine in Gion, praying to become a geisha in the hopes of seeing him again, keeping the handkerchief as a memento. Chiyo is envious of Pumpkin, who is on her way to becoming a geisha under Hatsumomo's tutelage, but soon after visiting the shrine, she is taken in as a protégé by Mameha, a rival of Hatsumomo and the owner of a kimono she previously made Chiyo ruin. Mameha persuades Mother to reinvest into Chiyo's training, and Chiyo adopts the new name of Sayuri, with Mameha acting as her "older sister" and mentor. Mameha mentions that despite Hatsumomo's popularity, she was in fact a failure due to once angering the mistress of her principal teahouse. As a result, she could never obtain a danna to sponsor her independence, which is why she has stayed in the okiya under Mother. Hatsumomo goes out of her way to destroy Sayuri by tarnishing her reputation in Gion, forcing Mameha and Sayuri to devise a plan to push Hatsumomo out of the Nitta okiya lest Sayuri's career ultimately die, and so arranges for her mizuage (portrayed as a deflowering "ceremony" for maiko as a step to becoming full-fledged geisha) to be bidden upon by several influential men, namely mentor Nobu Toshikazu, the president of Iwamura Electric; and reputed mizuage specialist "Dr. Crab", dubbed so by Sayuri due to his appearance. Unfortunately, Hatsumomo learns of the plan and tells Dr. Crab that Sayuri has already been deflowered. However, after gaining back the respect of Dr. Crab by convincing him that Hatsumomo is a known liar, he ultimately wins the bid for Sayuri's mizuage and she uses his payment to cover all of her fees. This leads Mother, who had already been considering adopting Pumpkin as her heiress, to adopt Sayuri instead, which ultimately destroys the two girls' friendship. This change enrages both Pumpkin and Hatsumomo for different reasons: Pumpkin was looking forward to the adoption so that she could have some kind of security in her old age, while Hatsumomo was looking forward to Pumpkin's adoption so she could secure her own position as head geisha. Hatsumomo's behaviour begins to worsen and she is eventually thrown out of the okiya, with Pumpkin leaving soon after. As it turns out, Dr. Crab was actually bidding against the Baron, Mameha's danna, for Sayuri's mizuage. The Baron had previously undressed Sayuri against her will at a party, which Mameha had warned against. Nobu instead bids to become Sayuri's danna, but loses out to General Tottori. At this time, Japan is on the brink of entering World War II and many Geisha are evacuated to other cities to work in factories, which require hard labor and are primary bomb targets. The General is demoted and is unable to use any influence to send Sayuri somewhere safer but Nobu, despite losing respect for Sayuri, is able to send her far north to live with Arashino, a kimono maker. At the end of the war, Nobu visits Sayuri and asks that she return to Gion to help entertain the new Deputy Minister Sato, whose aid can be instrumental in rebuilding Iwamura Electric, the company which the Chairman and Nobu run. Sayuri, Mameha and Pumpkin entertain the Minister together regularly and within time, Nobu formally begins proposals to become Sayuri's danna. Sayuri still maintains strong feelings for the Chairman and doesn't want Nobu to become her danna, so on a weekend trip to the Amami Islands with Iwamura Electric, she plans to seduce the Minister and be caught in humiliation by Nobu. She asks Pumpkin to bring Nobu to a theater while she is with the Minister. Pumpkin still harbors resentment towards Sayuri for being adopted by Mother and noticing her feelings towards the Chairman, purposely brings him to the theater instead. Nobu finds out about Sayuri and the Minister in any case and decides not to become her danna. Sayuri eventually meets the Chairman again and reveals that her acts in Amami were for personal reasons. He reveals to Sayuri that he had always had feelings towards her, despite her thinking he didn't, but explains that he felt it disrespectful to take away the woman his friend had showed so much interest in, especially considering Nobu had once saved the Chairman's life. Sayuri and the Chairman kiss, which she feels is her first kiss expressing true love. Sayuri eventually retires from being a geisha and the Chairman becomes her danna. It is revealed that they have an illegitimate son together. Foreseeing the consequences this could have regarding the inheritance of Iwamura Electric, she relocates to New York City in later life. Here she opens her own small teahouse for entertaining Japanese men on business in the United States, which Mother takes a financial interest in, but Sayuri severs her links to the Nitta okiya and in effect, Japan. The Chairman remains her danna until his death and the story concludes with a reflection on her life.

Chips, a mixed-breed German Shepherd-Collie-Husky, served as a highly decorated war dog in the United States Army between 1940 and 1946. Owned by Edward J. Wren of New York, Chips was one of many civilian-owned dogs who volunteered for military service during World War II. Trained at the War Dog Training Center in Virginia, he was assigned to Private John P. Rowell's unit in the 3rd Infantry Division. Chips played a pivotal role in several key battles, including those in North Africa, Sicily, Italy, France, and Germany. Notably, he even attended the historic Roosevelt-Churchill conference in 1943 as a sentry dog. A few months later, during the invasion of Sicily, Chips distinguished himself when his handler was pinned down by an Italian machine-gun team; Chips broke free and stormed the pillbox, forcing the gunners to surrender. Although he suffered injuries, including a scalp wound and severe burns, Chips went on to capture ten Italian prisoners that same day.

Vegetables au gratin is a delicious and comforting dish that combines layers of vegetables with creamy béchamel sauce and melted cheese. Here's how to make this classic French side dish:

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
- 1 small onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, and zucchini), chopped into bite-sized pieces
- 4 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk
- ½ cup heavy cream
- ¼ teaspoon nutmeg
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 2 cups shredded Gruyère or Swiss cheese
- ½ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a large baking dish with cooking spray or butter.
2. In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onions and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Add the chopped vegetables to the skillet and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
4. Transfer the vegetable mixture to the prepared baking dish.
5. In a separate saucepan, whisk together the flour and milk over medium heat. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 2-3 minutes more, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
6. Pour the béchamel sauce over the vegetables in the baking dish. Sprinkle the shredded Gruyère cheese evenly over the top of the sauce. Then sprinkle the Parmesan cheese over the top of the Gruyère.
7. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the vegetables are tender. Let cool for a few minutes

Beyond the desperate security situation in Iraq lies an economy in tatters.
A vicious cycle of unemployment, poor social services and poverty has been made worse by a lack of investment. So there is much hope that an elected government will break the deadlock. "First rule of law, then the economy," says Radwan Hadi, deputy managing director of Aberdeen-based oil and gas consultancy Blackwatch Petroleum Services, which entered Iraq in 2003. Mr Hadi's view about what the new government's priorities should be is shared by many Iraqis. The economy has become the second-most dominant issue for many political parties ahead of Sunday's election, according to Bristol University political scientist Anne Alexander, who is working on a project that looks at governance and security in post-war Iraq.
Job creation ranks high both on election manifestos and on the Iraqi people's wish list. Nobody knows exactly how many Iraqis are out of work, but it is clear that the situation is dire. "Estimates of Iraq's unemployment rate vary, but we estimate it to be between 30-40%," the Washington-based independent think-tank The Brookings Institution says in its Iraq Index. But some progress has been made, largely thanks to the country's oil revenues which have exceeded $22bn since June 2003.
Iraq's infrastructure is on the mend, with notable improvements having been made in areas such as electricity supply, irrigation, telephone networks and the re-opening of hospitals. But serious problems remain and the growing divide between haves and have-nots is angering voters. One Iraqi woman told Ms Alexander about her frustration as she watched TV adverts for private hospitals soon after having failed to track down basic medicines from Baghdad's pharmacies. Observes Mr Hadi: "The economy at present marks a big divide; the rich get richer, the poor get poorer." An indication of this can be seen in the world of finance where, in contrast with the daily plight of ordinary people, 19 private banks operate, only one of which is run in accordance with Islamic banking principles. Hopes are high for the future of finance, so foreign banks have been buying into the sector. National Bank of Kuwait has bought a majority stake in Credit Bank of Iraq, the Jordanian investment bank Export & Finance Bank has bought 49% of National Bank of Iraq.
Foreign firms also hope to cash in on the reconstruction effort. Bechtel's efforts to rebuild schools and restore power have attracted controversy as well as boosting its bottom line while Halliburton has enjoyed a wealth of military contracts. But the involvement of foreign firms in the health and banking sectors and beyond sits uneasily with many Iraqis who are accustomed to the state taking responsibility for functions that are essential to making society work, observes Ms Alexander. "It is seen as a selling off of Iraq's assets and bringing in multinationals at the expense of Iraqi businesses and Iraqi workers," she says. Consequently, the transitional government has been forced to backtrack in recent months over its proposal to allow 100% foreign ownership of Iraqi assets, she explains. In the West, it is easy to forget that the otherwise brutal Baathist regime used to look after the majority of Iraq's citizens rather well in terms of job creation, social security and healthcare. Opinion polls suggest that "people still want the state to take a leading role in providing these things", Ms Alexander says.
Yet in some areas of the economy, investment from abroad is still warmly welcomed, insists Mr Hadi, an Iraqi who left the country three decades ago. "I think the private sector will evolve incredibly fast," Mr Hadi says. "Iraq's vast natural resources can support any magnitude of economic growth."
Many foreign companies say they are keen to get in on the act, yet few are actually entering the country in any meaningful way. But there are exceptions. Mr Hadi's Blackwatch is just one of many small operators preparing for a much bigger future. Blackwatch's Baghdad-based affiliate Falcon Group has dozens of people working for it across the country in Kirkuk and Baghdad, and its engineers and geo-scientists work with the Iraqi oil ministry to hammer out technology transfer issues, Mr Hadi points out. "These guys are trying to work. The Iraqi business people will do business at all times. "Life goes on in Iraq, the people take responsibility, they want to live normal lives."

Deep learning models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) excel at various 2D medical image analysis tasks, but most real-world applications involve 3D images. To capitalize on the additional spatial context, researchers have developed 3D CNNs for volumetric image segmentation. However, limited GPU memory restricts the use of full 3D inputs, prompting the need for techniques that can process smaller patches. Existing methods often rely on patch-based processing, which restricts the incorporation of larger contextual information for improved performance. This paper introduces a new method called Holistic Decomposition Convolution (HDC), which combines periodic down-sampling with standard 3D convolution. By reducing data size during sequential processing, HDC effectively leverages the entire input regardless of the sampling rate. Experimental results on hip T1 MRI and intervertebral disc T2 MRI show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

This morning, I rear-ended God; I was certain I had the right of way.
Now He claims he's going to sue; can you believe the divine audacity?
"What happened to your sermon on love?"
"Not now, I'm preoccupied; I've been trying to get someone's attention.
I'm fed up with these well-meaning but misguided intentions."
"I have responsibilities - a schedule to maintain, bills to pay, family obligations, and a lawn to mow - not to mention my amateurish attempts at poetry.
God feels neglected and unchosen; always the last to be considered for anything worthwhile.
Perhaps a bit of tender loving care is in order.
Maybe then I'll avoid getting sued.
Let's grab coffee in a couple of days.
"I'm cutting back on caffeine," he says.
"So, what's my next move?" I nearly shout.
"Fine, I'll take you along as my personal chauffeur!"
"A road trip companion? That's unacceptable!
Will you also choose the music?"
"Is that too much to ask?"
I warned him I'd write about this...
"Be my guest; this won't be my first failure."
"All right, fine! Come along, but keep quiet and refrain from singing that annoying tune."
To avoid a lawsuit, I'm bringing him along everywhere - including vacations."

The story revolves around the life of Oskar Matzerath, as narrated by himself when confined in a mental hospital during the years 1952-1954. Born in 1924 in the Free City of Danzig (now Gdańsk, Poland), with an adult's capacity for thought and perception, he decides never to grow up when he hears his father declare that he would become a grocer. Gifted with a piercing shriek that can shatter glass or be used as a weapon, Oskar declares himself to be one of those "auditory clairvoyant babies", whose "spiritual development is complete at birth and only needs to affirm itself". He retains the stature of a child while living through the beginning of World War II, several love affairs, and the world of postwar Europe. Through all this a tin drum that he received as a present on his third birthday remains his treasured possession, and he is willing to kill to retain it. Oskar considers himself to have two "presumptive fathers" - his mother's husband Alfred, a member of the Nazi Party, and her secret lover and cousin Jan, a Danzig Pole, who is executed for defending the Polish Post Office in Danzig during the German invasion of Poland. Oskar's mother having died, Alfred marries Maria, a woman who is secretly Oskar's first mistress. After marrying Alfred, Maria gives birth to Oskar's possible son, Kurt. But Oskar is disappointed to find that the baby persists in growing up, and will not join him in ceasing to grow at the age of three. During the war, Oskar joins a troupe of performing dwarfs who entertain the German troops at the front line. But when his second love, the diminutive Roswitha, is killed by Allied troops in the invasion of Normandy, Oskar returns to his family in Danzig where he becomes the leader of a criminal youth gang. The Russian army soon captures Danzig, and Alfred is shot by invading troops after he goes into seizures while swallowing his party pin to avoid being revealed as a Nazi. Oskar moves with his widowed stepmother and their son to Düsseldorf, where he models in the nude with Ulla and works engraving tombstones. Oskar decides to live apart from Maria and her son Kurt after mounting tensions. He decides on a flat owned by the Zeidlers. Upon moving in, he falls in love with the Sister Dorothea, a neighbor, but he later fails to seduce her. During an encounter with Klepp, Klepp asks Oskar how he has an authority over the judgement of music. Oskar, willing to prove himself once and for all to Klepp, a fellow musician, picks up his drum and sticks despite his vow to never play again after Alfred's death and plays a measure on his drum. The ensuing events lead Klepp and Oskar and Scholle (guitarist) to form the Rhine River Three jazz band. They are discovered by Mr. Schmuh who invites them to play at the Onion Cellar club. After a virtuoso performance, a record company talent seeker discovers Oskar the jazz drummer and offers a contract. Oskar soon achieves fame and riches. One day while walking through a field he finds a severed finger: the ring finger of Sister Dorothea, who has been murdered. He then meets and befriends Vittlar. Oskar allows himself to be falsely convicted of the murder and is confined to an insane asylum, where he writes his memoirs.

Denbigh is a heritage-listed former vineyard, Clydesdale horse stude, Ayrshire cattle stud and dairy farm and now Hereford stud located at 421 The Northern Road in the southern-western Sydney suburb of Cobbitty in the Camden Council local government area of New South Wales, Australia. It was built during 1818 by Charles Hook in  and by Thomas and Samual Hassall, and Daniel Roberts in . The property is privately owned. It was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 22 December 2006. History 
The original owner of Denbigh was Charles Hook, who had been imprisoned by the rebel government for supporting Governor Bligh's attempt to control the military in New South Wales. Hook had suffered greatly over the previous events and was in his fifties when he received his grant in 1812 by Governor Macquarie. The grant consisted of  in the Parish of Cook, located at Cobbitty between the Cowpasture Road and Bringelly Road (later Northern Road). During 1818, Hook and his wife stayed at nearby Macquarie Grove while their own house was being built. The construction of Denbigh house was completed  and Hook began clearing the surrounding land for agricultural use. He died in 1826.

Announcing Christs resurrection in a splendid splash of color, the eggs for the Easter bread are dyed red. In earlier days this was done in water tinted scarlet from beets, the first spring vegetable, or, where it was available, reddish wood. Now cooks generally use commercial packets of dye. The dyeing begins on Holy Thursday, before the solemnity of Good Friday wraps the week in black. Indeed, Holy Thursday is sometimes called Kokkinopefti, the day red falls, to symbolize Christs blood. Actress Anna Keaveney, who appeared in Brookside, My Family and A Touch of Frost, has died of lung cancer aged 55.
Keaveney, who played Brookside's Marie Jackson when the Channel 4 soap began in 1982, died on Saturday. Born in Runcorn, Cheshire, she also starred in numerous films including 1989's Shirley Valentine. She played Nellie in Mike Leigh's latest film Vera Drake, which won the Golden Lion prize for best film at this year's Venice Film Festival.
And most recently she appeared alongside Richard Wilson in ITV's King of Fridges and with Martin Clunes in Doc Martin. Other TV appearances included the part of Matron in ITV drama Footballers' Wives and a cameo role as Tom Farrell's mother Sheila in BBC comedy Gimme Gimme Gimme. Keaveney's career also included stage performances in Neaptide for the National Theatre, Private Lives and The Rise and Fall of Little Voice. The actress died in hospital. Her agent Barry Brown said: "Anna was due to have had another operation on Friday but unfortunately she was too weak."

To prepare the dessert, start by preheating your oven to 375°F. On a lightly floured surface, lay out the chilled puff pastry and roll it into a large rectangle, approximately 8 inches by 12 inches and 1/8 inch thick. Spread 1/4 cup of honey evenly across the pastry, leaving the edges intact. Sprinkle half of the pastry with 1/4 cup of finely chopped almonds. Fold the honey-covered half over the nuts, similar to closing a book. Sprinkle some flour over the top, re-roll the pastry into a smaller rectangle roughly two-thirds the original size, and repeat the process of spreading honey and sprinkling almonds, folding, and re-rolling until all the ingredients have been used. Use a sharp knife to cut the pastry into thin strips about 1/3 inch wide. Gently twist each strip a couple of times before placing them on an ungreased baking sheet. Freeze the straws for 20 minutes to set them. Dab the tops lightly with an egg wash and sprinkle with sugar. Bake in the preheated oven until the straws turn a medium golden brown, taking around 12 to 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool for just a minute before carefully lifting them off the sheet with a spatula. Serve warm or at room temperature.

As smartphones continue to become an integral part of our daily lives, new research has shown that they are being used for an average of 20 years before being replaced.

The study by Ofcom, the UK's media regulatory authority, found that people keep their mobile phones for much longer than previously thought. In fact, the average person now keeps their phone for around eight years and six months, with some models lasting even longer.

This is largely due to the increasing popularity of smartphones, which offer a wide range of features and functions beyond just making calls and sending messages. From social media to streaming video, gaming, and more, smartphones have become essential tools for many people.

However, this also means that we are using our phones for much longer periods of time, leading to concerns about data privacy and security. With so much personal information stored on these devices, it is important to take steps to protect ourselves from potential threats such as hacking or identity theft.

Ofcom has called on manufacturers and retailers to be transparent about how long their products will last, and to provide users with clear information about the risks associated with keeping their phones for extended periods of time. They have also urged consumers to consider purchasing refurbished or second-hand phones instead of always buying new ones.

Researchers examine how individual components interact and their compatibility when working together in either simultaneous or sequential modes. The behavior of each component is formalized using Input/Output-Transition Systems. For synchronized interaction, both components execute shared inputs and outputs at the same time, whereas asynchronous interactions rely on unlimited queues to transfer messages. Regardless of the approach, the key concept is ensuring that every output from one component can serve as valid input for another. Two types of compatibility exist: strong and weak, with the latter permitting components to perform internal actions prior to accepting a message. This study considers open systems and identifies conditions where strong/weak synchronization is sufficient and/or necessary for achieving strong/weak asynchronous connectivity. It reveals that these conditions specifically define half-duplex systems. The researchers then delve into verifying weak asynchronous compatibility in potentially non-half-duplex systems and develop a decision-making criterion that guarantees weak asynchronous compatibility. Furthermore, they explore scenarios where this criterion is exhaustive, implying that its absence signifies a lack of weak asynchronous compatibility. The investigation also touches upon non-deadlock situations and examines correlations between deadlock-freeness in both synchronized and asynchronous environments.

When dealing with infinite mathematical or computational problems,
extending analysis and computation beyond that point becomes extremely challenging.
By applying specific singular transformations, which can be identified computationally,
it's theoretically possible to cross into the realm beyond infinity, allowing the
solution to regain normal behavior and computations to proceed smoothly.
In ODE models, this transition occurs instantly; however, in spatially distributed PDEs,
the crossing can take place over a finite period, requiring buffers to detect and apply
singular transformations locally, ensuring smooth computations.
These findings and accompanying tools pave the way for a methodical approach
to circumvent infinity and tackle a wider variety of evolutionary equations;
they also enable meaningful and seamless performance of necessary calculations.
Our analysis involves a regularization process through complexification and explores
its effects on system dynamics, as well as discussing various compactification
transformations and their underlying implications.

Ingredients:

1 cup yellow cornmeal

1 cup all-purpose flour

1 tablespoon sugar

1 teaspoon salt

1 teaspoon baking powder

1/2 teaspoon baking soda

1 egg

1 cup milk

1/4 cup butter, melted

Directions:

1. Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Lightly grease a baking sheet.

2. In a large bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda.

3. In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and milk. Stir in melted butter. Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients, stirring just until combined.

4. Drop dough by spoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.

THE moments passed as at a play;
I had the wisdom love brings forth;
I had my share of mother-wit,
And yet for all that I could say,
And though I had her praise for it,
A cloud blown from the cut-throat North
Suddenly hid Love's moon away.
Believing every word I said,
I praised her body and her mind
Till pride had made her eyes grow bright,
And pleasure made her cheeks grow red,
And vanity her footfall light,
Yet we, for all that praise, could find
Nothing but darkness overhead.
We sat as silent as a stone,
We knew, though she'd not said a word,
That even the best of love must die,
And had been savagely undone
Were it not that Love upon the cry
Of a most ridiculous little bird
Tore from the clouds his marvellous moon.
ALTHOUGH crowds gathered once if she but showed her face,
And even old men's eyes grew dim, this hand alone,
Like some last courtier at a gypsy camping-place
Babbling of fallen majesty, records what's gone.
These lineaments, a heart that laughter has made sweet,
These, these remain, but I record what-s gone.  A crowd
Will gather, and not know it walks the very street
Whereon a thing once walked that seemed a burning cloud

Matt Williams insists he has no thoughts of quitting as national coach as a result of the power struggle currently gripping Scottish rugby.
The chairman, chief executive and three non-executive directors all departed in a row over the game's future direction. But Williams said: "I want to make it clear that I'm committed totally to Scottish rugby. "I've brought my family here and we've immersed ourselves in Scottish life. There's no way that I'm walking away." However, he attempted to steer clear of taking sides in the dispute. "I'd like to stress that the national team is separate to the political situation," he said.
"When you come to an undertaking like this and you are trying to make a difference then there are always people who will begrudge you, who are jealous and want to try to drag you down. "When you have that situation, you have to have the courage of your convictions to see it through. "There was some very unhelpful and uninformed comment that the national team had received a massive increase in budget at the expense of other parts of Scottish rugby and that is simply not the case. "Like all good coaches, you go and ask for an increase. But we were told in no uncertain terms that the financial situation did not allow that. "The idea that we are lighting cigars with £20 notes while the rest of Scottish rugby flounders is absolutely untrue. "We also attracted criticism because of the number of days players spent with the national team. "But let me give you the truth. Our Irish counterparts, whom we have to compete with in a few days' time, had 70 days together at the summer. "They are currently in camp now and they will have another 21 days in camp before the Six Nations. "That means they will have 91 days away from their club from July until the Six Nations. We, on the other hand, will have 16. "There must be a win-win philosophy and attitude within Scottish rugby and that is what we are after - both groups winning, not competing."

Given a 3D surface defined by an elevation function on a 2D grid as well as
non-spatial features observed at each pixel, the problem of surface
segmentation aims to classify pixels into contiguous classes based on both
non-spatial features and surface topology. The problem has important
applications in hydrology, planetary science, and biochemistry but is uniquely
challenging for several reasons. First, the spatial extent of class segments
follows surface contours in the topological space, regardless of their spatial
shapes and directions. Second, the topological structure exists in multiple
spatial scales based on different surface resolutions. Existing widely
successful deep learning models for image segmentation are often not applicable
due to their reliance on convolution and pooling operations to learn regular
structural patterns on a grid. In contrast, we propose to represent surface
topological structure by a contour tree skeleton, which is a polytree capturing
the evolution of surface contours at different elevation levels. We further
design a graph neural network based on the contour tree hierarchy to model
surface topological structure at different spatial scales. Experimental
evaluations based on real-world hydrological datasets show that our model
outperforms several baseline methods in classification accuracy.

A new study has highlighted the mixed nature of internet search habits, revealing both simplicity and complexity. Approximately 87% of users successfully find what they're searching for on a search engine, yet many struggle to differentiate between sponsored and organic results. The Pew Research Center's findings indicate that nearly all internet users rely heavily on Google, Ask Jeeves, MSN, and Yahoo. Notably, around 50% of respondents stated they would lose trust in search engines if advertisers' payments were concealed. Researchers discovered that the average user spends roughly 43 minutes each month conducting 34 separate searches and views approximately 1.9 pages per hunt. Furthermore, a considerable portion of users – around 36% – conduct searches at least once a week, with 29% limiting their usage to occasional sessions. About 44% of users seek information that is essential to their activities, making it indispensable to them. Users often exhibit loyalty towards specific search engines; 44% rely exclusively on one site, while 48% use multiple search engines. Research conducted by Ask Jeeves revealed that individuals choose different search engines due to variations in data collection methods, which yield distinct results for the same query. Interestingly, over half of those surveyed acknowledged that alternative sources could provide equivalent information. Around 17% expressed indifference towards search engines, whereas 33% couldn't envision life without them. Approximately 68% believed that the presented results were a balanced representation of available information.

For this recipe, you'll need 6 ears of fresh corn on the cob, a quarter cup of olive oil, and a quarter cup of sliced onions. Begin by pulling back the husks but leaving them intact and removing the silk. Soak the corn in an ice bath for at least two hours before drying them thoroughly. Next, brush the kernels with oil and cover them with a few slices of onion, still wrapped in their husks. For a smoky flavor, set up a smoker to reach 225 degrees Fahrenheit using woods such as mesquite, fig, hickory, or apple. Alternatively, you can use a gas grill by placing wood chips in foil with holes for ventilation, then heating it to 225 degrees over low flames. Once the grill is ready, position the corn on it over indirect heat. Prepare your desired compound butter according to the provided recipes. After thirty minutes, apply a small amount of butter to each ear of corn, ensuring it coats as much of the exposed surface as possible. Repeat this process after another thirty minutes and let the corn smoke for an additional thirty minutes.

Vanilla Bean Rooibos Ice Cream
1 cup Whole Milk (avoid ultra-pasteurized)
2 cups Heavy Cream (avoid ultra-pasteurized)
2 tablespoons Organic Rooibos Tea Leaves
1 Madigascar Vanilla Bean, split and seeds scraped
3 tablespoons Honey
6 Large Egg Yolks
1 tablespoon Amaretto Liquer
3/4 cup Chopped Raw Almonds
Dulce de Leche
1 quart Whole Milk (avoid ultra pasteurized)
1 cup Sugar
3 tablespoons Honey
1 Vanilla bean, split and seeds scraped
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
Place the milk, sugar, vanilla bean, and honey into a medium saucepan, over medium heat. Bring the mixture just to a simmer, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar, and remove from the heat. Add the rooibos tea leaves, cover, and steep for 1 hour (NOTE: the long steep is critical for the best flavor). Add one cup of the cream to the tea/milk base, and warm the mixture (do NOT boil). Strain to remove the rooibos leave and vanilla bean (but don't worry if there are a few leaves remaining (they will be strained again). Discard the rooibos leaves; rinse and retain the vanilla bean. Set aside the remaining one cup of heavy cream in a medium bowl with a strainer on top. In a medium mixing bowl whisk the egg yolks until they lighten in color. Gradually add the warm cream base to the eggs. Temper the cream mixture into the eggs by gradually adding small amounts, until the remainder is incorporated. Return the egg and cream mixture to the saucepan and place over low heat. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon and reaches 170 to 175 degrees F. Strain the mixture into the one cup of cream previously set aside. Return the previously used vanilla bean to the mixture and place into an ice bath for 30 minutes. Place the mixture into the refrigerator for 4 to 8 hours or until the temperature reaches 40 degrees F or below. Remove the vanilla bean, pour the cooled cream mixture into an ice cream maker. Add one teaspoon of amaretto and process according to the manufacturer's directions. This should take approximately 25 to 35 minutes. In the last 5 minutes, add the raw almonds to incorporate (this step can be skipped if you don't care for nuts). Scoop the ice cream into a freezer proof container in sections, layering spoonfuls of the (refrigerated) Dulce De Leche between the layers, swirling to create a random pattern. Freeze for 3 to 4 hours to allow the ice cream to harden. Combine the milk, sugar, honey, vanilla bean and seeds in a large, 4-quart saucepan and place over medium heat. Bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved. Once the sugar has dissolved, add the baking soda and stir to combine. Reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered at a bare simmer. Stir occasionally, but do not re-incorporate the foam that appears on the top of the mixture. Continue to cook for 1 hour. Remove the vanilla bean after 1 hour and continue to cook until the mixture is a dark caramel color and has reduced to about 1 cup, approximately 1 1/2 to 2 hours. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh strainer. Store in the refrigerator in a sealed container until thoroughly cooled.

More than 5.2 million Germans were out of work in February, new figures show.
The figure of 5.216 million people, or 12.6% of the working-age population, is the highest jobless rate in Europe's biggest economy since the 1930s. The news comes as the head of Germany's panel of government economic advisers predicted growth would again stagnate. Speaking on German TV, Bert Ruerup said the panel's earlier forecast of 1.4% was too optimistic and warned growth would be just 1% in 2005.
The German government is trying to tackle the stubbornly-high levels of joblessness with a range of labour market reforms. At their centre is the "Hartz-IV" programme introduced in January to shake up welfare benefits and push people back into work - even if some of the jobs are heavily subsidised. The latest unemployment figures look set to increase the pressure on the government. Widely leaked to the German newspapers a day in advance, they produced screaming headlines criticising Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder's Social Democrat-Green Party administration. Mr Schroeder had originally come into office promising to halve unemployment.
Still, some measures suggest the picture is not quite so bleak. The soaring official unemployment figure follows a change in the methodology which pushed up the jobless rate by more than 500,000 in January. Adjusted for seasonal changes, the overall unemployment rate is 4.875 million people or 11.7%, up 0.3 percentage points from the previous month. Using the most internationally-accepted methodology of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), Germany had 3.97 million people out of work in January. And ILO-based figures also suggest that 14,000 new net jobs were created that month, taking the number of people employed to 38.9 million. The ILO defines an unemployed person as someone who in the previous four weeks had actively looked for work they could take up immediately.

Devastated, frustrated, angry at himself, he flees on foot in search of inner peace — to find it by running eastward until the dawn reveals whether or not it exists, a rash promise to himself made during a dreamlike evening alone in a hotel bar (with a pint!). He finds spiritual guidance along this journey when a Zen priest named Rinsho Takano agrees to drive Ethan across the country as Takano makes his own way back home after visiting an imprisoned brother monk. In exchange for the ride from Connecticut to Montana, Ethan will help the elderly, bald-as-a-billiard [and] half-blind monk track down old teacher-friends who have stopped returning his phone calls. This includes a reunion with Taka Takeda, author of On Jogging Through Womb With A View , a book which changed Ethan Jones' life over two decades ago and inspired him to become a jogger. But what Rinshodo seeks most of all are answers about death . . . namely, why we can never really be certain where our soul goes when the body dies! We propose Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based image analysis technique to segment raw RGB images taken of thin polished concrete samples under a digital optical microscope. Deep learning is gaining significant popularity in computer vision. We employ a state-of-the-art fully convolutional DNN (FCN) to extract semantic image segmentation of the microscopic RGB image. The network is trained on our custom-annotated concrete microscopy set (CS-Concrete Microscopy). Using the FCN-based semantic segmentation approach provides several key advantages in concrete petrographic image analysis. First, the resulting segmentation masks make it easier to interpret the images by automatically selecting the desired elements of interest and removing irrelevant information. Second, DNN-based segmentation enables precise measurement of petrographic image features and avoids the tedious process of manual human annotations that are highly susceptible to human subjectivity. To show the utility of our deep learning image analysis framework, we developed a quantitative segmentation evaluation metric, called Segmetric Index of Fidelity (SiF) for our CS-Concrete Microscopy. The segmentation metric is designed to evaluate the segmentation quality of the model on an unbiased test dataset. We found a correlation between the SiF score and the accuracy of automatic segmentation of microscopic image features. The automatic segmentation approach using SiF has the potential to significantly reduce time and effort of manual microscopic image analysis.
The paper is authored by a team of researchers/scientists from the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the Wisconsin Center for Advancing Research in Transportation, the Department of Engineering Professional Development, the Department of Civil Engineering at Pohang University of Science and Technology, and from Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS).
While the research paper appears to suggest that deep learning-based image recognition/ segmentation is better (objective) and more reliable, it's unclear to me why one cannot just measure concrete with digital callipers. It doesn't look like these researchers did a comparative study of the various image segmentation techniques on a standard dataset containing different variations of the images in their dataset. But then again, the study wasn't meant to be a comparison and may have other benefits.
One could also argue that while deep learning-based image segmentation is objectively better, it is also more expensive as it requires expensive deep learning-based AI

To make this dish, combine 3 eggs, 2 cups water, and 3 cups low-sodium chicken broth in a large pot. Add a pinch of salt and peel 10 garlic cloves; mash them and mix into the liquid. Then, add 2 bay leaves and 1 tsp of olive oil. Simmer on medium-high heat for 15 minutes. Chop the remaining garlic and add it to the pot along with the chopped chicken. Cook for another 10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked. Meanwhile, toast slices of French bread by brushing them with olive oil and cooking in a pan until golden brown. Fry eggs separately and sprinkle with parsley and pepper. Remove the soup from heat, then bring it to a boil and strain it before adding back the chicken and discarding the solids. Return the chicken to the pot and discard the remaining ingredients. Assemble each serving by placing toasted bread slices in a wide bowl, topping with 2 tbsp of Parmesan cheese, and ladling the soup over the cheese and bread. Top with an egg, garnish with parsley, and serve immediately. This dish pairs well with apple slices and steamed vegetables like broccoli or asparagus.

Ingredients:

- 4 large potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
- 1 cup skim milk
- 1/2 cup low-fat sour cream
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon paprika
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh chives
- 1/2 cup shredded low-fat cheddar cheese

Instructions:

1. In a large pot, combine the potatoes, onion, garlic, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil over high heat.

2. Reduce the heat to medium-low and let it simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15-20 minutes.

3. Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth. If you don't have an immersion blender, you can transfer the soup to a regular blender in batches and puree it that way. Just be careful as the soup will be hot.

4. Return the soup to the pot (if you used a regular blender) and stir in the skim milk, low-fat sour cream, salt, pepper, and paprika. Heat the soup over medium heat until it's heated through.

5. Ladle the soup into bowls and top each serving with a sprinkle of chives and shredded low-fat cheddar cheese.

6. Serve the soup hot with a side of crusty bread if desired.

This Creamy Potato Soup is low in fat but high in flavor. It's the perfect comfort food for a cold day. Enjoy!

A surge in students from southern England and Wales has applied to Scottish universities, despite fears of "fee refugees" attempting to evade higher education costs in England. According to Ucas, admissions rose by 17% between January 2005 and the previous year, reaching 27,700. This prompted Lifelong Learning Minister Jim Wallace to propose increasing tuition fees for English students studying in Scotland by £2,000 in an effort to curb the influx. Although legislation introducing these fees won't come into effect until autumn 2006, concerns persist about students seeking refuge in Scotland. However, universities' representatives argue that this uptick doesn't necessarily indicate Scottish institutions losing applicants; rather, prospective students are drawn by the perception of high-quality courses and Scotland's appeal as a study destination. David Caldwell, director of Universities Scotland, stated that some students might apply to Scottish universities to avoid potential increased fees at English institutions, but this isn't the primary driver. He noted that prospective students are aware they'll face top-up fees if enrolling in an English university in 2006, which may contribute to the apparent surge. Wallace concurred, emphasizing that these figures must be viewed in light of the broader context.

Rhubarb Crisp Ingredients:
Oat Topping:
* 2 cups rolled oats
* 1/4 tsp salt
* 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
* 1 cup brown sugar
* 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
* 1 cup margarine or butter

Rhubarb Filling:
* 2 tbsp cornstarch
* 1 cup granulated sugar
* 1 egg
* 3 cups chopped fresh or frozen rhubarb
* 1 cup canned crushed pineapple
* 1 tsp cinnamon

Instructions:
Preheat the oven to 350°F. 
Combine oat ingredients in a bowl until crumbly. Divide it between a 9x12 inch baking dish, pressing half down. Mix cornstarch, sugar, and beaten egg to form a smooth paste, then add chopped rhubarb, crushed pineapple, and cinnamon. Pour over the crust, sprinkle with the remaining crumbly mixture, and bake for 45-50 minutes, or until golden brown. Let cool slightly before serving with your preferred ice cream or whipped cream.

A contentious cartoon sparked a commotion in the Indian Parliament on May 11, 2012, prompting both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha to be adjourned due to the intense opposition from rival parties. Thirumavalavan, a Tamil Nadu-based MP, brought up the matter before the Lok Sabha, initially being denied permission to discuss it; however, he produced a copy of the offending cartoon featuring Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chairman of the drafting committee for India's constitution. The cartoon depicted Jawaharlal Nehru, the former prime minister, using a whip as he drove a snail alongside Ambedkar, symbolizing the Indian Constitution. This caricature was perceived as insulting to the Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes. It originated in a book published by the NCERT in 2006, under the UPA government led by Sonia Gandhi, with the support of the Ministry of Human Resource Development. Following the backlash, HRD Minister Kapil Sibal extended an apology to the nation regarding the cartoon, leading to its removal from NCERT textbooks.

By Edna St. Vincent Millay

Among the many hundred thousand people of Paris,
There is one who is quite unusually fair,
And when I saw her for the first time I felt uneasy,
As though I knew not what to do or where to turn.

It was not her eyes, though they were sweet and mild;
It was not her mouth, though the lips were fresh and red:
It was not her cheeks, though they were soft and warm;
It was not even he breast, though it was beautiful and round.

It was her hair: oh, glorious, glossy stuff!
It gleamed and it shone, a rich golden brown,
The glory of Youth, the joy of Summer's day,
And my heart stopped, and I forgot to run.

And then I knew 'twas not her hair alone,
But all of her body, and her spirit as well,
That made me know I had never seen anyone
Who looked, or felt, or thought, as she did.

And so I loved her, though I knew it all along,
From the moment that I first set eyes on her sweet,
Dear face, and her lovely, perfect body,
I loved her, and every day I love her yet.

But what is the use of talking about love?
For Heaven knows, in this dull world Love's dreams are vain,
And so I shut my eyes and dream about her none,
But live and work, and pray for a better time.

And though there were a million other girls
Just as lovely as she is anywhere,
I know that in all the world there is only one
Who is exactly like she is, and that is she.

And when I die, I will surely go to her,
For Death could not come between us, were it tried,
And so I have no fear of dying suddenly,
For I shall only be going to her side.

Though she will not know it, unless God should will
That women here on earth should have a soul as men,
Still, when I reach the other side, and leave this world of sin,
I'll find her waiting, and tell her all.
