Gordon Brown is to freeze petrol duty increases, fund a £1bn package to avoid big council tax rises and boost childcare and maternity leave.
In an upbeat pre-Budget report, he slightly increased borrowing but insisted economic targets would be met. The chancellor also hailed the longest period of growth in UK "industrial history" but denied he was "gloating". But Oliver Letwin, for the Tories, attacked government red tape and debt, dubbing Mr Brown "Sir Wastealot".
The shadow chancellor said Mr Brown's "golden rule" had "turned to dross in his hands" and said he was borrowing to spend, not invest, with predicted debt over the coming years totalling £170bn. Mr Letwin told MPs: "The tide is going out on the chancellor's credibility. He is spending, borrowing and taxing so much because he is not getting value for taxpayer's money."
Vincent Cable, for the Liberal Democrats, accused Mr Brown of ducking tough choices.
He said: "Last week the prime minister gave us the politics of fear; this week the chancellor has offered the economics of complacency. "There are serious challenges ahead from the falling dollar and from the rapid downturn in the UK housing market and rising personal debt. But they have not been confronted." Mr Brown rejected the Lib Dem's call to open up the government's books to the National Audit Office, saying decisions on tax and spending should be made by ministers. Some economists say his forecasts on public finances are wishful thinking. BBC economic editor Evan Davis said the figures were plausible but also a gamble.
Mr Brown's insistence he was not "gloating" was a pointed rebuttal of a warning from new European Commissioner Peter Mandelson. In his speech, he set out a 10-year childcare strategy for if Labour wins the next election.
It includes a £285m cash injection to extend paid maternity leave from six months to nine, with parents able to transfer leave from the mother to the father. He also promised to increase free nursery education for three and four-year-olds to 15 hours from April 2007. And funds would be provided to keep schools open from 0800 to 1800GMT to look after children while their parents were at work. Taken together, the measures would create a "welfare state that is truly family-friendly for the first time in its history", said Mr Brown. He also announced a cash hand-out for older pensioners, with payments of £50 for the over-70s as part of the winter fuel allowance. In a move ministers say should keep council tax rises below 5% next year, the chancellor said he was providing an extra £1bn for local councils. The money is expected to come from government departments such as health and education.
Mr Brown said he was set to meet his two fiscal rules - to borrow only to invest and keep debt "low and sustainable" - both in this economic cycle and the next. Borrowing figures for 2003/4 are £35bn - £2.5bn less than the £37.5bn predicted in March's budget, as already announced by the Office for National Statistics. Borrowing is tipped to fall to £31bn by 2005/06 - but that is still £2bn more than Mr Brown predicted in his March budget. Inflation would be 1.75% next year and 2% in the years to follow, Mr Brown forecast. He also pledged an extra £105m for security and counter-terrorism. Business groups have welcomed efforts to improve competitiveness and invest more in skills and innovation. But there worries about the costs of more family-friendly working. Simon Sweetman, from the Federation of Small Businesses, said: "The proposals on maternity leave have clearly been made with a general election in mind and with little thought to the impact on small employers."

Here is the abstract for the academic paper titled "A 2D dilated residual U-Net for multi-organ segmentation in thoracic CT":

Abstract: We present a 2D dilated residual U-Net for multi-organ segmentation in thoracic CT scans. Our network is designed to address the challenges of segmenting multiple organs in thoracic CT, which often have complex shapes and overlapping structures. The key innovation in our network is the use of dilated convolutions, which enable the network to capture more context and details from the input images. We also introduce a residual connection module that facilitates the training process and improves the performance of the network. Our network is trained on a large dataset of thoracic CT scans and evaluated on the publicly available MICCAI 2017 Multi-Organ Segmentation Challenge dataset. We achieve competitive results on the challenge dataset and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in segmenting multiple organs in thoracic CT.

The sachem (sakim, sagamore, sagamo, sahe) was the chief or head among the indigenous people of New England. The title was used during the 17th and 18th centuries. According to the Oxford English Dictionary the word is a corruption "by folk etymology" of the phrase "by and by chief", in imitation of the Algonquian expression for it, meaning "Great Sachem" or "Head-Man-By-And-By" (cf. Byram).
The English word "sachem" derives from the earlier pronunciation "sagamore".
The title Sachem was typically used for the leaders of a given sachemdom or wampum belt. Wampum belts were similar to the Roman "tribute of nations" or Iroquois "league of nations", representing a confederacy of tribes. A sachemdom could comprise numerous individual (or autonomous or semi-autonomous?) bands, which could be identified by a local term. There was great fluidity among bands, so that at any given time one could identify many bands but any particular band might represent a different collection of tribes several decades hence.
Sachemdoms were ruled by a "Great Sachem". The Great Sachem was usually selected in a way similar to other forms of autocracy, sometimes through a trial by combat. In some places there was a council of sachems who advised the Great Sachem. However, it is not clear that the Great Sachem actually held sway over all the sachems (e.g. if he could override their decisions, etc.), but in general seemed to rule through consensus.
The Sachemship of Narragansett, for example, was established in 1643 and the first Great Sachem was Canonicus, son of Miantunnomu.
After the Great Sachem's death or retirement, his son often became successor. In some cases, when there was no clear heir, the Narragansett elected a Great Sachem. The last Great Sachem of the Narragansett, Joseph Jenks, was elected and ruled until 1858, when the Great Sachem was deposed, and the sachemship was abolished.

In the dimly lit hallway of my childhood home, a faded photograph hangs of a young self at just four years old, holding hands with my grandfather and wearing a traditional plaid cap and a sweater adorned with reindeer. The image captures the simplicity and innocence of youth, with a recent haircut evident on the skin above his ears. This younger version of myself gazes up with a sweet smile, oblivious to the hardships that life will bring.

Standing near the edge of despair, I yearn to impart some wisdom to my past self, in the comfort of our family's backyard in Rochester, New York, during a warm summer in 1951. I wish to warn him about the pain and difficulties that await him – shattered hearts, tragic accidents, and devastating losses. I want him to understand the emptiness that can overwhelm even the strongest souls.

I would urge him to be cautious and prepared, to watch out for potential dangers and to stay warm during harsh winter months. I'd implore him to be mindful and gentle, to take care of himself. But he wouldn't listen, lost in his own world, smiling serenely.

All I could do was stand by and watch as life unfolded its course. That was a constant truth – life had a way of finding its own path, no matter what. So, all I'm left with now is this enduring feeling of affection for that young boy, and the hope that he knows how much I cherish him.

On their first journey through the Wall of Light, they travel to Boston in 1775, to help Paul Revere and the Sons of Liberty spread the word that British Redcoats are on the march. Shadow has discovered seven gaps in the story of Paul Revere's midnight ride. If those gaps are not filled, the American Revolution may never be fought, and liberty as we know it will cease to exist. Travel through time with them and follow Paul Revere, William Dawes, and Samuel Prescott, ordinary men who choose to act for the cause of liberty. Meet Dr. Joseph Warren, one of the leaders of the Sons of Liberty, as he sets the famous ride in motion. Watch Robert Newman and John Pulling as they attempt to place signal lanterns in the steeple of the Old North Church. But, look out for Pratt! If he has his way, you could become trapped in a time when King George III rules, and there is no liberty and justice for all.

Cole makes five central points. First, he states that Al-Qaeda is better thought of as a small cult rather than a true mass movement like fascism or communism in the early 20th century. Second, he states that the Muslim world contains large sections of people who can be potential allies to the U.S. Third, he states that American energy independence cannot really happen. Fourth, he states that Iran is not an implacable enemy of the U.S. and should be engaged with. Fifth, he states that coalition forces in Iraq should undergo a careful, deliberate military disengagement rather than an immediate withdrawal or an extended military presence. Cole makes an analogy between Islamists and what he sees as similar American groups. He views Salafi jihadists as fundamentalist vigilantes similar to Timothy McVeigh while Wahabis can been seen similar to the Amish. Cole argues that a distinction should be made between al-Qaeda and non-violent, compromising political Islamists such as the Muslim Brotherhood the same way far right militas in the U.S. are distinguished from the center-right Republican Party.

Other People's Money begins just before the 1987 stock market crash, and describes the conflict between a ruthless, predatory leveraged buyout specialist, Larry Crowne, and his longtime rival, Henry Ross, who is the CEO of a well-established family-owned bank. Crowne specializes in hostile takeovers of companies, buying them, and breaking them up for profit. In this instance, Crowne is attempting to buy United States Electrical, a lighting fixture company based in Providence, Rhode Island. Ross is convinced that UE is a solid company and will not break up the company, and he tries to rally the UE employees to fight off the takeover.

As the story progresses, Crowne's leveraged buyouts grow larger and more daring, and he becomes increasingly entangled with the political establishment, most notably with GovernorDX, who is running for the United States Senate. Crowne initially supports DX's campaign, but ends up supporting his opponent Jack Riley when DX takes a stance that favors organized labor, which would make it more difficult for Crowne to take over companies.

The novel traces Crowne's meteoric rise as he arranges ever-larger takeovers of major corporations, while Henry Ross tries in vain to rally the company owners whose businesses are being taken over. Meanwhile, DX's political career becomes increasingly entangled with Crowne's business dealings. In the end, Crowne's ambitions get the better of him when he attempts to buy a major New York bank, and instead ends up being wiped out when the stock market crash of 1987 occurs.

The story is of three sisters, of whom the youngest is chosen by Tsar Saltan (Saltán) to be his wife, while he makes the other two his royal cook and royal weaver. They are jealous, of course, and when the tsar goes off to war, and in his absence the tsaritsa gives birth to a son, Prince Gvidon (Gvidón), they arrange to have her and her child sealed up in a barrel and thrown into the sea. The sea itself takes pity on them, and they are cast up on the shore of a remote island, Buyan. The son, having quickly grown while in the barrel, goes hunting. He ends up saving an enchanted swan from a kite. The swan creates a city for Prince Gvidon to rule, but he is homesick, and the swan turns him into a mosquito. In this guise, he visits Tsar Saltan's court, where he stings his aunt in the eye and escapes. Back in his distant realm, the swan gives Gvidon a magical squirrel. But he continues to pine for home, so the swan transforms him into a fly. In this guise, Prince Gvidon visit's Saltan's court again and he stings his older aunt in the eye. The third time, the Prince is transformed into a bumblebee and stings the nose of his grandmother. In the end, he expresses a desire for a bride instead of his old home, at which point the swan is revealed to be a beautiful princess, whom he marries. He is visited by the Tsar, who is overjoyed to find his wife and newly-married son.

A commonly utilized metric in data clustering and image segmentation known as the Normalized Cut (NCut) function assesses the cost of dividing a graph in such a manner that clusters or segments that have a more balanced composition tend to have lower scores than those with uneven distributions. Unfortunately, this approach has a severe drawback – it consistently prevents the formation of singletons, even when individual nodes are only loosely connected to the remaining part of the graph. To address this issue, the Compassionately Conservative Balanced (CCB) Cut costs were introduced, which incorporate a tunable parameter allowing users to find an optimal balance between preventing excessive singletons and maintaining balanced partitions. Our analysis reveals that these modified costs can be reformulated as an orthogonal $\ell_{\tau}$-minimization problem, equivalent to finding Piecewise Flat Embeddings (PFE) for specific cases, and propose an efficient method for resolving the relaxed problem through the sequential minimization of reweighted Rayleigh quotients. By applying this approach to image segmentation using the BSDS500 dataset, our results demonstrate improved accuracy relative to ground truth and increased regional variability compared to NCut-based methods.

Engineering firm Balfour Beatty and five railway managers are to go on trial for manslaughter over the Hatfield rail crash in 2000.
Four people died when a section of rail broke and a high speed train derailed. Balfour Beatty's railway maintenance arm was in charge of the upkeep of the line at Hatfield, Hertfordshire. Balfour Beatty managers Anthony Walker and Nicholas Jeffries, and Railtrack managers Alistair Cook, Sean Fugill and Keith Lea all face individual charges. All five men, along with four others, are also accused of breaches of health and safety laws. Balfour Beatty Rail Maintenance faces a corporate manslaughter charge. It is expected the trial could last as long as a year. The accident, on 17 October 2000, happened when the London to Leeds express came off the tracks at 115 mph, when it was derailed by a cracked section of rail. The accident on the East Coast Main Line sparked major disruption. The overall responsibility for the line was Railtrack's - the company that has now become Network Rail. Those who died in the accident were Steve Arthur, 46, from Pease Pottage, West Sussex; Peter Monkhouse, 50, of Headingley, Leeds; Leslie Gray, 43, of Tuxford, Nottingham; and Robert James Alcorn, 37, of Auckland, New Zealand.

Arthritis of the joints is a significant concern for older adults. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is widely used to monitor the progression of arthritis. Nevertheless, its high costs and potential for human mistake make the evaluation process costly and unreliable. Furthermore, the inconsistencies between different observers complicate the assessment. Computer-assisted segmentation of knee MRI images holds great promise as a means to streamline the diagnostic process and enhance accuracy. Over the years, numerous studies have explored automated and semi-automated techniques for segmenting knee MRIs. To date, however, there lacks a thorough review of existing methods. This study aims to categorize these approaches based on their underlying principles, summarize the present state of research, and outline future directions.

In this paper, we present a state-of-the-art architecture for real-time person segmentation. Our method is fully automatic, requires no user input, and can be run on CPUs. We do so by training a single deep network that operates on RGB images of a whole person. Our network is trained to predict a confidence map that is used to obtain pixelwise human masks. Our main contribution is a novel loss function for training the network, composed of pixel-wise and group-wise losses. The group-wise loss explicitly penalizes segmentation errors on the boundary, leading to precise predictions in challenging situations, such as occlusions and self-occlusions. To achieve real-time performance, our network, dubbed keypoint transfer (KT), is based on keypoint detection and transfer, where segmentation masks are predicted for keypoint locations, and transferred to all pixels of the image. This step requires very few operations, compared to convolutions, and therefore is suitable for efficient inference on a CPU. We also use it to generate new training data, which is made compatible with the network through the use of a group-wise loss. KT provides state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy for multi-person scenarios, while also running at 30 frames per second on an unmodified CPU.

China's biggest spirits maker, Kweichow Moutai, has signed a deal to boost its presence in Italy's booming wine market by distributing its products through Illva Saronno, one of the country's oldest and biggest liquor companies.

The partnership, sealed on Thursday, gives Illva Saronno, producer of the Disaronno liqueur, distribution rights to Moutai's portfolio of baijiu, a distilled grain spirit usually made from sorghum.

Illva said in a statement that the partnership aimed to "strengthen the presence of both companies on their respective home markets and to develop business opportunities in third countries".

Moutai, whose fiery liquor is a favourite tipple of China's ruling Communist Party elite, has been looking to expand its global footprint.

The company's lustre has dimmed somewhat in China in recent months as its flagship baijiu product has fallen out of favour with some younger consumers, who have turned to imported spirits such as Scotch whisky.

However, it remains immensely popular in China, with its sales jumping 25% in the first half of 2022, and it is hoping to win over new consumers in Europe and elsewhere.

Chinese drinks companies have been looking to expand abroad as domestic consumption slows and foreign sales of Chinese spirits, wine and beer are growing quickly.

China's beer giant Budweiser Brewing Co Ltd, formed by the merger of Budweiser and local giant Tsingtao, has said it aims to become one of the world's top 10 beer companies within a decade.

In July, Budweiser Brewing signed a deal with Coca-Cola Co's Costa coffee chain to roll out a line of coffee-flavoured drinks in China.

The unemployment rate in Australia has reached its highest point in four years, according to recent data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The jobless rate increased from 5.5% in December 2018 to 5.7% in January 2019, marking the first rise since August last year.

While this increase may be cause for concern, experts have noted that it is still within the range considered healthy for the economy. In addition, they pointed out that the participation rate - which measures the proportion of working-age people who are either employed or looking for work - remained steady at 65.6%, indicating that there was no significant drop in workforce engagement.

Furthermore, Prime Minister Scott Morrison hailed the figures as evidence that his government's economic policies were paying off. He emphasized that over 500,000 jobs had been created under his administration and vowed to continue supporting businesses and workers alike.

However, opposition leader Bill Shorten criticized the government's handling of the situation, arguing that inadequate investment in education and training was contributing to skill shortages and wage stagnation. He called on the government to do more to address these issues and ensure sustainable growth for all Australians.

Overall, while the latest employment numbers paint a mixed picture, they serve as a reminder that Australia's labour market remains resilient despite global uncertainties and domestic challenges.

We present a fully relativistic calculation of the observed galaxy number
counts in the linear regime. We show that besides the density fluctuations and
redshift-space distortions, various relativistic effects contribute to
observations at large scales. These effects all have the same physical origin:
they result from the fact that our coordinate system, namely the galaxy
redshift and the incoming photons' direction, is distorted by inhomogeneities
in our universe. We then discuss the impact of the relativistic effects on the
angular power spectrum and on the two-point correlation function in
configuration space. We show that the latter is very well adapted to isolate
the relativistic effects since it naturally makes use of the symmetries of the
different contributions. In particular, we discuss how the Doppler effect and
the gravitational redshift distortions can be isolated by looking for a dipole
in the cross-correlation function between a bright and a faint population of
galaxies.

Germaine Greer has criticised Celebrity Big Brother's "bullying" of housemates after quitting the reality TV show.
She said "superior" bullying tactics, like making housemates cold and hungry, could encourage playground bullying. She also condemned the "complete irresponsibility" of adding Brigitte Nielsen's former mother-in-law Jackie Stallone to the house on Monday. Nielsen had panicked that if she reacted badly it could harm her access to her children, Greer said. The feminist writer and broadcaster said Big Brother had behaved "like a child rather than a parent" by taunting contestant John McCririck after denying him a cola drink. "I thought it was actually demonstrating the role of taunting in the playground and there are so many children whose lives have actually been destroyed by taunting in the playground," Greer said. She also said that her fellow housemates had publicity-seeking "agendas".
"I had no idea who would be in here and it's wrong for me to present myself in the same context as they are." Media observers had been surprised by Greer's initial decision to join the third celebrity version of the Channel 4 reality TV show, given that she has written critical articles about the format in the past. As she packed her suitcase to leave the house she told fellow housemates: "I'm leaving over specific issues, but best for everyone if I don't discuss them. "I have a problem with decisions, I make them fast and when I make them, I stick to them." Greer had earlier failed to persuade other contestants to stage a naked protest against Big Brother.
Other celebrities to walk out of a reality show TV include Sex Pistol John Lydon, former EastEnders actress Danniella Westbrook and ex-E17 singer Brian Harvey who all left I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here. Previous Big Brother housemates to leave before their time were Sunita Sharma and Sandy Cumming from the third series of the non-celebrity version of the show.

GW Pharmaceuticals' prescription cannabis-based medication is poised for approval in Canada, targeting multiple sclerosis patients. Initially, UK regulators expressed skepticism over its effectiveness but Canadian authorities have announced plans to consider it. Following a recent stock surge, GW Pharmaceuticals anticipates full Canadian approval within the next few months, marking a significant milestone for both the company and MS patients worldwide. With final approval expected soon, GW Pharmaceuticals CEO says they're optimistic about the prospect of getting regulatory clearance for Sativex in early 2005. The UK government previously authorized GW Pharmaceuticals to cultivate cannabis for research purposes, which includes Sativex, a compound comprising THC and CBD, proven beneficial in treating arthritis as well. Tens of thousands of plants are cultivated in a secluded area in England. Although initial expectations were high last year, several setbacks have pushed back the UK launch of Sativex; however, the latest development led to an 8.5% increase in GW Pharmaceuticals' shares.

For Dipping Sauce
5 ounces apricot jam
1/4 cup crushed pineapple
1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes
For Coleslaw
1/4 cup water
1/4 cup olive oil
1/2 cup chopped scallion
1/2 cup cilantro
1 garlic clove
1 pinch salt
2 limes, juiced
1/2 cup sour cream
1 cup chopped green cabbage
1 1/2 cups chopped purple cabbage
For Coconut Shrimp
12 shrimp
3 ounces beer
2 eggs
1/2 cup milk
1 cup flour
1/4 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon salt
5 ounces coconut flakes
6 sheets rice paper
To Make Dipping Sauce: In a bowl, combine apricot jelly, crushed pineapple, apple cider vinegar and red pepper flakes. To Make Coleslaw: In a food processor, add water, olive oil, scallions, cilantro, garlic, salt and lime juice. Pulse until combined. Then add sour cream and pulse again. In a bowl, add chopped green and purple cabbage. Drizzle olive oil mixture over the cabbage and mix well. To Make Coconut Shrimp: In a bowl, whisk beer, egg, milk, flour, baking powder, and salt. Dip peeled, headless shrimp in the batter. Then coat with coconut flakes. Fry the breaded shrimp in hot oil until the coconut flakes are golden bown. Place shrimp on a drying rack over a sheet tray to allow the excess oil to drip off. Let cool. Assembling the Roll: On a sheet of moistened rice paper, place a scoop of coleslaw in the middle, edge of the paper (think of it as about 1/3 in from the edge). Then roll and fold until the top of the coleslaw is covered by the rice paper. After the shrimp cools down and excess oil drips off onto the rack, place two shrimp on the roll and continue to wrap until the shrimp is sealed well. Slice in half and serve with the dipping sauce.

Mitzvah Day International is an annual day of faith-based social action that takes place in November each year, primarily in the United Kingdom. On Mitzvah Day each year, community groups and individuals undertake a range of volunteer projects for those in need in their local community. Organizations register with Mitzvah Day, which in turn helps match volunteers with local projects. The objective is to encourage people to give their time, rather than their money, to worthwhile local causes, whilst also creating deeper linkages within communities and supporting charities. In 2013, close to 30,000 people participated in Mitzvah Day around the world.
Though based within the UK's Jewish Community, Mitzvah Day traditionally marks the first day of UK National Inter Faith Week, and as a result has expanded to include participants from other faith communities as well.
'Mitzvah' is the Hebrew biblical term for 'deed' or 'commandment', which has come to mean 'good deed' or 'charitable act' in contemporary English. The 2020 date was Sunday November 15.

Mexican outfit Red Sharks Veracruz hope to sign Juninho if the Brazilian decides to leave Celtic frustrated at his lack of first-team action.
Their president, Gustavo Parente Sanchez, says Juninho "does not wish to remain in Scottish football anymore". Agent Brian Hassell insists that the 31-year-old Brazilian midfielder is determined to win back his place. "But, if the manager is not going to pick him, that's a different ball game," he told The Sun. "That's something we'd have to look at. Juninho deserves respect. He is not a little kid." Hassell warns that Juninho could reconsider his future at Celtic unless he is given a run of games by the end of the January transfer window.
Juninho was signed from Middlesbrough during the summer, but he has failed to live up to high expectations and has lost his place to 18-year-old Aiden McGeady. "He has 50 caps for Brazil and he's the best signing Celtic ever made," insisted Hassell. "He wants to play for Martin O'Neill, but does Martin O'Neill want to play him? "Juninho is not someone who has come through the Celtic ranks. He deserves much more respect." Sanchez is bullish about his hopes of prising Juninho from the Scottish champions, although Hassell believes Mexico would not be his preferred destination. "We have already spoken with Juninho and he said, if he has no firm offer from a club in Spain, Veracruz will be his destination," Sanchez told his club's official website. Celtic manager O'Neill is no respecter of reputations. "The onus is on Juninho to force his way into the team," he said. "Players get a game on merit. That's the way it has always been and that is certainly the case at Celtic Park."

The human brain functions as a multi-layered system that involves both forward and backward information flow between layers. This complexity can be replicated by a neural network, which is mathematically modeled after the brain's neuron structure. However, current implementations typically utilize only the forward flow of information from lower to higher layers, bypassing the inherent feedback mechanism. To address this limitation, our approach introduces Feedback U-Net, leveraging Convolutional LSTM for both segmentation and feedback processes. Unlike traditional U-Nets relying solely on forward processing, our proposed method incorporates feedback loops, where the output of each iteration serves as input for subsequent rounds, enhancing feature extraction capabilities. Our results demonstrate the superiority of this hybrid approach over conventional U-Nets, achieving better performance on the Drosophila cell image and Mouse cell image datasets.

A struggling actor named Guy Fletcher stumbles upon a humorous anecdote in a local pub about his late mother, renowned actress Selina Moore, while she was still alive. The joke, which compared Selina Moore to Ferrero Rocher chocolates, originated from a different context - it was initially used to poke fun at Princess Diana's untimely demise. Intrigued by its origins, Guy embarks on a quest to uncover the joke's history, despite his agent's warnings. Along the way, he encounters a captivating woman named Sally, whom he becomes smitten with. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he attracts the attention of a shadowy organization, spearheaded by the enigmatic Rupert Liddy, whose exceptional memory makes him nearly uncatchable. These agents employ tactics typical of jests, such as using archetypes and stereotypes, to thwart Guy's efforts. Framed for a murder, he flees, seeking solace in Sally, only to find her house destroyed and her mother, suffering from a rare condition, injured but alive. Determined to unravel the truth, they join forces to follow the trail of clues, leading them to a company called Sphinx, supposedly a vacuum cleaner manufacturer. Despite numerous dead ends and failed attempts, they eventually pinpoint the joke's origin to a location near the Suffolk coastline. Guided by a hunch, they arrive at a seaside town, where they spend the night in an abandoned amusement park and surrender to their desires. Their investigation continues in the nearby village of Kelford.

Dinosaurs. Amusement Park. Tourists. Disaster.

Jurassic World has them all.

Naturally, I had to see it.

The beginning holds much promise, and it gets your hopes up for the disaster to come. When it does, there are some great action sequences, especially ones with the glass ball containing the soft, chewy child centre.

Unfortunately the final act unravels into outright farce.

Chris Pratt is great as the affable yet bad-ass Raptor Whisperer. He's got an easy going charisma that could easily carry an iconic character like Indiana Jones.

Bryce Dallas Howard plays Claire Dearing, the uptight park manager, who initially clashes with the laid back Owen. Of course you know where the tension goes.

The film tries to flesh out Claire's character by throwing in her two nephews (someone and another kid), who do double duty as McGuffins.

Vincent D'Onofrio shows up as Hoskins, a villainous representative of the military-industrial complex angling to weaponize velociraptors. He's all sneers and scenery chewing, so obviously evil he's got a goatee. D'Onofrio does it well but the evil plan he's been saddled with by the writers makes no sense at all.

The director, Colin Trevorrow, said in interviews that he wanted the dinosaurs to act like real animals, not cartoon monsters. Quelle surprise! I had no idea, as he has well-fed winged dinos (or near enough to dinos) go on a crazed orgy of violence against hapless tourists. Why? Because cool action sequence!

One poor soul is even treated to the most outlandishly elongated death sequence I've ever seen, all to no end. It didn't justify anything, paid nothing back, offered no comeuppance. It was just gleeful indulgence in sadistic torture of a minor character. It was an Itchy & Scratchy moment.

Which brings us to the final act: turn off your brain before it begins.

The first movie proved you could have a smart script and dinosaurs in the same movie. After that, the IQ of the series dropped with each outing. The first one had chaos theory and amber and DNA extraction and cleverness up the whazoo. It was AWESOME.

What does this one have? Hackneyed evil plans, a clunky plot, and characters so smart they run from T-Rex's in high heels.

The franchise has had a lobotomy.

The Indianapolis Zoo is a zoo located in White River State Park, in Indianapolis, Indiana, United States, housing more than 3,800 animals of more than 320 species and subspecies. The institution is accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) and the American Alliance of Museums as a zoo, an aquarium, and as a botanical garden. The zoo is a private non-profit organization, receiving no tax support and is supported entirely by membership fees, admissions, donations, sales, grants, and an annual fundraiser. History
In 1944, Lowell Nussbaum, columnist for the Indianapolis Times, and later the Indianapolis Star, began to advocate for a zoo through his column "Inside Indianapolis", which inspired the incorporation, in October 1944 of the Indianapolis Zoological Society.  Soon the members of this group had outlined the plans for their zoo. Group members were adamant that "the zoo will rely on admissions, in-park sales, contributions, and memberships to support the zoo". However, it would not be until 20 years later, in 1964, that the zoo opened to the public.

"Moonrise Kingdom" is a whimsical delight, as expected from auteur Wes Anderson whose stylistic flair and unique storytelling techniques shine throughout this film. The plot revolves around two love-struck pre-teens, Sam and Suzy, who decide to run away together, prompting a quaint New England town's obsessive search for them.

The movie is a strikingly profound portrait of adolescence yearning that beautifully combines innocence, love, and adventure, delivering it through Anderson's indelible lens. The visualization is a testament to Anderson's singular vision, conjuring a world filled with vivid color palettes, symmetrical frames, and a detailed aesthetic that emits a magical touch of nostalgia and child-like wonder.

The performances are endearing and impactful, particularly by the young leads Jared Gilman and Kara Hayward. They navigate their roles with an inherent maturity that makes their characters' journey believable and engaging. The supporting cast adds more extraordinary layers to the film with the likes of Bill Murray, Tilda Swinton, Edward Norton, and Bruce Willis, all turning in memorable performances.

The music score is poignant and captures the essence of the 1960s setting impeccably. It forms an integral part of the film, acting as a character unto itself, and helping unveil the depths of emotions and pivotal plot developments. From classical pieces to folksy tunes, the score permeates every scene, enhancing the dynamics between the characters and their environment.

"Moonrise Kingdom" is a heartwarming tale of young love, rebellious spirit, and the enchanting pull of the great outdoors; it is as charming and quirky as it is insightful. It's a vibrant piece of cinematic art that resonates deeply with viewers, regardless of age. Its clever additives of humor are well-placed, providing a balanced mix of laughter, sentimentality, and intensity.

This film, while keeping in sync with Anderson's distinct narrative technique, stands as a testament to his exceptional ability to create captivating, original stories. It is a brilliant, emotionally rich film that reminds us of the rousing whirlwind that is young love and the indomitable spirit of childhood. Thus, "Moonrise Kingdom" is much more than an escapist adventure; it is a precious tribute to the youthful courage, uncomplicated love, and unvanquished imagination we often forget after crossing the bridge to adulthood. For any cinema enthusiast or admirer of unique storytelling, this film comes highly recommended.

segmentation, as dense labels demand significant human intervention. Generally,
the annotation burden is mitigated by labeling datasets with weaker forms of
supervision, e.g. image-level labels or bounding boxes. Another option are
semi-supervised settings, that commonly leverage a few strong annotations and a
huge number of unlabeled/weakly-labeled data. In this paper, we revisit
semi-supervised segmentation schemes and narrow down significantly the
annotation budget (in terms of total labeling time of the training set)
compared to previous approaches. With a very simple pipeline, we demonstrate
that at low annotation budgets, semi-supervised methods outperform by a wide
margin weakly-supervised ones for both semantic and instance segmentation. Our
approach also outperforms previous semi-supervised works at a much reduced
labeling cost. We present results for the Pascal VOC benchmark and unify weakly

A comprehensive book by Boyer explores how our minds construct fundamental aspects of religion through cognitive inference systems, mirroring the way humans perceive meaningful patterns in nature, such as recognizing faces in inanimate objects. Drawing on insights from various fields like anthropology, neuroscience, and linguistics, Boyer argues that these ideas have evolved naturally. He uses the concept of "cognitive modules," which are like mental devices that aid in making inferences and assumptions. According to Boyer, widespread beliefs in supernatural entities, like deities, ancestors, and spirits, stem from the innate tendency to detect agency - the instinctual notion that something or someone is responsible for events, even if no one is present. When we notice unusual occurrences, such as branches swaying or strange noises, our brains automatically attribute them to a conscious entity. Boyer references E.E. Evans-Pritchard's anecdote about a termite-infested roof collapse, where both the anthropologist attributed the cause to termites but sought to understand the underlying reason behind the timing and specific circumstances. In Boyer's framework, religion emerges as a secondary development from cognitive modules, akin to how language relies on pre-existing linguistic modules.

To prepare the lamb, remove it from the refrigerator about 30 minutes prior to cooking. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Use a sharp knife to create six small punctures on the fatty side of the roast and gently push the garlic cloves into these openings. Sprinkle both sides of the lamb liberally with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of oil. Carefully insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of the leg, avoiding direct contact with the bone. Place the lamb on a roasting rack in a large pan and roast at 400°F (200°C) for 40 minutes, allowing the exterior to brown. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C) and continue cooking for an additional 40 to 50 minutes or until the internal temperature reaches 140°F (60°C). 

If you prefer medium-rare, adjust the cooking time accordingly to achieve an internal temperature of 145 to 150°F (63 to 66°C). Once done, let the lamb rest for half an hour before slicing. The Liberal Democrats have unveiled plans to build 100,000 new "affordable" homes on publicly owned land.
The party's scheme would allow people to buy a share in a home through a mutual home ownership trust, as a way of getting onto the housing ladder. The Lib Dems would also encourage the conversion of existing buildings in an effort to protect greenfield sites. Labour has already announced plans to help first-time buyers and the Tories would extend right-to-buy schemes.
All the major parties are focusing on the issue in the run-up to the election after a survey suggested first-time buyers could not afford a home in 92% of UK towns. The Lib Dems say their "mutual homes" would let people buy a share of a property, usually worth about 5% of the building costs. Party leader Charles Kennedy said the homes would be affordable because they would be built on surplus public sector land, donated by central or local government. People would also only have to pay for the cost of the building and not the land, he added.
They would spend about 30% of their monthly salary on rent and buying extra shares in the property. When they moved house, they would be able to cash in on any rise in property prices by selling their share. It would also allow councils to vary discounts to tenants given the right to buy their council homes so local needs were taken into account. Mr Kennedy said: "Mutual homes will offer people the opportunity to build up an equity stake in a home gradually, investing only as much as they can afford."
There are also plans to prevent high house prices forcing people out of their local communities. The kind of "golden share" used by the Lib Dems in South Shropshire could be rolled out more widely. Under the plan, councils secure deals with developers where they keep a 1% share in a property scheme so properties cannot be sold on the open market. Instead, they are sold at "build cost" to people who the local council decides have local needs. The party says its help for first-time buyers can be funded at no extra cost to the taxpayer. But the plans involve changing the VAT system, which the party says often makes it too expensive to renovate existing buildings.
The Conservatives claimed the plans would amount to an extra tax of up to £11,000 on every new house. "This is typical of Lib Dem hypocrisy," said Tory shadow local government secretary Caroline Spelman. "They claim that they want to help people on to the property ladder, but the small print of their policies reveal how they intend to price even more people out of the housing market." The flagship Tory proposal on housing policy is to give a million more housing association tenants the right to buy their homes. Labour has said it will allow 300,000 council and housing association tenants to buy a share in their homes. Housing Minister Keith Hill said much of the Lib Dem plans mimicked the government's strategy. "However, as usual, the Lib Dems' proposals are completely uncosted," he said. Mr Hill said he also asked whether the Lib Dems would match Labour's promise to spend £42bn on making refurbishing and repair council homes by 2010.

Reading the back cover of the DVD and seeing that Colin Firth and Ben Kingsley are given top billing, I expected an intelligent King Arthur story. Well, it really wasn't either, although I did find it entertaining. I must not have read the description carefully enough. No matter; overall, it was fun but just a little too silly. I'm beginning to wonder about the discernment of some of these actors, how they can play such intelligent roles for a film or two and then revert to something like this.

Anyway, the story is really a Roman empire one, not a King Arthur story. We only see the tie-in to the later in the last few minutes of the film, in the epilogue. This action story is all about the last Caesar, a small boy, and the last legion that fought as Rome had now been taken over by the Goths. The Roman Empire had come to an end.

Mixed in with that tale was the famous "excalibur" sword. We see the origins of that and how it eventually got into the hands of King Arthur. But, once again, that is only explained in the final minutes. However, the sword is used by the good Roman general who protects the last Caesar from the Goths, who want him imprisoned for life, or killed.

What made the story interesting, at least for me, was the chase-scene type atmosphere of a small band of heroes protecting a little boy, fleeing the bloodthirsty Goths until they could mount some sort of counter-attack in the north in Brittania. That, and the pretty computer-generated scenery and action stunts, kept it interesting. However, don't look for credibility in those action scenes and expect the typical political-correctness of today (i.e. where a woman beats up hundreds of men and the good guys of all colors prevail despite ridiculous odds).

Some parts of this will leave you shaking your head in disbelief. You will feel you're watching a kids' film at times. However, if you want an hour-and-a-half of decent escapist fare, and can put your brain on hold for that time, it fits the bill and will at least entertain you.

Ingredients:
1(14-16 lb) whole turkey, neck and giblets removed
2 large apples, cored and thinly sliced
2 poblano peppers, seeded and thinly sliced
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 teaspoon dried thyme
Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions: 

Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Rinse the turkey inside and out with cold water and pat dry with paper towels. Place the turkey breast side up in a roasting pan or a turkey roaster. 

In a small bowl, mix together the garlic, olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper. Rub the mixture all over the turkey, both inside and out.

Reusing old mobile phones offers both ecological and social advantages.
A study by the Forum for the Future discovered that in certain underdeveloped countries, refurbished mobile phones can bridge the digital gap. Due to their low cost, these reclaimed devices can serve as viable alternatives for individuals in less affluent regions. However, more needs to be done to collect discarded phones instead of allowing them to deteriorate in landfills.

In the United Kingdom alone, approximately 15 million mobile phones become obsolete annually. Approximately 37.5 percent of these outdated units are returned to manufacturers for recycling or reuse. Unfortunately, this results in a massive accumulation of approximately 90 million unused, discarded phones – roughly equivalent to 9,000 tons of waste. According to James Goodman, the report's author and senior advisor at the Forum for the Future, people often possess multiple phones, resulting in a considerable amount of electronic waste.

These discarded phones pose a risk of releasing hazardous materials into the environment if sent to landfills. Goodman prefers that people return their used phones to operators, which can then be repurposed overseas, giving them a new life. While there is a well-known environmental argument supporting this approach, Goodman emphasizes the importance of the social aspect. Older mobile phones prove particularly valuable in impoverished nations where residents seek to stay connected with loved ones yet cannot afford cutting-edge devices. A recent study conducted by the Forum for the Future focused on Romania, a nation with limited telecommunications infrastructure, found that refurbished mobile phones to be highly sought after. Romania's low wages make it one of the poorest European countries, exacerbating the need for affordable communication options.

In this study, we propose a novel approach to medical image segmentation called PGL (Prior-Guided Local Self-supervision). Our method leverages prior knowledge about the structure of the target object in an image and uses it to guide self-supervision during training. Specifically, we use local patches from the input image as well as corresponding patches from a set of reference images with known labels to train a neural network. We also incorporate a regularization term that encourages the learned features to be consistent across different patches within each image. The results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating prior knowledge into self-supervised learning for medical image segmentation tasks.

4 cups pear nectar
1/4 teaspoon agave nectar
Zest of 1 lemon, in long pieces
4 inches peeled fresh ginger, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
4 teaspoons maple syrup
Generous pinch of saffron (12 to 15 threads)
2 ripe but firm pears, preferably Bosc or Comice, peeled, cut in half, seeded, and stemmed
Pistachio Cream (page 181) or Cashew Cream (page 180), for serving (optional)
To make the broth, stir the pear nectar, agave nectar, lemon zest, ginger, maple syrup, and saffron together in a large saucepan or 3-quart saute pan over medium-high heat. Bring to a boil, then place the pear halves in the saucepan, flat side down. Place a piece of parchment paper over the pears and cover with a small plate to weight the pears down as they simmer. Lower the heat and simmer until the pears are tender and a knife pierces them all the way through without resistance. Remove the pears from the saucepan. Return the liquid to the heat, bring to a lively simmer, and cook until syrupy, about 10 minutes. Taste the liquid for a quick FASS check. It may need a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon juice to balance the flavors. Serve the pears drizzled with the poaching liquid and topped with a dollop of nut cream if you like. For vanilla broth, omit the lemon zest, ginger, maple syrup, and saffron, and instead stir 2 teaspoons of agave nectar into the pear nectar. Cut a vanilla pod in half lengthwise, scrape the seeds into the saucepan, then throw in the pod. Proceed with the recipe as above. For star anise broth, omit the lemon zest, ginger, maple syrup, and saffron, and instead stir in 4 pods of star anise, 4 whole cloves, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 teaspoons of agave nectar, and 2 teaspoons of freshly squeezed lemon juice. Proceed with the recipe as above. To seed and stem a pear beautifully, once its cut in half, use a melon baller to scoop out the center, making sure to remove all of the seeds. Then use a sharp paring knife to make a small angled slice on each side of the core, running out from the center of the pear to the stem. This will remove a clean and even triangle-shaped piece where the stem and the core had been. You can garnish the pears with the solids from the broth. Lemon peel, vanilla pods, star anise pods, and cloves all make beautiful garnishes. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days. In times past, a god of war was revered by mortals, who offered their loyalty and strength from the land of Israel to distant lands. 
His presence, marked by bloodshed and chaos, was invoked by rulers seeking power and plunder, often invoking his name in verse and incantation.
On battlefields, his radiant aura illuminated the carnage, and even the bodies of the fallen bore witness to his glory.
Many notable leaders, including Wolfe, Napoleon, and Nelson, were said to have caught sight of this divine being.
However, as time went on, his image began to fade, its golden splendor diminishing until only a faint shadow remained.
This decline was attributed to the growing awareness of the devastating consequences of war, which shook the foundations of human morality.
Some argue that it was the writings of poets and thinkers that played a significant role in exposing the horrors of war and bringing about this change.
Others suggest that the sheer scale of atrocities committed during conflicts contributed to the decline of the warrior god.
Despite this, seeds of compassion and understanding were sown by individuals who advocated for peaceful coexistence among nations.
As people gained insight into the complexities of conflict and the suffering it causes, they began to see enemies as fellow human beings rather than mere adversaries.
Warriors today fight with less fervor, their passions muted, and they struggle to find the courage to inspire others to follow them.
Although battles still erupt, the former deity of war seems distant and forgotten, even as people cling to outdated notions of martial valor.
Let us celebrate both the legacy of the past and the emergence of a new era of peace and cooperation.

We perform a rigorous spectral analysis of the intrinsic $B$-mode power spectrum $P_{BB}$ in the limit of a large horizon and at leading order in the slow-roll approximation. This analysis requires a clear definition of the polarized $B$-mode spectrum on the whole probed angular scale range, which is lacking in the current literature. We introduce a new parametrization that is both well-defined and suitable for performing the slow-roll approximation. By means of this parametrization, we show that the amplitude of $P_{BB}$ is given by the usual expression in terms of the scalar tilt $n_S$, but with a spectral index $n_S^{(B)}$ different from the scalar one $n_S$. We evaluate the corresponding running of the $B$-mode spectral index, and provide a simple fitting function that depends on the two standard slow-roll parameters $\epsilon$ and $\eta$ and on a single extra parameter $\beta_B$ that governs the running. We show that the running of the $B$-mode spectral index is constrained by the Planck satellite, even though $P_{BB}$ itself is too small to be detectable yet. We also show that a detection of gravitational waves with an r.m.s. amplitude of $1$ would lead to a significant improvement of the constraint, and we quantify the effect of neglecting the running.

The work reported in this article presents a high-order, stable, and
efficient Gegenbauer pseudospectral method to solve numerically a wide variety
of mathematical models. The proposed numerical scheme exploits the stability
and the well-conditioning of the numerical integration operators to produce
well-conditioned systems of algebraic equations, which can be solved easily
using standard algebraic system solvers. The core of the work lies in the
derivation of novel and stable Gegenbauer quadratures based on the stable
barycentric representation of Lagrange interpolating polynomials and the
explicit barycentric weights for the Gegenbauer-Gauss (GG) points. A rigorous
error and convergence analysis of the proposed quadratures is presented along
with a detailed set of pseudocodes for the established computational
algorithms. The proposed numerical scheme leads to a reduction in the
computational cost and time complexity required for computing the numerical
quadrature while sharing the same exponential order of accuracy achieved by
Elgindy and Smith-Miles (2013). The bulk of the work includes three numerical
test examples to assess the efficiency and accuracy of the numerical scheme.
The present method provides a strong addition to the arsenal of numerical
pseudospectral methods, and can be extended to solve a wide range of problems
arising in numerous applications.

Ultracold neutron (UCN) detectors are crucial tools in various fields of research, including particle physics, materials science, and nuclear medicine. However, current UCN detectors suffer from limited efficiency and spatial resolution due to their simple design, which consists of a single layer of converter material.

In this work, we present a novel approach to UCN detection that utilizes a multilayer surface detector. By stacking multiple layers of different materials with varying neutron interaction cross-sections, we enhance the detection efficiency and improve the spatial resolution. The additional layers also allow for better discrimination between UCNs and background particles, leading to improved signal-to-noise ratio.

The proposed detector design consists of alternating layers of boron carbide (B4C) and graphite, which provide efficient conversion of UCNs into charged particles. The B4C layers have high thermal conductivity, ensuring fast heat dissipation and reducing the risk of thermal neutron absorption. In contrast, the graphite layers have low atomic number, minimizing the probability of UCN absorption.

We simulate the performance of our multilayer surface detector using Monte Carlo simulations and compare it to traditional single-layer detectors. Our results show an increase in detection efficiency by up to 50% and an improvement in spatial resolution by a factor of 2-3. We also experimentally validate our design using a prototype detector at a UCN source.

Our findings demonstrate the potential of multilayer surface detectors for enhancing UCN detection capabilities. This technology can be applied in various areas, such as fundamental neutron physics experiments, neutron scattering and imaging applications, and medical treatments involving UCNs.

The Lennox Bridge, Glenbrook is a heritage-listed road bridge that carries the Mitchell's Pass across Brookside Creek (also known as Lapstone Creek), located at Glenbrook, in the City of Blue Mountains local government area of New South Wales, Australia. The bridge was designed by David Lennox and built from 1832 to 1833 by James Randall and other convicts. It is also known as Lennox Bridge or The Horseshoe Bridge. The property is owned by Blue Mountains City Council. It was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999. The stone arch bridge is a single arch of  span and is  above water level, with a road width of . History 
The first road up the eastern slopes of the Blue Mountains, built by William Cox (1814–15), was in Governor Macquarie's words "pretty steep and sharp" and was found to be subject to serious washways. This road was superseded in 1824 by what was known as the Bathurst Road (now Old Bathurst Road). It avoided watercourses, but its grade was very steep and this rendered it hazardous to travellers. When Major Thomas Mitchell was appointed as Surveyor General in 1828, one of the first matters to which he turned his attention was the improvement of the Great Western Road. Mitchell's attention was focussed on providing a more direct and easily graded route for the Great Western Road. Mitchell surveyed and recommended the construction of a road along this route midway between the other two in preference to the Governor's suggestion of stationing a permanent repair gang on the Old Bathurst Road.

A Plaid Cymru MP believes UK security services were involved in some arson attacks blamed on Welsh extremists.
It is 25 years since the start of 12 years of fire-bombings, attributed to a shadowy group known as Meibion Glyndwr. Plaid Cymru's Elfyn Llwyd has suggested the security services could have been involved, with the intention of discrediting the nationalist vote. Ex-Welsh Office Minister Lord Roberts of Conwy denied security services were involved. In March this year, North Wales Police reopened the case, saying materials kept during their investigations would be examined to find whether it would yield DNA evidence.
Meibion Glyndwr - which means "sons of Glyndwr" - began burning property in December 1979 in protest at homes in rural Wales being sold as holiday cottages to people from England. The group was linked to most of the 220 or so fire-bombing incidents stretching from the Llyn Peninsula to Pembrokeshire. The campaign continued until the early 1990s. Police were accused in some quarters of targeting anyone who was a nationalist. Twelve organic lemons, preferably Meyer varieties, should be chosen and washed thoroughly. To remove pesticide residues, if using non-organic lemons, scrub them gently. Remove the tops and bottoms of each lemon to create a stable surface. Place a lemon upright and make two parallel cuts, one three-quarters of the way through the fruit, without cutting it in half. Flip the lemon over and make another perpendicular cut, dividing it into four sections. Each section should be filled with kosher salt, which can be replenished as needed. Stack the prepared lemons in a sterilized, wide-mouthed glass container until they're tightly packed, allowing the juice to fill the gaps. Repeat the process with the remaining lemons. Store the jar at room temperature and cover the lemons completely with their own juice. Freshly squeezed lemon juice can be added if necessary. After five to six weeks, the lemons' rinds become soft and tender, making them ready for use. Before serving, rinse them lightly. Once opened, the preserved lemons can be stored in the refrigerator for up to six months.

Visual domain adaptation is an important problem in computer vision, and has been studied extensively by researchers at Google, Microsoft Research, and elsewhere. However, there are many challenges to overcome before we can achieve visual domain adaptation that are not well understood. We present VisDA (Visual Domain Adaptation), a novel approach to solving these problems. Our goal is to develop a general framework for visual domain adaptation that allows us to address all of the known issues with existing approaches. In particular, we aim to provide a unified model for visual domain adaptation that can be used to solve any problem involving visual domain adaptation. This includes both simple and complex cases. We also propose a new algorithm for visual domain adaptation that is based on a combination of two previously proposed algorithms. These algorithms have proven successful in other domains such as object recognition and speech recognition, but they do not yet fully capture the complexity of visual domain adaptation. We demonstrate how our new algorithm can be applied to several real-world applications, including image classification, face detection, and object localization.

Ingredients:
- 1 bag (12 oz) milk chocolate chips
- 1 bag (12 oz) dark chocolate chips
- 1 cup coconut oil, melted
- 1/2 cup caramel sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt

Instructions:

1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set it aside.

2. In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the milk chocolate chips, dark chocolate chips, and melted coconut oil. Microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring after each interval until the chocolate is smooth and fully melted.

3. Pour the chocolate mixture onto the prepared baking sheet and use a spatula to spread it into an even layer.

4. Drizzle the caramel sauce over the chocolate layer and use a knife to swirl it into the chocolate.

5. Sprinkle the sea salt over the caramel and chocolate.

6. Place the baking sheet in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes, or until the chocolate is firm.

7. Break the chocolate bark into small pieces and serve. Store any remaining bark in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Addams Family Reunion is a 1998 American direct-to-video comedy horror children's film based on the characters from the cartoon created by cartoonist Charles Addams. This fourth and final installment in the Shrek series has many things going for it, but it never quite comes together as a whole. While the previous installments managed to find a perfect balance between hilarious slapstick humor, witty references, and an actual story, this one seems to have forgotten the latter, favoring instead cheap laughs and spectacle over genuine wit and emotion. As a result, the movie feels long and drawn out, even at a relatively short 84 minutes. 

The story picks up shortly after the events of the third film, with Shrek (Mike Myers) and Fiona (Cameron Diaz) married and dealing with the responsibilities of being parents to their young son Arthur (Diablo Cody). However, Shrek starts to become overwhelmed by the monotony of his daily life and loses his edge. His friends Donkey (Eddie Murphy) and Puss In Boots (Antonio Banderas) try to help Shrek find his former self by transporting him back in time to when he was a scared and nervous teenager who had yet to find his confidence. The majority of the film is then spent with Shrek interacting with his younger self ( Milo Murphy) as he tries to teach him the importance of being true to oneself and not backing down from what you want.

The concept of Shrek losing his edge and needing to be reminded of the importance of being true to oneself is a compelling one, and it could have made for a really powerful and emotional story. However, the movie opts for a much more lighthearted and simplistic approach, with little focus on genuine character development or exploration of the theme. Instead, it relies on cheap gags and slapstick humor, much of which feels forced and unnecessary. 

The animation is as impressive as ever, with the movie's universe expanding to include new locations and characters. However, the characters themselves feel somewhat flat this time around, with little growth or development over the course of the film. The voice acting is also lack-ranging from Myers and Murphy's lackluster performances to Cody's grating teenaged vocal affectations. 

In the end, Shrek Forever After is a disappointing end to an otherwise fantastic series. While it has some memorable moments and laughs, it fails to live up to the standards set by the previous films and feels like a missed opportunity to go out with a bang.

Dictogloss is an open-source software tool used by speech and language therapists, educators, and linguists to transcribe audio recordings into text in real time. It was developed as part of the Open Source Speech Recognition Project (OSSR) with funding from the European Commission's Human Languages Technologies Consortium program.

The software uses state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms to recognize spoken words and convert them into written text. The user simply records a conversation or podcast using their computer microphone, and Dictogloss will automatically generate captions that are displayed on the screen word for word. As the audio plays back, users can also edit and correct any misrecognized words directly within the application.

One advantage of Dictogloss is its ability to transcribe different accents and languages accurately. This makes it a useful tool for anyone who wants to improve their writing skills in another language or needs assistance reading complex material in their native tongue. Additionally, its modular design allows users to customize the experience to meet their specific needs, such as adjusting the speed at which the captions are generated.

Dictogloss has gained popularity due to its accessibility and affordability compared to other commercial transcription services. With its simple interface and rich features, it provides researchers and instructors with a powerful tool to analyze audio content or provide feedback to their students in a more efficient way than ever before.

Bring the butter and egg to room temperature. Toast the walnuts for 7 minutes in a 180C oven (no need to pre-heat). When the walnuts have cooled slightly, crush with your hands into fairly small bits. Strain the egg through a sieve. You will need 20 g for the bread dough, and the rest can be set aside for later. If you have a bread machine, put all of the ingredients into the bread pan and turn it on! (If kneading by hand, see.) In the meantime, make the filling. Work quickly. For this recipe, I would recommend cutting the apples into 5 mm-1 cm slices, as opposed to wedges. When the apples have cooled a bit, drain them well in a colander. When the bread maker finishes, do a "finger check" (coat your finger with flour and poke a hole in the dough. If it doesn't spring back, you know that the first rising is complete). If the dough springs back, it hasn't finished rising. Let it sit for about another 5 minutes. If the dough has shrunk, it means you have let it rise too much. There's nothing you can do about this, so it's best just to proceed to the next step, bearing in mind that your rolls might not turn out the greatest! Carefully take the dough out of the bread machine with a bench scraper. Punch down the dough. Shape the dough into a ball. Make it nice and smooth. Close the seam tightly on the bottom. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 15 minutes. Place the dough seam-side up and, using a rolling pin, lightly mark the dough with a cross. Roll out the dough, but leave approx. 1 cm on either end un-rolled (this helps achieve an even thickness). Roll out the dough into a 25 cm square. (This is easiest if you work from the centre, leaving the top, bottom, and sides until the very end). Thoroughly drain the apple filling and spread it out on the dough, leaving 2 cm at the end furthest from you empty. Roll it up from the end nearest you. Close the seam tightly, as you did when making the dough. Cut the dough into 6 pieces with a bench scraper (start by cutting it in half, then cut each half into 3 pieces.) Spread out the aluminum foil baking cups and place a roll in each cup. Let rise once more, this time at 40C on your oven's 'bread rising' setting. This is what they look like after the second rising. Pre-heat the oven to 190C. While waiting for it to heat, brush the rolls with the leftover egg and top with sliced almonds and walnuts. When heated, pop them into the oven for 12 minutes. Adjust the baking time according to your oven. Take the rolls out of the oven and cool on a wire rack... Mix together the icing ingredients until thick (make sure not to over-mix or it'll be hard). Drizzle the icing on the rolls! Even if you just drizzle it on at random, these will look surprisingly professional when finished, so don't worry too much. And with that, you're done!

To investigate the non-homogeneous Cauchy problem for a system of first-order linear partial differential operators {A_i}, we define suitable Sobolev spaces of negative differentiability to examine this problem. Specifically, we outline expressions for the trace of the tangential part t_i (u) and normal part n_i (u) of a vector-valued function u within the corresponding Sobolev space and formulate the problem accordingly. Assuming that the Laplace operators in the system satisfy a uniqueness condition near zero, we derive solvability conditions for the problem and provide formulas for both exact and approximate solutions. When dealing with the Cauchy problem in the L^2 space over the entire domain, we construct approximate and exact solutions to maximize regularity. Furthermore, utilizing Hilbert space techniques, we develop Carleman's formulae for a vector-valued function u in the Sobolev space H^1(R) based solely on Cauchy data t_i (u) on a subset S of the boundary of R and the values of A_i u within R relative to the null space of the Cauchy problem. Several illustrative examples of elliptic systems of operators with constant coefficients are examined.

Barbara Harris (December 14, 1935 – August 11, 2020) was an American bishop in the Episcopal Church and the first woman to become a bishop in the Anglican Communion. She was also the first woman to be ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church, and the first woman to serve as a diocesan bishop in the Anglican Communion.

Harris was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Temple University with a degree in education in 1957. She worked as a teacher and counselor in the Philadelphia public school system before attending the Episcopal Divinity School in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where she earned her master of divinity degree in 1966. She was ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church in 1967, and served as curate at All Saints' Church in Worcester, Massachusetts. She became the first woman to serve as a priest in the Episcopal Church. In 1974, she became the chaplain at MIT and minister at Saint Paul's Church in Cambridge, Massachusetts. She was named the eleventh bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts in 1989 and was consecrated on March 16, 1990, by Edmond L. Browning, the presiding bishop of the Episcopal Church. 1/3 cup ranch dressing

24 (1-inch) pieces red onion
12 slices thick cut bacon
salt and black pepper to taste
12 (6 inch) bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 2 hours
Whisk together ranch dressing and hot chile paste in a large bowl. Mix in chicken pieces and toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 hours. Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove chicken from the bag and transfer to a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Pat chicken pieces dry with more paper towels. Thread a piece of onion about 1 1/2 inches down the skewer. Thread the end portion of one strip of bacon onto skewer so the rest of the strip is hanging down. Skewer on a piece of chicken; thread on the next portion of the bacon. Turn the skewer so that the long end of the bacon is again hanging down. Repeat this process of skewering and turning until the entire strip of bacon is threaded, using 4 to 5 chicken pieces. Thread a second piece of onion onto the end of the skewer. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for all twelve skewers. Season chicken skewers with salt and pepper as desired. Cook the skewers on the preheated grill, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until nicely browned on all sides and the meat is no longer pink in the center, 12 to 16 minutes total per skewer. Deep learning has made significant progress in semantic segmentation, but its adoption in practical applications is hindered due to the need for extensive data. Biomedical images present an added challenge as annotated data and corresponding labels are scarce. Manual annotation requires significant expertise and resources, typically involving labeling multiple instances of specific structures within complex samples. To address this issue, researchers have developed a framework employing the U-Net architecture and uncertainty measures to identify essential samples for active learning. This method leverages Monte Carlo sampling and dropout regularization to inform annotation decisions. In a real-world application, experiments were conducted on microscopic histology samples, focusing on myelin segmentation in spinal cord and brain tissues. Using two small datasets comprising 14 and 24 images acquired through various microscopy techniques, results showed that incorporating uncertainty-selected samples into the initial training set led to improved segmentation accuracy compared to random selection. By leveraging active learning, the proposed approach significantly reduced annotation requirements. This efficient strategy demonstrates potential benefits for biomedical researchers seeking to achieve accurate image segmentation with limited labeled data, with the underlying code available online.

In 1884, the International Anti-Intoxicants League issued a global call to action, urging nations to prohibit the production and international trade of liquor and narcotics, as well as restrict licensed vice. Initiated by the American Woman's Christian Temperance Union (WCTU), led by President Frances Willard, it was disseminated globally by four World WCTU missionaries who collected over eight million signatures from more than 50 countries. The signatures fell into three categories: personal statements from female supporters, male endorsements, and collective affirmations from group leaders. In the US, nearly 750,000 signatures were sent to Evanston, Illinois, where they were carefully mounted on white fabric and secured with colored ribbons. Meanwhile, over 350,000 British signers delivered their documents on pre-mounted cloth to the US president in February 1885. Today, the Polyglot Petition is preserved at the Woman's Christian Temperance Union Headquarters in Evanston, Illinois, USA.

In this work, we tackle the problem of source-free domain adaptation for image segmentation. To this end, we propose a simple and effective approach based on Cycle-Consistency Training (CCT). Our key idea is to train a segmentation model to be cycle-consistent, meaning that it should be able to map an image from the source domain to the target domain and back to the source domain while preserving the segmentation. Rediffusion Singapore was a pioneering cable-transmitted, subscription-based radio station in Singapore that broadcasted predominantly in Chinese and English from 1949 to 2012. It is historically noteworthy as one of the earliest examples of subscription-based radio broadcasting. 

Highlighting its beginnings in Singapore back in 1949, Rediffusion began as Associate Rediffusion Services, a British-owned company. Based mainly in the city area, the Rediffusion service comprised of a network of cables that ran across the city linking homes and businesses. It featured daily broadcasts in four different languages: English, Malay, Chinese, and Tamil.

Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, it underwent several significant changes, including a name change from Associate Rediffusion Services to Rediffusion Singapore Pte Ltd in 1963. The next notable development in the company's progression came in the 1970s when Rediffusion underwent a period of localization and transitioned into an entirely Chinese language radio service.

In 1980, Rediffusion was sold to the Singaporean entrepreneur See Hoy Chan and became a wholly local company. During this period, it devoted substantially to the broadcasting of Chinese drama serials along with the sponsoring of several prominent local events, thereby reinforcing its cultural significance in the community. 

Rediffusion Singapore faced a significant challenge with the advent of free-to-air TV and FM radio services in the 1990s that led to a reduction in its subscriber base. The company attempted to reinvent itself by targeting niche listeners through content such as dialect programming, health, and wellness programs. The company underwent additional changes in management over the next few decades, yet continued to face declining subscriptions and financial difficulties. 

Amidst these challenges, Rediffusion decided to bid adieu to the cable radio broadcasting in 2011 after broadcasting for 62 years. The following year, in 2012, the company made its much-awaited return as a digital radio platform, but the revival was short-lived and the station ceased broadcasting permanently later in 2012.

Despite its cessation, Rediffusion Singapore holds a significant place in the history of Singapore's media landscape, having played a crucial role in the development of contemporary radio broadcasting in Singapore. To date, it echoes as an icon of nostalgia for those who recall the golden age of subscription-based radio stations.
