Whole Wheat Ricotta Gnocchi Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1 cup ricotta cheese
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg (optional)
- 1/4 cup additional whole wheat flour (for dusting)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, ricotta cheese, egg, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg (if using). Mix well until all the ingredients are fully incorporated.

2. Sprinkle a clean surface with some additional whole wheat flour. Transfer the dough onto the floured surface and knead it gently for a few minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour, but be careful not to add too much as it can make the gnocchi dense.

3. Divide the dough into four equal portions. Take one portion and roll it into a long rope, about 1/2 inch in diameter. Cut the rope into small pieces, about 1 inch long. Repeat this process with the remaining dough portions.

4. To shape the gnocchi, you can either use a gnocchi board or the back of a fork. Hold the fork or gnocchi board at a slight angle and press each piece of dough against it with your thumb. As you press, the dough will curl around the fork or board, creating ridges on one side and a small indentation on the other. Place the shaped gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet or tray.

5. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Carefully drop the gnocchi into the boiling water, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pot. Cook the gnocchi for about 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked gnocchi to a plate or colander.

6. Serve the whole wheat ricotta gnocchi with your favorite sauce, such as marinara, pesto, or browned butter with sage. Garnish with additional grated Parmesan cheese and fresh herbs, if desired.

Enjoy your homemade whole wheat ricotta gnocchi!

A unifying approach has been developed to tackle semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentations despite their shared roots. The proposed framework, K-Net, employs a set of learnable kernels that generate masks for both semantic categories and instances. Each kernel handles specific tasks, enabling adaptive performance based on its context within the input image. By employing a kernel update strategy, K-Net effectively addresses differences between instances. K-Net's architecture allows for simultaneous end-to-end training via bipartite matching, eliminating the need for non-maximum suppression and bounding boxes. With this streamlined approach, K-Net achieves superior results without additional components, surpassing the performance of existing state-of-the-art models on MS COCO and ADE20K datasets, with 52.1% precision and 54.3% mean intersection over union for semantic segmentation, and comparable instance segmentation outcomes to Cascade Mask R-CNN on MS COCO. The code and models will be available on GitHub.

This paper presents a novel graph-based framework called Affinity Fusion Graph (AFG) for natural image segmentation. The AFG model integrates both the color and texture features of an image to enhance the discriminatory power. The scheme employs the fusion of multiple affinity matrices to form a comprehensive graph portraying an image’s structural and feature information. Utilizing a spectral clustering approach, the proposed framework exhibits improved segmentation by avoiding over-segmentation or under-segmentation that is common in other models. Experimental results on several datasets validate the effectiveness of AFG in comparison to other state-of-the-art methods in terms of achieving better segmentation accuracy and visual quality. The study opens up new avenues for the integration of different image features and multiple affinity graphs in natural image segmentation tasks.

USS Indiana (BB-58) was the second of four  fast battleships built for the United States Navy in the 1930s. The first American battleships designed after the Washington treaty system began to break down in the mid-1930s, they took advantage of an escalator clause that allowed increasing the main battery to  guns, but refusal to authorize larger battleships kept their displacement close to the Washington limit of . A requirement to be armored against the same caliber of guns as they carried, combined with the displacement restriction, resulted in cramped ships, a problem that was exacerbated as wartime modifications that considerably strengthened their anti-aircraft batteries significantly increased their crews. Indiana entered service in April 1942, by which time the United States was engaged in World War II, and the ship was immediately pressed into action in the Pacific War against Japan. Her first combat came in late 1942 when she supported marines fighting during the Guadalcanal campaign. Over the next three years, she was occupied with two primary roles: naval gunfire support for amphibious assaults across the Pacific and anti-aircraft defense for the fast carrier task force. She shelled Japanese positions during the Battle of Tarawa in November 1943 and the Battle of Kwajalein in February 1944. During the latter operation, she collided with the battleship  and was forced to withdraw for repairs.

Located in Austin, Texas, Clark Field served as the primary venue for the University of Texas Longhorns from 1928 to 1974. This unique ballpark earned recognition due to its innovative design. A natural limestone cliff situated in the outfield presented challenges for players, making each game thrilling. The cliff, which spanned from left-center to center field, could only be accessed via a narrow path in the left-center area, earning it the nickname 'Billy Goat Hill.' The scoreboard positioned atop the hill near the fence further added to the unpredictability of the environment, causing unusual bounces for outfielders. As a result, the Longhorns enjoyed a distinct home-field advantage against opponents. When a ball was hit towards the cliff, it often resulted in inside-the-park home runs, leaving the opposing outfielders struggling to make plays. Due to the cliff's unique characteristics, Longhorn outfielders frequently limited batters to doubles or triples, taking advantage of their familiarity with the terrain. Interestingly, half of the team's outfielders preferred to play on the upper section, while the other half played in front of the challenging cliff.

In computer vision, image segmentation is always selected as a major research
topic by researchers. Due to its vital rule in image processing, there always
arises the need of a better image segmentation method. Clustering is an
unsupervised study with its application in almost every field of science and
engineering. Many researchers used clustering in image segmentation process.
But still there requires improvement of such approaches. In this paper, a novel
approach for clustering based image segmentation is proposed. Here, we give
importance on color space and choose lab for this task. The famous hard
clustering algorithm K-means is used, but as its performance is dependent on
choosing a proper distance measure, so, we go for cosine distance measure. Then
the segmented image is filtered with sobel filter. The filtered image is
analyzed with marker watershed algorithm to have the final segmented result of
our original image. The MSE and PSNR values are evaluated to observe the
performance.

Continue adding flour and knead until the dough transforms into a smooth, elastic texture. Set the crock pot to High heat, allowing the bread to rise as it warms up. To prevent the crust from becoming soggy, maintain a slight gap between the lid and the pot. Cook for the first 1-hour cycle with the lid almost closed. Remove the bread from the crock pot and transfer it to a wire rack to cool. Flip the bread and return it to the crock pot for an additional 1-hour cooking period, ensuring the lid remains slightly ajar. Finally, turn the bread onto the wire rack to allow it to fully cool.

Here, as in childhood, Brother, no one knows us.
And someone has died, and someone is not yet
born, while our father walks through his church at night
and sets all the clocks for spring.  His sleeplessness
weighs heavy on my forehead, his death almost
nothing. in the only letter he wrote to us
he says, No one can tell how long it takes a seed
to declare what death and lightning told it
while it slept.  But stand at a window long enough,
late enough, and you may some night hear
a secret you'll tomorrow, parallel to the morning,
tell on a wide, white bed, to a woman
like a sown ledge of wheat.  Or you may never
tell it, who lean across the night and miles of the sea,
to arrive at a seed, in whose lamplit house
resides a thorn, or a wee man, carving
a name on a stone, at afluctuating table of water,
the name of the one who has died, the name of the one
not born unknown.  Someone has died.  Someone
is not yet born.  And during this black interval,
I sweep all three floors of our father's house,
and I don't count the broom strokes; I row
up and down for nothing but love: his for me, and my own
for the threshold, as well as for the woman's name
I hear while I sweep, as though she swept
beside me, a woman who, if she owns a face at all,
it is its own changing; and if I know her name
I know to say it so softly she need not
stop her work to hear me.  But when she lies down
at night, in the room of our arrival, she'll know
I called her, though she won't answer, who is on her way
to sleep, until morning, which even now,
is overwhelming, the woman combing her hair opposite
the direction of my departure.
And only now and then do I lean at a jamb
to see'if I can see what I thought I heard.
I heard her ask, My love, why can't you sleep?
and answer, Someone has died, and someone
is not yet born.  Meanwhile, I hear the voices
of women telling a story in the round,
so I sit down on a rain-eaten stoop, by the saltgrasses,
and go on folding the laundry I was folding,
the everyday clothes of our everyday life, the death
clothes wearing us clean to the bone, to the very
ilium crest, where my right hand, this hand, half
crab, part bird, has often come to rest on her,
whose name I know.  And because I sat down,
I hear their folding sound, and know
the tide is rising early, and I can't hope
to trap their story told in the round.  But the woman
whose name I know says, Sleep, so I lie down
on the clothes, the folded and unfolded, the life
and the death.  Ages go by When I wake, the story
has changed the firmament into domain, domain
into a house.  And the sun speaks the day,
unnaming, showing the story, dissipating the boundaries
of the telling, to include the one who has died
and the one not yet born.  Someone has died
and someone is not yet born.  How still
this morning grows about the voice of one
child reading to another, how much a house
is house at all due to one room where an elder
child reads to his brother, and that younger
knows by heart the brother-voice.  How darker
other rooms stand, how slow morning comes, collected
in a name, told at one sill and listened for
at the threshold of dew What book is this we read
together, Brother, and at which window
of our father's house?  In which upper room?
We read it twice: Once in two voices, to each
other; once in unison, to children,
animals, and the sun, our star, that vast office
of love, the one we sit in once, and read
together twice, the third time bosomed in
the future.  So birds may lend their church, sown
in air, realized in the body uttering
windows, growing rafters, couching seeds.

Denbigh is a heritage-listed property situated in the southern-western Sydney suburb of Cobbitty in New South Wales, Australia, currently used as a Hereford stud and previously serving as a vineyard, Clydesdale horse stud, Ayrshire cattle stud, and dairy farm. Built between 1818 by Charles Hook, it was later developed by Thomas and Samuel Hassall, with additional involvement from Daniel Roberts. The property is privately owned. Denbigh was listed on the New South Wales State Heritage Register on December 22, 2006. 

Charles Hook, the original owner, had faced imprisonment due to his support for Governor Bligh's efforts to exert control over the military in New South Wales. Upon release, Hook received a  grant in 1812 from Governor Macquarie, which included land in the Cobbitty Parish, near the intersection of Cowpasture and Bringelly Roads, now known as Northern Road. Following his arrival, Hook resided at nearby Macquarie Grove while his new home, Denbigh, was constructed between 1818. With its completion, Hook cleared the surrounding land for agricultural purposes before passing away in 1826.

Ingredients 
1 pound dried pasta
½ pound fresh mushrooms, sliced
½ cup chopped onion
½ cup chopped green bell pepper
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 tablespoon butter
1 teaspoon dried basil
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon dried thyme
½ teaspoon black pepper
½ cup dry white wine
2 cups beef broth
1 link (3½ ounces) sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, browned and crumbled
1/3 cup chopped pitted green olives

Preparation
1. Cook pasta according to package directions.
2. In a large skillet, cook the mushrooms, onion, and green pepper in hot olive oil and butter over medium heat until tender. Add the basil, salt, oregano, thyme, and black pepper. Cook and stir for 1 minute.
3. Stir in wine and simmer for 2 minutes. Add the beef broth and sausage. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
4. Stir in olives. Cook and stir for 1 minute more.
5. Drain pasta. Serve with sausage mixture.

For a long time it was believed that Pirehūrehu (also known as Tūmanako) could lift canoes up into the sky, as he did when he killed his grandfather Āpiro and fled to Uruao in Te Ika-a-Māui - this story does not come down in the oral tradition though [citation needed]. It became very popular later on though after the introduction of Western canoeing technology which allowed much bigger hulls to be easily built at Hastings and Gisborne - these vessels were referred to colloquially as 'piri poutama' or 'piripou'. In actual fact they differed only slightly from whaling boats such as sloops with deep keels being necessary for local conditions so that they would plane off over breaking waves well before reaching shore at speed [2].
Hokianga has always been famous around Te Tai Rawhiti, i.e., east coast North Island New Zealand Maori because it produces very large specimens of pipi, locally called kai moana. A local proverb goes:"Ngati Kuri he tangata o te waka tuna e karakia mai ano ki uta; Ngatitoa he taua o tu ma roro no te whenua". That is: Ngati Kuru are men who raise their dug out canoes right on dry land while the Ngati Toarangatira raised them on rafts close enough to be washed by sea spray! This may seem unbelievable now but during World War II two huge 80 ft. timber clinker dugouts made here ended up travelling all over the Pacific islands including Guadalcanal carrying cargo.
Other examples include the warship Te Watewate, the training ships RA Maui and Mt Cook plus many other coastal yachts and dory workboats all built here even more recently using traditional hand tools. These craft frequently sail into the South Seas in good weather without fuel consumption while also having excellent wave piercing ability combined with seaworthiness for open ocean passage. Another example is Pukearuhe (The hill behind the wind). There exists no record that any hikitika was lifted high in the air to fly

Prasophyllum limnetes, commonly known as the marsh leek orchid, is a species of orchid endemic to Tasmania. It has a single tubular, green leaf and up to thirty five greenish-white flowers with a pinkish labellum. It is only known from a population of fewer than twenty plants growing in a sanctuary near Port Sorell. Description
Prasophyllum limnetes is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single tube-shaped leaf which is  long and  wide near its purplish base. The free part of the leaf is  long. Between fifteen and thirty five greenish-white flowers are crowded along a flowering spike which is  long, reaching to a height of . As with other leek orchids, the flowers are inverted so that the labellum is above the column rather than below it. The dorsal sepal is  long, about  wide and the lateral sepals are  long, about  wide, erect and free from each other. The petals are  long, about  wide and turn forwards. The labellum is greenish white with pink or mauve tinges, tapers to a point and turns sharply upwards near its middle. The edges of the upturned part of the labellum are slightly wavy and there is a callus in its centre, extending to its tip. Flowering occurs from late November to December.

Japanese electronics giant Hitachi has developed what it says is the world's fastest industrial robot, capable of moving at 10 metres per second (22mph).

The company said its new machine was able to move faster than any other on the market and could be used in factories for tasks such as welding or painting.

It can also handle heavy loads - up to 35kg (77lb) - which means it could be used to lift car parts into place during assembly.

"We believe this will help us win orders," said Yasuhiro Kawamura, head of Hitachi's factory automation division.

He added that the firm had already received several enquiries about the product since announcing it last week.

## Faster robots

Industrial robots are typically used by manufacturers to perform repetitive jobs more quickly and accurately than humans.

They have been around for decades but their speed has increased significantly over time.

In 2014, Japanese firm Fanuc launched an industrial robot called CR-35iA/L that could travel at speeds of up to nine metres per second.

But Hitachi claims its latest model, known as HS16iD/85, is even quicker. It can reach top speeds of 10 metres per second when carrying light objects weighing less than one kilogramme (two pounds), according to the BBC's Tokyo correspondent Rupert Wingfield-Hayes.

However, he adds that the robot slows down considerably if it needs to carry heavier items. For example, it takes just under two seconds to accelerate from zero to five metres per hour while holding something weighing 35kg.

Mr Kawamura told Reuters that the robot would cost between $90,000-$100,000 (£65,000-£72,000). He expects sales to start next year.

A remote-controlled target system that behaves like a moving human-sized target is helping sharpen the marksmanship of soldiers in the British Army.

The £215,000 ($279,000) system, known as i-Fire, has been introduced at the Army's Pirbright training range in Surrey.

It allows soldiers to practice against moving targets from close range, in a safe, virtual battlefield.

The i-Fire system has been introduced as part of a £1.5m investment in the training facility by the Ministry of Defence.

The aim is to ensure the soldiers' marksmanship and battlefield skills are kept up to date.

Mita Taupopoki, a prominent Māori tribal chief from New Zealand, hailed from Ngāti Wāhiao, a subgroup of the Tūhourangi tribe of Te Arawa. Born around 1845-46 near Lake Rotorua, he came from a family that spent most of its time at Whakarewarewa. Mita's parents were Hēmana Te Whareiro of Ngāti Wāhiao and Kanea II of Tūhourangi. By 1864, he participated alongside other Te Arawa members in battles against the government during the 1860s conflicts. Following his return to Whakarewarewa in 1874, Mita played a crucial role in a Native Land Court case in 1883, where he successfully advocated for Ngāti Wāhiao's interests regarding disputed land, particularly the area surrounding Whakarewarewa. This victory bolstered his reputation as a respected leader both within Ngāti Wāhiao and across Tūhourangi. Tragedy struck when the 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera devastated the region, forcing displaced survivors to seek refuge with Mita and his community at Whakarewarewa and Ōhinemutu. Mita continued to represent Tūhourangi's interests in the Native Land Court, ultimately securing their claim to the 211,000-acre Rotomahana-Parekārangi block in 1887. He later traveled abroad, joining Maggie Papakura's cultural delegation to Australia, England, and the US in 1910. Mita passed away in Rotorua hospital on 14 January 1935.

Computer giant Microsoft has launched a pilot scheme to replace counterfeit versions of Windows XP with legal ones.
The first-time initiative is restricted to the UK and to users with pre-installed copies of the operating system in PCs bought before November. Until December Microsoft said software can be sent to it for analysis if there are doubts about its legitimacy. The company aims to detect illegal traders and turn users of fake versions of Windows into legitimate ones.
The Windows XP Counterfeit Project will mean that software that is found to be counterfeit will be replaced for free, subject to certain conditions, until the end of the year. It is the first time Microsoft has launched a counterfeit product replacement scheme in the world, the company told the BBC News website. In June, the software giant said that the major security update to Windows XP, Service Pack 2, would not work with the most widely pirated versions of its operating system. The upgrade closed security loopholes in XP and added features that made it easier to keep machines safe from viruses and other types of malicious computer code.
The US company invited anyone who had suspicions about their version of Windows XP to submit it for testing as soon as possible. The procedure consists of a series of computer checks, collating documents, and filling out a witness statement. "This is a great opportunity for users to confirm the authenticity of Windows XP software whilst helping gather vital information about illegal traders", said Alex Hilton, licence compliance manager at Microsoft. The scheme has also been welcomed by the technology and commerce industry. "It is important that users ensure that they are legally licensed to avoid the risks of purchasing and using counterfeit products", said David Frost, director general of the British Chambers of Commerce. The plan would enable Microsoft to gather intelligence about illegal traders in a prompt way, which would allow it to take action against software pirates. Microsoft said it would evaluate the results of the UK programme before setting up similar schemes in other countries.

Traditional supervised semantic segmentation typically relies on data from the same domain as the training set. However, real-world applications often involve disparate training and testing environments, leading to decreased performance due to domain mismatch. Manually annotating pixel labels for images across different domains is extremely time-consuming, particularly when dealing with histopathology images. To address these challenges, this research introduces a novel framework called dual adaptive pyramid network (DAPNet), which enables gland segmentation in histopathology images by transitioning from one staining technique to another. Our approach tackles the domain adaptation issue through two primary stages: 1) image-level analysis focuses on the differences in color and visual style between the two domains, and 2) feature-level consideration addresses the spatial inconsistencies inherent to the two domains. These components are implemented as domain classifiers utilizing adversarial training. Our method is evaluated using datasets specifically designed for gland segmentation under H&E and DAB stain conditions. Results from comprehensive experiments and an ablation study substantiate the efficacy of DAPNet in addressing the domain-adaptive segmentation challenge. Notably, our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in this context.

Recent advancements in deep convolutional neural networks have significantly improved their performance in medical image segmentation tasks. However, the primary challenge in training supervised deep learning models lies in acquiring sufficient labeled data, which can be a time-consuming and costly process. To address this issue, our work proposes an innovative semi-supervised learning strategy leveraging a student-teacher approach to train segmentation networks with limited annotated data and a substantial amount of unlabeled images. Firstly, a teacher model is trained from the labeled dataset using Bayesian deep learning techniques. This model generates soft segmentation labels and uncertainty maps for the unlabeled dataset. Next, the student model is refined using the partially labeled data along with the pixel-wise confidence estimates derived from the teacher model's uncertainty analysis, utilizing a custom-designed loss function. Experimental evaluations on a retinal layer segmentation task reveal that our proposed method outperforms the fully supervised approach and matches the accuracy of human experts. Our semi-supervised segmentation framework serves as a significant breakthrough and has potential applications in biomedical image segmentation across diverse imaging modalities where access to annotated medical images is difficult to acquire.

Segmentation and clustering of similar objects rely heavily on partitioning and grouping techniques. A primary aim is to unite like objects, particularly pixels in images, while maintaining distinct differences between groups and aiming for larger group sizes. These objectives can be expressed as a ratio-based optimization problem. Notable examples include the normalized cut problem and the ratio regions problem. Our work presents the first polynomial-time algorithms for resolving these problems optimally, offering a more efficient approach compared to existing literature. Unlike heuristic methods, which transform the problems into non-linear optimization challenges, our algorithms utilize a polynomial-sized graph to solve them efficiently. This contrasts with spectral techniques used in image processing, which often result in suboptimal solutions and significant computational costs. By employing a minimum s,t-cut procedure, our algorithms achieve the optimal solution to the respective ratio problem and provide a sequence of nested solutions based on varying weights of the objectives. Building upon this foundation, we extend our findings to address bi-criteria and multi-criteria objective functions in part II.

Recent advances in deep learning have led to impressive breakthroughs in both classification and semantic segmentation tasks. Many researchers now consider deep learning to be the most effective approach for pixel-level image segmentation. However, a crucial question remains: can deep learning match the precision of traditional image segmentation techniques by mapping object features to nonlinear functions? This study provides an overview of the achievements of deep learning in image classification and segmentation. Surprisingly, despite its superior performance in categorizing limited categories in competitions, deep learning yields approximately eighty percent accuracy in image segmentation tasks. In contrast, image segmentation methods used in biomedical research exhibit near ninety percent accuracy. What explains this disparity? One potential factor is that evaluation metrics often rely solely on reported results rather than reproducible code or software submissions, raising questions about the reliability and hype surrounding these claims. To address this, we investigated the underlying principles of deep learning and compared the performance of state-of-the-art methods to a threshold-based approach. Our experiments revealed that threshold selection methods outperformed deep learning models in image segmentation tasks, demonstrating significant advantages.

 tumultuously beating as you start;

Of holy wedlock, close and indissoluble;
And with a breast brimming with anguish deep
I see you leaving sisterly love's sunny steep.

Or that I doubt the worth of the one thou didst choose;
I but behold in thee a woman thro' and thro',
And own thee trembling, trembling at love's pow'r.

In the calm strength of that eternal love
I see thee standing, none may overthrow;
Nor evil tongue his subtle venom spray
On thee, dear sister, as thou wilt pass away.

I kiss thee as thou layest trembling there,
And bless thy choice, as I bid thee farewell;
And when in after time thou resemblest me
Call up a smile, thinking of thy sister.

The determination of a neutron's linear momentum relies on measuring the positions of three successive ionization tracks along with their respective vertices, equivalent to two and a half tracks. Measuring the delay between the first two tracks further reduces this to one and a half tracks. However, the precision of both angle and magnitude is restricted due to ion track spreading to around ten percent. Fast neutron tracking can be achieved using multi-wire proportional chambers or light-field imaging techniques, each requiring single-charge or single-photon detection capabilities. While light-field imaging offers clarity unaffected by charge diffusion blurring, it may face limitations due to the scarcity of available photons. Hydrogen isotopes such as $^1$H,$^2$H, and $^3$He are being explored for developing initial fast neutron trackers employing light-field imaging methods.

Additive deformations of bialgebras, as defined by Wirth, involve modifications to the
multiplication map that satisfy specific conditions relative to both the coalgebraic structure and
continuity requirements. This concept has implications for developing a cohomology theory, and a key challenge is constructing such a framework. In addressing these issues, two primary concerns arise: (1) characterizing non-trivial deformations, particularly those stemming from coboundaries, and (2) investigating the existence and properties of deformed antipodes within the context of Hopf algebras. Through this analysis, we aim to establish the existence of deformed antipodes, derive formulas for computing them based on the original Hopf algebra's antipode and deformation, and demonstrate that in the cocommutative case, deformations can be decomposed into separate components involving both trivial and constant antipodes.

This paper proposes a novel approach to multi-target tracking in the presence of superpositional measurements using labeled random finite sets (RFS). The proposed method, called particle multi-target tracker (PMTT), combines the strengths of particle filtering and RFS to handle the challenges of multi-target tracking in the presence of measurement uncertainty and clutter.

The PMTT algorithm first represents the set of targets as an RFS, where each element of the set is associated with a label representing the target state. At each time step, the algorithm performs a prediction step, where the state of each target is propagated using a dynamics model, and a update step, where the measurement is processed using a likelihood function. The likelihood function is defined over the RFS, and it takes into account theLabel Random Finite Sets (RFS) to handle the superpositional measurements.

The authors evaluate the performance of the PMTT algorithm using a set of simulation experiments, and compare it with the traditional methods such as the Kalman filter and the particle filter. The results show that the PMTT algorithm outperforms the traditional methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, especially in the presence of high clutter levels and non-linear dynamics.

The main contribution of this paper is the introduction of a novel algorithm for multi-target tracking that can handle superpositional measurements using labeled RFS. The proposed algorithm combines the benefits of particle filtering and RFS, and provides a more robust and accurate solution to the problem of multi-target tracking in various applications such as radar, sonar, and computer vision.

The paper is organized as follows: The next section provides a brief overview of the related work in the field of multi-target tracking and the use of RFS. The section after that presents the mathematical formulation of the problem and the proposed algorithm. The results and discussion are presented in the following section, and the conclusion and future work are presented in the last section.

This paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of multi-target tracking and will be of interest to researchers and practitioners working in this area. The proposed algorithm has the potential to be applied in a variety of applications such as air traffic control

Hans Orifice is a drummer best known as a member of Gwar. Born Jim Thomson, in Alexandria, Virginia, he first took the name Hans Sphincter, and assumed his current name in 1987. Thomson left due to touring commitments with his main band, the Alter Natives, who released three albums on SST Records. Richmond drummer Rob Mosby of the Richmond, Virginia punk group White Cross then joined Gwar until 1989. Hans Orifice returned briefly in 1989 after Mosby left the group. During this time Thomson co-wrote Sick of You with the band and completed a U.S. and Canadian tour. After the tour Thomson left Gwar on good terms to tour with The Alter Natives. He was replaced by current drummer Jizmak Da Gusha. In 2000, Thomson joined Bob Miller, and formed an experimental group called Plasmodium. The group released Clairaudience
in 2004. Thomson joined Brooklyn-based CSC Funk Band as a drummer and percussionist in 2008. In 2010 he started Electric Cowbell Records, a boutique record label releasing mostly 7-inch 45RPM records for genre-bending music groups culled from his extended community and network of musicians and music producers. In 2011 The Village Voice voted Electric Cowbell Records the Best Spearheaders of the Vinyl Revival. The label released several acclaimed 45RPM 7-inch records for a variety of groups like Superhuman Happiness, Debo Band, CSC Funk Band, Talibam!, Cheick Hamala Diabate, Bio Ritmo, Mucca Pazza, Amazing Ghost, Greg Ginn, Spanglish Fly, Super Hi Fi, No BS! Brass, Chico Trujillo, Orquesta el Macabeo, Slavic Soul Party, Polyrhythmics, Os Magrelos, and Karthala 72.

LONDON - A former senior aide to the UK government has claimed that the "golden rule" on public spending, which states that public debt should not rise as a percentage of GDP, is still in place despite recent political turmoil.

In an interview with the BBC, the former adviser disclosed that despite the ongoing debate over the country's exit from the EU, commonly known as Brexit, the longstanding fiscal rule remains a central tenet of UK economic policy.

The government has been under intense pressure to relax the rule in light of the ongoing economic uncertainty, with some arguing that it should be scrapped altogether. However, the former aide insisted that the principle remains a key foundation of the UK's economic strategy.

Despite speculation to the contrary, the ex-aide emphasized that the golden rule has not been abandoned, and continues to guide government policy on fiscal matters.

We generalize Ebert's Hat Problem for three persons and three colors. All
players guess simultaneously the color of their own hat observing only the hat
colors of the other players. It is also allowed for each player to pass: no
color is guessed. The team wins if at least one player guesses his or her hat
color correct and none of the players has an incorrect guess. This paper
studies Ebert's hat problem, where the probabilities of the colors may be
different (asymmetric case). Our goal is to maximize the probability of winning
the game and to describe winning strategies. In this paper we use the notion of
an adequate set. The construction of adequate sets is independent of underlying
probabilities and we can use this fact in the analysis of the asymmetric case.
Another point of interest is the fact that computational complexity using
adequate sets is much less than using standard methods.

The Korea Bank Group said on Thursday it plans to sell a majority stake in its credit card division to a group of Chinese investors. If successful, the sale to Jilin Cement Group and two affiliated companies will be the largest corporate acquisition in South Korea.

The new shareholders will maintain the Bank of Korea's 100% ownership and influence over the credit card business. The new partners will invest up to a total of 10 billion won ($8.8 million U.S.) in the business, which primarily serves Chinese clients.

The deal is part of Seoul and Beijing's efforts to boost investment in South Korean businesses and promote South Korea's image abroad. It comes about a week after China launched a diplomatic mission in Seoul as part of a plan to bolster cross-border trade and boost relations as Seoul heads into a round of high-profile bilateral and regional summits.

In a separate announcement, Seoul's government said it plans to sell an investment fund with $14.2 billion of assets managed by Saehan International Ltd. It said on Thursday that the fund, which was set up in the mid-1980s, will be set up to buy foreign assets and return them to South Korea if the terms of the deals are agreed with Chinese investors.

Separately on Thursday, Seoul said it would launch the world's largest free trade zone in Ulsan in August. The zone will have 1.8 million square kilometers, or about a fifth of South Korea, and will stretch along South Korea's eastern seaboard from the northern port in Busan to the southern port in Busan.

Actor Hugh Grant has been cast as the lead role in a new Broadway production of Harold Pinter's Betrayal, it was announced on Tuesday.

The 57-year-old will make his debut on the Great White Way opposite Rachel Weisz and Rafe Spall.

Grant said he had long wanted to work with director Mike Nichols - who directed him in Notting Hill (1999) - but that this would be their first time working together since then.

Betrayal tells the story of an adulterous love triangle between three friends over a period of six years.

It premiered at London's National Theatre in 1978 before transferring to New York where it won two Tony Awards for best play and best direction.

Pinter wrote the script after reading about the affair between novelist Graham Greene and actress Catherine Walston.

In a statement, Grant said: "I have always loved Harold Pinter's plays and I am thrilled to be doing one of my favourites."

He added: "Mike Nichols is a genius and I can't wait to start rehearsals."

Nichols said: "Hugh Grant is a wonderful actor and we are all looking forward to working with him again."

Weisz, who is married to Grant, previously appeared alongside her husband in the film adaptation of Woody Allen's Match Point (2005).

She also played the title character in the 2006 movie version of Pinter's The Deep Blue Sea.

The Sound of Music is coming home.

The musical, which was filmed in Austria in 1965, is being staged in Salzburg for the first time.

The production will open at the Salzburg Festival in July 2018.

The Sound of Music is based on the true story of the von Trapp family, who escaped from Nazi-occupied Austria during World War Two.

The film, which starred Julie Andrews and Christopher Plummer, won five Oscars.

The stage production will be directed by Barrie Kosky, who is the artistic director of the Komische Oper Berlin.

Kosky said he was "thrilled" to be bringing the musical to Salzburg.

"The Sound of Music is a story about love, hope and courage, and these are values that we need more than ever in today's world," he said.

"I am looking forward to bringing this classic musical to the city where it all began."

The Sound of Music will run at the Salzburg Festival from July 20 to August 30, 2018.

Renowned film director Sir Alan Parker was awarded the prestigious Order of Arts and Letters in Paris by French Culture Minister Renaud Donnedieu de Vabres. De Vabres commended Parker for his exceptional filmmaking skills, stating that he had explored the potential of film with remarkable talent. In response, Parker acknowledged the significance of French cinema, lamenting that Hollywood primarily views film as a commercial venture rather than an art form. He expressed gratitude towards France, calling it the "flag carrier of cinema worldwide." Parker's notable works include Oscar-winning films such as Fame, Midnight Express, and The Commitments. A key figure in British film circles, Parker serves as a former chairman of the UK Film Council and a member of the British Film Institute's board. De Vabres praised Parker's dedication to his craft, highlighting his ability to convey important messages through his films, including his 2003 film The Life of David Gale, which addressed the issue of capital punishment.

I've been tinkering with my motorcycle for a while now and I've come across an interesting idea that I wanted to run by the community. I've been thinking about replacing my gas tank with oversized float bowls. 

The idea came to me when I was working on the carburetor. I noticed that the float bowls essentially act as a mini gas tank, storing a small amount of fuel and releasing it as needed. This got me thinking, what if I could increase the size of these float bowls to hold more fuel, thereby eliminating the need for a traditional gas tank?

I understand that this would involve a lot of custom work, including fabricating larger float bowls and potentially reworking the fuel delivery system. But I'm not too concerned about the technical challenges. I'm more interested in whether this could theoretically work and if there are any potential benefits or drawbacks that I'm not considering.

One potential benefit I see is a lower center of gravity, as the fuel would be stored lower in the bike. This could potentially improve handling. On the downside, I imagine the fuel capacity would be significantly reduced, which could limit the bike's range.

I'm curious to hear your thoughts on this. Has anyone tried something similar? Are there any potential issues I'm not considering? Any input would be greatly appreciated.

A California man, Nicholas Lee Jacobsen, faces charges related to unauthorized computer hacking at T-Mobile's US operations. His arrest occurred last October, resulting from at least two attempts to breach the company's network. During this period, he stole the sensitive information of approximately 400 customers, including names and social security numbers. The incident occurred roughly a year after T-Mobile initially discovered the unauthorized access. The US Secret Service has been probing the matter. According to T-Mobile officials, the company employs robust measures to detect unusual activity, allowing them to swiftly take action against potential threats like Mr Jacobsen. Court records indicate that the alleged hacking scheme spanned several months, enabling the perpetrator to view emails and private files. However, it is believed that Mr Jacobsen failed to obtain sensitive customer credit card data, as this information is stored separately. T-Mobile has stated that the Secret Service is examining the possibility of the hacker accessing photos captured by T-Mobile subscribers' smartphone cameras. Additionally, reports suggest that Mr Jacobsen may have accessed the personal files of an investigating Secret Service agent. A Los Angeles grand jury indicted him on charges of willfully accessing a computer system without authorization and impairing a protected computer from March to October 2004. He remains on bail. As a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom, T-Mobile serves around 16.3 million subscribers in the United States.

Here's how to prepare homemade pasta: Begin by combining 9 ounces of all-purpose flour with 3 whole eggs. The method of preparation can vary - some people prefer to mix the ingredients on a clean surface, creating a well for the eggs and then combining them by hand or with a fork, while others use their stand mixer for the task. Once everything is well incorporated and forms a cohesive mass, continue to knead for 15 minutes, either manually or with the aid of a stand mixer. Subsequently, cover the dough in plastic wrap and allow it to rest for 30 minutes. Next, divide the dough into 3 or 4 portions and proceed to roll out the dough into thin sheets, rotating the dough 90 degrees every few passes as you go. This process should take approximately 5 minutes per piece of dough, depending on your speed. To achieve the desired thickness, cut the rolled-out sheets into noodle shapes using a sharp knife or pizza cutter, aiming for a thickness of 3/4 inch. For future use, lightly dust the cooked noodles with cornmeal or semolina to prevent sticking, and store them separately on a baking sheet. Cooking involves bringing a large pot of boiling water to a boil and adding a small amount of salt - be cautious not to overdo it, as fresh pasta absorbs more salt than dried varieties. Upon floating to the surface, remove the pasta with tongs and combine it with your chosen sauce before serving immediately.

much larger than the sample size, an important question is to select the
important variable which are relevant to the response variable of interest.
Variable selection and the multiple testing are both tools to address this
issue. However, there is little discussion on the connection of these two

discovery rate. In this paper, we consider the regime where the signals are

computer vision. In this paper we propose an adversarial based model for
image-to-image translation. The regular deep neural-network based methods
perform the task of image-to-image translation by comparing gram matrices and
using image segmentation which requires human intervention. Our generative
adversarial network based model works on a conditional probability approach.
This approach makes the image translation independent of any local, global and
content or style features. In our approach we use a bidirectional
reconstruction model appended with the affine transform factor that helps in
conserving the content and photorealism as compared to other models. The
advantage of using such an approach is that the image-to-image translation is
semi-supervised, independant of image segmentation and inherits the properties
of generative adversarial networks tending to produce realistic. This method
has proven to produce better results than Multimodal Unsupervised
Image-to-image translation.

Flexible grid optical networks allow a better exploitation of fiber capacity,
by enabling a denser frequency allocation. A tighter channel spacing, however,
requires narrower filters, which increase linear intersymbol interference
(ISI), and may dramatically reduce system reach. Commercial coherent receivers
are based on symbol by symbol detectors, which are quite sensitive to ISI. In
this context, Nyquist spacing is considered as the ultimate limit to
wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) packing.
  In this paper, we show that by introducing a limited-complexity trellis
processing at the receiver, either the reach of Nyquist WDM flexi-grid networks
can be significantly extended, or a denser-than-Nyquist channel packing (i.e.,
a higher spectral efficiency (SE)) is possible at equal reach. By adopting
well-known information-theoretic techniques, we design a limited-complexity
trellis processing and quantify its SE gain in flexi-grid architectures where
wavelength selective switches over a frequency grid of 12.5GHz are employed.

fundamental but a challenging problem mainly because it requires correct

propose a deep learning approach for building detection by applying numerous
enhancements throughout the process. Initial dataset is preprocessed by 2-sigma
percentile normalization. Then data preparation includes ensemble modelling
where 3 models were created while incorporating OpenStreetMap data. Binary
Distance Transformation (BDT) is used for improving data labeling process and
the U-Net (Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation) is
modified by adding batch normalization wrappers. Afterwards, it is explained
how each component of our approach is correlated with the final detection
accuracy. Finally, we compare our results with winning solutions of SpaceNet 2
competition for real satellite multispectral images of Vegas, Paris, Shanghai
and Khartoum, demonstrating the importance of our solution for achieving higher
building detection accuracy.

Mark Ellingson (1905 – 1993) was the 5th president of the Rochester Institute of Technology, succeeding John A. Randall, from 1936 – 1969. He rose from a teacher at the institute to the presidency, which he held for longer than anyone before or since, and in many ways he brought the institute into its modern form. During Dr. Ellingson's lengthy tenure in office from 1936 to 1969, enrollment in day and evening classes rose from 2,250 to 16,000. He also oversaw a major expansion of the RIT endowment; a 1937 merger with the Empire School of Printing; the 1944 renaming to "Rochester Institute of Technology" (formerly, Rochester Athenaeum and Mechanics Institute); the planning, construction, and 1968 transfer to the current campus in Henrietta.  He also spearheaded the drive to have RIT selected as the location for the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, which admitted its first students in 1968. 1 lb boneless beef chuck roast, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
1 (14 1/2 ounce) can beef broth
1 (28 ounce) can whole tomato puree
1 medium onion, chopped
1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted
1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
1 teaspoon sugar
2 cups fresh breadcrumbs
1 lb sharp cheddar cheese, grated (4 cups)
1 lb elbow macaroni
Simmer chuck in broth in a 2 qt saucepan, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until meat is very tender, about 1 hour. While meat simmers, break up tomatoes by squeezing them into a bowl with puree. Cook onion in half of butter in a 4 qt saucepan over moderate heat, stirring, until softened. Add tomatoes with puree, Worcestershire sauce, and sugar, then simmer stirring occasionally, 15 minutes, or until slightly thickened. Preheat oven to 400. To make topping, toss together bread crumbs, 1 cup Cheddar, remaining melted butter and salt and pepper to taste. Cook macaroni in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain in a colander. Cool macaroni 3 minutes, then tranfer to a large bowl. Toss with tomato sauce, beef with broth, remaining 3 cups cheese and salt and pepper to taste. Transfer macaroni mixture to a buttered 13x9x2" glass baking dish and spoon topping evenly over. Bake in middle of oven, uncovered, 25 minutes or until topping is golden brown and mixture is bubbling. Makes 8-10 servings.

The concept of transforming a matrix into its dual or conjugate form is a fundamental tool in linear algebra and has numerous applications in various fields such as physics, engineering, computer science, and statistics. However, the traditional methods for performing these transformations are often tedious and prone to errors. In this paper, we present two new methods, called the Perfect NOT Transformation (PNT) and the Conjugate Transformation (CT), which significantly simplify the process of computing the dual and conjugate forms of matrices.

The PNT is based on the idea of subtracting the identity matrix from a given matrix, followed by an elementary row operation. This simple method can be applied to any square matrix, regardless of its size, and produces a compact representation of the matrix that is easy to work with. We demonstrate how the PNT can be used to efficiently compute the inverse, transpose, and determinant of a matrix, making it an essential tool for linear algebra computations.

The CT is based on the concept of similarity transformation, which states that two matrices are similar if they have the same eigenvalues. By applying a series of similarity transformations to a given matrix, we can easily obtain its conjugate form. We show how the CT can be used to quickly compute the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of a matrix,which has important implications for many applications in physics, engineering,and data analysis.

Our experimental results demonstrate that both the PNT and CT outperform existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. We also compare the performance of our methods with state-of-the art software libraries such as MATLAB and NumPy, showing that they offer significant improvements over current practices. Finally,we discuss potential applications and future directions for research involving these techniques .

Fourteen ounces of firm tofu
Two teaspoons of pure olive oil
Four cloves of garlic, minced
One cup of finely chopped tomatoes
Half an ounce of oil-soaked sun-dried tomatoes, sliced thin from their packaging
One teaspoon of lemon juice, or as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Thin strips of fresh basil leaves
Cut each block of tofu into six identical pieces. Gently pat dry the tofu with clean kitchen cloths. In a large pan, warm one tablespoon of oil over high heat. Place the tofu slices in a single layer and cook until golden brown, turning every five to seven minutes. Meanwhile, heat the other tablespoon of oil in a separate small pan. Sauté the garlic over low heat until lightly golden. Combine the fresh and dried tomatoes and lemon juice in the same pan. Cook over medium heat until the tomatoes have just softened, about two minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Serve by arranging three slices of tofu on each plate and topping them with a spoonful of the tomato-garlic sauce. Garnish each serving with a few basil strips before serving immediately. This dish pairs well with a hearty salad for a light summer meal. It also complements pasta dishes such as cauliflower and spinach pasta or creamy pasta with asparagus and peas. Alternatively, serve it with a simple mixed green salad, accompanied by fresh bread and grilled corn on the cob. Nutrition facts: 415 calories, 25 grams of fat, 38 grams of protein, 19 grams of carbohydrates, seven grams of fiber, eighty milligrams of sodium.

> We reformat AdaBoost, Logitboost and XGBoost as primal optimization problems over linear constraints or semidefinite programming formulations that are differentiable with respect to both parameters and data points. Given this differentiability property we develop an automatic methodology called dual augmentation (augmentA) that augments stochastic gradient descent based methods by taking advantage of the convex lower bound implied due to strict complementarity in duality theory; thereby improving learning speeds on average over time per iteration while maintaining optimal overall solution accuracy via theoretical convergence guarantees . This is in contrast to previously proposed algorithms which either used approximation heuristics such as sub-gradient boost, hessian free gradients/Newton step approximates like HingeBoost or require access only to partial information, i.e., not all input coordinates at every iteration (which becomes possible here through our use of SDPs). Furthermore we also provide error bounds showing strong consistency (existence guarantee), asymptotic normality (limit distribution guarantee) in terms of statistical estimators obtained using stochastic optimizers applied onto these new reformulated algorithms whose loss functions possess certain smoothness properties under appropriate assumptions about errors present during training process .

Oscar-winner Andrea Arnold has been congratulated by the UK Film Council, the organisation which partly funded her project.
Arnold's film Wasp won the best live action short film award on Sunday. "The UK Film Council spends millions of pounds of lottery investment on short filmmaking in Britain every year," said chief executive officer John Woodward. "It certainly pays off when you see new film-makers winning such prestigious awards," he added.
Wasp, which was commissioned by the Film Council and Channel 4, beat films by fellow UK nominees Gary McKendry and Ashvin Kumar to the prize. It stars actress Nathalie Press, who appeared in the Bafta-winning drama My Summer Of Love, as a single mother who is forced to take drastic action when she is invited on a date and is unable to find a babysitter to look after her four daughters. The film has already won over 30 other international awards including the Sundance Short Film Prize. Arnold, from Dartford in Kent, described her victory as "truly overwhelming. I'm really not used to this kind of thing," she said, after receiving her Oscar from actor Jeremy Irons. "Thanks to everyone who worked on this - the beers are on me when we get home." The director was one of only two British winners on the night, the other being Sandy Powell, who won the costume design Oscar for her work on The Aviator.

In this paper, we explore the potential contributions of non-contact atomic force microscopy (ncAFM) to the measurement of the Casimir force, a fundamental interaction between objects that arises from quantum fluctuations in vacuum. The Casimir force has important implications for various fields such as nanotechnology and materials science, yet its precise measurement remains challenging due to the fragile nature of the interaction. Conventional methods rely on indirect techniques, which can be limited by thermal noise or sample damage. Non-contact AFM offers an attractive alternative for directly measuring the Casimir force with high sensitivity and spatial resolution. Our study demonstrates the capabilities of ncAFM in probing the Casimir force between various surfaces, including dielectric and metallic samples. We discuss the theoretical framework for interpreting the experimental data and highlight the advantages of ncAFM over conventional techniques. Our results open up new opportunities for investigating the Casimir effect at the nanoscale and pave the way for novel applications in surface engineering and material design.

1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
6 tablespoons hot water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter
1 tablespoon canola oil
3 tablespoons all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon ground hazelnuts or 1 tablespoon almonds
1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
3 tablespoons dark brown sugar, firmly packed
2 tablespoons honey
1/8 teaspoon salt
3/4 cup 1% low-fat milk
4 egg whites
3 tablespoons granulated sugar
1 cup fresh berries (blueberries, raspberries or strawberries)
confectioners' sugar
Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Lighlty spray six 1-cup individual souffle dishes or ramekins with cooking spray. In a small bowl, combine the cocoa and hot water, stirring until smooth; set aside. In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter, stir in the canola oil; stirring to combine. To the butter mixture, add the flour, ground nuts and cinnamon. Cook mixture for approximately 1 minute, stirring constantly with a wire whisk. Stir in brown sugar, honey and salt. Gradually add the milk and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat and add the cocoa mixture. Allow mixture to cool slightly. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer on high setting, beat the egg whites until foamy. Add the granulated sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, and continue to beat until stiff peaks form. With rubber spatula, gently fold 1/3 of egg whites into cocoa mixture. Then fold in the remaining egg whites, mixing only until no white streaks remain. Gently scoop the mixture into prepared dishes and bake until souffle rises above the rim and is set in the center, approximately 15 to 20 minutes. Using a fine sieve, dust the tops with confectioners sugar and garnish with fresh berries. Serve immediately.

On 25 October 1946, Popper (then at the London School of Economics), was invited to present a paper entitled "Are There Philosophical Problems?" at a meeting of the Moral Sciences Club, which was chaired by Wittgenstein. The two started arguing vehemently over whether there existed substantial problems in philosophy, or merely linguistic puzzles—the position taken by Wittgenstein. In Popper's, and the popular account, Wittgenstein used a fireplace poker to emphasize his points, gesturing with it as the argument grew more heated. When challenged by Wittgenstein to state an example of a moral rule, Popper (later) claimed to have replied "Not to threaten visiting lecturers with pokers", upon which (according to Popper) Wittgenstein threw down the poker and stormed out. Wittgenstein's Poker collects and characterizes the accounts of the argument, as well as establishing the context of the careers of Popper, Wittgenstein and Bertrand Russell, also present at the meeting. The book follows three narrative threads, each pivoting off the 1946 confrontation at Cambridge; the first is a documentary investigation into what precisely took place and the controversy over the differing accounts from observers; the second, a comparative personal history of the philosophers, contrasting their origins in Vienna and their differing ascents to philosophical prominence; and thirdly an exploration of the philosophical significance of the disagreement between the two and its relevance for the great debates in the early 20th century concerning the philosophy of language.

The first episode covers the period from the betrothal of Hrútr Herjólfsson and Unnr to the ugly legacy of their divorce. We are shown Hrútr's exploits in Norway, where he gains honour at court and in battle, but he ruins his subsequent marriage by becoming the lover of the aging queen mother Gunnhildr. When he denies having a woman in Iceland, she curses him so that he is unable to consummate his marriage. After Unnr divorces him, he retains the dowry by challenging Unnr's father, Mörðr, to combat. Mörðr refuses, as he knows Hrútr's reputation and that he will lose the fight. Because of this, Hrútr keeps the dowry. While this conforms to Icelandic law, it offends justice. The first chapter gives one of Hrútr's insights when he comments of his beautiful niece, "I do not know how thieves' eyes came into the family". The saga next follows this niece, Hallgerðr, through her first two marriages. Both husbands die by the axe of Hallgerðr's doting, brutish foster-father,Þjóstólfr. Hallgerðr provokes the first death but not the second, although it follows from a disagreement between her and her husband. It is Hrútr who, despite the family ties, avenges the death by killing Þjóstólfr. Gunnarr Hámundarson and Njáll Þorgeirsson are now introduced. Gunnarr is a man of outstanding physical prowess, and Njáll has outstanding sagacity; they are close friends. When Gunnarr is obliged to revive Unnr's dowry-claim against Hrútr, Njáll gives him the means to do so. By skillful play-acting, Gunnarr begins the legal process in Hrútr's own house. He follows Hrútr's doubtful example when it comes to court, and Hrútr, who has previously won by threat of violence, loses to a threat of violence. Despite his humiliation, he sees future links with Gunnarr. This comes about when Gunnarr returns with honours from a trip to Scandinavia. He goes to the Althing – the annual assembly – in splendour, and meets Hallgerðr. They are impressed with one another and are soon betrothed, despite Hrútr's warnings about Hallgerðr's character, and Njáll's misgivings. Hrútr and Njáll are proven right when Hallgerðr clashes with Njál's wife, Bergþóra. Hallgerðr charms a number of dubious characters into killing members of Njáll's household and the spirited Bergþóra arranges vengeance. After each killing, their husbands make financial settlements according to the status of the victims. The fifth victim is Þórðr, foster-father of Njáll's sons. Þráinn Sigfússon, Gunnarr's uncle and Hallgerðr's son-in-law, accompanies the killers. When the feud ends and settlements are made, Þráinn’s presence at that killing later causes conflict. Hallgerðr now uses one of her slaves, Melkólfr, to burgle the home of a churlish man named Otkell. Gunnarr immediately seeks to make amends, but his handsome offers are not accepted. A lawsuit is started against him which, with Njáll's help, he wins, gaining great honour. However, while remonstrating with Hallgerðr about the burglary, Gunnarr slaps her. This is followed by Otkell accidentally wounding Gunnarr. Insult follows injury and Gunnarr reluctantly goes to avenge himself. With belated help from his brother Kolskeggr, he kills Otkell and his companions. Under Njáll's influence a new settlement is arranged, and Gunnarr's reputation grows. Njáll warns him that this will be the start of his career of killings. Next, Gunnarr accepts a challenge to a horse-fight from a man called Starkaðr. In the course of the fight, his opponents cheat, and Gunnarr find himself in a fresh squabble. Njáll tries to mediate but Þorgeir Starkaðsson refuses to accept it. On a journey with his two brothers, Gunnarr is ambushed by Starkaðr and his allies. In the battle, fourteen attackers and Gunnarr's brother Hjörtr are killed. Worming through all this is Unnr's son, Mörðr Valgarðsson. Mörðr envies and hates Gunnarr, and uses other men to attain his aims. He has learned that Njáll prophesied that Gunnarr will die if he kills twice in the same family. He instigates an attack on Gunnarr by persons dissatisfied by the settlement. Again, Gunnarr wins the fight, but he kills a second man in the same family. The settlement that follows requires that Gunnarr and Kolskeggr leave Iceland for three years. Arrangements are made for exile. But as Gunnarr leaves home, he looks homeward and, touched by the beauty of his homeland, resolves not to leave Iceland, thus becoming an outlaw. He goes about as though nothing has changed but his enemies, Mörðr among them, seek revenge. He defends himself in his home until his bowstring is cut. Hallgerðr refuses to give him strands of her hair to restring his bow; this is in revenge for the slap he once gave her. Some readers choose to interpret this episode as her forgiveness since human hair is unusable as bowstring; i.e. he asks for something he knows is useless and she answers by denying as revenge, fully knowing too. Gunnarr's enemies resist Mörðrs proposal to burn him in the house as shameful, but eventually they take the roof off to get to Gunnarr. Njáll's son Skarp-Heðinn assists Högni Gunnarsson in some acts of vengeance before a settlement is achieved. Scandinavian rulers honor two Icelandic expeditions: those of Þráinn Sigfússon and of Njáll's two younger sons. Both return with enhanced honor, but also with companions. Þráinn brings back the malevolent Betrayal-Hrappr; the sons of Njáll the noble Kári Sölmundarson, who marries their sister. But Njáll's sons also bring back a grievance, blaming Þráinn for the way in which the de facto ruler of Norway, Jarl Hákon, has treated them while looking for Hrappr, who had been hidden by Þráinn. While Njáll says they have been foolish in raising the matter, he advises them to publicise it so that it will be seen as a matter of honor. Þrain refuses a settlement, and his retainers, including Hallgerðr, on her last appearance, insult them. The most dramatic of the saga's battles follows. Njáll's sons, with Kári, prepare to ambush Þráinn and his followers. There is a bridge of ice over the river between them. Skarp-Heðinn overtakes his brothers, leaps the river, and slides on the ice past Þráinn, beheading him in passing. Between them the attackers kill four men, including Hrappr. Þráinn's brother, Ketill, has married Njáll's daughter, and between them they bring about a settlement. Wishing to stop further contention, Njáll adopts Þráinn's son Höskuldr as his foster-son. Höskuldr grows up in Njáll's household, and is loved and favoured by him. When he is fully grown, Njáll attempts to find a suitable wife for him, Hildigunnr. However, she refuses, saying that she will only marry Höskuldr if he becomes a chieftain. Njáll manages to get Höskuldr a chieftaincy by instituting the Fifth Court at the Althing, and Höskuldr and Hildigunnr are married. At this point the saga recounts the conversion of Iceland to Christianity in AD 999. Mörðr Valgarðsson now finds Höskuldr to be such a successful chief that his own chieftaincy is declining. He sets the sons of Njáll against Höskuldr; the tragedy of the saga is that they are so susceptible to his promptings that they, with Mörðr and Kári, murder him as he sows in his field. As one character says, "Höskuldr was killed for less than no reason; all men mourn his death; but none more than Njal, his foster-father". Flosi, the uncle of Höskuldr's wife, takes revenge against the killers, and seeks help from powerful chieftains. He is pressured (against his better judgement) by Hildigunnr to accept only blood vengeance. Njáll's sons find themselves at the Althing having to plead for help. Skarp-Heðinn has become grimly fatalistic, and insults many who might help them. After some legal sparring, arbitrators are chosen, including Snorri goði, who proposes a weregild of three times the normal compensation for Höskuldr. This is so much that it can only be paid if the arbitrators, and many at the Althing, contribute. The great collection is gathered, and Njáll adds a gift of a fancy cloak. Flosi claims to be insulted by the offer of a unisex garment (an insult from Skarp-Heðinn also adds fuel to the fire) and the settlement breaks down. Everyone leaves the Althing and prepares, amid portents and prophecies, for the showdown. A hundred men descend on Njáll's home, Bergthorsknoll (Bergþórshváll), to find it defended by about thirty. Any victory for Flosi will be at some cost. But Njáll suggests that his sons defend from within the house, and they, while realizing that this is futile, agree. Flosi and his men set fire to the building. Both the innocent and the guilty are surrounded. Flosi allows the women to leave but beheads Helgi Njálsson, who attempts to escape disguised as a woman. Although Flosi invites Njáll and Bergþóra to leave, they refuse, preferring to die with their sons and their grandson Þórðr (the son of Kári). Eventually eleven people die, not including Kári who escapes under cover of the smoke by running along the beam of the house. Flosi knows that Kári will exact vengeance for the burning. At the Althing, both sides gather. Flosi bribes Eyjólfr Bölverksson, one of the finest lawyers in Iceland, into taking over the case, while his opponents blackmail Mörðr Valgarðsson into prosecuting, advised by Þórhallr, Njáll's foster-son, who was trained in the law by Njáll, but is kept away from the proceedings by an infected leg. There is a legal joust between the parties. Eventually, when his legal action seems to be failing, Þórhallr lances his boil with his spear and begins fighting. Flosi's men are driven back until Snorri separates the parties. In the confusion, several are killed including Ljótr, Flosi's brother-in-law. Ljótr's father, Hallr of Síða, takes advantage of the truce to appeal for peace, and seeks no compensation for his son. Moved by this, all but Kári and Njáll's nephew Þorgeir reach a settlement, while everyone contributes to Ljótr's weregild, which in the end amounts to a quadruple compensation. The burners are exiled. Before the sons of Sigfús reach home, Kári attacks them, and most of the rest of the saga describes his vengeance for the burning. He is supported by Þorgeir and an attractive anti-hero named Björn. He pursues them to Orkney and Wales. The most dramatic moment is when he breaks into the earl's hall in Orkney and kills a man who is giving a slanderous account of those killed at the burning. After a pilgrimage to Rome, Flosi returns to Iceland. Kári follows, and is shipwrecked near Flosi's home. Testing Flosi's nobility he goes to him for help, and they arrange a final peace. Kári marries Höskuldr's widow. Finally, there is a full reconciliation.

Sure! Here's a recipe for Lemon Chicken and Leek Rice Pilaf:

Ingredients:

* 1 cup uncooked white rice
* 3 cups water
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* 2 leeks, cleaned and chopped (about 1 cup)
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
* 1/2 cup lemon juice
* 2 teaspoons lemon zest
* 1 teaspoon dried thyme
* Salt and pepper to taste
* Fresh parsley, chopped (optional)

Instructions:

1. Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped leeks and cook until they are softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
2. Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
3. Add the chicken to the saucepan and cook until it is lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Add the rice to the saucepan and stir to coat the rice in the oil and mix with the chicken and leeks.
5. Add the water, lemon juice, lemon zest, thyme, salt, and pepper to the saucepan. Bring the mixture to a boil.
6. Reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and the liquid has been absorbed.
7. Fluff the rice pilaf with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley, if using.
8. Serve hot, garnished with additional lemon wedges and parsley if desired.

Enjoy your delicious Lemon Chicken and Leek Rice Pilaf!

ONE morning (raw it was and wet---
A foggy day in winter time)
A Woman on the road I met,
Not old, though something past her prime:
Majestic in her person, tall and straight;
And like a Roman matron's was her mien and gait.
The ancient spirit is not dead;
Old times, thought I, are breathing there;
Proud was I that my country bred
Such strength, a dignity so fair:
She begged an alms, like one in poor estate;
I looked at her again, nor did my pride abate.
When from these lofty thoughts I woke,
'What is it,' said I, 'that you bear,
Beneath the covert of your Cloak,
Protected from this cold damp air? '
She anwered, soon as she the question heard,
'A simple burthen, Sir, a little Singing-bird.'
And, thus continuing, she said,
'I had a Son, who many a day
Sailed on the seas, but he is dead;
In Denmark he was cast away:
And I have travelled weary miles to see
If aught which he had owned might still remain for me.
The bird and cage they both were his:
'Twas my Son's bird; and neat and trim
He kept it: many voyages
The singing-bird had gone with him;
When last he sailed, he left the bird behind;
From bodings, as might be, that hung upon his mind.
He to a fellow-lodger's care
Had left it, to be watched and fed,
And pipe its song in safety;---there
I found it when my Son was dead;
And now, God help me for my little wit!
I bear it with me, Sir;---he took so much delight in it.'

Sir John Gordon Noel Wilton, a prominent Australian Army commander, held key positions from 1963 to 1970. As Chief of the General Staff and Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, he oversaw the country's military during the entirety of its involvement in the Vietnam War. Born in Sydney in 1910, Wilton attended the Royal Military College, Duntroon, before joining the British Army due to limited opportunities in Australia upon graduating in 1930. He spent much of his early career with the Royal Artillery in India. Returning to Australia just before WWII, Wilton joined the Royal Australian Artillery and participated in conflicts in Syria and New Guinea, where he earned recognition for his actions. After completing the war, he became a temporary colonel and received honors including an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1947. In 1953, Wilton led the 28th Commonwealth Brigade in Korea, where he demonstrated exceptional leadership and was subsequently promoted and honored with the Commander of the Order of the British Empire and the US Legion of Merit.

$\omega\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{R}$ and any list assignment $L\colon
E(G)\to2^{\mathbb{R}}$ with $|L(e)|\geq |E(G)|+k$ there exists an edge labeling
$f$ such that $f(e)\in L(e)$ for all $e\in E(G)$, labels of edges are pairwise
distinct, and the sum of the labels on edges incident to a vertex plus the
weight of that vertex is distinct from the sum at every other vertex. In this
paper we prove that every graph on $n$ vertices having no $K_1$ or $K_2$
component is $\lfloor{\frac{4n}{3}}\rfloor$-weighted-list-antimagic.
  An oriented graph $G$ is $k$-$oriented-antimagic$ if there exists an
injective edge labeling from $E(G)$ into $\{1,\dotsc,|E(G)|+k\}$ such that the
sum of the labels on edges incident to and oriented toward a vertex minus the
sum of the labels on edges incident to and oriented away from that vertex is

graph on $n$ vertices with no $K_1$ component admits an orientation that is

Drug intolerance occurs when individuals cannot withstand the negative side effects of medications, typically at standard or prescribed dosages. In contrast, someone who can handle these side effects is said to be tolerating the medication. Certain genetic differences in how the body processes medications can lead to this intolerance. 

The amount of medication present in the bloodstream determines how much of the drug reaches other parts of the body. A specific concentration of the drug in the blood is necessary to achieve the desired therapeutic effect (the lowest effective dose) and another level that causes unwanted adverse reactions (the lowest toxic dose). The gap between these levels is called the therapeutic range. Each medication has its own unique therapeutic range, and individuals may have varying thresholds for both the beneficial and toxic effects. Those with a very low threshold for a particular medication are more prone to experiencing adverse effects even at doses that wouldn't cause harm to most people, making them intolerant to the substance. As a result, they will exhibit significant toxicity at doses deemed safe for others.

Recipe for Spice Cake and Winter Fruit Compote:

Ingredients for Spice Cake:
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda
- 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder

- 1 teaspoon cinnamon
- 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg
- 1/4 teaspoon allspice
- 1/4 teaspoon cloves
- 1 1/2 cups sour cream
- 2 teaspoons vanilla
- 1/4 cup orange juice
- 1 1/2 teaspoons orange zest
- 3/4 cup unsalted butter
- 1 1/2 cups sugar
- 3 eggs
- Powdered sugar for garnish

For Winter Fruit Compote:
- 2 cups water
- 2 cinnamon sticks
- 4 whole cloves
- 1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 4 Golden Delicious apples, cored, peeled and sliced
- 4 Red pears, cored, peeled and sliced
- 1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries
- 2 tablespoons Calvados, Grand Marnier or brandy

To prepare the spice cake, preheat the oven to 350°F and set a 10-cup bundt or tube pan aside. Sift the flour mixture and set it aside. Combine sour cream, orange juice, orange zest, and vanilla, setting them aside as well. Cream together sugar and butter, adding eggs one at a time. Alternate between dry ingredients and sour cream mixture, blending until combined. Pour batter into prepared pan and bake for 45-50 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before transferring it to a plate to cool completely. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

For the winter fruit compote, bring water, cinnamon sticks, cloves, and vanilla bean to a boil for 5 minutes. Add fruit and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes or until desired consistency is reached. Discard the spices and serve the compote warm over a slice of cake.
