The Medusa Algorithm is a novel approach to performing polynomial matings in machine learning. This algorithm improves upon traditional methods by utilizing an efficient matrix multiplication technique to streamline the mating process. The algorithm takes advantage of parallelism and specialized hardware accelerators, such as graphics processing units (GPUs), increasing both speed and accuracy.

Furthermore, the Medusa Algorithm incorporates a unique genetic recombination step that allows for more effective exploration of the solution space. By using this method, the algorithm can generate diverse solutions with high quality, making it particularly useful in cases where there are no clear local optima. Additionally, the algorithm includes a convergence test that ensures accurate results within a reasonable timeframe.

Overall, the research outlines the effectiveness of the Medusa Algorithm in addressing common problems in polynomial mating found in previous research. The algorithm's combination of efficient matrix multiplication, parallelization, genetic recombination, and convergence testing make it a valuable tool for improving the efficiency and reliability of machine learning techniques.

Segmentation of organs or lesions from medical images plays an essential role
in many clinical applications such as diagnosis and treatment planning. Though
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have achieved the state-of-the-art
performance for automatic segmentation, they are often limited by the lack of
clinically acceptable accuracy and robustness in complex cases. Therefore,
interactive segmentation is a practical alternative to these methods. However,
traditional interactive segmentation methods require a large amount of user
interactions, and recently proposed CNN-based interactive segmentation methods
are limited by poor performance on previously unseen objects. To solve these
problems, we propose a novel deep learning-based interactive segmentation
method that not only has high efficiency due to only requiring clicks as user
inputs but also generalizes well to a range of previously unseen objects.
Specifically, we first encode user-provided interior margin points via our
proposed exponentialized geodesic distance that enables a CNN to achieve a good
initial segmentation result of both previously seen and unseen objects, then we
use a novel information fusion method that combines the initial segmentation
with only few additional user clicks to efficiently obtain a refined
segmentation. We validated our proposed framework through extensive experiments
on 2D and 3D medical image segmentation tasks with a wide range of previous
unseen objects that were not present in the training set. Experimental results
showed that our proposed framework 1) achieves accurate results with fewer user
interactions and less time compared with state-of-the-art interactive
frameworks and 2) generalizes well to previously unseen objects.

Following the fall of the Berlin Wall that same year, he began traveling extensively across Africa and India, exploring new creative horizons. By 1990, he established an art studio in Weimar's Atelierhaus. FC Union Berlin, and collaborating on projects like the Hiddensee Edition in 2007 and 2010, as well as the Well women-High Priestesses of the Market project at Gerhart Hauptmann Haus in 2008.

The Lehigh Division was a railway division of the Pennsylvania Railroad (PRR) in the United States, active from 1873 until 1968. It consisted of 154 miles (248 kilometers) of track in eastern Pennsylvania.

The Lehigh Division was created in 1873, when the Lehigh Valley Railroad merged with the PRR. The division's name came from the Lehigh River, which runs through the eastern part of its territory.

In the early 1900s, the Lehigh Division was home to some of the PRR's busiest coal mines, shipping coal to destinations as far away as New York City and Boston. The division's routes also served the cities of Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Harrisburg.

During the decline of coal mining in the mid-20th century, the Lehigh Division saw its passenger traffic decrease significantly. In 1958, Amtrak took over passenger service in the region, but this only further reduced the division's popularity.

The Lehigh Division was officially disbanded in 1968, but its legacy can still be seen in the numerous rail lines that continue to operate in the area today. Many of these lines have been converted to freight-only service, while others have been abandoned altogether.

Despite its history of decline, the Lehigh Division remains an important part of the region's transportation infrastructure. The division's former tracks continue to serve as critical connections for businesses and residents throughout eastern Pennsylvania.

A book about the evolution of mutants and the science of abnormality has won the Guardian First Book Award 2004.
Armand Marie Leroi, a lecturer at London's Imperial College, scooped the £10,000 prize for Mutants: On the form, varieties and errors of the human body. "It is profoundly cultured and beautifully written in the very best tradition of popular science writing today," said judge Claire Armistead. The award recognises and rewards new writing across fiction and non-fiction. A panel of literary experts, including novelists Hari Kunzru and Ali Smith, director Sir Richard Eyre and comedian Alexei Sayle chose the winner from a five-strong shortlist.
The shortlist included Susanna Clarke's Jonathan Strange and Mr Norrell, a novel about the magic arts at the turn of the 19th Century and The Places In Between, Rory Stewart's account of his trek, on foot, across Afghanistan. "What we found so impressive about Armand Marie Leroi's book was the scope of its reference, its elegance and its inquisitiveness," said Ms Armistead, chair of the judges and the Guardian literary editor. "While the subject matter of Mutants unsettled some involved in the judging process, the overwhelming majority found it fascinating," she added. Her words were echoed by Iris director Sir Richard Eyre who called Marie Leroi's work "extraordinarily thought provoking". The award, for first time authors, is open to books from genres including fiction, poetry, biography, memoir, history, politics, science and current affairs. Previous winners include White Teeth by Zadie Smith, in 2000, which went on to become a bestseller.

Global aphasia is a severe form of aphasia, a language disorder that results from damage to portions of the brain responsible for language. It is characterized by a significant impairment in all aspects of language comprehension and production. Individuals with global aphasia have difficulty understanding spoken or written language, finding the right words to express themselves, and reading or writing.

Global aphasia is most commonly caused by a stroke, particularly in the left hemisphere of the brain, which is responsible for language and communication. Other potential causes include traumatic brain injury, brain tumors, infections, and degenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's.

Symptoms of global aphasia can vary depending on the extent of brain damage. However, common symptoms include difficulty speaking or understanding speech, inability to read or write, and difficulty finding the right words. Some individuals may also experience physical difficulties such as weakness or paralysis on one side of the body.

Diagnosis of global aphasia is typically made through a series of language and cognitive tests conducted by a speech-language pathologist. These tests assess the individual's ability to understand, speak, read, and write. Brain imaging techniques such as MRI or CT scans may also be used to identify the location and extent of brain damage.

Treatment for global aphasia is usually centered around speech and language therapy. The goal of therapy is to improve the individual's ability to communicate by restoring as much language function as possible and teaching alternative methods of communication when necessary. The intensity and duration of therapy can vary depending on the severity of the aphasia.

The prognosis for individuals with global aphasia varies. Some individuals may make significant improvements, particularly with intensive speech and language therapy. However, others may continue to experience significant language difficulties. The extent of recovery is generally dependent on the size and location of the brain damage, the individual's age and health status, and the intensity of speech and language therapy.

Research into global aphasia is ongoing, with scientists seeking to better understand the brain mechanisms involved in language and communication, as well as develop more effective treatment strategies. Current research areas include the use of technology in aphasia therapy, the role of music therapy in language recovery, and the potential of certain medications to enhance language function.

In conclusion, global aphasia is a severe language disorder that significantly impacts an individual's ability to communicate. Despite the challenges it presents, many individuals with global aphasia are able to improve their communication skills with the help of speech and language therapy and other treatment strategies.

Japan's biggest bank, Mizuho Financial Group, has agreed to pay $1bn (£650m) in compensation and other costs after being accused by regulators of manipulating its benchmark interest rate for years. The deal will see the lender admit wrongdoing over its role in setting the Libor inter-bank lending rate between banks around the world. It also means that it will be forced to sell off assets worth more than $20bn. The settlement comes as Japan's financial regulator prepares to announce new rules on how banks should report their dealings with each other. The move could lead to further fines or even criminal charges against some of the country's largest lenders. The scandal erupted last year when Barclays was fined £290m for rigging Libor. But the Japanese government said it would not pursue any individual bankers involved in the scandal. Instead, it decided to settle with Mizuho, which had been accused of using its influence to help clients manipulate the rate. The bank admitted to having manipulated the rate since 2004. It paid $972m in penalties and $2.5bn in compensation. The settlement includes a provision for another $3.6bn in damages. The bank will have to sell off about $21bn of assets, including stakes in Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. The sale process will take several months. The bank will also have to make changes to its internal controls and procedures.

As you can see, this is just one part of a much larger story. As I've written before, there are many reasons why the US and UK governments want to bring down the big banks. One reason is because they know that if these banks fail, then we'll all suffer. Another reason is that they don't want to lose control of our money. And yet another reason is that they're afraid that if the big banks collapse, then they won't be able to continue to print money like crazy. So they're trying to force them into bankruptcy so that they can keep printing money.

But what happens if the big banks do go bankrupt? Well, that depends on who owns them. If the big banks were owned by the public, then they'd probably be nationalized. That way, the people who own them wouldn't be allowed to use them to create money out of thin air. They'd have to pay taxes on those profits

1/4 cups Melted Butter
3/4 cups Heavy Cream
8 ounces, weight Good Dark Chocolate
16 ounces, weight Good Milk Chocolate
1 cup Heavy Cream
1 Tablespoon Gelatin
1/4 cups Water
2 cups Heavy Cream
1 teaspoon Vanilla Extract
Butter a 10" springform cake pan. First Layer: Crush 8 ounces of Oreo cookies. (I used my Cuisinart to crush them). Add 1/4 cup melted butter to the crumbs and pulse again. Once the butter is well mixed with the Oreo cookies press the mixture into the bottom of the springform pan. Second Layer: Bring 3/4 Cup of heavy cream to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and then add 8 ounces of dark chocolate. (yeah baby!) Whisk until smooth and then pour over the Oreo crust. Chill the cake in the refrigerator while you make the third layer Third Layer: Combine 16 ounces of good milk chocolate and 1 Cup of heavy cream in a double boiler. Boil the water in the bottom and stir the chocolate mixture in the top of the double boiler until smooth. Set aside to cool to barely luke warm. Sprinkle 1 Tablespoon of gelatin over 1/4 Cup water in a saucepan. Allow the gelatin to rest for 10 minutes. After the gelatin has rested stir over low heat til dissolved. In a bowl begin to beat 2 Cups of heavy cream. While beating, add 1 teaspoon of vanilla and the dissolved gelatin mixture. Continue to beat until you reach soft peaks. Fold in the milk chocolate mixture and then pour the mixture on top of the other two layers. Chill until set-about 6 hours. After the cake has been chilled for 6 hours run a sharp knife around the edge of the pan before releasing the sides of the cake. If you don't, the cake will crack while releasing the pan.

The high-fidelity storage of quantum information is crucial for quantum
computation and communication. Many experimental platforms for these
applications exhibit highly biased noise, with good resilience to spin
depolarisation undermined by high dephasing rates. In this work, we demonstrate
that the memory performance of a noise-biased trapped-ion qubit memory can be
greatly improved by incorporating error correction of dephasing errors through
teleportation of the information between two repetition codes written on a pair
of qubit registers in the same trap. While the technical requirements of error
correction are often considerable, we show that our protocol can be achieved
with a single global entangling phase gate of remarkably low fidelity,
leveraging the fact that the gate errors are also dominated by dephasing-type
processes. By rebalancing the logical spin-flip and dephasing error rates, we
show that for realistic parameters our memory can exhibit error rates up to two
orders of magnitude lower than the unprotected physical qubits, thus providing
a useful means of improving memory performance in trapped ion systems where
field-insensitive qubits are not available.

Muhammad Zayni al-Baghdadi, whose full name was Sayyid Muhammad ibn Zayn al-Din Ahmad ibn Ali bin Sayf al-Din bin Ridha al-Din al-Hassani al-Baghdadi, was a renowned Iraqi Muslim scholar, poet, and writer born in Najaf in 1735. He belonged to a prominent Shia Muslim family and studied under notable scholars like Mahdi Bahr al-Ulum at his hometown before becoming a key figure in Islamic literature. Al-Baghdadi's literary career spanned various genres, encompassing poetry written in both Arabic and Persian. His notable works include a comprehensive poetry collection and several scholarly books on Tafsir and Arabic literary studies. As a respected advocate for religious causes, he played a significant role in shaping Najaf's intellectual landscape during the late 17th century. Known for hosting salons featuring esteemed poets and writers, al-Baghdadi earned a reputation as a leading literary personality in the city. After passing away in 1801, he was laid to rest in Kadhimiya.

Chinese online game operator Shanda Interactive Entertainment has bought a 20% stake in Sina, the country's biggest internet portal firm.
The move may be a precursor to a full takeover, with analysts saying that a better-known international firm may also now show an interest in Sina. Shanda said that it may boost its stake in Sina, even buying it outright. A merger would create a firm that offers online role-playing games, news, entertainment and wireless messaging.
Sina said that the purchase of a stake by Shanda would have no impact on its business.
The board of directors said in a statement that it would "continue to act in the best interests of all the company stakeholders, including shareholders, employees and customers". Both companies are listed on the New York Stock Exchange's (NYSE) technology-dominated Nasdaq index. In a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Sina said its shares were purchased between 12 January and 10 February for about $230m. Rumours about a possible takeover boosted Sina's shares by more than 10% on Friday. They added an extra 6.4% to $27.24 in electronic trading after the trading session had finished. And there may be more gains amid bid speculation when trading resumes in New York on Tuesday after Monday's public holiday, analysts forecast. "There could still be some potential parties that could still counter bid," said Wallace Cheung, an analyst at DBS Vickers. "Even though Shanda has 20% of Sina, they still have quite a long way to take full control." However, Mr Cheung noted that a foreign company trying to take control of a Chinese internet portal firm, with its ability to filter and pass on news, may not be viewed very favourably by Beijing.

Image segmentation remains an essential area of study due to its widespread applications.
Traditional approaches primarily employed unsupervised techniques that relied on manually defined features to segment images into numerous distinct areas. Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs)-based methods, which significantly outperformed their predecessors. Nevertheless, these methods require substantial human-annotated data, which can be costly to obtain. This paper proposes a novel deep unsupervised approach to image segmentation, comprising two primary stages. Firstly, a Superpixelwise Autoencoder (SuperAE) is designed to learn a high-level representation and produce a smoothed version of the input image. The resulting image is then fed into a novel clustering algorithm called Deep Superpixel Cut (DSC), which assesses the similarity between superpixels by leveraging deep feature information and reframes image segmentation as a soft partitioning problem. Through this process, DSC dynamically partitions the superpixels into visually coherent regions using backpropagation. Experimental evaluations on the BSDS500 dataset validate the efficacy of the presented methodology.

Extracting a connectome from an electron microscopy (EM) data set requires
identification of neurons and determination of synapses between neurons. As
manual extraction of this information is very time-consuming, there has been
extensive research effort to automatically segment the neurons to help guide
and eventually replace manual tracing. Until recently, there has been
comparatively less research on automatically detecting the actual synapses
between neurons. This discrepancy can, in part, be attributed to several
factors: obtaining neuronal shapes is a prerequisite first step in extracting a
connectome, manual tracing is much more time-consuming than annotating
synapses, and neuronal contact area can be used as a proxy for synapses in
determining connections.
  However, recent research has demonstrated that contact area alone is not a
sufficient predictor of synaptic connection. Moreover, as segmentation has
improved, we have observed that synapse annotation is consuming a more
significant fraction of overall reconstruction time. This ratio will only get
worse as segmentation improves, gating overall possible speed-up. Therefore, we

pre-synaptic structures are detected using a Deep and Wide Multiscale Recursive

In LCN, the expansion rate of the plasma is much slower than that of the baryon-free radiation fluid, so that the baryons are dragged along by the latter. This leads to an effective cooling of the baryonic matter which can be used as a mechanism to produce light elements such as 4He or D during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) or primordial black holes (PBHs) after inflation. However, this process has been shown to fail when the number density of baryons becomes too large due to the strong Coulomb interaction between protons and electrons. Here we show how the inclusion of Coulomb screening effects allows one to extend the range of validity of LCN up to densities where the standard BBN scenario applies. Segmenting images of low quality or with missing data is a challenging
problem. Integrating statistical prior information about the shapes to be
segmented can improve the segmentation results significantly. Most shape-based
segmentation algorithms optimize an energy functional and find a point estimate
for the object to be segmented. This does not provide a measure of the degree
of confidence in that result, neither does it provide a picture of other
probable solutions based on the data and the priors. With a statistical view,
addressing these issues would involve the problem of characterizing the
posterior densities of the shapes of the objects to be segmented. For such
characterization, we propose a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling-based
image segmentation algorithm that uses statistical shape priors. In addition to
better characterization of the statistical structure of the problem, such an
approach would also have the potential to address issues with getting stuck at
local optima, suffered by existing shape-based segmentation methods. Our
approach is able to characterize the posterior probability density in the space
of shapes through its samples, and to return multiple solutions, potentially
from different modes of a multimodal probability density, which would be
encountered, e.g., in segmenting objects from multiple shape classes. We
present promising results on a variety of data sets. We also provide an
extension for segmenting shapes of objects with parts that can go through
independent shape variations. This extension involves the use of local shape
priors on object parts and provides robustness to limitations in shape training
data size.

If your period is delayed, it can be incredibly stressful and worrying. There are many factors that can cause a period to be late, including hormonal changes, stress, and other medical conditions. Here are some tips to help manage your concerns:
1. Wait - Sometimes a period can be up to two weeks late and still considered normal. If you're anxious about it, try distracting yourself with something fun or relaxing until you get your next period.
2. Keep track - Track when you expect your period typically starts and ends so you can better keep track if it's running late. This will also allow you to notice any patterns or potential issues more quickly.
3. Call for backup - Contact your healthcare provider right away if your period has been absent for over typical time frame. They may recommend further testing or treatment options based on the cause.
4. Take care of yourself - Make sure you're eating well, exercising regularly, getting enough sleep and managing stress levels because these factors can affect your menstrual cycle.
Remember, everyone's body is unique and there can be many reasons why periods run late. Don't let worry get in the way of enjoying life. Seek professional advice if you need to and try to stay positive and relaxed during this trying times.

Breaking up is never easy, and ending things with someone who you still have feelings for can be especially difficult. 2. Set boundaries: Try setting boundaries with your partner. Maybe limit your interactions or take some space until you both feel ready to have an honest conversation. This can help ease the pain and give you time to process what's going on.
3. Talk to trusted friends and family: Sometimes talking things through with others can be helpful. Reach out to people you trust to get their perspective on the situation and gain support during a difficult time.
4. Use positive self-talk: Be gentle and kind to yourself. Remember that this decision will likely hurt at first, but reminding yourself of how much your happiness matters can make starting fresh easier.
5. Focus on your future goals: Consider where you see yourself personally and professionally in the next few years. Ending things with someone may be the best choice if it means you can work towards building a better life for yourself without them holding you back.

Remember, you deserve to be happy and healthy. Lean into that feeling and know that you made the right decision for your own well-being.

Naina’s Stuffed Chicken Recipe

Ingredients: 
- 6 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts 
- 1 cup uncooked white rice 
- 2 cups vegetable broth 
- 1 tablespoon olive oil 
- 1 medium onion, diced 
- 3 cloves garlic, minced 
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained 
- 1 teaspoon dried basil leaves  
- Salt and pepper to taste 
- Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (optional garnish) 

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a large baking dish with cooking spray or olive oil.

2. In a saucepan over high heat, bring the vegetable broth to boil. Add the rice, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 18 minutes until cooked. Fluff the rice with a fork and set aside.

3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onions and cook until softened, around 5 minutes.

4. Add in the minced garlic and cook for another minute, until fragrant.

5.Add the cooked rice, diced tomatoes, dried basil leaves, salt and pepper to the skillet. Mix well and Cook for additional 3-5 minutes

6. Use a sharp knife to slice a pocket into the side of each chicken breast, being careful not to cut through to the other side.

7. Stuff each chicken breast with the rice mixture, and use toothpicks to secure the opening closed.

8. Place the stuffed chicken breasts in the prepared baking dish, seam-side down. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C)

9. Remove from oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired. Enjoy!

Liverpool and Millwall have been charged by the Football Association over crowd trouble during their Carling Cup match on 26 October.
Millwall, who lost the match 3-0, have also been charged over alleged racist behaviour by their supporters. During the match at Millwall's new Den Stadium, seats were ripped up and four people were ejected from the ground. A disabled fan was injured at the perimeter of the pitch and riot police were needed to control the situation. Liverpool fans claimed the trouble was sparked by chants about the Hillsborough disaster, where 96 supporters were crushed to death in April 1989. But Lions chairman Theo Paphitis has denied the claims. He has said CCTV footage showed the catalyst for the trouble was a Liverpool fan attacking a Millwall fan in the west stand. However, Millwall have been charged with two breaches of FA rules. They have been charged with failing to ensure that fans refrained from racist and/or abusive behaviour and for failing to prevent spectators throwing missiles onto the pitch. Liverpool have been charged with one breach for failing to prevent their fans conducting themselves in threatening and/or violent and/or provocative behaviour. Both clubs have until 23 December to respond.

He began to establish himself among his country's top hurdlers the following season and ran a personal best of 13.69 seconds to win at Zhaoqing leg of the Chinese Grand Prix. At the end of the year he represented the Jiangsu province at the 11th Chinese Games and finished in fifth place.

Internet search engine users are an odd mix of naive and sophisticated, suggests a report into search habits.

It also shows that few can spot the difference between paid-for results and organic ones. The report reveals that 84% of net users say they regularly use Google, Ask Jeeves, MSN and Yahoo when online.
Almost 50% of those questioned said they would trust search engines much less, if they knew information about who paid for results was being hidden. According to figures gathered by the Pew researchers the average users spends about 43 minutes per month carrying out 34 separate searches and looks at 1.9 webpages for each hunt. A significant chunk of net users, 36%, carry out a search at least weekly and 29% of those asked only look every few weeks. For 44% of those questioned, the information they are looking for is critical to what they are doing and is information they simply have to find.
Search engine users also tend to be very loyal and once they have found a site they feel they can trust tend to stick with it. According to Pew Research 44% of searchers use just a single search engine, 48% use two or three and a small number, 7%, consult more than three sites. Tony Macklin, spokesman for Ask Jeeves, said the results reflected its own research which showed that people use different search engines because the way the sites gather information means they can provide different results for the same query. Despite this liking for search sites half of those questioned said they could get the same information via other routes. A small number, 17%, said they wouldn't really miss search engines if they did not exist. The remaining 33% said they could not live without search sites. Commenting Mr Macklin said sponsored results must be clearly marked and though they might help with some queries user testing showed that people need to be able to spot the difference.

transmitter and a legitimate receiver (say, Alice and Bob). There is a jammer
group consisting of $S$ jammers among which Bob selects $K$ jammers. The
selected jammers transmit independent and identically distributed Gaussian
signals to hinder the eavesdropper (Eve). Since the channels of Bob and Eve are

We propose and study a task we name panoptic segmentation (PS). Panoptic
segmentation unifies the typically distinct tasks of semantic segmentation
(assign a class label to each pixel) and instance segmentation (detect and
segment each object instance). The proposed task requires generating a coherent
scene segmentation that is rich and complete, an important step toward
real-world vision systems. While early work in computer vision addressed
related image/scene parsing tasks, these are not currently popular, possibly
due to lack of appropriate metrics or associated recognition challenges. To
address this, we propose a novel panoptic quality (PQ) metric that captures
performance for all classes (stuff and things) in an interpretable and unified
manner. Using the proposed metric, we perform a rigorous study of both human
and machine performance for PS on three existing datasets, revealing
interesting insights about the task. The aim of our work is to revive the
interest of the community in a more unified view of image segmentation.

He was the son of Henry Parker and Mary A. (Holmes) Holden.  He moved to Palmer, Massachusetts, in 1871 when his father purchased interests in several local businesses.  Holden was educated in the Palmer schools and graduated from the Phillips Andover Academy in 1886.  He studied for three years at Amherst College before transferring to the University of Michigan.  He played college football and was the starting quarterback for the 1890 Michigan Wolverines football team.  Holden was a member of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity while attending both Amherst and Michigan.  He graduated from Michigan in 1891.  In March 1896, he married Katherine Cramer of Ann Arbor, Michigan.  They had three children, Roger Cramer Holden, Philip Holmes Holden, and Henry Parker Holden.  He worked in the woolen business in Palmer, Massachusetts, and became the superintendent of the Palmer Woolen Mill in 1895 and the financial manager starting in 1900.  In July 1935, Holden died at his home in Palmer.

Advances in deep learning-based image segmentation techniques have achieved human-like performance in real-time, but even top-performing methods can falter due to poor image quality, artifacts, or unforeseen behavior in complex algorithms. Predicting segmentation quality without access to ground truth is crucial in both clinical settings and large-scale research to prevent the inclusion of invalid data in subsequent analyses.

This work proposes two approaches to real-time quality control for cardiovascular MRI segmentations utilizing deep learning. Firstly, a neural network is trained on 12,880 samples to forecast Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) for each case, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.03 on 1,610 test samples and 97% binary classification accuracy for distinguishing between low and high-quality segmentations. Secondly, in scenarios where manual annotation data is unavailable, a network is trained to predict DSC scores based on estimated quality derived through a reverse testing strategy. The proposed approach reports an MAE of 0.14 and 91% binary classification accuracy for this case.

Real-time predictions enable immediate feedback on whether an acquired scan is analysable during the scanning process, allowing for optimized image acquisition strategies that yield better analysis results.

As a professor specializing in WWII studies, I've gained extensive knowledge through coursework and interviews with survivors on both sides of the conflict. This film stands out as one of the most compelling portrayals of the war, rivaling other notable films such as "Come and See" and "Schindler's List." 

I recently screened the film alongside two veterans – a US soldier who fought from Omaha to Czechoslovakia and a German infantry officer who served on the Eastern Front for four years. The German veteran, having met Hitler multiple times, expressed admiration for the film's meticulous attention to detail, particularly the accurate depiction of Hitler's distinct Munich accent. His fellow veteran, who survived in East Prussia during the final stages of the war and witnessed the chaotic evacuation efforts, was deeply moved by the film's graphic content, including scenes of hospitals, mass violence, and children fighting. He noted that his own experiences in East Prussia were not as horrific as those depicted in the film, which left him shaken. The film's portrayal of the devastation of Berlin, akin to the "Gotterdammerung" of a nation, brought back haunting memories for him. The chilling finale, featuring the brutal fate of Hitler's children, is particularly unsettling for parents of young children.

What struck me about the film is its nuanced portrayal of Hitler, moving away from the common stereotype of a deranged leader. Through his performances, Hitler is shown as capable of being charming, attentive, and courteous, yet simultaneously issuing orders that reveal his darker nature. Those familiar with Hitler, including a childhood companion of his daughter Helga Goebbels, concur that he possessed these complexities, making the film's exploration of his dual persona thought-provoking.

Max Ferdinand Perutz  (19 May 1914 – 6 February 2002) was an Austrian-born British molecular biologist, who shared the 1962 Nobel Prize for Chemistry with John Kendrew, for their studies of the structures of haemoglobin and myoglobin. He went on to win the Royal Medal of the Royal Society in 1971 and the Copley Medal in 1979.  At Cambridge he founded and chaired (1962–79) The Medical Research Council (MRC) Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB), fourteen of whose scientists have won Nobel Prizes. Perutz's contributions to molecular biology in Cambridge are documented in The History of the University of Cambridge: Volume 4 (1870 to 1990) published by the Cambridge University Press in 1992. Early life and education
Perutz was born in Vienna, the son of Adele "Dely" (Goldschmidt) and Hugo Perutz, a textile manufacturer. His parents were Jewish by ancestry, but had baptised Perutz in the Catholic religion. Although Perutz rejected religion and was an atheist in his later years, he was against offending others for their religious beliefs.

Mountview House is a heritage-listed detached house at 37 Leichhardt Street, Spring Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was originally built in the 1860s with a new wing added in 1882 designed by Andrea Stombuco. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 13 May 2004. History 
The earliest section of Mountview House, a two-storeyed stone residence, is believed to have been erected in the 1860s for Brisbane foreman carpenter Daniel McNaught. A two-storeyed brick wing designed by architect Andrea Stombuco was added in 1882, when the house was converted into a preparatory school for boys. This part of Spring Hill was surveyed officially into suburban allotments in 1856, but was soon subdivided for closer residential settlement by speculative landowners. Along with Kangaroo Point and Petrie Terrace, Spring Hill was among the earliest of Brisbane's dormitory suburbs, attracting wealthier residents to the high land along the ridges, and the less affluent to the hollows in between: Hanly's Hollow (between Wickham Terrace and Leichhardt Street), Spring Hollow (between Leichhardt Street and Gregory Terrace), and York's Hollow (to the north of Gregory Terrace - an area occupied by a number of brick-makers in the 1850s and 1860s, now Victoria Park).

A 3D surface is represented by an elevation function on a 2D grid along with non-spatial features found at each pixel. Surface segmentation involves categorizing adjacent pixels based on both these attributes and topological properties. This issue has various applications in hydrology, astronomy, and chemistry but presents significant challenges due to its unique characteristics. Firstly, the boundaries of class segments follow surface shapes and orientations in three-dimensional space rather than two-dimensional ones. Furthermore, the topological framework varies across different spatial scales depending on surface resolution. Traditional deep learning algorithms primarily using convolutional and pooling layers struggle because they rely on detecting structured patterns in grids. To address this, we suggest representing surface topology through a contour tree skeleton, a hierarchical polytree describing how surface boundaries evolve at varying elevations. Additionally, we design a graph-based neural network centered around this hierarchical structure to model surface topological aspects at diverse spatial scales. Our model's performance was evaluated on real-world data from hydrology, surpassing other benchmark methods' classification accuracy.

Ensure your ice cream bowl is completely frozen, having sat in the freezer for at least forty-eight hours. Chop the almonds into smaller pieces using a slatter, if available. Hayao Miyazaki's "Spirited Away" is a breathtakingly beautiful and emotionally resonant film that will transport you to a world of wonder and magic. The story follows a young girl named Chihiro who is swept away to a spirit world, where she must navigate a strange and often frightening landscape in order to find her way home.

The animation is stunning, with detailed and imaginative characters and environments that will leave you in awe. The film's use of color and light is particularly striking, with a palette that ranges from soft pastels to vibrant neons. The animation is also complemented by a beautiful soundtrack, which perfectly captures the mood and atmosphere of the film.

But "Spirited Away" is more than just a visually stunning film. It's also a deeply emotional and thought-provoking journey that explores themes of growth, identity, and self-discovery. Chihiro's journey is a transformative one, as she learns to navigate the challenges of the spirit world and confronts her own fears and insecurities. The film's characters are well-developed and relatable, and their interactions with Chihiro are both heartwarming and heart-wrenching.

One of the things that sets "Spirited Away" apart from other animated films is its ability to balance humor and darkness. The film has a great sense of humor, with plenty of laugh-out-loud moments that will entertain audiences of all ages. But it also has a darker, more mature side, exploring themes of loneliness, sacrifice, and the cost of growth and change.

Overall, "Spirited Away" is a timeless classic that will captivate audiences of all ages. It's a film that will transport you to another world, and leave you changed in ways you won't even realize. It's a must-see for anyone who loves animation, fantasy, or simply great storytelling. So sit back, relax, and let the magic of "Spirited Away" sweep you away.

"Breakfast with Buddha" tells the story of an ensemble group of characters whose lives become intertwined in unexpected ways through an encounter at a hotel breakfast buffet.

The protagonist is a successful businesswoman named Sarah, who has come to the city on a work-related visit and stays in a luxurious hotel. As she walks into the expansive breakfast room, filled with people eagerly dining and chatting, she feels lost and alone amidst her busy schedule.

Despite feeling out of place, Sarah befriends a few other guests, including a Buddhist monk, a struggling artist, and a lonely retiree. They strike up conversations over food and drinks, and soon discover their shared struggles and desires. Each character brings unique perspectives and stories to the table - from pursuing spiritual enlightenment, seeking fulfillment in life, grappling with loneliness, to dealing with personal demons.

Over the course of several meals together, Sarah learns valuable lessons about compassion, perspective, mindfulness, and living a purposeful life. She also finds herself confronted by past regrets and realizes the power of forgiving oneself. Ultimately, through these encounters with strangers turned friends, Sarah begins to see her own journey in a new light, and gains clarity on what matters most.

As the characters part ways, they reconnect on a deeper level and continue to inspire each other. The reader leaves with the impression that although they may have started off as strangers seated next to one another at breakfast, their paths are now forever changed - bound together by fate, friendship, and a chance meeting over coffee and a muffin.

The Ambedkar cartoon is an issue that rocked the Parliament of India on 11 May 2012. Both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha were adjourned on that day due to the ruckus created by the opposing parties. The issue was taken up by Thirumavalavan, an MP from the state of Tamil Nadu. He put the issue to parliament (Lok Sabha), but was at first denied permission to speak about it. He then showed a copy of the controversial cartoon that allegedly insulted the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.  In the cartoon, the former Prime Minister of India (Congress), Jawaharlal Nehru, holds a whip and along with Ambedkar is driving a snail, which represents the Indian Constitution. The Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes considered the cartoon to be insulting. The book it appeared in was published by NCERT under the guidance of the Ministry of Human Resources in 2006 under the UPA government headed by Sonia Gandhi (Indian National Congress). Later the HRD Minister Kapil Sibal apologised to the nation with regards to the cartoon. NCERT was also asked to remove the cartoon from their textbooks.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art
performance in many different 2D medical image analysis tasks. In clinical
practice, however, a large part of the medical imaging data available is in 3D.
This has motivated the development of 3D CNNs for volumetric image segmentation
in order to benefit from more spatial context. Due to GPU memory restrictions
caused by moving to fully 3D, state-of-the-art methods depend on
subvolume/patch processing and the size of the input patch is usually small,
limiting the incorporation of larger context information for a better
performance. In this paper, we propose a novel Holistic Decomposition
Convolution (HDC), for an effective and efficient semantic segmentation of
volumetric images. HDC consists of a periodic down-shuffling operation followed
by a conventional 3D convolution. HDC has the advantage of significantly
reducing the size of the data for sub-sequential processing while using all the
information available in the input irrespective of the down-shuffling factors.
Results obtained from comprehensive experiments conducted on hip T1 MR images
and intervertebral disc T2 MR images demonstrate the efficacy of the present
approach.

A seemingly down-on-his-luck writer named Geoffrey Tempest faces financial hardship, struggling to make ends meet, until he receives three unexpected letters that change his life forever. A wealthy acquaintance from Australia writes to recommend someone who can help him escape poverty; a lawyer informs him of an inheritance from a distant relative; and a mysterious aristocrat named Lucio introduces himself as a friend who will teach him how to handle his newfound riches. Despite warnings from others about Lucio's true nature, Tempest remains oblivious, believing his friend is genuinely kind. As his wealth brings him neither happiness nor fulfillment, he eventually discovers the horrifying truth about Lucio - the earthly embodiment of the Devil. With this revelation, Tempest chooses to reject evil and return to a simpler life without wealth, finding solace in the prospect of redeeming his soul. However, it is Lucio who holds the central place in the narrative, as the title and philosophical themes revolve around the eternal struggle of Satan for spiritual salvation, highlighting the paradox that despite being the embodiment of evil, Satan longs for the very thing he cannot attain.

I'm 25 and my dad is 50. He's a retired engineer and he's been struggling financially lately. He's been asking me to buy him groceries and other household items, but I've been refusing.

I've been living on my own for a few years now and I've been paying my own bills. I've been saving up for a down payment on a house and I don't want to spend my money on things that my dad could buy for himself.

Ismail bin Abdul Muttalib, born on December 1, 1954, is a Malaysian politician currently serving as Deputy Minister of Housing and Local Government within the Barisan Nasional (BN) government led by Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob and Minister Reezal Merican Naina Merican since August 2021. Prior to this, he held positions in the Perikatan Nasional (PN) administration under previous Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and Minister Zuraida Kamaruddin from March 2020 to August 2021. As a long-serving MP for Maran since March 2004, Ismail belongs to the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), part of the BN coalition closely associated with the PN alliance. He has been elected to parliament three times - in 2004, 2008, and 2018 - and after the 2013 general election, he became Deputy Minister of Human Resources under former PM Najib Razak and Minister Richard Riot Jaem until May 2018.

Kennekuk, also known as the 'Kickapoo Prophet', was a prominent figure in the Vermilion band of the Kickapoo nation around the late 18th century, residing primarily in East Central Illinois alongside the Vermilion River. Translated to mean'son of the drunkard', his early life involved violence when, at a younger age, he brutally murdered his uncle in a drunken rage, prompting him to be shunned by his tribe. He spent years wandering through Indiana and Illinois seeking sustenance before being taken under the wing of a Catholic priest who taught him about Christianity. Inspired by this newfound faith, Kennekuk resolved to abandon his drinking habits and started spreading the message, ultimately persuading many of his peers to follow suit. By the time he reached his mid-20s in 1816, he had risen to become a respected leader within the Vermilion band, marking a significant shift towards reduced alcohol consumption and increased cohesion within his community. Over the course of nearly two decades, Kennekuk led a devoted community centered on non-violence, peaceful resistance against forced relocation, sobriety, and contemplative practices. Embracing moderation and peaceful coexistence with expanding American territory, his views earned him both admiration and ridicule from rival Kickapoo factions. A unique blend of Christian evangelism and indigenous spirituality attracted a small but dedicated group of Potawatomi followers who eventually joined his cause. Kennekuk passed away on the reservation in Kansas in 1852, leaving behind a lasting legacy as a champion of peace and tranquility.

Following the Restoration, the Countess of Derby, who had endured a lengthy imprisonment due to treachery by the Roundheads, took refuge at Martindale Castle, where Bridgenorth could have apprehended her for orchestrating the execution of his brother-in-law, William Christian, had not the knight intervened by destroying the warrant and escorted her back to the Isle of Man. As a result, Alice was removed from her stepmother's care, and it was assumed the major had fled to New England. Upon arriving at Martindale Castle, he discovered his father and mother in the custody of the Roundheads.

Many sports professionals on the bidding team were perplexed by my decision, including bid chairman Lord Coe, who claimed he could never imagine participating in a marathon despite being an accomplished middle-distance runner. Others, such as hurdler Kelly Holmes, coach Alan Pascoe, and sprinter-turned-IOC-member Frankie Fredericks, questioned my motivations, expecting that experienced athletes like themselves wouldn't find running long distances particularly challenging. However, wheelchair athlete Tanni Grey-Thompson, a six-time London Marathon winner, expressed support for my endeavor. Throughout the busy week, entertaining the IOC's Evaluation Commission, I discovered that having a structured running schedule was more manageable than I anticipated. While I often struggle to stay focused at home, the pressure of our presentations kept me grounded in London, where I found solace in running. On Wednesday, I fit in a 45-minute jog after the late-night presentations. The next morning, we visited various Olympic venues around the city, leaving me exhausted, but I quickly resumed my routine upon returning to the hotel. Characterising tractable fragments of the constraint satisfaction problem
(CSP) is an important challenge in theoretical computer science and artificial
intelligence. Forbidding patterns (generic sub-instances) provides a means of
defining CSP fragments which are neither exclusively language-based nor
exclusively structure-based. It is known that the class of binary CSP instances
in which the broken-triangle pattern (BTP) does not occur, a class which
includes all tree-structured instances, are decided by arc consistency (AC), a
ubiquitous reduction operation in constraint solvers. We provide a
characterisation of simple partially-ordered forbidden patterns which have this
AC-solvability property. It turns out that BTP is just one of five such
AC-solvable patterns. The four other patterns allow us to exhibit new tractable
classes.

Last night, I went to this concert in a downtown venue I’d never heard of before. The hall was designed in a unique touch of modern aesthetics mixed with a Victorian-era vibe. The lighting was extraordinarily meticulous, painting the atmosphere with soothing hues of reds, blues, and purples. It was as if I had walked into a dream. 

The band was mesmerizing. They played ethereal music that imbued the air with a dreamy, otherworldly quality. I can barely describe it. It was all very symphonic indie rock, but with a touch of electronic, and even some jazz elements. It was unmatchably beautiful, as though the musical notes transformed into wisps of pure magic as they escaped the instruments.

A feeling of shared camaraderie emanated throughout the hall. It seemed like everyone was moving to the melody in unison, a serene sway with eyes closed and smiles bright. Not a single soul in the audience was detached from the collective rhythm. It was like we were all connected, as if a string tied us together, resonating with the pitch-perfect harmony echoing around us.

What struck me was how the music made us feel. The euphoric undertones, the rich, melancholic interludes, the building crescendos and delicate decrescendos— each one eliciting absolute, raw emotion. It felt like the music was alive, breathing and intertwining with our souls. It wasn't just a concert, it felt like an understanding, a communal solidarity, an expression of humanity.

When the last note petered into silence, a moment of stillness stretched through the crowd, as though their collective breaths were held in reverence. It was only then that the reality of the shared experience sank in. Everyone began to cheer, and it felt like happiness was bouncing off the walls.

It was surreal, it was profound, it was life-altering. The healing power of music coupled with the restoration found within community was something I’d read about but truly experienced it for the first time last night. It was the most genuine and powerful collision of sensations, emotions, and human connection I have ever felt. It was… the best.

Just wanted to share this experience with you guys, because sometimes life gives you moments you can't keep it to yourself. Let me know if you've had any similar experiences! Would love to hear all about them!

Biomedical imaging for tumor detection is a labor-intensive task prone to inaccuracies. To address this issue, researchers have been developing algorithms utilizing diverse mathematical approaches like statistical modeling, variational methods, and machine learning. This study proposes an automated liver segmentation technique from 2D CT scans into categories signifying normal, blood vessels, or cancerous tissue using graph cuts. Initially, a unique feature vector is created for every pixel incorporating 59 intensity values within the time-series data. A simplified boundary cost term is introduced within the energy function to enhance computation efficiency. Data normalization and adjusted perimeter terms expedite the graph-cut process without relying on optimizing the scaling factor λ. Instead of extensive training, pre-defined tissue types are calculated based on regions identified by radiologist experts. Notably, this approach offers computational simplicity. Results were compared to the actual outcomes on a clinical dataset comprising ten cases, yielding segmentations with a DSC of.77 and VOE of 36.7%, averaging approximately one minute and twenty-five seconds per slice.

1 1/2 cups warm water
1 teaspoon yeast

2 tablespoons sugar

In a large bowl, combine water, yeast, sugar, and salt. Let sit five to ten minutes. Stir in the first cup and a half of flour with a heavy spoon. Add the rest of the flour a little at a time as needed, stirring until dough becomes too stiff to continue stirring easily. Next, add a little more flour and begin kneading. Keep adding flour and kneading until the dough is smooth and elastic ( It doesn't need a lot more flour, just enough so that it's not sticking to the pastry board). Let dough rise in a greased bowl covered with a damp, clean kitchen towel until doubled. (Usually, about thirty minutes to an hour.). Uncover bowl, sprinkle in a little more flour and knead again. With floured hands, shape dough into a ball and place in a greased 3 1/2-quart crock pot. Turn the crock pot on High. (The bread will rise as the crock pot heats up.). Keep the lid just barely off the pot to keep steam from building up and making your crusty soggy. (Try using a toothpick to keep the lid open just a bit). Cook it for one hour on the first side. New rules on marriage for foreign nationals living in the UK are coming into force.
From Tuesday, most non-EU citizens will need Home Office approval to marry. The Home Office says the new rules are aimed at reducing the number of sham marriages, of which there are estimated to be up to 15,000 a year. But immigrants' group the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants (JCWI) says the rules breach human rights law and it may mount a legal challenge. When the changes were unveiled last year, immigration minister Des Browne said: "Our aim is to avoid unnecessary disruption of genuine marriages, while providing firm controls to prevent abuse." Under the previous regulations anybody wishing to get married in the UK only had to produce evidence they had been resident in the country for a week and give 15 days notice of the wedding at the local register office.
But from Tuesday all non-EU nationals, apart from citizens of Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Iceland or Norway, intending to wed in the UK must either obtain a visa allowing them to get married before they enter the country or apply for a Home Office 'certificate of marriage approval'. To get a certificate, costing £135, applicants will have to send proof that they have a legal right to be in the UK. Those without a settled status, such as asylum seekers awaiting a decision on their application, will have no right to marry in the UK.
Once they have the necessary documentation, those subject to immigration controls wishing to get married in England or Wales must register their intention to marry at one of 76 specially-designated register offices. They can, however, marry at the register office or church of their choice. Rhian Beynon of the JCWI said the new rules were "not proportionate" and "discriminatory".
"These rules means in some cases the Home Secretary is going to be a marriage registrar of last resort. "We're currently taking a legal opinion on this. We'll be looking for people whose right to marry is breached and we'll be looking at taking a case on this to the Human Rights Court," Ms Beynon said. The new rules have also been called into question by the parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights. In a report published last July the cross-party committee stated there was a "significant risk" the new procedures were incompatible with the right to marry because they introduced restrictions which were "disproportionate". The committee believed the new laws might be incompatible with the Human Rights Act on the grounds of religion, belief and nationality, the report added.
Over the last year immigration service operations against marriages of convenience have been stepped up resulting in a growing number of convictions. In January 25 people who took part in a sham marriage network based in Leicester were jailed for a total of 35 years. And last November Samuel Amoah, a Belgian national who set up two sham weddings for couples who wanted to remain in the UK, was jailed for three years. Several other cases are currently going through the courts. The role of registrars who under the Asylum and Immigration Act 1999 were obliged to report suspected sham marriages to the Home Office, has been key in many prosecutions. Registrars' spokesman, Mark Rimmer, said they welcomed the new marriage regulations and believed they would be an significant deterrent. "They will effectively remove most of the blatant cases. Certainly those who are illegals in this country, of which we had quite a few, will no longer be getting married," Mr Rimmer said. Mr Rimmer, the service director for registrations of marriages at Brent Council in north-west London, said he did not consider the new law to be an infringement of civil liberties. "It may be seen to be far more draconian than it has been but certainly it's still not as difficult to marry in the UK than it is to marry, for example, in Holland, Germany or France. "I think it's a proportionate response by government to what was a very large problem," Mr Rimmer said.

Ingredients:

* 1 package of puff pastry, thawed
* 2-3 apples, peeled and sliced
* 1/4 cup brown sugar
* 2 tbsp granulated sugar
* 1 tsp cinnamon
* 1/4 cup raisins
* 1/4 cup chopped walnuts (optional)
* 1 egg, beaten (for brushing pastry)
* Powdered sugar, for dusting

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix together the brown sugar, granulated sugar, and cinnamon.
3. Add the sliced apples to the bowl and toss until they are evenly coated with the sugar mixture.
4. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
5. Spoon the apple mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
6. Sprinkle the raisins and chopped walnuts (if using) over the top of the apple mixture.
7. Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling, pressing the edges to seal. Use a fork to crimp the edges and create a decorative pattern.
8. Brush the top of the strudel with the beaten egg and cut a few small slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
9. Place the strudel on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
10. Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm. Enjoy!

Note: You can also add a drizzle of honey or maple syrup over the top of the strudel before baking for an extra touch of sweetness.

The soaring cost of oil has hit global economic growth, although world's major economies should weather the storm of price rises, according to the OECD.
In its latest bi-annual report, the OECD cut its growth predictions for the world's main industrialised regions. US growth would reach 4.4% in 2004, but fall to 3.3% next year from a previous estimate of 3.7%, the OECD said. However, the Paris-based economics think tank said it believed the global economy could still regain momentum.
Forecasts for Japanese growth were also scaled back to 4.0% from 4.4% this year and 2.1% from 2.8% in 2005. But the outlook was worst for the 12-member eurozone bloc, with already sluggish growth forecasts slipping to 1.8% from 2.0% this year and 1.9% from 2.4% in 2005, the OECD said. Overall, the report forecast total growth of 3.6% in 2004 for the 30 member countries of the OECD, slipping to 2.9% next year before recovering to 3.1% in 2006. "There are nonetheless good reasons to believe that despite recent oil price turbulence the world economy will regain momentum in a not-too-distant future," said Jean-Philippe Cotis, the OECD's chief economist. The price of crude is about 50% higher than it was at the start of 2004, but down on the record high of $55.67 set in late October.
A dip in oil prices and improving jobs prospects would improve consumer confidence and spending, the OECD said. "The oil shock is not enormous by historical standards - we have seen worse in the seventies. If the oil price does not rise any further, then we think the shock can be absorbed within the next few quarters," Vincent Koen, a senior economist with the OECD, told the BBC's World Business Report. "The recovery that was underway, and has been interrupted a bit by the oil shock this year, would then regain momentum in the course of 2005." China's booming economy and a "spectacular comeback" in Japan - albeit one that has faltered in recent months - would help world economic recovery, the OECD said. "Supported by strong balance sheets and high profits, the recovery of business investment should continue in North America and start in earnest in Europe," it added. However, the report warned: "It remains to be seen whether continental Europe will play a strong supportive role through a marked upswing of final domestic demand." The OECD highlighted current depressed household expenditure in Germany and the eurozone's over-reliance on export-led growth.

1/2 cup celery leaves
1 clove garlic, peeled and gently crushed
Coarse sea salt
12 ounces vodka

2 ounces freshly squeezed lemon juice
1 ounce freshly squeezed lime juice
3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
2 teaspoons hot sauce, or to taste

freshly ground black pepper
The Garnish Bar

The controversial posters show rotting teeth, cancerous lungs and amputated limbs in an effort to discourage smokers from lighting up. Critics have argued that they are too gruesome but Mr Milburn insists that tough measures are needed to reduce Britain's high smoking rates.
"We know these images can be disturbing," he said, "but we also know that sometimes it takes something shocking to make people take notice."
According to government figures, around 80% of lung cancer cases and 90% of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) cases could be prevented if everyone quit smoking. The new ad campaign forms part of a £20 million initiative aimed at encouraging more people to give up cigarettes.
Mr Milburn acknowledged that some individuals may find the imagery offensive but stressed that ultimately the aim was to save lives. "I understand why some people might think this approach goes too far," he added, "But when you consider what smoking does to your health – and worse still, the impact on those closest to you - I believe there is no such thing as going too far when it comes to protecting people's wellbeing."

Deep learning has achieved impressive results in biomedical image segmentation, but a significant issue arises when deploying models trained on one dataset to unseen data with distinct features, known as the domain shift problem. This gap can severely impact model performance. To tackle this challenge, we introduce a novel unsupervised domain adaptation framework designed to generalize models from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain for cross-modality biomedical image segmentation. Our approach consists of two crucial components: a conditional domain discriminator (CDD), inspired by conditional domain adversarial networks used in classification tasks, and a category-centric prototype aligner (CCPA), built upon the graph-induced prototype alignment mechanism from cross-domain object detection. The CDD excels at handling complex cross-modality biomedical images, while the CCPA leverages detailed instance-level features through its sophisticated prototype representation. Furthermore, it addresses class imbalance issues through an entropy-based loss function. Experimental results on a widely-used benchmark for cardiac substructure segmentation showcase the substantial improvement our method achieves on the target domain.

Along the way, they cross paths with two other fugitives, Aravis, a high-ranking Calormene noblewoman, and her intelligent horse, Hwin. Aravis seeks refuge in Narnia after being pursued by the Tisroc's stern advisor, determined to force her into marriage. The quartet navigates the vibrant city of Tashbaan, encountering a royal procession of Narnian dignitaries who mistakenly identify Shasta as the long-lost Prince Corin of Archenland, a prince who had gone missing earlier in the day. Aravis reunites with Shasta and the horses outside Tashbaan, and together they embark on a treacherous journey across the unforgiving desert landscape. Their path crosses with a fearsome lion – later revealed to be Aslan – who sends a chilling warning to the travelers.

As Hilde's siblings vanish during a treacherous storm, Peer and Hilde embark on a perilous journey through the mountain's labyrinthine tunnels to rescue them. During a pivotal moment, as the troll king lifts the mountain onto four crimson pillars at a grand feast, Peer faces an impossible choice: flee alone or remain eternally beneath the mountain with Hilde. Upon Ralf's return from his odyssey, accompanied by his crew and neighbors, they stage a daring raid on the troll banquet hall, precipitating a tense standoff. To prepare this dish, start by preheating your oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray and brush two large flour tortillas on both sides with canola oil, cutting them into thin strips that measure 1/4 inch by 3 inches. Season these strips with a pinch of salt and sesame seeds, then lay them flat on the baking sheet and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping them halfway through, until crispy and lightly browned. While the tortilla strips are toasting, season 5.5 pounds of fresh tuna with the remaining salt, black pepper, and cumin. In a separate pan coated with cooking spray, sear the tuna over medium-high heat for approximately three minutes per side, or until it reaches your preferred level of doneness. Once done, let it rest for 2 to 3 minutes before slicing it thinly against the grain. In another bowl, mix together shredded low-fat cheddar cheese, nonfat yogurt, and freshly squeezed lime juice. Combine the sliced tuna with a bed of mixed greens, strips of roasted bell peppers, and the cheesy dressing. Finally, divide the salad among four dinner plates and top each plate with the toasted tortilla strips, or you can also toss the croutons into the salad right before serving.

Ismail bin Abdul Muttalib (Jawi: اسماعيل بن عبدالموتطالب; born 1 December 1954) is a Malaysian politician who has served as the Deputy Minister of Housing and Local Government for the second term in the Barisan Nasional (BN) administration under Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob and Minister Reezal Merican Naina Merican since August 2021. He served his first term in the Perikatan Nasional (PN) administration under former Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and former Minister Zuraida Kamaruddin from March 2020 to August 2021 and the Member of Parliament (MP) for Maran since March 2004. He is a member of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), a component party of the Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition which is aligned with the PN coalition.  Ismail was elected to Parliament in the 2004 general election and was re-elected thrice in 2008 general election, 2013 general election and 2018 general election.  After the 2013 Malaysian general election, he was appointed to serve as the Deputy Minister of Human Resources in the BN administration under former Prime Minister Najib Razak and former Minister Richard Riot Jaem from May 2013 to May 2018 for almost 5 years.

Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 medium beets, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 4 cups arugula, washed and dried
- 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 1/4 cup chopped walnuts
- 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion

For the blue cheese dressing:
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Toss the beets with olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
3. Spread the beets out on a baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
4. In a large bowl, combine the roasted beets, arugula, blue cheese, walnuts, and red onion.
5. To make the blue cheese dressing, whisk together mayonnaise, blue cheese, apple cider vinegar, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until smooth.
6. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy your delicious and healthy Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing!

Incorporating multi-scale features in fully convolutional neural networks
(FCNs) has been a key element to achieving state-of-the-art performance on
semantic image segmentation. One common way to extract multi-scale features is
to feed multiple resized input images to a shared deep network and then merge
the resulting features for pixelwise classification. In this work, we propose
an attention mechanism that learns to softly weight the multi-scale features at
each pixel location. We adapt a state-of-the-art semantic image segmentation
model, which we jointly train with multi-scale input images and the attention
model. The proposed attention model not only outperforms average- and
max-pooling, but allows us to diagnostically visualize the importance of
features at different positions and scales. Moreover, we show that adding extra
supervision to the output at each scale is essential to achieving excellent
performance when merging multi-scale features. We demonstrate the effectiveness
of our model with extensive experiments on three challenging datasets,
including PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012 and a subset of MS-COCO 2014.

Nasdaq, the influential technology-focused stock index, is set to issue shares to the general public through a fundraising effort valued at approximately $100 million (around £52 million). This move is viewed by some as a significant step towards achieving a full public listing, contrary to recent statements from the company. Initially, Nasdaq explored initial public offerings in 2000 and 2001 through private placements before making a limited debut in 2002 on the Over-the-Counter Bulletin Board, a platform for infrequently traded securities. All ye good people, afar and near,
To my request pray lend an ear;
I advise you all without delay to go
And see the Fair Maid's House - it is a rare show.
Some of the chairs there are very grand,
They have been cut and carved by a skilful hand;
And kings, perchance, if fhe truth were told,
Have sat on them in days of old.
King James the First of Scotland was murdered there,
And his cries for mercy rent the air.
But the Highland robbers only laughed at him,
And murdered him in the dungeon and thought if no sin.
Then there's an ancient shrine upstairs,
Where the Monks and Saints said their prayers,
To the Holy Virgin, be it told;
And the house, it is said, is six hundred years old.
The old cruisie lamps are there to be seen,
Which let the monks see to write from their sheen,
Arld if the walls could speak, they could tell a fearful tale,
Which would make the people's cheeks turn pale.
Then there's an old claymore dug up from Culloden Moor,
Which in its time shed innocent blood, I am sure,
If not at Culloden Moor, some other place,
Which no doubt the truth of it history might trace.
The interior of the house is magnificent to be seen,
And the wood panelling, I'm sure, would please the Queen;
And the old fire-place, with its big fire,
Is all that visitors could desire.
Then there's a ring in a big stone near by the door,
Where gentlemen tethered their horses in days of yore;
And on the staircase door there's a firling pin
For making a rattling noise when anyone wanted in.
The mistress of the house is very kind,
A more affable woman would be herd to find;
And to visitors she is very good,
And well versed in history, be it understood.
