In October 1946, Popper, then at the London School of Economics, delivered a paper titled "Are There Philosophical Problems?" at a gathering of the Moral Sciences Club, moderated by Wittgenstein. Their debate became increasingly intense as they disagreed on the existence of fundamental philosophical issues versus mere linguistic conundrums, with Wittgenstein taking the latter stance. As their argument escalated, Wittgenstein employed a fireplace poker to drive home his points, using gestures that intensified the tension. When challenged by Popper to provide an example of a moral rule, Popper responded with "Not to threaten visiting lecturers with pokers," prompting Wittgenstein to slam down the poker and storm out of the room. Wittgenstein's Poker examines the accounts of this confrontation, as well as the backgrounds and careers of Popper, Wittgenstein, and Bertrand Russell, who were all present at the meeting. This book weaves together three narratives: one documenting the actual events of the 1946 encounter and the controversy surrounding different observer accounts; another provides a comparative biography of the philosophers, highlighting their Viennese roots and distinct paths to fame; and a third explores the philosophical implications of their disagreement and its connection to pivotal debates in early 20th-century philosophy regarding the nature of language.

Structured boosting is a technique that involves training a highly accurate model by combining multiple less accurate, yet specialized learners. Building upon the concept of structured support vector machines, this approach draws inspiration from these methods, giving rise to a novel algorithm called StructuredBoost. Unlike traditional boosting techniques, StructBoost enables nonlinear structured learning through the integration of multiple weak structured learners. This framework broadens the applicability of boosted models, encompassing established algorithms like AdaBoost and LPBoost. Notably, the optimization problem posed by StructBoost presents a significant challenge due to its potentially vast number of variables and constraints. In contrast, structured support vector machines typically feature a large number of constraints, and cutting-plane methods are commonly employed to address this issue. To overcome these complexities, we reformulate StructBoost as a 1-slack optimization problem and leverage a combination of cutting planes and column generation to efficiently tackle the optimization task. Our approach is demonstrated through various applications, including tree loss minimization for hierarchical multi-class classification, robust visual tracking via the Pascal overlap criterion, and conditional random field parameter estimation for image segmentation.

John Samuel Rowell (1837-1915) was a Canadian businessman and politician.

Rowell was born in Fredericton, New Brunswick, the son of John Rowell and Jane Ann McLean. He was educated in Fredericton and at the University of New Brunswick. In 1856, he went to Saint John, New Brunswick, where he was employed as a clerk in a hardware store. He later became a partner in the firm. In 1868, he married Elizabeth Ann McLean. Rowell served as mayor of Saint John from 1874 to 1875. He was also a director of the New Brunswick Railway and the Saint John Harbour Commission. He was elected to the House of Commons of Canada for the riding of Saint John City in an 1878 by-election, and was reelected in 1882 and 1887. A Liberal, he served as Postmaster General from 1887 to 1888. He was defeated in the 1888 election. Rowell died in Saint John in 1915.

The trial of Bernie Ebbers, former chief executive of bankrupt US phone company WorldCom, has started in New York with the selection of the jury.
Mr Ebbers, 63, is accused of being the mastermind behind an $11bn (£6bn) accounting fraud that eventually saw the firm collapse in July 2002. His indictment includes charges of securities fraud, conspiracy and filing false reports with regulators. If found guilty, Mr Ebbers could face a substantial jail sentence. He has firmly declared his innocence.
Under Mr Ebbers' leadership, WorldCom emerged from Mississippi obscurity to become a $160bn telecoms giant and the darling of late 1990s investors. Yet as competition intensified and the telecoms boom petered out, WorldCom found itself under growing financial stress. When WorldCom finally collapsed, shareholders lost about $180bn and 20,000 workers lost their jobs. Mr Ebbers' trial, which is expected to last two months, is the latest in a series of attempts by US prosecutors to pursue senior executives for fraud. It will coincide with the retrial of former Tyco International chief Dennis Kozlowski and his top lieutenant, accused of looting the industrial conglomerate to the tune of $600m. Trail preparations are also preparing for former executives of shamed US energy firm Enron.

The owners of embattled Russian oil giant Yukos are to ask the buyer of its former production unit to pay back a $900m (£479m) loan.
State-owned Rosneft bought the Yugansk unit for $9.3bn in a sale forced by Russia to part settle a $27.5bn tax claim against Yukos. Yukos' owner Menatep Group says it will ask Rosneft to repay a loan that Yugansk had secured on its assets. Rosneft already faces a similar $540m repayment demand from foreign banks. Legal experts said Rosneft's purchase of Yugansk would include such obligations. "The pledged assets are with Rosneft, so it will have to pay real money to the creditors to avoid seizure of Yugansk assets," said Moscow-based US lawyer Jamie Firestone, who is not connected to the case. Menatep Group's managing director Tim Osborne told the Reuters news agency: "If they default, we will fight them where the rule of law exists under the international arbitration clauses of the credit."
Rosneft officials were unavailable for comment. But the company has said it intends to take action against Menatep to recover some of the tax claims and debts owed by Yugansk. Yukos had filed for bankruptcy protection in a US court in an attempt to prevent the forced sale of its main production arm. The sale went ahead in December and Yugansk was sold to a little-known shell company which in turn was bought by Rosneft. Yukos claims its downfall was punishment for the political ambitions of its founder Mikhail Khodorkovsky and has vowed to sue any participant in the sale.

1 pint strawberry
1 (12 ounce) bag chocolate chips
8 ounces cream cheese
1 tablespoon powdered sugar
1 tablespoon milk
sliced almonds (optional)
Wash the strawberries. Then, slice the bottom point off the strawberry, so that it can stand up straight. Next, pluck the stem off. Using a paring knife or strawberry huller, scoop out the top to make room for the cheesecake. This is the most important step...dry off the strawberries individually with paper towels. If the strawberries are wet, the chocolate will not stick. Melt the chocolate in a double broiler or microwave. (Note: if using a microwave, only melt it in 20-second increments to make sure it doesn't burn). I use Ghirardelli 60% Cacao Bittersweet Chocolate Chips. Line a cookie sheet (that will fit in your freezer) with waxed paper or a Silpat. Dip the bottom half of each strawberry into the melted chocolate and place on the lined pan. Once the pan is full, place it in the freezer for about 5 minutes or until the chocolate has hardened. While the chocolate is cooling, make the cheesecake filling. In a small bowl, beat together the cream cheese, powdered sugar and milk, until smooth. If it seems too thick, add a splash more milk. Spoon the cheesecake mixture into a piping bag with a star tip. If you don't have a piping bag, scoop it into a large Ziploc bag and snip off the corner. Remove the strawberries from the freezer and pipe in the cheesecake filling. Top with a slivered almond and serve or refrigerate until ready to serve.

Recent advancements in multimedia technologies have raised concerns about identifying visually salient regions in image processing. The proliferation of terminals in diverse multimedia environments presents ample opportunities for enhancing image visualization. Feature-based image extraction has emerged as a prominent method in image processing. The primary goal of image segmentation is to divide an image into distinct, homogeneous regions, characterized by specific properties like grayscale, texture, or color. This process serves as the initial and crucial step in object recognition, scene comprehension, and image analysis. Applications of image segmentation span various fields, including mobile devices, quality control, medical equipment, robotics, geophysical surveys, and military operations. Ultimately, the quality of the final outcome heavily relies on the effectiveness of preprocessing. Typically, obtaining clean, high-quality preprocessing data demands extensive computational resources and mathematical computations. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel feature-based fuzzy rule-guided technique that operates independently of external input. Experimental results indicate that this approach outperforms existing methods, as demonstrated through evaluations using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) metrics.

Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered weak and weary,  
Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore—    
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,   
As of someone gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door—. 
"'Tis some visitor," I muttered, "'tapper at my window lent;     
Only this and nothing more." 

Ah distinctly I remember it was in the bleak December;      
And each separate dying ember writhed upon the floor.   
Eagerly I wished the morrow ; - vainly had I sought to borrow       
From my books surcease of sorrow — sadness measured out her hours         
 
To an early grave or two removed from all human dwellings          
 
 But little thought they stumbling over me that ever again           

 Would be masterless their chosen dwelling place forlorn        


 As dreaming on things happy long past far off voices seem            

 
 To whisper unto one another low sounds like distant thunder                



 While I struggled through decades dark as dreams where hope is never born               




 Suddenly there burst into bloom before mine eyes once more

In his malodorous brain what slugs and mire,
Lanthorned in his oblique eyes, guttering burned!
His body lodged a rat where men nursed souls.
The world flashed grape-green eyes of a foiled cat
To him. On fragments of an old shrunk power,
On shy and maimed, on women wrung awry,
He lay, a bullying hulk, to crush them more.
But when one, fearless, turned and clawed like bronze,
Cringing was easy to blunt these stern paws,
And he would weigh the heavier on those after.
Who rests in God's mean flattery now? Your wealth
Is but his cunning to make death more hard.
Your iron sinews take more pain in breaking.
And he has made the market for your beauty
Too poor to buy, although you die to sell.
Only that he has never heard of sleep;
And when the cats come out the rats are sly.
Here we are safe till he slinks in at dawn
But he has gnawed a fibre from strange roots,
And in the morning some pale wonder ceases.
Things are not strange and strange things are forgetful.
Ah! if the day were arid, somehow lost
Out of us, but it is as hair of us,
And only in the hush no wind stirs it.
And in the light vague trouble lifts and breathes,
And restlessness still shadows the lost ways.
The fingers shut on voices that pass through,
Where blind farewells are taken easily ....
Ah! this miasma of a rotting God!

John D. Goldman is a prominent businessman and philanthropist based in San Francisco, California. Born on August 18, 1949, he belongs to the influential Haas family through his mother. Family Background
Goldman was born into a Jewish household in San Francisco on August 18, 1949, to Rhoda (née Haas) and Richard Goldman. As the second of four children, he had siblings Richard Goldman, who passed away in 1989, Douglas E. Goldman, and Susan R. Gelman. His maternal grandfather, Walter A. Haas, was the former president and chair of Levi Strauss & Co., while his paternal great-grandfather, Abraham Haas, co-founded Hellman-Haas Grocery, later becoming Smart & Final. The family's history also includes Simon Koshland, a major wool merchant in the US. Raised in San Francisco's Presidio Heights neighborhood, he attended Lick-Wilmerding High School before graduating from Swarthmore College and earning an MBA from Stanford University in 1975. Post-graduation, he worked in the California Legislative Analyst's office. In 1978, he joined the administration of Governor Jerry Brown as the assistant secretary of transportation. In 1981, he attempted to launch a chain of children's clothing stores called Jamboree, but it ultimately failed. In 1986, he partnered with his father to join Richard N. Goldman and Company, now known as Goldman Insurance Services, which his father founded. By 1991, he took over as president, and the company was sold by the family in 2002. Following his mother's passing in 1998, he oversaw the Richard and Rhoda Goldman Fund as a trustee.

6 tsp baking pwdr
4 1/2 c. flour
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. In an electric mixer, or possibly with a wire whisk, beat Large eggs, sugar, oil, and anise till well blended. On low speed, gradually fold in baking pwdr and 3 c. of flour. Turn out dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead in the additional 1 1/2 c. flour to make a soft dough. The dough should be soft but not sticky. Dust with flour if dough is too sticky to handle. Divide the dough into four equal pcs and roll each piece to create a 12-inch-long loaf. Place on a parchment-lined cookie sheet, spacing loaves 3 inches apart. Bake 20 to 25 min, or possibly till golden. Remove cookie sheet from the oven. Using two metal spatulas, carefully lift the loaves off the cookie sheet and onto a wire cooling rack. Cold. Place cooled loaves on a cutting board. Using a large sharp knife, slice loaves diagonally into 1/2-inch-wide strips and place in a single layer on the cookie sheet. Return to the oven for 12 to 15 min, or possibly till lightly browned. Remove cookie sheet from the oven. Cold toasted biscotti on a wire cooling rack. Store in an airtight container. This recipe yields 48 cookies. Comments: Using anise extract or possibly oil produces a greater flavor than using the actual Anisette or possibly Sambuca liqueur. Yield: 48 cookies

The Endeavour Leadership Program, formerly Endeavour Scholarships and Fellowships, formerly Endeavour Awards, was an internationally competitive, merit-based scholarship programme that formed part of the Australian Government's $1.4 billion Australian initiative. Deep learning models require rich and varied representations to perform well.
This study focuses on leveraging privileged data to enhance these representations,
aiming to improve model generalization capabilities. A new type of neural network,
called Group Orthogonal Convolutional Neural Network (GoCNN), is proposed to
learn distinct representations within each layer by incorporating external information.
The approach is tested using image classification tasks, specifically when annotated image
segmentations serve as the privileged data during training. Experimental results show
that GoCNN demonstrates superior generalization skills on two popular benchmarks,
ImageNet and PASCAL VOC. Notably, on ImageNet, the proposed method outperforms
the ResNet-152 model by 1.2% in terms of accuracy, despite relying on only
10% of the training data, underscoring the potential benefits of utilizing existing
information to construct more effective deep models.

Bravura is insulted and wonders how the women put up with them. The next day Bravura asks Impedimenta about this, and tells her not to let her husband boss her around. Impedimenta then tells Vitalstatistix that since she is the chief's wife, she has as much power as he does. They both lose their tempers and Impedimenta hits Vitalstatistix. He then leaves the village, joining Cacofonix in the forest. Impedimenta is then made chief by majority vote (all the women vote for Impedimenta, but the men do not dare vote or even speak up against their wives). Meanwhile, Julius Caesar has another plan to take over the village of indomitable Gauls. His special agent for the task, Manlius Claphamomnibus, swears to bring the "secret weapon" over the ocean discreetly. Back at the village, the "woman dominance" has caught on to every family, basically destroying the village. Asterix, troubled by all of this from the start, is met by Bravura who tells him that if both of them settle down together they could become chiefs of the village. Asterix accuses her of coming to the village to do just that and loses his temper. Bravura picks Asterix up and kisses him, and Asterix hits her out of reflex, though he feels shame and regret immediately after. Asterix is brought before the new chief for breaking their laws by striking a woman, and is given temporary exile. Getafix objects to this, but Bravura argues with him, getting him angry and causing the druid to leave the village also. And not only does Obelix join them, but every other village man as well. The men actually have a good time in the forest, drinking beer and eating wild boar. Claphamomnibus's ship lands at Gaul, and he unleashes the secret weapon: female legionaries (strongly resembling amazons). Claphamomnibus's reasoning for the forming of this strange unit is that because of the Gaul warriors' code of chivalry, they cannot fight women and thus could be easily defeated. Asterix, while scouting the Romans, learns of the arrival of Claphamomnibus and his female legionnaries and is sent as an ambassador to warn the village women of the threat (they worriedly send clothes to their husbands via Asterix and Obelix, in case it gets cold at night in the forest). Bravura tries to meet the women as an ambassador, claiming that since they are all women, they are sisters. The Roman sentry pounds her and Claphamomnibus insults her. Asterix watches it all; he also sees her slapping Clapharmomnibus which gives the Gaul hero a new perspective about the lady bard. Asterix approaches Bravura with a plan to get rid of this new problem. Part of his plan is to have Cacofonix sing songs in the forest, causing it to rain and scaring off all animals such as rabbits and snakes (and in one scene even a dragon). This scares the female Roman scout parties, causing them to retreat many times. (Humorously Asterix' departure to talk to Bravura was misinterpreted by the men, who by their passed comments assumed he was proposing marriage.) The rest of the plan involves the women of the village setting up a mall with the latest styles and accessories from Lutetia, and thus when the Roman women arrive to attack the supposedly undefended village they immediately become absorbed in shopping. In the meantime, the men of the village take out the fortified camps filled with male legionaries; Obelix is even allowed to destroy one of the camps single-handedly, as acknowledgment that he has not been much involved with the storyline until that point. Finally, Cacofonix sings once again as the Roman women leave the village with their shopping, and the terrified women (along with the dragon) flee Gaul on their ship with Claphamomnibus left behind. The story ends with the Gauls in a good mood, and there seems to be a good mood in Rome as well, for Julius Caesar is the laughing stock of his nation for having had to hire women to defeat the Gauls, and, on top of this, it is again a failure. Bravura and Asterix settle their original angst and develop a regard for one other.

The middle-levels graph $M_k$ ($0<k\in\mathbb{Z}$) has a dihedral quotient
pseudograph $R_k$ whose vertices are the $k$-edge ordered trees $T$, each $T$
encoded as a $(2k+1)$-string $F(T)$ formed via $\rightarrow$DFS by: {\bf(i)}
($\leftarrow$BFS-assigned) Kierstead-Trotter lexical colors $0,\ldots,k$ for
the descending nodes; {\bf(ii)} asterisks $*$ for the $k$ ascending edges. Two
ways of corresponding a restricted-growth $k$-string $\alpha$ to each $T$
exist, namely one Stanley's way and a novel way that assigns $F(T)$ to $\alpha$
via nested substring-swaps. These swaps permit to sort $V(R_k)$ as an ordered
tree that allows a lexical visualization of $M_k$ as well as the Hamilton
cycles of $M_k$ constructed by P. Gregor, T. M\"utze and J. Nummenpalo.

Petrel Resources' stock plummeted over 50% after learning that they were excluded from an Iraqi oil contract worth $500 million. According to Reuters, Iraq's Oil Ministry has issued the first post-war oilfield contracts to a Canadian and a Turkish firm. As of 17:00 GMT, Petrel's shares dropped from 97p ($1.87) to 44p ($0.85). In response, Petrel stated that it had no confirmation or denial regarding the report from Iraqi authorities. Iraq aims to award contracts for three major projects, including the development of the Khurmala Dome and the Himrin fields. Everasia, a Turkish company, reportedly secured the contract for Khurmala, while IOG, a Canadian firm, was selected for the Himrin project. However, Ironhorse Oil and Gas denied being involved in the process. The successful bidders will construct new pipelines and gas processing facilities to increase production rates to 100,000 barrels per day, effectively raising overall output. The Suba-Luhais field contract remains pending as the Oil Ministry assesses bids. This deal would mark the first agreement between Iraq and a foreign oil company if approved by the cabinet. Iraq seeks to revive its oil production levels, aiming to double output by the end of the decade, which had previously reached the same levels during the 1980s prior to the Iran war.

Turner is a guest conductor and clinician in Canada, United States, and abroad. A Canadian, Turner completed her Bachelor of Music and Bachelor of Education degrees at Queen's University and her Master of Music in music education and conducting at the University of Victoria. Touring with her ensembles inspired her master's thesis on the musical and personal transformations that occur on tours, and her D.M.A. thesis at the Eastman School of Music centered on Dialogues and Entertainments by William Kraft. At Eastman, she was the recipient of the Eastman Graduate Teaching Award in conducting. She was nominated for the Canadian Prime Minister's Leadership in Teaching Award and received the National Leadership in Education Award (Readers Digest Foundation), the Excellence in Education Award (Ontario Secondary School Teachers Federation), and the Marion Drysdale Leadership Among Women Teachers Award (also from OSSTF).

The foundation sire of the Tennessee Walking Horse, Black Allan, was born in 1886 and passed away in 1910. This influential stallion was sired by Allendorf, who came from lines of Narragansett Pacer, Canadian Pacer, and Gaited Spanish Mustangs brought over from Texas. Initially intended for racing as a trotter, Black Allan displayed a preference for pacing and instead excelled in the lateral ambling gait known today as the running walk. Standing approximately five feet tall, he held registration number 7623 with the American Trotting Registry. After being recognized as a potential breeding stallion by the Tennessee Walking Horse Breeders' Association, which later became the Tennessee Walking Horse Breeders' and Exhibitors' Association, Black Allan had several owners before settling with James Brantley and Albert Dement. During his lifetime, Black Allan fathered 111 foals, including notable offspring like Roan Allen, Hunters Allen F-10, and Merry Legs F-4. His life came to an end on September 16, 1910, at the age of 29.

Richard Williams (born ca. 1971)  is a former American professional baseball executive and the former president of baseball operations of the Cincinnati Reds of Major League Baseball. Before his promotion, announced on December 27, 2016, he was the Reds' senior vice president and general manager. Williams is a graduate of the University of Virginia. He was an Echols Scholar at UVA, giving him priority to sign up for any class. He worked as an investment banker and from 2003–04 for the George W. Bush presidential re-election campaign.  He joined the Reds in 2006, upon their purchase by a group led by majority owner Robert Castellini, as director of baseball business operations. He later became vice president of baseball operations and then was named vp/assistant GM in November 2014. Twelve months later, he was promoted to general manager, working under Walt Jocketty, then president of baseball operations. Jocketty became an advisor to Castellini with Williams' December 2016 appointment.

Additive deformations of bialgebras in the sense of Wirth are deformations of
the multiplication map of the bialgebra fulfilling a compatibility condition
with the coalgebra structure and a continuity condition. Two problems
concerning additive deformations are considered. With a deformation theory a
cohomology theory should be developed. Here a variant of the Hochschild
cohomology is used. The main result in the first partad of this paper is the
characterization of the trivial deformations, i.e. deformations generated by a
coboundary. Starting with a Hopf algebra, one would expect the deformed
multiplications to have some analogue of the antipode, which we call deformed
antipodes. We prove, that deformed antipodes always exist, explore their
properties, give a formula to calculate them given the deformation and the
antipode of the original Hopf algebra and show in the cocommutative case, that
each deformation splits into a trivial part and into a part with constant
antipodes.

A former CIA operative forced back into action after being hunted by his former agency, reunites his old team for one final mission. This isn't a groundbreaking narrative, drawing inspiration from films like the Bourne series, The Expendables, and The Losers. As the fourth adaptation from a graphic novel this year, it's part of a pattern of movies centered around a team embarking on a perilous assignment and involving government agencies. Initially, skepticism arose due to similarities with previous works, but upon reviewing the cast, it became clear that 'RED' aims to be a comedic take. The ensemble features John McClane, God, Cyrus the Virus, and The Queen joining forces to carry out a mission with humor. Given the cast's dynamics, storytelling takes a backseat to entertainment value. 

Bruce Willis, known for his 'good guy having a bad day' persona, continues to deliver an engaging performance, this time infused with self-aware humor. He exudes confidence throughout the film, as if he's performed countless missions before. Scenes showing his adjustment to retirement, including aimless wandering around the house in his pajamas, are reminiscent of Carl Fredricksen's introduction in 'Up.' However, deeper characterization highlights his true nature, and it's enjoyable to watch him in action.

The rest of the cast, consisting mainly of actors unfamiliar with high-octane action sequences, makes for an interesting contrast. Helen Mirren's unexpected presence adds depth, particularly since her character appears to balance her flower-arranging demeanor with her inner life as a deadly hit-woman. Her casting helps mitigate the predictability associated with Bruce Willis's involvement. Despite some unpolished moments, the film's tone remains lighthearted and entertaining.

Liver lesion segmentation is a difficult yet critical task for medical image
analysis. Recently, deep learning based image segmentation methods have
achieved promising performance, which can be divided into three categories: 2D,
2.5D and 3D, based on the dimensionality of the models. However, 2.5D and 3D
methods can have very high complexity and 2D methods may not perform
satisfactorily. To obtain competitive performance with low complexity, in this
paper, we propose a Feature-fusion Encoder-Decoder Network (FED-Net) based 2D
segmentation model to tackle the challenging problem of liver lesion
segmentation from CT images. Our feature fusion method is based on the
attention mechanism, which fuses high-level features carrying semantic
information with low-level features having image details. Additionally, to
compensate for the information loss during the upsampling process, a dense
upsampling convolution and a residual convolutional structure are proposed. We
tested our method on the dataset of MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS)
Challenge and achieved competitive results compared with other state-of-the-art
methods.

I may be biased since it was my first Arkham game, but my feelings extend beyond that - these games hold a special place in my heart as the first to feature an M-rated storyline, which I think added depth to my gaming experience. The Arkham City narrative, combat, and overall design set the bar high for me. I find it puzzling why some fans claim Arkham Origins is superior; the gameplay mechanics remain consistent with Arkham City, and the story lacks the complexity and nuance that made Arkham Asylum so compelling. It's clear that Arkham Origins is not without its detractors, who unfairly dismiss the game, likely to encourage players to try it out. On the other hand, Knight is often overlooked, yet it surpasses Arkham Origins in many respects, making it a strong contender among the Arkham series.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates for the third time this year, following a two-day meeting that ends on Wednesday.
The move, which would mark the third interest rate increase this year, is expected to be announced later in the day.
The rate hike is seen as a sign of a strong US economy, with low unemployment and steady economic growth.
However, some experts have warned that rising interest rates could lead to a slowdown in housing sales and construction, which could eventually dampen economic growth.
Analysts also say that the Fed's tightening of monetary policy could lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, which could slow down spending and investment.
Despite these concerns, most economists expect the Fed to continue to gradually raise interest rates over the next few years as the economy continues to grow.

A leading European trading platform, Euronext, is planning to make a bid for the London Stock Exchange, according to recent UK media reports. Last week, the LSE turned down a £1.35 billion takeover proposal from its German counterpart Deutsche Boerse, citing that the offer severely undervalued the business. Euronext, created by the merger of exchanges in Brussels, Paris, and Amsterdam, is reportedly collaborating with three major investment banks on a potential offer. As the largest stock market in Europe, the LSE is a highly prized target, boasting over £1.4 trillion in listed assets. Euronext, which acquired the London-based options and futures exchange Liffe in 2001, already has a significant presence in London through its stake in Clearnet, the clearinghouse used for trades on the LSE. Euronext, which also operates an exchange in Lisbon, recently added UBS and ABN Amro as additional advisors and is working with Morgan Stanley. Despite the initial rejection of the Deutsche Boerse bid, Euronext's CEO Werner Seifert may revisit the proposal with an enhanced offer, having previously attempted to merge with the LSE in 2000. In response to the LSE's refusal, Deutsche Boerse stated that its proposal presented benefits and expressed hope to submit a cash bid. The LSE acknowledged that the initial bid was undervalued and noted that there was no guarantee that a deal could be successfully completed. However, the exchange remains open to further discussions. German magazine Der Spiegel reported that part of Seifert's negotiations with the LSE involved determining the location of the merged exchange's headquarters, with Seifert initially suggesting London as the site. Nevertheless, the mayor of Frankfurt expressed concern that such a relocation could result in job losses. Many analysts believe a merger between Euronext and the LSE would have far-reaching implications.

The streets of Chicago take on a serene quality when winter wraps them in a layer of snow, effectively erasing the city's past transgressions and giving it a fresh start. The gentle flakes settle upon the trees' delicate branches, caressing the air that carries the scent of Lake Michigan. I've never experienced such tranquility until I stepped onto the city's shores, breathing in the crisp lake air and exhaling it through the trees, feeling invigorated by the cold, damp snow. In those moments, my thoughts quieten, as if seeking forgiveness for my own errors. "Can you genuinely pardon your wrongdoings?" someone might query – but perhaps that's merely the voice of the lake, whispering words of solace. Sometimes, however, the snowy landscape appears worn and weary, as if bearing the weight of its towering neighbor, Chicago. It yearns for more snowfall, craving the chill to cling to tree trunks and freeze their limbs. If I were an unflawed branch, swaying gently in the gusts, I'd stretch towards the sky as the snow falls, growing stronger roots that taste the lake's icy waters. Yet, Chicago's relentless grip keeps me grounded, stifling my pursuit of perfection. What does true cleanliness entail? I fail to grasp the serenity of trees battered by Chicago's unyielding forces, which seem to celebrate the city's flaws, sparkling like stars on the lake's surface before the snow shrouds everything. Alas, to envision how much time has passed since the first snowfall – how can something so ancient remain untainted and dance through the wind sweeping in from the lake? Is it the tender touch of the thorny branches, trusting that there will be no further mistakes, leaving only these pristine landscapes amidst Chicago's chaotic sprawl? As the snow begins to fall, blanketing the trees once more, do I finally find redemption? Where have my transgressions gone? Chicago lies at peace alongside the lake, a testament to the beauty that can arise from embracing imperfection.

In recent days, I visited this site with bouquets of roses in hand,
Only to be confronted by a disembodied voice rising from beyond the grave.

I was given an option by my roommate: he would either a) pay the bills and have the place to himself or b) I could stay and we would split everything. Being a recent graduate, I didn’t have much choice but to stay and split or live in my car. I picked door B.

I figured I could save money and eventually buy a house. I was already spending half of what I made on rent, but I made the best of a bad situation by splitting the rent. I was “stuck” spending almost as much as I did when it was just me and my roommate, which made saving difficult, but I managed. 

I lived with this guy for 3 years. The living situation got progressively worse as time went on. Picking teeth out of the bathroom sink, roommates bringing dates or new “best friends” home for the weekend, etc. After 3 years, my patience was wearing thin. I had already started looking for a new living arrangement when COVID-19 hit. Here I am, living in my car. 

I’m fortunate enough to live in Southern California, so the weather allows me to live in my car most of the year. It’s not ideal, and as a 6’4” male, it’s quite cramped, but it beats paying rent. I’ve basically been forced into an extreme form of saving money. I’ve got a freshwater shower at my gym, so showering is cost-effective and easy. I use the laundry mats, so laundry is cheap. I do all my “home” cooking in my car with a single burner induction cooktop. 

I’m able to save almost 70% of my monthly income, allowing me to place a generous offer on a house. If it weren’t for this unexpected turn of events, I would probably still be splitting rent, and not able to buy a house for another 1–2 years, if not more. It can be done, but it requires a disciplined lifestyle that not many people are willing to adopt. After experiencing this “lifestyle”, I don’t think I could go back to paying rent without putting most of my paycheck towards savings.

3 sweet potatoes (about 1 pound each)
3/4 cup low fat cottage cheese
3/4 cup fuji apple, diced (skin on)
3 tablespoons chives, fresh, chopped
1 ounce parmesan cheese, grated
1 ounce parmesan cheese, shaved
1/4 teaspoon coarse salt
fresh ground pepper, to taste
oil, for the baking pan
1 tablespoon walnut oil
1 ounce walnuts, toasted, chopped
Preheat oven to 375. Wrap 1 sweet potato in parchment, and then in foil. Pierce several times with a fork. Bake until tender, about 1 hour. Let cool. Reduce oven temperature to 350. Meanwhile, peel remaining sweet potatoes. Using a mandoline or a chef's knife, cut potatoes lengthwise into very thin slices until you have 30 slices. Trim each to a 2-by-4-inch rectangle. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add half the sweet potato slices, and cook until tender, about 2 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, place slices on a baking sheet to cool slightly. Repeat. Remove peel from baked sweet potato, and puree flesh in a food processor until smooth. Add cottage cheese, and puree until smooth. Transfer potato-cheese mixture to a large bowl. Stir in apple, chives, grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Coat a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with oil. Place 1 heaping tablespoon filling in center of a sweet potato slice, and roll up. Place, seam side down, in dish. Repeat. (Cannelloni can be refrigerated, covered, overnight; bring to room temperature before baking.) Brush oil over cannelloni. Bake until heated through, 10 to 15 minutes. Sprinkle with walnuts and shaved Parmesan.

Recent semi-supervised instance segmentation methods mostly focus on modeling spectral or spatial relationships between pixels in different images through consistency and/or similarity learning. These methods either treat all pixels within an object as a unit or assign labels independently at each pixel without considering their spatial coherence, which limits their ability to capture complex object structures. In this paper, we propose a Mask-guided Sample Selection (MSS) approach for training a semi-supervised pixel-level classifier. Given a pixel of interest, our method selects its class-consistent neighboring pixels as semantic contextual samples through a learned mask. We pose the learning of the mask as a binary classification problem, where the mask is the decision boundary between the foreground (object) and background (rest of the image). Specifically, given an initial guess of the mask, we minimize the cross-entropy loss by iteratively refining the mask through gradient descent. We optimize the mask in a bottom-up fashion, starting from the pixels with the highest response and traversing the areas with the most uncertain labels. We evaluate MSS on four semi-supervised segmentation benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

Ron Williamson has returned to his hometown of Ada, Oklahoma after multiple failed attempts to play for various minor league baseball teams, including the Fort Lauderdale Yankees and two farm teams owned by the Oakland A's. An elbow injury inhibited his chances to progress. His big dreams were not enough to overcome the odds (less than 10 percent) of making it to a big league game. His failures lead to, or aggravate, his depression and problem drinking. Early in the morning of December 8, 1982, the body of Debra Sue Carter, a 21-year-old cocktail waitress, was found in the bedroom of her garage apartment in Ada. She had been beaten, raped and suffocated. After five years of false starts and shoddy police work by the Ada police department, Williamson—along with his "drinking buddy", Dennis Fritz--were charged, tried and convicted of the rape and murder charges in 1988. Williamson was sentenced to death. Fritz was given a life sentence. Fritz's wife had been murdered seven years earlier and he was raising their only daughter when he was arrested. Grisham's book describes the aggressive and misguided mission of the Ada police department and Pontotoc County District Attorney Bill Peterson to solve the mystery of Carter's murder. The police and prosecutor used forced "dream" confessions, unreliable witnesses, and flimsy evidence to convict Williamson and Fritz. Since a death penalty conviction automatically sets in motion a series of appeals, the Innocence Project aided Williamson's attorney, Mark Barrett, in exposing several glaring holes in the prosecution's case and the credibility of the prosecution's witnesses. Frank H. Seay, a U.S. District Court judge, ordered a retrial. After suffering through a conviction and eleven years on death row, Williamson and Fritz were exonerated by DNA evidence and released on April 15, 1999. Williamson was the 78th inmate released from death row since 1973. Williamson suffered deep and irreversible psychological damage during his incarceration and eventual stay on death row. For example, on September 22, 1994, he was five days away from being executed when his sentence was stayed by the court, following the filing of a habeas corpus petition. He was intermittently treated for manic depression, personality disorders, alcoholism and mild schizophrenia. It was later proven that he was indeed mentally ill and therefore was unfit to have been tried or sentenced to death in the first place. The State of Oklahoma, the city of Ada, and Pontotoc County officials never admitted any errors and threatened to re-arrest him. Another criminal from Ada, Glen Gore, was eventually convicted of the original crime on June 24, 2003. He was sentenced to death He was convicted at a second trial on June 21, 2006 and sentenced by Judge Landrith to life in prison without parole. This was required by law due to a jury deadlock on sentencing. Williamson and Fritz sued and won a settlement for wrongful conviction of $500,000 in 2003 from the City of Ada, and an out-of-court settlement with the State of Oklahoma for an undisclosed amount. By 2004, Williamson was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver and died on December 4, 2004 in a Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, nursing home. Fritz returned to Kansas City, where he lives with his daughter, Elizabeth . In 2006, Fritz published his own account of being wrongly convicted in his book titled Journey toward Justice. The book includes accounts (as subplots) of the false conviction, trial and sentencing of Tommy Ward and Karl Fontenot in the abduction, rape, and purported murder of Denice Haraway, as well as the false conviction of Greg Wilhoit in the rape and murder of his estranged wife, Kathy. At one time, all the men were incarcerated in the same death row. About two decades before Grisham's book, Ward and Fontenot's wrongful convictions were detailed in a book published in 1987 called The Dreams of Ada by Robert Mayer.

Adapromine is an antiviral drug of the adamantane group related to amantadine (1-aminoadamantane), rimantadine (1-(1-aminoethyl)adamantane), and memantine (1-amino-3,5-dimethyladamantane) that is marketed in Russia for the treatment and prevention of influenza. It is an alkyl analogue of rimantadine and is similar to rimantadine in its antiviral activity but possesses a broader spectrum of action, being effective against influenza viruses of both type A and B. Strains of type A influenza virus with resistance to adapromine and rimantadine and the related drug deitiforine were encountered in Mongolia and the Soviet Union in the 1980s. Electroencephalography (EEG) studies of animals suggest that adapromine and related adamantanes including amantadine, bromantane (1-amino-2-bromophenyladamantane), and memantine have psychostimulant-like and possibly antidepressant-like effects, and that these effects may be mediated via catecholaminergic processes. These psychostimulant effects differ qualitatively from those of conventional psychostimulants like amphetamine however, and the adamantane derivatives have been described contrarily as "adaptogens" and as "actoprotectors".

Concerns have been raised over a new school diploma plan that is set to be implemented in the coming years. The proposed plan aims to create a single diploma for all students, regardless of their chosen subject or career pathway.

Critics argue that this one-size-fits-all approach could have negative implications for students who have specialized interests or aspirations. They argue that by eliminating subject-specific qualifications, the new diploma may discourage students from pursuing their passions and limit their opportunities for further study or employment in their desired field.

Another concern is that a uniform diploma may not accurately reflect a student's capabilities or achievements. Supporters of subject-specific qualifications argue that they provide a more comprehensive and detailed assessment of a student's knowledge and skills. They fear that a single diploma may oversimplify a student's performance, ultimately leading to a lack of recognition for their individual strengths and achievements.

Additionally, there are concerns that the new diploma plan may undermine the autonomy of schools and teachers. Critics argue that by prescribing a standardized curriculum and assessment structure, the plan may limit the flexibility of teachers to tailor their teaching approaches to the needs and interests of their students. This could stifle creativity and innovation in the classroom and may result in a less engaging and fulfilling education experience for students.

Furthermore, some experts worry that the implementation of a single diploma could exacerbate existing inequalities in the education system. They argue that students from disadvantaged backgrounds or with specific learning needs may face additional challenges in meeting the requirements of the new diploma. This could potentially widen the achievement gap and hinder social mobility.

Despite these concerns, proponents of the new diploma plan argue that it will promote a more holistic and well-rounded education. They believe that by removing the emphasis on subject-specific qualifications, students will be encouraged to explore a broader range of subjects and develop a wider skillset. They also argue that a uniform diploma will simplify the university admissions process and provide employers with a clearer indication of a candidate's abilities.

The debate over the school diploma plan is likely to continue, with various stakeholders voicing their opinions and concerns. As the plan moves forward, it will be imperative for policymakers to carefully consider the potential implications and ensure that the education system continues to support and inspire students in their individual pursuits and aspirations.

With the addition of Williston, the WDA grew to its largest size, with 8 teams.

The RedHawks were represented in the 1994 National Baseball Congress World Series in Hutchinson, Kansas, where they went 1-2.

In January 1995, the Western Dakota Baseball League merged with the Northern Plains League. The league became known as the Western Dakota Association. The WDA contracted again before the start of the 1997 season, dropping to eight teams. The league has remained at this membership level ever since. 

In 1999, the Williston Lakers folded due to financial difficulties. The Lakers were replaced by the Williston Roughriders, who continue to compete in the WDA as of the 2023 season.

A man roams the streets with a basket
of freestone peaches hollering, "Peaches,
peaches, yellow freestone peaches for sale."
My grandfather in his prime could outshout
the Tigers of Wrath or the factory whistles
along the river. Hamtramck hungered
for yellow freestone peaches, downriver
wakened from a dream of work, Zug Island danced
into the bright day glad to be alive.
Full-figured women in their negligees
streamed into the streets from the dark doorways
to demand in Polish or Armenian
the ripened offerings of this new world.
Josef Prisckulnick out of Dubrovitsa
to Detroit by way of Ellis Island
raised himself regally to his full height
of five feet two and transacted until
the fruit was gone into those eager hands.
Thus would there be a letter sent across
an ocean and a continent, and thus
would Sadie waken to the news of wealth
without limit in the bright and distant land,
and thus bags were packed and she set sail
for America. Some of this is true.
The women were gaunt. All day the kids dug
in the back lots searching for anything.
The place was Russia with another name.
Joe was five feet two. Dubrovitsa burned
to gray ashes the west wind carried off,
then Rovno went, then the Dnieper turned to dust.
We sat around the table telling lies
while the late light filled an empty glass.
Bread, onions, the smell of burning butter,
small white potatoes we shared with no one
because the hour was wrong, the guest was late,
and this was Michigan in 1928.

Auroroborealia is a small bodied euichthyosaurian ichthyosaur discovered on the New Siberian Islands in the Russian Arctic. The animal was likely similar in size to Hudsonelpidia, around 1 to 1.5 meters in length. Although the fragmentary nature doesn't allow to determine its exact ontogenetic state, other remains from the area suggest that it was simply a small bodied taxon. It contains a single species, Auroroborealia incognita. Discovery and naming
The fossils of Auroroborealia were discovered by a joint expedition of the Geological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Trofimuk Institute of Petroleum Geology and Geophysics, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, during excavations in 2006 and 2009. These expeditions yielded a variety of ichthyosaurian remains from six stratigraphic levels ranging from the lower Carnian to middle Norian. Although most specimens were fragmentary, Zverkov et al. (2021) could nevertheless differentiate between a host of different ichthyosaurs. One fossil in particular, specimen ZIN PH 5/250, included cranial remains as well as anterior presacral vertebrae with associated neural arches and ribs. A bone fragment associated with the pectoral girdle is also part of this specimen. Based on this material Zverkov  et al. erected the species Aurororborealia incognita, while also describing a series of referred specimens (which however did not factor into the diagnosis of the genus).

Semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentations have been addressed using
different and specialized frameworks despite their underlying connections. This
paper presents a unified, simple, and effective framework for these essentially
similar tasks. The framework, named K-Net, segments both instances and semantic
categories consistently by a group of learnable kernels, where each kernel is
responsible for generating a mask for either a potential instance or a stuff
class. To remedy the difficulties of distinguishing various instances, we
propose a kernel update strategy that enables each kernel dynamic and
conditional on its meaningful group in the input image. K-Net can be trained in
an end-to-end manner with bipartite matching, and its training and inference
are naturally NMS-free and box-free. Without bells and whistles, K-Net
surpasses all previous state-of-the-art single-model results of panoptic
segmentation on MS COCO and semantic segmentation on ADE20K with 52.1% PQ and
54.3% mIoU, respectively. Its instance segmentation performance is also on par
with Cascade Mask R-CNNon MS COCO with 60%-90% faster inference speeds. Code
and models will be released at https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection.

Current image segmentation techniques heavily rely on accurate annotations, which are often prohibitively expensive, especially when applied to medical data. To address this challenge, our research proposes a novel approach combining deep learning with a geodesic prior to create a weakly supervised image segmentation method. This technique leverages prior knowledge from an auto-encoder to generate object-specific maps and incorporates it into the loss function of the segmentation model. We evaluated our method using cardiac substructure segmentation under clean and two levels of noisy label conditions (L1 and L2) and found significant improvements over baseline deep learning-based approaches. Specifically, our results indicate a boost in Dice scores of 4.4% for clean labels and 4.6% for L1 noise, and 6.3% for L2 noise, demonstrating enhanced performance and robustness in the presence of high-level noise thanks to the inclusion of shape priors.

"The Double Life of Véronique" is a breathtaking and enigmatic film that weaves a complex narrative, blurring the lines between reality and imagination. Directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski, the film explores themes of identity, fate, and the interconnectedness of human lives.

The film centers around two women, Weronika in Poland and Véronique in France, who share an uncanny resemblance and a mysterious connection. We follow their parallel lives as they navigate personal struggles, passions, and opportunities. Kieślowski's masterful storytelling beautifully captures the intimacy and intricacies of their existence.

The cinematography is stunning and poetic, with every shot meticulously framed and lit. The use of colors and symbolism adds another layer of depth to the film, enhancing the overall visual experience. Zbigniew Preisner's hauntingly beautiful score perfectly complements the ethereal atmosphere, immersing the audience in the emotional journey of the characters.

The performances by Irène Jacob in the dual roles of Weronika and Véronique are mesmerizing. She effortlessly embodies each character, imbuing them with vulnerability, grace, and a sense of mystery. Jacob's subtle and nuanced acting adds to the enigmatic nature of the film, leaving the viewer captivated and intrigued.

"The Double Life of Véronique" is not a film that can be easily classified or dissected. Its open-ended narrative invites interpretation and reflection, and it skillfully challenges the audience's perception of reality. Kieślowski's ability to evoke emotion through visual storytelling is nothing short of genius, and this film is a testament to his talent.

This cinematic masterpiece offers a unique and thought-provoking viewing experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. It is a film that requires multiple viewings to fully appreciate its depth and nuances. "The Double Life of Véronique" is a true work of art, an exploration of the human condition that transcends boundaries and leaves a lasting impact.

The story concerns Bernice, a wealthy girl from Eau Claire, Wisconsin, who goes to visit her cousin Marjorie for the month of August. Marjorie feels that Bernice is a drag on her social life, and none of the boys want to dance with Bernice. Bernice overhears a conversation between Marjorie and Marjorie's mother where the younger girl complains that Bernice is socially hopeless. The next day, Bernice threatens to leave town, but when Marjorie is unfazed, Bernice relents and agrees to let Marjorie turn her into a society girl. Marjorie teaches Bernice how to hold interesting conversations, how to flirt with even unattractive or uninteresting boys to make herself seem more desirable, and how to dance. Bernice's best line is teasing the boys with the idea that she will soon bob her hair and they will get to watch. The new Bernice is a big hit with the boys in town with her new attitude, especially with Warren, a boy Marjorie keeps around as her own but neglects. When it becomes clear that Warren has shifted his interest from Marjorie to Bernice, Marjorie sets about humiliating Bernice, tricking her into going through with bobbing her hair. When Bernice comes out of the barbershop with the new hairdo, her hair is flat and strange. The boys suddenly lose interest in her, and Bernice realizes she's been tricked. Marjorie's mother points out that Bernice's haircut (which at the time was only seen on "liberated" women) would cause a scandal at an upcoming party held in her and Marjorie's honor. Bernice, deciding it would be best to leave the town before the party the next day, packs her trunk in the middle of the night and decides to leave on a train at 1 a.m. Before she goes, she sneaks into Marjorie's room and cuts off her cousin's two braids, taking them with her on her run to the station and throwing them onto Warren's front porch.

Organisers of the third Bangkok International Film Festival have been determined to carry on with this year's event despite the ravages of the Asian tsunami disaster.
The festivities have been scaled down, red carpets have been mothballed and profits from ticket sales are being donated to the tsunami relief fund. Apart from this, however, the festival has continued as originally planned. "When the disaster happened, we naturally asked ourselves if we should cancel," said the festival's executive director, Craig Prater. "The decision was made that we would continue, but that the focus would change.
"Our premieres became fundraisers, the opening night was visibly toned down and 10% of every ticket sold goes to the disaster fund," he continued. "But we feel like we've turned a page. We've acknowledged our position, and now it's business as usual."
Mr Prater's sentiments were echoed by Christine Rush, director of the festival's sister event, the Bangkok Film Market. "We have been careful to be respectful of the Thai nation's recovery from this terrible disaster," she said.
"However, the nation's recovery very much depends upon it continuing its economic life. "We are encouraging attendees to keep the victims in mind and aggressively support the aid organisations helping out," she added. Given the conspicuously low audience figures, that support may be more symbolic than significant. However, poor ticket sales have less to do with any fallout from the disaster and more to do with administrative and promotional difficulties.
The eclectic programme contains a wide range of titles, including such Oscar hopefuls as Ray Charles biopic Ray and Mike Leigh's abortion drama Vera Drake. That said, the absence of Thai subtitles on most film prints might have proved offputting to local cinemagoers.
On a more positive note, the celebrity guests attending the event have generated huge media interest in this busy capital city. Problems securing air transport, the clash with last Sunday's Golden Globes ceremony in Los Angeles and other factors have forced some big names to cancel.
But the festival has still attracted such Hollywood directors as Oliver Stone and Joel Schumacher, alongside such screen stars as Michael Douglas, Jeremy Irons and Jean-Claude Van Damme. Irons, whose film Being Julia is in competition for the festival's Golden Kinnaree awards, said he had wondered whether he should attend after December's catastrophe. "I questioned whether I should come when such a tragedy had happened," the British actor said. "I thought it might be in rather bad taste. But then I spoke to the organisers and I was encouraged to let life go on. "Now I've come here I'm very glad. What impresses me about Thai culture is they get over these things far quicker than we do in the West," he continued. "Basically I was invited here by Thailand. If they still want you to come, you should."
Now in its third year, Bangkok is a relatively recent addition to the hectic film festival calendar. And while it has yet to attain the stature of more established events held in Hong Kong, Tokyo and Pusan in South Korea, Mr Prater predicts it will soon become their equal. "It's grown awfully fast in three years - maybe too fast," he concedes. "We've had some bumps in the road, but that's only because the festival is still a baby. "I have no doubt in my mind that in five years, this will be the top Asian film festival in the world." The Golden Kinnarees will be awarded on Friday. The festival itself runs until 24 January.

Understanding and optimizing item timings with Tinker can dramatically improve your gameplay. Here are some tips you can utilize:

1. **Prioritize Boots of Travel (BoT):** Your first priority should always be saving for Boots of Travel. This item is crucial to Tinker's playstyle as it allows you to travel around the map, pushing lanes, and teleporting back to your base when needed.

2. **Farming Patterns:** Tinker is all about farming efficiently. Using March of the Machines, you can continually clear out waves of creeps. When farming the jungle, move strategically between camps to use March of the Machines to best effect.

3. **Stacking Neutral Creeps:** While farming waves with March, try to stack neutral camps whenever possible, this will allow for maximizing your gold and experience gain.

4. **Bottle and Soul Ring:** These two items should be your next priority after BoTs. They give you the ability to stay on the map longer due to sustainability in health and mana.

5. **Blink Dagger Timing:** Blink Dagger is another high priority item. Try to get it before the 20-minute mark. It offers a great deal of mobility and can save you from many sticky situations.

6. **Scythe of Vyse and Dagon:** These are your luxury items. The former is great for control and adding an extra layer of disable in team fights, whereas the latter will let you burst down enemies quickly. Their timings largely depend on how well you have farmed.

Remember that both your individual skill level and the state of your specific game can affect this schedule. Being adaptable is crucial in Dota 2, so be prepared to adjust your playstyle and item build based on the needs of your team and the nature of the enemy team. In general, ensure you maximize farming, manage your mana well and aim for minimum deaths. Good luck!

It was back to official duties last week in my role as an ambassador to London's 2012 Olympic bid. But I still managed to do all my marathon training.
All the sporting people on the capital's bid team think I'm mad to be taking part in the London Marathon. The bid chairman, Lord Coe, admitted he would never dream of running a marathon, even though he was an Olympic middle-distance runner.
Kelly Holmes, former hurdler Alan Pascoe and former sprinter Frankie Fredericks - who is now an IOC member - all wanted to know why anyone would want to run that far. You'd have thought all these athletes, who have been running for most of their lives, wouldn't think it would be that bad. But the only person who was positive about my intentions was Tanni Grey Thompson, who has won the London Marathon wheelchair race six times. Even though it was a very busy week entertaining the International Olympic Committee's (IOC) Evaluation Commission, I actually found my running schedule easier to follow. When I'm at home, I get distracted by all sorts of things but for the five days I was in London, I was in a pressurised situation, but I found it easy to relax by running.
On Wednesday, the presentations to the IOC team did not finish until the early evening, so I just managed to squeeze in a 45-minute run. We had an early start on Thursday because we had to visit all the Olympic sites around London, that was pretty shattering, but when we got back to the hotel, I got back on the treadmill. On Friday evening I went along to the special dinner at Buckingham Palace which was a nice occasion. I never feel guilty about eating, especially when I'm exercising. And because it was a rest day I didn't have to feel bad about missing my training either. Anyway, I managed to do another quick run on Saturday ahead of the final IOC presentations, before heading home for my daughter's birthday.
When I was in London I did all of my runs on the treadmill, which isn't the same as exercising outdoors. One of the IOC's technical staff from Australia ran alongside me one day. We talked about the Sydney Olympics and that made the time go past more quickly. I do find it quite comfortable running in the gym because there is more cushioning. But when you're gearing up to running on the road you need your body to get used to that jarring feeling when your feet hit the pavement. It was good to get out on the road for my long run on Sunday. After the week I'd had I was a bit concerned I wouldn't be able to complete it. But I coped with it very well and, even though it was bitterly cold, I put in 15-and-a-half miles - only another 11 to go then.

Ingredients 
1/2 pound beef top sirloin, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
1/2 cup chopped red onion
1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper
1/2 cup chopped red bell pepper
1 cup cherry tomatoes
Salt and pepper to taste

For the Salsa
2 cups diced fresh tomato
1/4 cup diced red onion
1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro
1 tablespoon olive oil
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper

For the Chimichurri
1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 teaspoon red wine vinegar
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions
In a large bowl, combine the beef, sausage, onion, green and red bell peppers, tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Thread the mixture onto eight 10-inch skewers.
For the salsa, in a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Cover and refrigerate until serving.
For the chimichurri, in a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.
Grill the skewers, covered, over medium-hot heat for 10-15 minutes, or until the meat is cooked through, turning and basting frequently with the chimichurri. Serve with the salsa.

The UK has welcomed the decision by India and Pakistan to open a bus link across the ceasefire line dividing the disputed region of Kashmir.
Foreign Secretary Jack Straw, touring South East Asian countries, praised the "spirit of cooperation" in achieving the breakthrough. Media reports in both countries describe the deal as a major step in the ongoing peace process. Mr Straw said he hoped the agreement would make a difference to Kashmiris. The bus service was one of several announcements made after a meeting of foreign ministers of both countries in Islamabad on Wednesday. Kashmiri politicians on both sides of the Line of Control which divides the region welcomed the move.
In a statement, Mr Straw said the bus service between Srinagar and Muzaffarabad "will be able to reunite families that have been divided for decades". "This will make a real difference to the lives of Kashmiris on both sides of the Line of Control," he said. "I warmly applaud the efforts of both India and Pakistan to make this happen. "This spirit of cooperation will, I hope, lead to many more measures that will benefit all in the region."
On Thursday Mr Straw was in India visiting Sikhism's holiest shrine, the Golden Temple in Amritsar where he tried his hand at making Indian bread or roti. He is due to take part in talks with the Indian government on Friday. A second bus service linking the Pakistani city of Lahore with Amritsar in India was also announced as well as a rail link between Rajasthan state and Pakistan's Sindh province. Both sides agreed to begin talks on reducing the risk of nuclear accidents and also said they planned to reopen their respective consulates in Karachi and Mumbai (Bombay). The mountainous region of Kashmir has been a flashpoint between the two nuclear powers for more than 50 years.

The novel follows the journey of young Richard Bolitho as he embarks on a career in the Royal Navy during the late 18th century. Starting as a lowly midshipman, Bolitho is eager to prove himself and climb the ranks, despite the challenges that come with being the son of a relatively unknown and uninfluential naval officer.

As he navigates the complexities of naval life, Bolitho faces numerous obstacles, from hazing and bullying by his fellow sailors to the harsh realities of war. He serves aboard several ships, encountering a diverse cast of characters, including the gruff but fair Captain Pascoe, who becomes a mentor and father figure, and the calculating and ambitious Lieutenant Telfer, who sees Bolitho as a rival.

Bolitho witnesses and participates in several key naval battles, including the Glorious First of June and the Battle of the Nile, where he distinguishes himself through bravery and quick thinking. He also becomes embroiled in political intrigue, as the Navy struggles to counter the threats of the French Revolutionary forces and their designs on Britain's colonies.

Through his experiences, Bolitho learns valuable lessons about leadership, loyalty, and the importance of standing by one's principles. He also begins to develop feelings for a young woman named Catherine, the daughter of a naval officer, who shares his love of the sea and his desire for adventure.

As the novel progresses, Bolitho matures from a naive and impulsive young man into a confident and capable officer, earning the respect of his comrades and superiors. He must confront the ultimate test of his mettle, however, when he is falsely accused of a crime and must fight to clear his name and restore his reputation.

With its rich historical backdrop, vividly detailed naval battles, and compelling coming-of-age story, this novel is a thrilling and poignant portrayal of a young man's journey to find his place in the world and make a name for himself in the British Navy.

In the fictional Chinese kingdom of Syai, a bond of sisterhood is forged through the ancient tradition of jin-shi, a vow of eternal loyalty that defies societal norms and conventions. Inspired by the real-life Nü Shu, a hidden script used by Chinese women, the lives of the sisterhood continue to interweave across generations. The narrative centers around Tai, the daughter of a humble seamstress, who becomes the jin-shi bao of the young Empress Antian after a devastating earthquake wipes out the royal family. As Antian lies on her deathbed, she entrusts Tai with caring for her sister Liudan, and they form a new bond through the promise of jin-shi. Comforted by Yuet, a skilled healer, Tai takes on the role of caretaker, while navigating the complexities of palace politics. Meanwhile, Tai's childhood friend Nhia, a young girl born with a disability, discovers her own calling as a wise and compassionate leader, eventually becoming the Syai Chancellor. Nhia forms a deep connection with Khailin, a seeker of truth, but Khailin's relentless pursuit of knowledge ultimately leads her down a dark path. > We present an algorithm to solve the crystallographic phase problem by means of dynamical scattering theory, which we have implemented and tested on simulated data. Our method uses only information contained within the diffracted intensities (i.e., no additional experimental input such as absorption or anomalous dispersion). It can be applied to any crystal structure with arbitrary symmetry, including non-centrosymmetric space groups. In addition, it does not require that the unit cell contains more than one atom per asymmetric unit. This makes our approach particularly well suited for solving structures containing heavy atoms, where conventional methods based on anomalous scattering are often unsuccessful due to insufficient anomalous signal. As a proof of principle, we demonstrate how our method can be used to determine the atomic positions in a small organic molecule consisting of two chiral centers.

The March of Dimes is a US-based non-profit organization focused on enhancing maternal and infant health. Initially established in 1938 by President Franklin D. Roosevelt under the name National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis, it aimed to combat polio. This name was suggested by entertainer Eddie Cantor. Following funding for Jonas Salk's polio vaccine, the organization shifted its emphasis towards preventing birth defects and infant mortality. By 2005, as premature births became the top cause of child deaths globally, the group concentrated on researching and preventing preterm births. 

March of Dimes addresses maternal and infant health through five main areas: medical research, prenatal education, community initiatives, lobbying at the government level, and supporting pregnant women and mothers. The organization offers expectant parents with educational materials on baby care, pregnancy, conception, and postpartum, as well as providing assistance and support to families dealing with newborns in NICUs affected by prematurity, congenital issues, or other health problems.

To make this drink, combine two cups of sugar and two cups of water in a saucepan over medium heat, allowing the sugar to dissolve completely. Remove from heat and let the vanilla bean infuse for one hour; store the resulting syrup in the fridge for up to five days. Next, mix equal parts Earl Grey tea and white rum in a container and let them steep together for four hours at room temperature, shaking periodically to ensure thorough mixing. Strain the tea-rum mixture through a fine mesh strainer to remove the leaves. Store the rum separately in a dark, cool place for three months. Once you've prepared both components, combine the vanilla syrup, tea-infused rum, and freshly squeezed lemon juice in a large container. Heat one cup of milk, cinnamon sticks, and seven whole cloves over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it reaches 180 degrees Fahrenheit. Let it cool slightly, then pour it into the rum mixture and set aside for thirty minutes to allow the ingredients to meld. After this time has passed, strain the mixture through multiple layers of cheesecloth to remove the solids. The resulting milk punch can be refrigerated for up to a month and strained again before serving if desired. Chill the drink in the freezer before serving over ice.

- 1 package of dry yeast
- 1 tablespoon of sugar
- 1/3 cup of warm water (between 105° to 115°)
- 2 cups of all-purpose flour
- 1/2 teaspoon of salt
- 2 teaspoons of vegetable oil
- Vegetable cooking spray
- 1/2 cup of dry sherry
- 1/2 cup of water
- 1 pound of chicken thighs without skin
- 1 tablespoon of cornstarch
- 2 teaspoons of vegetable oil
- 1/2 cup of finely chopped onion
- 2 teaspoons of curry powder
- 2 teaspoons of minced peeled gingerroot
- 1 crushed garlic clove
- 1/2 teaspoon of salt
- Steamed green cabbage leaves

Instructions:

Mix yeast and sugar in 1/3 cup warm water for 5 minutes. Then combine flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a food processor and blend until smooth. Gradually add the yeast mixture along with 2 teaspoons of oil, processing until the dough leaves the sides of the bowl and forms a ball. Knead the dough lightly on a lightly floured surface. Place it in a bowl coated with cooking spray, cover it, and let it rise in a warm place for an hour or until it has doubled in size. 

Combine sherry, 1/2 cup of water, and chicken in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 25 minutes or until the chicken is cooked. Remove the chicken, let it cool, and discard the excess liquid. Keep half of the cooking liquid and let it cool. Remove the chicken from its bones, shred it, and mix with the reserved liquid. Combine the other half of the cooking liquid and cornstarch and stir well. Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then stir in curry powder, gingerroot, and garlic for 30 seconds. Bring the mixture to a boil and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Remove from heat, add the shredded chicken and salt, and set aside.

Punch down the dough, divide it into 14 equal parts, and work with one part at a time, covering the rest.

The 1906 World Series featured a crosstown matchup between the Chicago White Sox and the Chicago Cubs. The home teams alternated, starting with the National League Cubs being home in Game 1. The teams split the first four games; then the Hitless Wonders (a name coined by sportswriter Charles Dryden) exploded for 26 hits in the last two games. True to their nickname, the White Sox hit only .198 as a team in winning the series, but it beat the .196 average produced by the Cubs. In Game 3, White Sox pitcher Ed Walsh struck out 12 Cubs, breaking the previous record of 11 set by Bill Dinneen in .

Convolutional neural networks have been applied to a wide variety of computer
vision tasks. Recent advances in semantic segmentation have enabled their
application to medical image segmentation. While most CNNs use two-dimensional
kernels, recent CNN-based publications on medical image segmentation featured
three-dimensional kernels, allowing full access to the three-dimensional
structure of medical images. Though closely related to semantic segmentation,
medical image segmentation includes specific challenges that need to be
addressed, such as the scarcity of labelled data, the high class imbalance
found in the ground truth and the high memory demand of three-dimensional
images. In this work, a CNN-based method with three-dimensional filters is
demonstrated and applied to hand and brain MRI. Two modifications to an
existing CNN architecture are discussed, along with methods on addressing the
aforementioned challenges. While most of the existing literature on medical
image segmentation focuses on soft tissue and the major organs, this work is
validated on data both from the central nervous system as well as the bones of
the hand.
