DEC has contacted US domain registrars and the hosting firm maintaining the site online. Any funds raised through the site will be redirected to the legitimate organization. Both BT and DEC's hosting provider are working together to shut down the site. Sanders emphasized that DEC typically does not solicit donations via unsolicited emails and would never engage in such tactics. Her team aims to bring down the fake site swiftly. Efforts by the BBC News website to reach the site's administrators have been unsuccessful; the provided email addresses do not function, and the site's true owner remains hidden.

Researchers utilize Caenorhabditis elegans as a prominent biological model to explore basic biological principles. Studies involving this roundworm focus on understanding how genes influence movement patterns. Assessing movement involves analyzing the worm's movement types and quantifying them systematically. Through numerous experiments conducted over several years, scientists have analyzed C. elegans' movement in diverse settings, such as navigating solid surfaces, swimming in liquids, and moving through tiny fluid channels. However, each environment necessitates tailored image processing techniques requiring manual adjustments. To address this issue, a new Multi-Environment Model Estimation framework called MEME was proposed. This MEME platform relies on mixture of Gaussian models, where statistical models for both the environmental background and nematode appearance are separately learned and applied for precise segmentation of the nematode. Unlike existing methods, MEME simplifies user burdens by requiring only a single image containing a nematode within its environment for model training. Furthermore, MEME enables efficient extraction of nematode'skeletons,' allowing straightforward measurement of movement patterns. Results show that MEME surpasses the performance of traditional threshold-based approaches in most cases tested. By providing a versatile platform, MEME offers researchers a convenient solution for segmenting and'skeletonizing' C. elegans in various movement tests.

He later headed to Louisiana to recruit African American soldiers, leading them at the Siege of Port Hudson in 1863. A year later, Merriam commanded the 73rd Infantry Regiment, United States Colored Troops, which attacked Confederate positions at Fort Blakely, Alabama, in 1865. This daring move earned him a brevet promotion to colonel and ultimately led to the awarding of the Medal of Honor on June 28, 1894. The medal citation notes that Merriam volunteered for an unauthorized attack and successfully launched it with courage.

2. Zest 2 of the Meyer lemons and set aside. Cut the lemons in half and juice them to obtain 1/4 cup of lemon juice.

3. In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the lemon zest and cook for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.

4. Add the lemon juice and heavy cream to the skillet, and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.

5. Add the cooked fettuccine pasta to the skillet and toss with the lemon cream sauce. Add the grated Parmesan cheese and mix well.

6. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

7. Plate the fettuccine and garnish with freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

Longing for renewal, I yearn for the arrival of spring.
Let its revitalizing energy begin now.
Bring forth the vibrant, life-giving pulse of nature's rebirth!
Unleash the torrent of creation and let life burst forth from this stagnant state.
Sweep away the delicate, eerie early blooms that are mere precursors to true blossoming.
Dissolve the cold, ominous undertones that have been lingering in the air.
Come, spring, bring warmth and vitality to this frozen landscape.
I take great joy in crushing the early blooms that symbolize the bleakness of winter.
The thought of their fleeting beauty only serves to remind me of my desire for something more profound.
I crave the rich, dynamic essence of spring, which brings new life to the earth.
It's the same energy that nurtures the ripening wheat and fills the air with an abundance of fruit.
Imagine the vibrant, star-like blooms dancing in mid-air, tempting us with their allure.
Then, without warning, the blossoms of various fruits - pears, apples, almonds, and quinces - explode onto the scene.
Surrounded by swirling clouds of blossoms, our senses are overwhelmed.
In the spring, the gentle rustle of leaves and chirping birds fill the air, invigorating us.

I yearn for the thunderous beat of footsteps on the earth, signaling a fresh beginning.

And an orator said, "Speak to us of Freedom."
And he answered:
At the city gate and by your fireside I have seen you prostrate yourself and worship your own freedom,
Even as slaves humble themselves before a tyrant and praise him though he slays them.
Ay, in the grove of the temple and in the shadow of the citadel I have seen the freest among you wear their freedom as a yoke and a handcuff.
And my heart bled within me; for you can only be free when even the desire of seeking freedom becomes a harness to you, and when you cease to speak of freedom as a goal and a fulfillment.
You shall be free indeed when your days are not without a care nor your nights without a want and a grief,
But rather when these things girdle your life and yet you rise above them naked and unbound.
And how shall you rise beyond your days and nights unless you break the chains which you at the dawn of your understanding have fastened around your noon hour?
In truth that which you call freedom is the strongest of these chains, though its links glitter in the sun and dazzle the eyes.
And what is it but fragments of your own self you would discard that you may become free?
If it is an unjust law you would abolish, that law was written with your own hand upon your own forehead.
You cannot erase it by burning your law books nor by washing the foreheads of your judges, though you pour the sea upon them.
And if it is a despot you would dethrone, see first that his throne erected within you is destroyed.
For how can a tyrant rule the free and the proud, but for a tyranny in their own freedom and a shame in their won pride?
And if it is a care you would cast off, that care has been chosen by you rather than imposed upon you.
And if it is a fear you would dispel, the seat of that fear is in your heart and not in the hand of the feared.
Verily all things move within your being in constant half embrace, the desired and the dreaded, the repugnant and the cherished, the pursued and that which you would escape.
These things move within you as lights and shadows in pairs that cling.
And when the shadow fades and is no more, the light that lingers becomes a shadow to another light.
And thus your freedom when it loses its fetters becomes itself the fetter of a greater freedom.

2 cups all-purpose flour (9 ounces)
1 tablespoon baking powder
4 tablespoons sugar
1/2 teaspoon salt
4 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
3/4 cup heavy cream
1 egg, slightly beaten
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
2 teaspoons milk or 2 teaspoons cream, divided
2 tablespoons sparkeling sugar, for the top
Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Place the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and butter in a food processor and plulse everything in 3-second intervals until it resembles course meal, (If doing this by hand, use 2 knives, a pastry blender or your fingers until the mixture resembles course meal). Transfer everything to a large bowl. Stir in heavy cream, egg, and vanilla mixing the dough by hand until it forms into a uniformed and slightly moistened dough. *You can also use your Kitchenaid with the dough hook on the slowest speed for a few minutes. divide the dough into 4 equal portions. Make dough to make 4 circles and 16 scones: On a floured surface gently roll one portion at a time into a ball. Flatten the ball until your disk is approximately 3/4" in height. Press down the outside of the dough circle so the center is slightly taller. Dampen tops of each disk with a 1/2 tsp milk or cream and evenly sprinkle sugar on top of each circle. Cut each circle in quarters. Bake on a ungreased cookie sheet, or line a baking sheet with parchment paper and bake for 15 minutes or until they are lightly golden brown. Remove scones from baking sheet and cool on a wire rack. Serve with butter and jam. Enjoy!

Philippe Sautet is a French chemist born on 8 May 1961 in Salon-de-Provence (France). He was elected to the French Academy of sciences on 30 November 2010. He was a research director at the CNRS and works in the chemistry laboratory of the École normale supérieure de Lyon where he devoted a large part of his scientific activity to molecular modelling. Now he is a professor at the University of California - Los Angeles. Biography 
Philippe Sautet is an engineer from the École polytechnique (Paris). He prepared his thesis at the University of Paris (Orsay) from 1985 to 1988 under the supervision of Odile Eisenstein. He was then a researcher at the CNRS in the Institut de Recherche sur la Catalyse (Villeurbanne, France) from 1988 to 1995, then Visiting Scientist at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory (Berkeley, California) from 1991 to 1992. Upon his return from the United States, he was a lecturer and then professor at the École Polytechnique from 1993 to 2005. He then took over the management of UMR 5182 (Chemistry Laboratory of the École normale supérieure de Lyon, France) between 2003 and 2010. This is a research team of 80 people. He is also Director of the Institut de Chimie de Lyon, FR CNRS 3023 (1,000 people) since 2007.

Kodomo is the moniker for electronic musician Chris Child, an Emmy award-winning full-time composer who lives and works in Portland, Maine. As Kodomo, he is best known for his work on the Harmonix video games Amplitude, and Frequency as well as the iPod game Phase, which features Kodomo's "Spira Mirabilis."  is the Japanese word for "child"—both a reference to his surname and the fact that he grew up in Japan. Kodomo's first full-length album Still Life is a highly conceptual piece in which the music was all inspired by a set of photographs taken during Kodomo's travels in the US and abroad. The tracks are all titled using the photographic images rather than words. For example, Concept 13 started with a photograph that reflects the Fibonacci proportions that are repeatedly found in nature. These proportions were used to govern the musical composition in the melodic theme, the sonic texture, and even the pace of development of the piece. In this case, .618 is the governing number, and themes are introduced at these intervals, which give the whole composition a balanced and natural-feeling proportion.

Microsoft has said it will replace more than 14 million power cables for its Xbox consoles due to safety concerns.
The company said the move was a "preventative step" after reports of fire hazard problems with the cables. It affects Xboxes made before 23 October 2003 for all regions but mainland Europe - and consoles in that region made before 13 January 2004. Microsoft said it had received 30 reports of minor injury or property damage due to faulty cables. The firm said fewer than one in 10,000 consoles had experienced component failures. The recall affects almost three quarters of all Xboxes sold around the world since its launch in 2001.
In a statement, it added: "In almost all instances, any damage caused by these failures was contained within the console itself or limited to the tip of the power cord at the back of the console." But in seven cases, customers reported sustaining a minor burn to their hand. In 23 cases, customers reported smoke damage, or minor damage to a carpet or entertainment centre. "This is a preventative step we're choosing to take despite the rarity of these incidents," said Robbie Bach, senior vice president, Microsoft home and entertainment division. "We regret the inconvenience, but believe offering consumers a free replacement cord is the responsible thing to do." Consumers can order a new cable from the Xbox website or by telephoning 0800 028 9276 in the UK. Microsoft said customers would get replacement cords within two to four weeks from the time of order. It advised users to turn off their Xboxes when not in use. A follow-up to Xbox is expected to released at the end of this year or the beginning of 2006.

What more can be said of Raimi's legendary cult-classic that hasn't already been beaten to death like a puss-oozing zombie that crosses paths with Ash? Possibly nothing, but I'll try.

Before Spiderman and before the countless spin-offs of this movie were made or even conceived, Raimi and friends decided to make a low budget zombie flick mainly for fun, and surprisingly it has become a masterpiece of shock and horror. Possibly a perfect example of how to make an entertaining film on a shoe-string budget, The Evil Dead delivers what it promises, the ultimate in grueling horror. Even with it's mild budget and sometimes shaky acting, TED shocks and spooks the audience through chilling atmosphere and some of the most violent effects ever put on film. Those who are squeamish need not apply. As a matter of fact, just run for your girly life.

There are several reasons this film succeeds. First, Raimi's camera work is truly masterful. By using fast camera work and aggressive shots, Raimi has created an eerie world that is sometimes hard to look at but too entertaining to turn away from. His style from behind the camera is absolutely unmistakable. This is perfectly exemplified in the beginning of the film, where the camera alone creates enough atmosphere to leave you biting your nails in suspense of what's to come. You feel at any moment someone is going to get their neck chomped on by some zombie hiding just out of view. One of the most impressive openings I can think of, perfection in pacing and atmosphere. It gets even better once the action starts. Some shots hold for a seeming eternity, and part of you wishes for it to stop for it's unrestrained gore and violence...but the other part of you is getting a sick kick out of it. One of the most impressive shots is where the darkness from the trees begins to chase people, knocking any tree or obstacle down that happens to be in it's way. Truly magnificent technique, however they did it.

TED also succeeds because it's self-aware of the fact that it's a simple zombie movie and never takes itself too seriously, and doesn't expect the audience to do so either. It's meant to be campy, cheesy, revolting and chilling at the same time. There are moments in the film where it seems to be making fun of itself and the genre in general. For this fact alone, one cannot hold certain things against it such as sometimes questionable acting from the supporting cast and sometimes the downright implausibility of certain situations. If you can accept this and you're not put off by mannequin ultra-violence, then you should find yourself on the supporter's side of the fence. I think some don't like it because it can be ridiculous and cheesy in parts, although it was meant to be. Even with the fact that it's sometimes cheesy, there are some downright chilling moments in this film that most horror films nowadays cannot begin to muster. Case in point, the zombie screaming from the cellar door. The zombie growls and howls themselves are enough to send shivers up one's spine. And let's not forget the unforgettable tree love scene, ridiculous and hilarious simultaneously.

Last but certainly not least: Bruce Campbell as Ash, the badass of all zombie films. Campbell is Ash, period, and always will be.

In my opinion, this is by far the best of the trilogy, and although there could have been more of the chainsaw, this is the definitive zombie film and probably always will be. I feel it succeeds over it's sequels due to it's increased violence and lack of humor in comparison. It's blood, gore, camera work, and shock factor are still formidable even today and are what make this such a cult classic. If you've ever liked any horror film, this is an absolute must-see.

A woman fled from her lodging,
Driven out into the unknown;
In the spot where she had nowhere to go,
Her own people were at ease at home.
Nearby stood a humble stable with creaking beams,
Its foundation unstable and its floor uneven,
Yet it seemed more sturdy than the ancient structures of Rome.
People often feel restless in their own homes,
While travelers are alone in unfamiliar lands,
They find solace when the day ends and they're left with nothing but memories.
Our lives are marked by uncertainty and fierce emotions,
By chance encounters, honor, and unexpected surprises,
But true comfort lies beneath the vast, celestial expanse,
Where the origins of our stories began.
A young child was born in a simple stable,
Surrounded by animals that fed and frolicked;
It's only in places where we're without a fixed abode
That we truly feel at home;
We possess skills to create and understanding to grasp,
However, our deepest desires have been lost for a long time now.
There's no map or vessel that can guide us through this journey,
Under the vast, starry sky above.
Life is unpredictable, much like a myth or legend,
And even the most ordinary things hold a sense of awe,
The earth provides enough, and the air offers what we need,
For our imagination and our struggles;
However, our rest is elusive, like the path of a dragonfly,
And our peace is unattainable, existing only in impossible realms,
Where mythical creatures soar and thunderous storms rage,
Around a distant, shimmering star.
As night falls, people will return home,
To a place that surpasses the Garden of Eden,
And a city that exceeds the grandeur of Rome;
To the endpoint of our wanderings, to the things that defy logic,
To the location where God himself was without a home,
And we'll finally find our haven.

I've been doing some soul searching lately, and I think I've finally figured out why I struggle with self-esteem issues. It all goes back to my childhood.

Growing up, I was constantly criticized and belittled by my parents. They were always finding fault in everything I did, no matter how hard I tried. My grades weren't good enough, my clothes weren't clean enough, my hair wasn't neat enough. You name it, they found something wrong with it.

At first, I thought it was normal for parents to be critical of their kids. But as I got older, I realized that my friends didn't experience the same kind of criticism from their parents. They were encouraged and praised for their efforts, even when they made mistakes. Meanwhile, I felt like I could never do anything right.

The constant negativity took a toll on my self-esteem. I started to believe that I really was worthless and that I would never amount to anything. No matter how hard I tried to succeed, I felt like I was destined to fail.

It's taken me years to realize that this negative self-talk is not reality. It's a product of the programming I received as a child. But now that I know where these feelings are coming from, I can start to work on changing them.

I'm not saying it's easy. Old habits die hard, and it's tough to shake off years of negative conditioning. But I'm determined to break free from this cycle of self-doubt and low self-esteem. I deserve better, and I'm willing to put in the work to get there.

If you're struggling with similar issues, know that you're not alone. It may take time and effort, but we can overcome our past and build a brighter future for ourselves.

Combine 5 tablespoons of sugar and 1 to 2 tablespoons of dried lavender flowers in a grinder and grind until finely ground, discarding any lumps. In a saucepan, whisk together 2% reduced-fat milk, ½ cup of honey, and 3 egg yolks over medium heat, stirring frequently. Once the mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon (around 8 minutes), remove it from the heat and stir in the ground lavender. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, discarding the solids. Refrigerate for two hours. Pour the mixture into the freezer compartment of your ice cream maker according to its manual instructions. Transfer the mixture to a freezer-safe container once frozen solid, then stir in ¼ cup of chopped almonds. Chill for another hour. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 350°F. Serve the chilled ice cream topped with the baked figs and the sweet syrup.

Feeling guilty for not doing more to help Hannah while she was still alive, Clay decides to pass on the tapes to the others who Hannah blamed for her suicide. The novel explores themes of suicide, mental health, bullying, and the power of forgiveness.

To prepare this recipe, you will need eight tablespoons of softened butter, half a cup of sugar, two egg yolks, four ounces of melted semisweet chocolate, half a cup of all-purpose flour, a quarter cup of self-raising flour, five ounces of thawed and chopped cherries, unsweetened cocoa powder for dusting, five ounces of chopped semisweet chocolate for the ganache, one-third cup of heavy cream, preheated oven at 350 degrees Fahrenheit, grease and line an 8x4-inch loaf pan with parchment paper that extends beyond the sides for easy handling. Start by beating the butter and sugar together until they become light and airy using an electric mixer, then gradually incorporate the egg yolks, mixing until well combined. Next, mix in the melted chocolate until it's fully incorporated. In another bowl, whisk together the combined flours and pour them into the main bowl, gently folding until everything is combined. Set aside. Beat the egg whites separately using an electric mixer until they develop soft peaks, then gently fold them into the mixture in two portions until just combined, followed by adding the chopped cherries. Pour the mixture into the prepared loaf pan and level the top. Bake for sixty minutes, or until the edges start to pull away when a toothpick is inserted into the center. Allow it to cool in the pan for ten minutes before transferring it to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cake cools, make the ganache by combining the chocolate and one-quarter cup of heavy cream in a small saucepan over low heat and melting the chocolate. Remove it from the heat and let it sit for twenty minutes, stirring occasionally, until it reaches the desired consistency. Stir the ganache every five minutes to achieve the perfect texture. Then, whisk it for thirty seconds to give it a light and airy finish. Finally, add the remaining cream and cut the cake into three layers. Place the bottom layer on a serving plate, spread half of the whipped ganache on top, repeat the process, and finish with the top layer, dusting it with cocoa powder before slicing to serve.

Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas has said he will not tolerate attacks such as last Friday's suicide bombing in the Israeli city of Tel Aviv.
In an interview ahead of a meeting in London to discuss Palestinian reforms, Mr Abbas said such attacks were against Palestinian interests. The Palestinian Authority (PA) was exerting "a 100% effort" to end the violence, Mr Abbas added. The attack, which killed five, was the first of its kind since he took office. Mr Abbas confirmed Israel shared information with the PA in the hunt for the organisers of the attack. The Israeli government refuses to accept Syria's denials that it was implicated in the nightclub bombing. Israeli officials gave an intelligence briefing to foreign ambassadors on Monday, explaining Syria's alleged involvement. British foreign minister Jack Straw said there had been a "continuing stream" of information suggesting Palestinian militant groups were operating from within Syria.
In an email interview in the British newspaper the Independent, Mr Abbas said: "We believe peace is possible now and we are ready to negotiate with Israel to reach a true and lasting peace based on justice and international legitimacy." He added: "We have an opportunity and it would be irresponsible if we, the Israelis, or the world allow it to slip away." Tuesday's meeting on Palestinian reform is being hosted by British Prime Minister Tony Blair. Also due to attend are US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, UN Secretary General Kofi Annan, World Bank officials and foreign ministers from 23 European and Arab countries. The conference was a "vital step" in renewing the peace process, Mr Straw said. "It's a high-level attendance, which reflects the sense of momentum and opportunity created by recent events," he added. A spokesman for Mr Blair said the Prime Minister expected the conference to discuss "a comprehensive, co-ordinated and, above all, practical work plan for both the Palestinian Authority and the international community". Israel will not attend, but is said to be closely watching the outcome.

This letter investigates a novel approach to interferometry using diffraction instead of beam combination, inspired by Young's double-slit experiment. By incorporating a nonlinear material after one slit, the system loses its transverse spatial symmetry, causing a shift in the intensity pattern across the plane. Gerhard Albert Baum  (June 20, 1923 – October 18, 2017), better known as Gregory Baum, was a German-born Canadian priest and theologian in the Catholic Church. He became known in North America and Europe in the 1960s for his work on ecumenism, interfaith dialogue, and the relationship between the Catholic Church and Jews. In the later 1960s, he went to the New School for Social Theory in New York and became a sociologist, which led to his work on creating a dialogue between classical sociology (Marx, Tocqueville, Durkheim, Toennies, Weber, etc.) and Christian theology. In the 1970s, he welcomed the insights of the Theology of Liberation that came from Latin America and other societies. He also became interested in the work of Karl Mannheim and developed a program of ideology critique that he hoped would eliminate the ideological elements in religion, especially those elements that preached contempt for others and allowed Christians to remain unmoved by the suffering of the victims of social injustice and structural violence.

For years, home entertainment has evolved from humble VHS tapes to DVDs, and now Hollywood is poised on the cusp of another significant leap forward – high-definition. This emerging format promises breathtaking, 3D-like visuals and immersive surround sound. Although DVD disks and equipment won't be available until soon, several challenges must be addressed before their release. However, when high-definition films become widely available on new DVDs, it will revolutionize home entertainment. According to Rick Dean, director of business development at THX, a leading digital content company, a high-definition future holds tremendous potential. Having worked on notable titles such as the Star Wars trilogy, Finding Nemo, The Incredibles, and Indiana Jones, Dean acknowledges that the distinction between the film world and video world is no longer clear-cut. "The technology we're utilizing today blurs these boundaries significantly." He emphasizes that the digital files used for theater releases are identical to those used for home video masters.

However, creating a master feature film for DVD requires substantial compression due to the limitations of current DVD technology, which struggles to handle the demands of high-definition content. As a result, each time data is compressed, the image quality suffers. Dean expresses his desire to showcase his work in its true high-definition form, finding the prospect highly exciting. High-definition DVDs can store up to six times more data than standard DVDs, but convincing consumers to invest in upgraded players and displays within the next 18 months will require time. Despite this, Dean remains optimistic, stating that once people experience genuine high-definition, the differences will be striking. He notes that others have commented on how the images appear to "pop off the screen" after witnessing unaltered high-definition.

Today, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated state of
the art performance for supervised medical image segmentation, across various
imaging modalities and tasks. Despite early success, segmentation networks may
still generate anatomically aberrant segmentations, with holes or inaccuracies
near the object boundaries. To mitigate this effect, recent research works have
focused on incorporating spatial information or prior knowledge to enforce
anatomically plausible segmentation. If the integration of prior knowledge in
image segmentation is not a new topic in classical optimization approaches, it
is today an increasing trend in CNN based image segmentation, as shown by the
growing literature on the topic. In this survey, we focus on high level prior,
embedded at the loss function level. We categorize the articles according to
the nature of the prior: the object shape, size, topology, and the
inter-regions constraints. We highlight strengths and limitations of current
approaches, discuss the challenge related to the design and the integration of
prior-based losses, and the optimization strategies, and draw future research
directions.

The creators of the popular reality television show "Wife Swap" are taking legal action against a US production company for alleged copyright infringement. RDF Media, the UK-based company behind the show, has filed a lawsuit against American producer T Group Productions, accusing them of creating a "carbon copy" of the format.

"Wife Swap" first aired in the UK in 2003 and quickly gained international recognition. The show follows two families who exchange wives for a period of time, allowing them to experience different lifestyles and parenting techniques. The program has since been adapted in multiple countries, including the US, where it aired on the ABC network for over a decade.

RDF Media alleges that T Group Productions, in collaboration with A&E Networks, has produced a near-identical show called "Neighbor Swap," infringing upon their copyright and intellectual property rights. According to court documents, RDF Media claims that T Group Productions "directly and intentionally copied numerous episodes, storylines, and formats from 'Wife Swap.'"

The lawsuit accuses T Group Productions of not only stealing the show's concept but also replicating its distinctive visual elements, such as the logo and graphics used in the opening credits. RDF Media argues that "Neighbor Swap" is an "illicit clone" of their show, causing confusion among viewers and potentially harming their brand.

In response to the lawsuit, T Group Productions denies any wrongdoing, arguing that their show presents a different premise and is not an unauthorized copy of "Wife Swap." They claim that "Neighbor Swap" focuses on neighbors exchanging homes, rather than spouses, and that the format differs significantly from the UK original.

The outcome of the legal battle between RDF Media and T Group Productions remains uncertain. However, this lawsuit once again raises questions about the boundaries of copyright protection in the television industry. As reality shows continue to gain popularity worldwide, creators and production companies face mounting challenges in safeguarding their intellectual property rights and preventing unauthorized imitations.

Both RDF Media and T Group Productions are influential players in the reality television industry, making this copyright dispute a significant case to watch. It will ultimately fall upon the court to determine whether T Group Productions has unlawfully infringed upon RDF Media's rights and potentially impacted the future of the "Wife Swap" franchise.

A critical consideration is that the 70 limit for resistance only applies after calculating Pierce damage, according to developer notes. As a result, if an enemy has 76 resistance and an ally has 36 Pierce, the enemy's resistance drops to 40 - below the threshold that triggers the cap, but above 50 where it significantly reduces effectiveness. Nevertheless, this limitation is irrelevant when shields come into play, as the shield absorbs the initial Pierce damage, effectively capping the remaining resistance at 70 and reducing its impact due to the limit function. The problem arises with certain schools of attacks that can repeatedly exploit weaknesses without being affected, maintaining high resistance levels despite crippling opponents' damage output. Although this change may introduce improvements, the unclear implementation of the limit function and unchanged open hit mechanics lead me to question the design decision behind this approach.

We propose a novel superpixel-based multi-view convolutional neural network
for semantic image segmentation. The proposed network produces a high quality
segmentation of a single image by leveraging information from additional views
of the same scene. Particularly in indoor videos such as captured by robotic
platforms or handheld and bodyworn RGBD cameras, nearby video frames provide
diverse viewpoints and additional context of objects and scenes. To leverage
such information, we first compute region correspondences by optical flow and
image boundary-based superpixels. Given these region correspondences, we
propose a novel spatio-temporal pooling layer to aggregate information over
space and time. We evaluate our approach on the NYU--Depth--V2 and the SUN3D
datasets and compare it to various state-of-the-art single-view and multi-view
approaches. Besides a general improvement over the state-of-the-art, we also
show the benefits of making use of unlabeled frames during training for
multi-view as well as single-view prediction.

The goal of this research was to use the ultrasound images from conventional and ultrasonography-guided fluorescence in situ hybridization (fISH) to identify and segment thyroid nodules that are small enough (≤ 20 mm3) to be considered to be diagnostically relevant for thyroid cancer screening.

Methods. To analyze the ultrasonography-guided ultrasound images (10 µm × 10 µm x 2 mm) of thyroid nodules obtained from a number of patients with localized thyroid cancer, two separate groups of 50 individuals each were analyzed and their characteristics were observed.

Results. The proportion of nodules that were too small (≤20 mm3) for analysis for each group ranged from 1.8% (1 of 14) in group 1 to 24.5% (10 of 52) in group 2.

Conclusions. A small number of thyroid nodules would not be an adequate basis for the diagnostic evaluation for thyroid cancer. Additionally, in groups one, two, and three of the study, only 1 of 40 (5.5%) to 12.3 of 46 (13.5%) nodules were identified as being biopsied for thyroid cancer, depending on the imaging algorithm used.

For an unstable quantum system quantum Zeno effect represents total decay
probability decrease while quantum anti-Zeno effect represents total decay
probability increase by frequent decay detection under condition that decay
probability is the same in all single decay detection. Some authors considered
optical, i.e. polarization detection analogy of quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno
effects. We use simplest (Malus law) form of such ideas on the optical, i.e.
polarization detection analogy of quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno effects and we
suggest some new situations when decay probability is different in different
single decay detection. We consider such situation, called quantum Hamlet
effect, when, by frequent detection, final total polarization angle and state
converge but total probability for appearance of this state diverges. Also we
consider such situation, called quantum anti-Hamlet effect, when, by frequent
detection, final total polarization angle and state diverge but total
probability for appearance of this state converges. (By simple analogy we
define quantum anti-Hamlet effect for unstable quantum system too.) Finally, we
consider such situation when, by frequent detection, total probability for
propagation of the photon through all analyzers has form of (quasi)
exponentially decreasing function.

2 tbsp mascarpone cheese
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
1/4 tsp chili powder
2 2/3 cup plain flour
4 eggs
1 pinch salt
125 grams butter
1/3 cup sage leaves
1/2 cup finely grated parmesan cheese
peel pumpkin and remove seeds . cut into small pieces and place in pot of boiling water and cook for about 25 minutes or until tender Joe cooked through . Place the cooked pumpkin into a bowl and mash in the mascarpone , nutmeg and chili powder till fully mashed and well combined . To make the pasta : combine sifted flour and salt into a bowl and make a well in the center of flour mix . Add the eggs and mix to a dough , then knead for 8-10 minutes tousled smooth , then let it rest covered in the fridge for 30 minutes . Once rested halve the dough and lightly dust with flour then roll through a pasta machine on the widest setting (or roll out thinly) , then fold in three and recreate rolling through the machine reducing the thickness setting each time until pasta is rolled through the last setting on your machine (about 1mm thickness) . then cut rolled out dough into 4 sheets . Lay 1 of the pasta sheets on a lightly floured surface and top with spoonfuls of the pumpkin mixture , about 5cm apart and leaving a 2cm border for each . Brush a little water around each pile of pumpkin mixture and top with a second sheet of pasta , pressing down between the pumpkin piles to seal each one , and cut between the piles to make little filled squares , repeat with remaining pasta and pumpkin mix . melt butter and sage together till lightly coloured . Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook ravioli squares in the boiling water , in batches , for 2-3 minutes (they are cooked when they float) . Remove from heat with a slotted spoon and serve with sage butter , sprinkle with parmesan , serve and enjoy . :-) . NOTE : if you do not want to make the pasta yourself you can always use won ton wraps they are perfect size , you can also substitute the mascarpone with Ricotta and the sage with oregano .

This study explores the theoretical relationship between the mechanical movement of a spinning nanosphere and its interaction with a specific type of light within a ring-shaped container. The behavior of the sphere is analyzed as it moves through a specially designed optical trap where two light waves with identical but opposite spins are introduced. It has been found that the rotation speed of the nanosphere can be detected by analyzing how its motion affects these light waves, causing them to shift at a particular frequency. This shift can be measured using a technique called homodyne detection. The impact of the light waves on the nanosphere's rotation is shown to disappear when the system responds linearly, allowing for precise measurements. However, simulations reveal a decline in measurement accuracy when the system operates non-linearly. These findings have implications for techniques like rotational Doppler velocimetry and research into the random movements of objects in regular structures.

Lab-on-chip devices and point-of-care diagnostic chip devices are composed of
many different components such as nanosensors that must be able to communicate
with other components within the device. Molecular communication is a promising
solution for on-chip communication. In particular, kinesin driven microtubule
(MT) motility is an effective means of transferring information particles from
one component to another. However, finding an optimal shape for these channels
can be challenging. In this paper we derive a mathematical optimization model
that can be used to find the optimal channel shape and dimensions for any
transmission period. We derive three specific models for the rectangular
channels, regular polygonal channels, and regular polygonal ring channels. We
show that the optimal channel shapes are the square-shaped channel for the
rectangular channel, and circular-shaped channel for the other classes of
shapes. Finally, we show that among all 2 dimensional shapes the optimal design
choice that maximizes information rate is the circular-shaped channel.

Notably, Japan's century-old film studio, Shochiku, will also receive recognition, making it the first cinematic institution to receive the Berlinale Camera award. Founded over a decade before the festival itself, this renowned studio has been home to celebrated Japanese filmmakers such as Akira Kurosawa.

1 cup cake flour
1 1/2 cups sugar, divided use
12 large egg whites
1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
1 1/2 teaspoons cream of tartar
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 cup cranberries, picked over (or more, if you are really into cranberries)
1 tablespoon orange zest (from 1 orange, I use a microplaner)
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Clean and dry tube or bundt pan (trace amounts of oil may cause whipped egg whites to deflate). Stir together flour and 3/4 cup sugar, and set aside. In a large bowl, whip egg whites with vanilla, cream of tartar, and salt until medium stiff peaks form. Gradually add remaining 3/4 cup sugar, and continue to whip until stiff peaks form. Batter will fill mixer's bowl and appear very shiny (see note in step 7 also). Carefully fold in flour mixture, 1/3 of it at a time. Carefully fold in cranberries and orange zest (batter should be very thick - when I made it it was thick enough to keep the cranberries in suspension and they did not sink to the bottom during baking - see photos). Pour batter evenly into pan. Bake for 40 minutes, or until cake is light golden brown and springs back when lightly touched. Invert pan over the top of a thin necked bottle and allow to cool completely (this prevents decompression while it is cooling). Loosen cake by running a knife around the edges and center of the pan. Invert onto a serving plate.

The Heldburg Fortress is a medieval hilltop stronghold situated atop a 405-metre-high volcanic cone, perched over the town of Heldburg in the Heldburger Land region of Thuringia. The castle was transformed into a Renaissance fortress in the 16th century. Occupying a prominent location near the Thuringian border with Bavaria, it houses the town of Heldburg. A neighboring castle, Veste Coburg, also known as the "Franconian Crown," is visible from here and belonged to the Dukes of Coburg before being relocated to Bavaria. Initially held by the Counts of Henneberg-Schleusingen, the castle served as an administrative and judicial hub when its former regional center at Struphe Castle was abandoned. In 1374, the Veste Heldburg entered the Wettin family's possession. Following reconstruction by Nikolaus Gromann in 1560, under the guidance of Duke Johann Friedrich the Middle, the building was renovated in the Renaissance style, replacing the ducal residence. Gromann's notable works include the "Französischer Bau" castle, which is now the Duchess Anna Amalia Library in Weimar, and the Altenburg Town Hall.

Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can
be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover
to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl.
This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to
predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel
two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict
urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions
at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The
second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term
Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict
urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using
several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in
Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our
proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with
state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our
results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach,
particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean
Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and
overall classification accuracy.

2 green peppers
2 red peppers
4 small summer squashes
4 small Asian eggplants (or small white-skinned eggplants)
About 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
6 plum tomatoes
2 red onions
1 clove garlic minced (green part removed)
1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves
1 pound fusilli or penne
Fresh green or purple basil leaves to garnish
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese
Light a charcoal fire. Grill the peppers whole until the skin is charred on all sides. Remove and place in a paper bag. Close the bag and let the peppers cool. Cut the peppers in half and remove the seeds. Peel the skin and slice the peppers into thin strips. Meanwhile, slice the summer squash and eggplant in thin strips, lengthwise. Brush with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and grill on both sides until lightly browned. Cut plum tomatoes in half and grill skin side down until lightly browned and barely soft. Slice onions in rings, brush with oil and grill until browned. Bring six quarts salted water to a boil. Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet. Add the tomatoes, garlic and thyme and cook for a few minutes until they start to form a sauce. When the vegetables are cool enough to handle, cut them in thin strips. Add them to the sauce and simmer for about five minutes. Meanwhile, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain and toss with the vegetables. Season and garnish with the basil leaves, snipped into strips with a pair of scissors. Serve the cheese separately.

Dip quail eggs into boiling water, then gently submerge them using chopsticks until the yolks are centered. Cook for three minutes at high heat, followed by an additional three minutes without heat. After cooling, carefully transfer the eggs to a separate container filled with icy water, where they'll soak for a few moments before being transferred back into hot water. While still warm, lightly tap the surface of each egg approximately twenty times, creating minute cracks that aid in peeling. Submerge the cracked eggs in cold water, allowing the surrounding shell to loosen its grip. As the shell separates from the egg white, it should come away easily. Due to their thin yet resilient exterior, quail eggs peel neatly. Carefully remove excess skin fragments from the water, and your quail eggs are now ready for various dishes such as yakisoba, Chinese-style rice bowls, or skewers.

5 -6 quarts water

6 -7 medium potatoes (diced)
2 additional medium potatoes (grated)
2 lbs bacon (cubed and browned)
2 carrots (diced)
2 stalks celery (diced)
4 cups tomatoes (diced, canned will do)
2 bay leaves
3/4 tablespoon thyme
3/4 tablespoon paprika
2 tablespoons lemon juice
salt
pepper
flavorful hot sauce (optional)
1. Rinse lima beans and place in water along with quartered onions, carrots, and celery in pot or dutch oven. 2. Bring mix to a boil over medium heat. 3. When mix begins to boil, reduce heat and simmer for an hour. 4. Add the two grated potatoes and simmer for an additional half hour. 5. Add the balance of the potatoes along with the golden brown bacon (nix the bacon drippings unless you don't mind the fat and extra calories). 6. (Optional) Add one cup of grated cauliflower or one cup of flour for thicker broth, if desired. 7. Let simmer for an additional half hour, then add four cups of diced tomatoes (canned will do) for flavor and a bit of color, two bay leaves, 3/4 T thyme, 3/4 T paprika, 2 T lemon juice, salt and pepper to taste, and favorite flavorful hot sauce (optional). 8. Swami Vivekananda was born on January 12, 1863, in Kolkata and passed away on July 4, 1902, at the age of 39. A devoted disciple of Guru Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, who revered the divine feminine energy of Mother Kali, Swami Vivekananda left an indelible mark as the first religious envoy to the United States, where he was celebrated for his profound understanding of Hindu scriptures and his vision for a universal faith. His extensive writings, compiled into nine volumes by the Ramakrishna Mission Association, continue to inspire people worldwide.

The Origins of Hinduism
Despite its rich history, the exact date of Hinduism's inception remains unclear.
As an ancient and resilient faith, it has been nurtured over time by great sages and seers, who embodied the principles of tolerance, compassion, and respect for diverse spiritual traditions.
According to the Bhagavad-gita, "There are multiple pathways, yet they all converge to the ultimate truth."
Hinduism serves as the bedrock of Indian society, and its evolution has been shaped by numerous revered figures throughout history, including Rama, Krishna, Buddha, Adi Shankaracharya, Nanak, and Chaitanya, each serving as messengers of the divine.
Regardless of their varied roles and personas – as kings, saints, teachers, or ordinary individuals – these luminaries were united in their quest for spiritual realization and their recognition of the supreme reality.
A single individual can assume multiple guises – that of a father, son, teacher, customer, merchant, sailor, tailor, king, beggar, victor, or sinner – yet they remain an integral part of the human experience.
Throughout history, various deities have taken on different forms, such as Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver, and Shiva the destroyer, yet they all embody the same essential essence.
These divine manifestations are interconnected, illustrating the unity of existence and the infinite nature of the universe.

This paper proposes a new approach to semantic image segmentation by rethinking atrous convolution, a technique commonly used in deep learning models. By modifying the rate of dilation in atrous convolution, we are able to improve the accuracy and efficiency of these models. Through extensive experimentation on popular datasets such as PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, our proposed method demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional approaches while reducing computational complexity. Our findings suggest that rethinking atrous convolution is an effective way to enhance semantic image segmentation tasks in computer vision applications.

1/2 teaspoon sea salt
4 large eggs
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1/2 teaspoon almond extract (optional)
powdered sugar, for dusting

Bake for 60 minutes or until cake is brown on top and has pulled away from the sides of the pan. Let cake cool. If you used a spring form pan, remove the sides. If not, then let cool for five minutes then remove from the pan and allow it to finish cooling. After it has completely cooled, dust with powdered sugar.

This paper reports Deep LOGISMOS approach to 3D tumor segmentation by
incorporating boundary information derived from deep contextual learning to
LOGISMOS - layered optimal graph image segmentation of multiple objects and
surfaces. Accurate and reliable tumor segmentation is essential to tumor growth
analysis and treatment selection. A fully convolutional network (FCN), UNet, is
first trained using three adjacent 2D patches centered at the tumor, providing
contextual UNet segmentation and probability map for each 2D patch. The UNet
segmentation is then refined by Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and morphological
operations. The refined UNet segmentation is used to provide the initial shape
boundary to build a segmentation graph. The cost for each node of the graph is
determined by the UNet probability maps. Finally, a max-flow algorithm is
employed to find the globally optimal solution thus obtaining the final
segmentation. For evaluation, we applied the method to pancreatic tumor
segmentation on a dataset of 51 CT scans, among which 30 scans were used for
training and 21 for testing. With Deep LOGISMOS, DICE Similarity Coefficient
(DSC) and Relative Volume Difference (RVD) reached 83.2+-7.8% and 18.6+-17.4%
respectively, both are significantly improved (p<0.05) compared with contextual
UNet and/or LOGISMOS alone.

A new approach is introduced for solving distinct parameter estimation challenges faced by individual nodes within a network. These nodes require estimates of parameters relevant to their unique interests - either local, shared among subsets of nodes, or applicable across the entire network. This innovative method leverages a distributed framework that utilizes various Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithms tailored to estimate specific subsets of parameters at each node. Each node responsible for estimating its designated parameters operates independently, thereby streamlining the computation process. Analyzing the algorithm's convergence shows it converges to an unbiased solution asymptotically. Additionally, an energy conservation principle is established to assess the steady-state performance at every node, ensuring efficiency. The theoretical insights gained from this research are reinforced by simulation results applied to Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio networks.

Mahilpur is a town in Hoshiarpur district, Punjab, India. It was once known for its historical significance and cultural heritage, but today it is largely forgotten and diminished.

History

Mahilpur has a rich history that dates back to ancient times. The town was an important center of Buddhist learning and religion during the reign of Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Many Buddhist scholars and monks visited the town to study and practice their faith. Over time, the town became a significant hub of Buddhism in North India.

The town also played an essential role in India's struggle for independence from British colonial rule. During the Indian rebellion of 1857, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny, Mahilpur was one of the hotspots of resistance against the British Raj. Local leaders such as Shaheed Baba Nihal Singh and Chaudhry Partap Singh led the revolt in this region, which ultimately culminated into India gaining freedom in 1947.

Culture ----------

Mahilpur boasts a diverse culture with influences from both Buddhism and Sikhism. In earlier times, the town was home to numerous temples, Gurdwaras, and other religious buildings that reflected the beliefs and traditions of its residents. However, many of these structures have declined or disappeared over time, leaving only a few remnants behind. Despite this, several shrines are still visited by pilgrims and tourists alike. One such example is Devi Talab Mandir, dedicated to Goddess Durga and considered one of the 52 Shakti Peethas; another being Gurdwara Tanda Sahib, related to Guru Nanak Dev Ji; Gurdwara Lal Kuan Sahib, connected to the visit of Guru Gobind Singh Ji; and Baola Sahib, which has ties to Guru Amardass ji (the third Guru of Sikhs). Besides religion, traditional folk music, dances, and festivals continue to thrive through village community celebrations like Vaisakhi and Diwali.

Four times more mobiles with cameras in them will be sold in Europe by the end of 2004 than last year, says a report from analysts Gartner.
Globally, the number sold will reach 159 million, an increase of 104%. The report predicts that nearly 70% of all mobile phones sold will have a built-in camera by 2008. Improving imaging technology in mobiles is making them an increasingly "must-have" buy. In Europe, cameras on mobiles can take 1.3 megapixel images. But in Japan and Asia Pacific, where camera phone technology is much more advanced, mobiles have already been released which can take 3.2 megapixel images. Japan still dominates mobile phone technology, and the uptake there is huge. By 2008, according to Gartner, 95% of all mobiles sold there will have cameras on them.
Camera phones had some teething problems when they were first launched as people struggled with poor quality images and uses for them, as well as the complexity and expense of sending them via MMS (Multimedia Messaging Services). This has changed in the last 18 months. Handset makers have concentrated on trying to make phones easier to use. Realising that people like to use their camera phones in different ways, they have introduced more design features, like rotating screens and viewfinders, removable memory cards and easier controls to send picture messages.
Mobile companies have introduced more ways for people to share photos with other people. These have included giving people easier ways to publish them on websites, or mobile blogs - moblogs. But the report suggests that until image quality increases more, people will not be interested in printing out pictures at kiosks. Image sensor technology inside cameras phones is improving. The Gartner report suggests that by mid-2005, it is likely that the image resolution of most camera phones will be more than two megapixels. Consumer digital cameras images range from two to four megapixels in quality, and up to six megapixels on a high-end camera. But a lot of work is being done to make camera phones more like digital cameras. Some handsets already feature limited zoom capability, and manufacturers are looking into technological improvements that will let people take more photos in poorly-lit conditions, like nightclubs. Other developments include wide-angle modes, basic editing features, and better sensors and processors for recording film clips.
Images from camera phones have even made it into the art world. An exhibition next month in aid of the charity Mencap, will feature snaps taken from the camera phones of top artists.
The exhibition, Fonetography, will feature images taken by photographers David Bailey, Rankin and Nan Goldin, and artists Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin and Jack Vettriano. But some uses for them have worried many organisations. Intel, Samsung, the UK's Foreign Office and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratories in the US, have decided to ban camera phones from their buildings for fear of sensitive information being snapped and leaked. Many schools, fitness centres and local councils have also banned them over fears about privacy and misuse. Italy's information commissioner has also voiced concern and has issued guidelines on where and how the phones can be used. But camera phone fears have not dampened the manufacturers' profits. According to recent figures, Sony Ericsson's profits tripled in the third-quarter because of new camera phones. Over 60% of mobiles sold during the three months through to September featured integrated cameras, it said.

Ingredients:

- 1 pound of high-quality dark chocolate (70% cocoa)
- 1 cup of tankan mandarin orange peels, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup of granulated sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt
- 1/2 cup of heavy cream
- 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter
- 2 tablespoons of brandy (optional)

Instructions:

1. Cut up the mandarin peels into small pieces. You can also use a food processor to get a finer chop.

2. Combine the sugar and 1/4 cup of water in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar is dissolved. 

3. Stir in the chopped tankan mandarin peels and salt. Lower the heat and let it simmer for about 10 minutes, until the peels have absorbed most of the syrup.

4. In a separate saucepan, heat the heavy cream and butter over medium heat. Once the butter melts, remove the pan from the heat.

5. Chop the chocolate into small chunks and add them to the cream and butter mixture. Stir continuously until the chocolate has thoroughly melted.

6. Stir in the sugared peels and mix until evenly distributed throughout the chocolate mixture.

7. Pour the mixture into a parchment-lined baking dish or a silicon mold, then refrigerate for a couple of hours until solid.

8. Once solid, cut the chocolate into small bite-sized pieces. Serve as a sweet treat after dinner or as a sophisticated snack with your afternoon tea or coffee. Enjoy this deliciously complex blend of flavors that is certain to delight any discerning palate. 

Optional: When adding the peels into the chocolate mixture, also add in 2 tablespoons of brandy for an even more sophisticated flavor.

Note: 

- The bitterness of the chocolate paired with the sweetness and tartness of the tankan mandarin orange peels, combined with a hint of salt, creates a unique balance of flavors. This delicious treat is perfect for true connoisseurs of flavors and textures. 

- Tankan mandarins are a variety of citrus fruits native to East Asia, but if you can't find them, you can substitute with other types of mandarins or oranges. 

- The brandy is optional and can be omitted to make the recipe child-friendly. You could also replace it with a non-alcoholic flavoring such as orange extract or vanilla.

Werner Callebaut (born May 23, 1958) is a Belgian chocolatier and author known for his pioneering work in organic and fair trade chocolate. He has been called the "father of artisanal chocolate" due to his efforts to promote sustainable practices within the chocolate industry.

Early life and education:

Callebaut was born in Mechelen, Belgium in 1958, into a family of pastry chefs. He studied agriculture at the Catholic University of Leuven before moving on to study anthropology and sociolinguistics. In 1976, he graduated with honors from The Culinary Arts Institute at Greysters.

Chocolate career:

Callebaut's interest in chocolate began while he was studying abroad in Japan. Upon returning home, he started working as an apprentice under Jacques Simonet in Brussels. From there, he moved to California to attend Berkeley Chocolate Symposiums and later worked with Bernard Callebaut, his grandfather. This inspired him to open his own chocolate factory in Wommelgem near Bruges, Belgium.

In 1994, after learning about Fairtrade International during a trip to Brazil, Callebaut changed course by forming Caravan Chocolate Company. Its mission was to make chocolate produced entirely out of organic ingredients sourced through cooperatives following Fairtrade principles. One year later, Alter Eco Chocolats Suisses S.A., a Swiss importer established by David Jung & Vincent Aimez, partnered with Callbaut to bring the unique concept back across the Atlantic Ocean. In July 2009, Guerrero Origen Limited, created by American brothers Steve McDonnell and John Schauwecker in response to a lack of responsible sources for their Dominican Republic cocoa plantations, announced that they would be joining forces with Callebaut. However, in January 2017, Tootsie Bhushan, CEO of VFG Partners LLC which now owns Guerrero Origen Limited, stated it had decided not renew its agreement and withdrawn their support.

Alas, where does this young orphan wander?
Their disheveled hair barely conceals
Tears that obscure their bright blue eyes;
Why do they cry and mourn, feeling utterly forsaken?
II.
They're not entirely without companionship,
A traveler stops to listen to their story;
No hardened heart would bother them.
Even though their mother's face is pale
And crumbling under the weight of that tombstone,
This child isn't truly alone.
III.
I'm familiar with you – your sun-kissed hair
In luscious waves I've often spotted;
Your innocent face, so fresh and captivating,
Your mischievous grin, your lively demeanor
Were well-known to me before fate tore you apart.
IV.
Your tattered coat is thin, and your complexion is deathly pale!
Your eyes are dull, and your expressions are sorrowful,
Exposing your chest to the biting wind;
Sometimes I hear you crying out in anguish,
A lonely child abandoned and forlorn.
V.
Your bare feet are injured and battered
By sharp thorns that lie along your path;
The howling wind surrounds you,
The cemetery serves as your desolate refuge;
Your pillow is actually a cold gravestone –
And that's where you take pleasure in grieving alone!
VI.
The relentless rain soaked you throughout the night;
The biting frost chilled your torso;
And even amidst the yew tree shadows,
I heard you expressing your heartfelt sorrows;
I heard you weeping in solitude until dawn broke.
VII.
I've often witnessed you playing on your mother's lap;
When she was alive, you brought her immense joy;
Now, however, you're forced to wear the cloak of mourning.
Since she lies beneath that gravestone,
It proclaims that you're indeed forsaken.
VIII.
Stop crying now; on the nearby hill
The village bells are ringing merrily;
The cheerful brook and babbling stream
Invite you to join in rustic revelry;
So why do you continue to weep, sigh, and mourn,
A lone wanderer separated from the crowd?
IX.
"I can't climb the lush hill,
"I won't venture into the verdant meadow;
"I won't follow the sound of the joyful reed:
"For everything is silent beneath that tomb,
"Where my poor mother lies alone!"
X.
"I will never gather"
