The Liberian economy started to grow in 2004, but "sustained and deep reform efforts" are needed to ensure long term growth, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said.
An IMF mission made the comments in a report published following 10 days of talks with the transition government. The IMF said that, according to data provided by the Liberians, the country's GDP rose by 2% in 2004, after a 31% decline in 2003. Liberia is recovering from a 14-year civil war that came to an end in 2003. The power-sharing National Transition Government of Liberia will remain in place until elections on 11 October, the first presidential and parliamentary ballots since the conflict ended.
The IMF said Liberia's economy started to grow last year thanks to a "continued strong recovery in rubber production, domestic manufacturing and local services including post-conflict reconstruction". The IMF however remains cautious about what it sees as a lack of transparency in government actions. In particular, it pointed to mystery surrounding the sale of iron ore stockpiles and the alleged disappearance of some import and export permits. These matters are now being investigated by the Liberian authorities and the IMF has called for their findings to be made public. The IMF also said it was crucial that the Central Bank of Liberia be strengthened, the national budget be effectively managed and a sound economic basis built to allow the country's large external debt to be addressed. "The IMF team stands ready to assist the (Liberian) authorities in strengthening the areas mentioned," said the report. "The team agreed with the (Liberian) authorities that the period until elections and the inauguration of a new government will pose exceptional challenges to fiscal management, and expresses its willingness to provide...continued support."

Calabrian wine (Italian: Vino Calabrese) is Italian wine from the Calabria region of southern Italy. Over 90% of the region's wine production is red wine, with a large portion made from the Gaglioppo grape. Calabria has 12 Denominazione di origine controllata (DOC) regions, but only 4% of the yearly production is classified as DOC wine. The region is one of Italy's most rural and least industrialized with per capita income less than half of the national average. Following World War II, many of Calabria's inhabitants emigrated to Northern Italy, the United States, Australia and Argentina. Those left behind have been slow to develop a vibrant wine industry with only the red wines of Cirò garnering much international attention. Today Calabrian wines are mostly produced to high alcohol levels and sold to co-operatives who transfer the wines to the northern Italian wine regions to use as blending component. There are no Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita (DOCG) regions, but Calabria does have 12 Indicazione Geografica Tipica (IGT) designations. History

In this paper, we propose an efficient semidefinite programming (SDP)
approach to worst-case linear discriminant analysis (WLDA). Compared with the
traditional LDA, WLDA considers the dimensionality reduction problem from the
worst-case viewpoint, which is in general more robust for classification.
However, the original problem of WLDA is non-convex and difficult to optimize.
In this paper, we reformulate the optimization problem of WLDA into a sequence
of semidefinite feasibility problems. To efficiently solve the semidefinite
feasibility problems, we design a new scalable optimization method with
quasi-Newton methods and eigen-decomposition being the core components. The
proposed method is orders of magnitude faster than standard interior-point
based SDP solvers.
  Experiments on a variety of classification problems demonstrate that our
approach achieves better performance than standard LDA. Our method is also much
faster and more scalable than standard interior-point SDP solvers based WLDA.
The computational complexity for an SDP with $m$ constraints and matrices of
size $d$ by $d$ is roughly reduced from $\mathcal{O}(m^3+md^3+m^2d^2)$ to
$\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ ($m>d$ in our case).

I decided to check out the movie after hearing all the hype surrounding it, having been moderately satisfied with Illumination's previous works without being blown away. Given the positive reception of Secret Life of Pets, I held onto the hope that this film might mark a turning point for Illumination, showcasing exceptional animation, storytelling, and character development. 

However, my experience with the movie left me underwhelmed. Upon watching the trailers, I noticed striking similarities to Toy Story, which raised concerns about predictability – and unfortunately, these concerns were confirmed. Although the film introduced various elements, the overall narrative felt fairly formulaic. One potentially poignant storyline involved Duke discovering his long-lost owner had passed away, a plot twist reminiscent of Finding Dory's heart-wrenching revelation about her parents' demise. Unfortunately, this scene fell flat due to its lack of emotional delivery; instead of showing the news, it relied on a random feline character to inform Duke, which left little impact. Furthermore, Duke's reaction to this news was surprisingly muted, especially considering the extensive flashbacks showcasing his bond with his owner. Liberal Democrat leader Charles Kennedy criticized Gordon Brown's budget, calling it "fundamentally unfair." He questioned how the lowest-income 20% continued to bear a larger burden compared to the highest 20%. The proposed £200 council tax rebate for pensioners was insufficient to rectify the issue. According to Kennedy, the government must fundamentally reform the tax system rather than just make temporary fixes. Speaking ahead of the likely general election, he noted that the UK enjoyed great economic success but expressed disappointment in the lack of progress on council tax revaluation. He warned that millions of English households would face significant increases after the revaluation. In response to the Chancellor's limited rebate, Kennedy proposed a local income tax that would save typical households over £450 annually, exempting half of all pensioners from taxation and benefiting approximately three million people. On pensions, Kennedy deemed it a "scandal" that the current system unfairly penalized mothers who missed National Insurance payments during child-rearing years. He vowed to abolish this inequality by eliminating the residency criterion. Kennedy's party prioritizes offering free long-term care for the elderly, eliminating university tuition fees, and replacing the council tax with an increased 50% income tax on those earning above £100,000 per year. This approach contrasts with Brown's earlier pledge not to raise income tax, which was later superseded by increased National Insurance contributions after the election.

Orris George Walker (born June 5, 1925) is an American former middle-distance runner. He competed in the men's 1500 metres at the 1948 Summer Olympics. In his career he won the AAU title thirteen times, the NCAA title nine times, the Canadian Amateur title three times, the Pan-American title twice, and broke ten world records. He went to college at Santa Clara University, where he majored in Electrical Engineering. At Santa Clara he joined the track team, and after a disappointing first year in track, which he attributed to having an injury, and after he came in eighth place in the national junior college championships, he turned all his attention to track and became one of the great milers of all time. He earned All-American honours three times, in 1946, 1947 and 1948, and was part of the winning team in the 1947 NCAA cross-country meet. In his senior year at Santa Clara he won national titles in the 440 yd (400 m), 880 yd (800 m), and mile (1500 m). In both the 880 yd and mile races he set a new world record. After graduating in 1948 he turned professional and started racing professionally at many venues in North America. He won the Professional title in the mile eight times (and nine times overall), the 880 yd once, and the 440 yd twice. In 1946 and 1947 he broke the professional mile record five times. Pan-European group Euronext is poised to launch a bid for the London Stock Exchange, UK media reports say.
Last week, the LSE rejected a takeover proposal from German rival Deutsche Boerse - the 530 pence-a-share offer valued the exchange at about £1.35bn. The LSE, which saw its shares rise 25%, said the bid undervalued the business. Euronext - formed after the Brussels, Paris and Amsterdam exchanges merged - is reportedly working with three investment banks on a possible offer. The LSE, Europe's biggest stock market, is a key prize, listing stocks with a total capitalisation of £1.4 trillion.
Euronext already has a presence in London due to its 2001 acquisition of London-based options and futures exchange Liffe. Trades on the LSE are cleared via Clearnet, in which Euronext has a quarter stake.
Euronext, which also operates an exchange in Lisbon, last week appointed UBS and ABN Amro as additional advisors. It is also working with Morgan Stanley. Despite the rejection of the Deutsche Boerse bid last week, Werner Seifert, chief executive of the Frankfurt-based exchange, may well come back with an improved offer. It has long wanted to link up with London, and the two tried and failed to seal a merger in 2000. Responding to the LSE's rebuff, Deutsche Boerse - whose market capitalisation is more than £3bn - said it believed it could show its proposal offered benefits, and that it still hoped to make a cash bid.
Last week the LSE said not only was the bid undervalued, but that it had "been advised that there can be no assurance that any transaction could be successfully implemented". However, it has indicated it is open for further talks. Meanwhile, German magazine Der Spiegel said part of Mr Seifert's negotiations with the LSE were about where to base the future board of any merged exchange. While Mr Seifert has suggested a merged company would be run out of London, the mayor of Frankfurt has raised concerns that such a move could cost German jobs. Many analysts believe German Boerse has more financial firepower than Euronext if it came to a bidding war.

Med Hondo (born Mohamed Abid Hondo; 4 May 1936 – 2 March 2019) was a Mauritanian-born French actor, producer, screenwriter and film director. He emigrated to France in 1959 and began to work in film during the 1960s. He received critical acclaim for his 1970 directorial début Soleil O. Biography
Hondo was born in 1936 in Ain Oul Beri Mathar in the Atar region of Mauritania. His mother was Mauritanian and his father Senegalese. In 1954 Hondo went to Rabat, Morocco, to train to become a chef at the International Hotel School there. He emigrated to France in 1959 and found work first in Marseille and then in Paris, variously as a cook, farm labourer, waiter, dockworker and delivery man. He found that he and other African immigrants were unable to gain work in their chosen professions, and in the menial jobs they could find, they were paid less than the French. The difficulty of making a living during this time, as well as the racism he experienced, eventually provided inspiration for his films, including Soleil O and Les 'bicots-Nègres' vos voisins.

Reducing the need for extensive supervision is crucial in image segmentation since densely labeled datasets require substantial human oversight. To alleviate this burden, datasets can be labeled using less stringent supervision levels, such as image-level annotations or bounding box labels. Alternatively, semi-supervised settings can capitalize on a limited number of strong annotations and a vast amount of unlabeled data. This paper revisits semi-supervised segmentation techniques and achieves a considerable reduction in annotation time compared to prior approaches. By implementing a straightforward methodology, we show that at lower annotation budgets, semi-supervised methods consistently outshine weakly-supervised alternatives in both semantic and instance segmentation tasks. Furthermore, our approach surpasses existing semi-supervised methods in terms of labeling efficiency. We evaluate our results on the popular Pascal VOC benchmark and provide a unified comparison of weakly and semi-supervised methods by taking into account the overall annotation expenditure, thereby enabling a more equitable assessment among techniques.

The US movie industry has launched legal action to sue people who facilitate illegal film downloading.
The Motion Picture Association of America wants to stop people using the program BitTorrent to swap movies. The industry is targeting people who run websites which provide information and internet links to movies which have been copied or filmed in cinemas. More than 100 server operators have been targeted in the actions launched in the US and UK, the MPAA added. The suits were filed against users of the file-sharing programs BitTorrent, eDonkey and DirectConnect in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Finland and the Netherlands, the MPAA said.
BitTorrent users can download movies by following a link to files which are found on websites called trackers. Unlike most peer-to-peer programs BitTorrent works by sharing a file, which could be anything from a legitimate digital photo to a copied movie, among multiple users at the same time. The movie industry hopes that suing the people who run the trackers will cut BitTorrent users off from illegal movies at source. Last month major film studios started legal action against 200 individuals who were swapping films online. The growth in broadband has made it quicker for people to download movies and the industry fears that if it does not take action now, it could suffer the same downturn as the music industry.

The US trade gap has swollen to a record high as strong consumer demand fueled by COVID-19 relief measures continued to push imports to record levels while export growth failed to keep up.

The trade deficit rose to $80.9bn in October, the widest gap on record, as imports hit an all-time high, while exports slipped 1.1% to $288.4bn, according to the Commerce Department.

The gap between what the US buys and sells to the rest of the world had hit a record $73.3bn in September.

Much of the October rise reflected stronger imports of Chinese goods, particularly of copper and steel, as well as toys, games and sporting goods ahead of the Christmas holiday season.

But businesses have also been rushing to stock up on items such as computers and drugs ahead of further US tariffs on Chinese imports which are set to take effect in December.

Meanwhile, a growing disparity in global shipping speeds as well as shortages of container ships is likely to continue to hit US export growth. Boarder officials have also struggled to keep up with the rapid shift in trading patterns.

"The fact that the deficit is widening to record levels despite a slowdown in imports of crude oil suggests that the problems many exporters are facing with shipping are continuing to impact trade flows," said Ian Shepherdson, chief economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

The transport bottlenecks come as businesses battle a shortage of workers in key sectors like trucking, warehousing and logistics, as well as a lack of key components such as semiconductors which are needed to make a wide range of goods.

As Yahoo celebrates a decade online, its status as a pioneering force in the digital landscape is undeniable, having weathered the turbulent dot-com bubble and maintained its position among the top web brands. However, a new rival, Google, has been steadily gaining ground, casting a shadow over Yahoo's dominance. Despite sharing similarities, including being the first to issue initial public shares and launching their respective search engines, Yahoo's strategic decision to outsource its search function to Google in 2000 has left analysts questioning its judgment. According to Olivier Beauvillain, a Jupiter analyst, this move was a significant blunder, as Yahoo prioritized building a portal business while underestimating the importance of search engine capabilities, which ultimately became a key area of competition for the company. In recent years, Yahoo has attempted to rectify this oversight by refocusing on search, yet Beauvillain notes that Google has successfully established itself as a comprehensive platform beyond mere search technology. Meanwhile, Allen Weiner, research director at Gartner, posits that the future of search will shift from technological advancements to providing premium content and user-friendly interfaces, suggesting that Yahoo must adapt to remain relevant.

In the dark and damp of the alley cold,
Lay the Christmas tree that hadn't been sold;
By a shopman dourly thrown outside;
With the ruck and rubble of Christmas-tide;
Trodden deep in the muck and mire,
Unworthy even to feed a fire...
So I stopped and salvaged that tarnished tree,
And thus is the story it told to me:
"My Mother was Queen of the forest glade,
And proudly I prospered in her shade;
For she said to me: 'When I am dead,
You will be monarch in my stead,
And reign, as I, for a hundred years,
A tower of triumph amid your peers,
When I crash in storm I will yield you space;
Son, you will worthily take my place.'
"So I grew in grace like a happy child,
In the heart of the forest free and wild;
And the moss and the ferns were all about,
And the craintive mice crept in and out;
And a wood-dove swung on my highest twig,
And a chipmunk chattered: 'So big! So big!'
And a shy fawn nibbled a tender shoot,
And a rabbit nibbled under my root...
Oh, I was happy in rain and shine
As I thought of the destiny that was mine!
Then a man with an axe came cruising by
And I knew that my fate was to fall and die.
"With a hundred others he packed me tight,
And we drove to a magic city of light,
To an avenue lined with Christmas trees,
And I thought: may be I'll be one of these,
Tinselled  with silver and tricked with gold,
A lovely sight for a child to behold;
A-glitter with lights of every hue,
Ruby and emerald, orange and blue,
And kiddies dancing, with shrieks of glee -
One might fare worse than a Christmas tree.
"So they stood me up with a hundred more
In the blaze of a big department store;
But I thought of the forest dark and still,
And the dew and the snow and the heat and the chill,
And the soft chinook and the summer breeze,
And the dappled deer and the birds and the bees...
I was so homesick I wanted to cry,
But patient I waited for someone to buy.
And some said 'Too big,' and some 'Too small,'
And some passed on saying nothing at all.
Then a little boy cried: Ma, buy that one,'
But she shook her head: 'Too dear, my son."
So the evening came, when they closed the store,
And I was left on the littered floor,
A tree unwanted, despised, unsold,
Thrown out at last in the alley cold."
Then I said: "Don't sorrow; at least you'll be
A bright and beautiful New Year's tree,
All shimmer and glimmer and glow and gleam,
A radiant sight like a fairy dream.
For there is a little child I know,
Who lives in poverty, want  and woe;
Who lies abed from morn to night,
And never has known an hour's delight..."
So I stood the tree at the foot of her bed:
"Santa's a little late," I said.
"Poor old chap! Snowbound on the way,
But he's here at last, so let's be gay."
Then she woke from sleep and she saw you there,
And her eyes were love and her lips were prayer.
And her thin little arms were stretched to you
With a yearning joy that they never knew.
She woke from the darkest dark to see
Like a heavenly vision, that Christmas Tree.
Her mother despaired and feared the end,
But from that day she began to mend,
To play, to sing, to laugh with glee...
Bless you, O little Christmas Tree!
You died, but your life was not in vain:
You helped a child to forget her pain,
And let hope live in our hearts again.

US singer Stacey Q has amassed a diverse discography consisting of five full-length albums, one compilation album, an EP, thirteen singles, four promotional tracks, and six music videos. Born Stacey Swain, she initially rose to fame as the lead vocalist for SSQ, a project initiated by record producer Jon St. James. In 1985, Swain began exploring solo material, maintaining ties with St. James and the original SSQ lineup. Following the release of her self-titled EP on On the Spot Records, Swain secured a deal with Atlantic Records and unveiled her debut studio album, Better Than Heaven, in 1986. This marked her entry into the mainstream, debuting at sixty-nine on the US Billboard 200 chart and earning a gold certification in the United States. The lead single, "Two of Hearts," garnered widespread critical acclaim and considerable commercial success, reaching third place on the Billboard Hot 100 and becoming one of the top-performing singles of 1986. Her subsequent single, "We Connect," also achieved moderate success, peaking at thirty-five on the same chart. However, "Insecurity" and "Music Out of Bounds" failed to replicate this level of performance as singles.

Germany's unemployment figure rose above the psychologically important level of five million last month.
On Wednesday, the German Federal Labour Agency said the jobless total had reached 5.037 million in January, which takes the jobless rate to 12.1%. "Yes, we have effectively more than five million people unemployed," a government minister said earlier on ZDF public television. Unemployment has not been this high in Germany since the 1930s.
Changes to the way the statistics are compiled partly explain the jump of 572,900 in the numbers. But the figures are embarrassing for the government. "With the figures apparently the worst we've seen in the post-war period, these numbers are very charged politically," said Christian Jasperneite, an economist with MM Warburg. "They could well put an end to the recent renaissance we've seen by the SPD [the ruling Social Democrats] in the polls, and with state elections due in Schleswig-Holstein and North Rhine-Westphalia, they may have an adverse effect on the government's chances there."
The opposition also made political capital from the figures. It said there are a further 1.5 million-2 million people on subsidised employment schemes who are, in fact, looking for real jobs. It added that government reforms, including unpopular benefit cuts, do not go far enough. Under the government's controversial "Hartz IV" reforms, which came into effect at the beginning of the year, both those on unemployment benefits and welfare support and those who are long-term unemployed are officially classified as looking for work. The bad winter weather also took its toll, as key sectors such as the construction sector laid off workers. Adjusted for the seasonal factors, the German jobless total rose by 227,000 in January from December.

A number of ancient civilizations, including the Thracians, ancient Greeks, Scythians, Celts, ancient Romans, Goths (Ostrogoths and Visigoths), Slavs (East and West Slavs), Varangians and the Bulgars have left their mark on the culture, history and heritage of Bulgaria. Due to this great variety of influences, Bulgaria has adopted many unusual traditions. Thracian artifacts include numerous temples, tombs, golden treasures and ancient rites and rituals, while ancient Bulgars have left traces of their heritage in statehood, early architecture, music and dances. Thracian rituals such as the Tryphon Zarezan which is dedicated to Saint Tryphon of Campsada, Kukeri and Martenitza are to this day kept alive in the modern Bulgarian culture.
The oldest treasure of worked gold in the world, dating back to the 5th millennium BC, comes from the site of the Varna Necropolis. Bulgaria functioned as the hub of Slavic Europe during much of the Middle Ages, exerting considerable literary and cultural influence over the Eastern Orthodox Slavic world by means of the Preslav and Ohrid Literary Schools. Bulgaria also gave the world the Cyrillic script, the second most widely used alphabet and sixth writing system in the world, which originated in these two schools in the tenth century.

Arie Lev Gruzman, born on October 3, 1970, is a distinguished professor of medicinal chemistry at Bar Ilan University. Born in what is now Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, Gruzman pursued a nursing degree, graduating summa cum laude in 1988. He then entered the pediatric faculty of Gorky Academy for Medicine before shifting focus to medical studies. In 1991, Gruzman relocated to Israel to continue his MD studies, completing a Bachelor of Science in medicinal chemistry at Bar-Ilan University in 1995 and earning a doctoral degree with honors from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. Following military service, Gruzman held postdoctoral research positions at UCSF and the California Pacific Medical Center from 2004 to 2007, guided by Professors Vishvanath Lingappa and others. Subsequently, he led a project at Yissum Research Development Company focused on developing an antidiabetic medication. Gruzman joined Bar Ilan University's chemistry department in 2009 and has since held leadership roles, including vice president of the Israel Chemical Society's medicinal chemistry section from 2011 to 2015. He co-founded the startup drug development firm AltA-ZuZ.

Tina von Lambert, wife of psychiatrist Otto von Lambert, has fled to an unnamed North African country (referred to as M.), where she is found raped and murdered in the [desert]. Otto hires F., a filmmaker, to travel to M. and reconstruct his wife's murder. The Chief of Police appears to be cooperative, however, after a police-escorted visit to the Al-Hakim ruins where the body was found, F.'s cameraman reveals that his footage has been replaced. The police then allow F. to question a number of foreign agents being held and tortured at the police ministry, all of whom tell her the same vague, inconclusive story, none confessing to the crime. Later, F. is taken to observe the execution of a Scandinavian spy in the central courtyard of the police compound; the Chief of Police claims that the spy has confessed to the crime and that the case is solved. They are shown the video of their investigation, which includes none of their footage; instead it has been turned into a propaganda film featuring the police. In despair, F. leaves her crew and walks alone through the marketplace, where she comes across the distinctive red fur coat she knows belonged to Tina von Lambert. She purchases the coat and wears it back to her hotel. At the hotel F.'s cameraman tells her that his footage has again been taken, this time that of the execution, and that aeroplane tickets out of the country have been booked for them for early the following morning. In her room, F. finds the Head of the Secret Service, who congratulates her on her work and explains that he will use her confiscated footage to expose the corruption, weakness, and incompetence of the Chief of Police, who is planning a coup against the state government. The Head of the Secret Service asks that she continue her investigation under his protection and without the knowledge of the Chief of Police. He offers a new crew, and provides a body double, complete with a red fur coat, to travel home with the old crew in F.'s place. F. is relocated to a derelict hotel, inhabited by a lone, aged maid. Björn Olsen, the cameraman hired by the secret service to assist F., arrives at the hotel and mistakes her for Jytte Sørensen, a Danish journalist; when he realizes his mistake, for F. speaks no Danish, he flees in a panic. Later, the Head of the Secret Police shows F. a gossip magazine with an article titled "Return from the Dead", featuring a photograph of Tina von Lambert reunited with her husband; he explains to her that the murdered woman was in fact Sörensen, a friend of Tina's, to whom Tina had given her red fur coat and passport. The reason for the murder, however, remains a mystery. Determined to find the truth, F. leaves the hotel and heads toward the desert. On the way she finds Olsen's dead body next to his exploded Volkswagen van, and while she examines the disaster she meets the cameraman Polypheme, who is filming her. Polypheme tells F. that he has video footage of Sørensen, who was on the trail of a secret before her death, and offers to show it to F. if she allows him to make a film portrait of her. Despite his dishevelled appearance and apparent drunkenness, she agrees. Polypheme takes F out in to the desert in his Land Rover, and eventually they arrive at a secret subterranean compound. The compound is a vast underground labyrinth, obviously built at great expense, though it appears to be uninhabited by anyone other than Polypheme. F. is taken to a grotesque room and left alone, and there, to her horror, she discovers a series of still frames of Olsen's death. Later in the evening she leaves her room and explores the compound, trying to track down the source of a mysterious hammering sound, which she traces to a locked door with a key in the keyhole. Out of fear she does not go inside. She finds the Land Rover and contemplates fleeing, but again is dissuaded by fear. Unable to locate her original quarters, she finds an empty room and falls asleep. In the morning, F. is found by Polypheme, now clean and sober, and over breakfast he explains the country's political situation. The primary source of revenue for the country is a meaningless war with a neighbouring country over the empty, largely uninhabited desert in which the compound is located. The already ten-year-long war is continued to serve as a testing ground for the military products of weapons-exporting nations, from tanks to intercontinental ballistic missiles. The compound was built to measure the effects of the weapons; at one time it was staffed by human observers, many of whom were eventually replaced by observational machines. Eventually a satellite was put in orbit directly above the compound, followed by a second satellite to observe the first. The satellites made the compound redundant, and the last of the people, excepting Polypheme, left. The power was cut, and the compound was running only on battery reserves which would soon be depleted and force even Polypheme to leave. Polypheme explains that he has taken shelter in the compound and military employment because his habit of collecting sensitive and potentially ruinous photographic documentation of criminals, police, and political figures makes him a target from all sides. Polypheme, when asked how he got his name, explains to F. that it was given to him by a man named Achilles, a bomber pilot and professor of Greek, who named him after the cyclops Polyphemus. He and Achilles were sent on a night raid of Hanoi from the USS Kitty Hawk, and Achilles lands their damaged plane despite sustaining serious head injuries, saving Polypheme in the process. From his wounds Achilles becomes criminally insane and is locked in a cell in a military hospital because of his tendency to rape and murder women. The hammering behind the locked door in the compound is revealed to be Achilles and truth about Jytte Sørensen's rape and murder comes out; Polypheme, indebted to Achilles, provided Sørensen as a sacrifice to the violent beast's only remaining desires. Polypheme shows his film portrait of Sørensen's rape and murder, and explains that F. will be the next victim. F. is taken out in to the desert wearing the red coat, forced to walk in front of the Land Rover carrying Polypheme and Achilles. The setting of Sørensen's portrait was flawed, and this time Polypheme chosen the perfect location out among the ruins of the tanks. F. has accepted her ultimate demise; however, when Achilles is almost upon she is struck by a powerful will to live. At the last possible moment the Chief of Police, his officers, and film crew come out of the tanks, and Achilles is shot repeatedly until he dies. Polypheme races off in the vehicle, but is killed soon after in an explosion, likely from a missile test. F. returns home and her film is rejected without explanation by the television studios. She reads that the Chief of Police and the Head of the Secret Service have been executed by order of the Head of State for high treason and attempting to overthrow the government. The Head of State denies rumours that the desert is being used as a missile test ground. On the opposite page of the newspaper F. reads that a baby boy has been born to Tina and Otto von Lambert.

Orris George Walker, Jr. (November 5, 1942 – February 28, 2015) was seventh bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Long Island. Educational Achievements
Walker was born in Baltimore, Maryland on November 5, 1942. He graduated from Baltimore City College - (a Baltimore magnet high school) in 1960. Later he attended the University of Maryland from where he earned his degree in Political Science and Philosophy in 1964. The 15th Massachusetts Battery (or 15th Battery Massachusetts Light Artillery) was an artillery battery that served in the Union Army during the American Civil War. The unit was organized partly at Camp Chase in Lowell, Massachusetts and partly at Fort Warren during the winter of 1862-1863. The majority of its members were mustered into federal service on February 17, 1863. It was assigned to the Department of the Gulf commanded by Major General Nathaniel P. Banks and departed Massachusetts by steamship on March 9. During its term, the unit suffered from a large number of desertions and gained an unfortunate reputation despite the service of its many loyal members. The unit arrived in New Orleans on April 9, 1863. Before being issued guns, they made a brief expedition on foot to Brashear City, Louisiana but soon returned to New Orleans. They were assigned to garrison two small forts just outside New Orleans, each armed with four 32-pounder guns mounted in barbettes. One of these was located at Bayou St. John and the other at Gentilly. They remained posted there from June 3 until December 29.

Robert Lee Hill, born on June 8, 1892, was a sharecropper from the Arkansas Delta who also became a prominent figure in the fight for civil rights as the founder of the Progressive Farmers and Household Union of America after World War I. Operating primarily in Arkansas, his organization aimed to improve the economic conditions faced by sharecroppers and tenant farmers against white landowners. In 1919, Hill attended a gathering of black farmers near Elaine, Arkansas, but the event turned violent when deputized white men and a black trustee showed up to disrupt it. The ensuing confrontation escalated into what came to be known as the Elaine Massacre, resulting in the deaths of several whites and approximately 100-237 blacks over two days. White militiamen then swept through the area, prompting federal troops to intervene. Robert Lee Hill took refuge in Kansas, where he was eventually arrested and granted release after the NAACP intervened on his behalf. Despite Governor Henry Justin Allen's refusal to extradite Hill due to concerns about his safety and a fair trial in Arkansas, the federal charges were ultimately dropped, allowing Hill to return home in October 1920.

We present a novel semidefinite programming approach to worst-case linear discriminant analysis, building upon traditional linear discriminant analysis but considering the dimensionality reduction from a worst-case perspective, which is generally more robust for classification tasks. However, the original WLDA formulation is non-convex and challenging to optimize. This paper addresses this issue by reformulating the optimization problem as a series of semidefinite feasibility problems, utilizing quasi-Newton methods and eigen-decomposition as key components. Our method outperforms standard interior-point based SDP solvers in terms of speed and scalability. Results from various classification experiments show that our approach yields superior performance compared to standard LDA, surpassing both speed and efficiency. Notably, the computational complexity of our method is significantly reduced, specifically from $\mathcal{O}(m^3+md^3+m^2d^2)$ to $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ when $m>d$, thereby achieving substantial gains in processing time.

The development of a sensitive and efficient neutron detection system is crucial in various scientific applications, particularly in studying ultra-cold neutrons (UCNs). In this study, we present an innovative approach to UCN detection using multi-layer surfaces. The proposed method involves utilizing multiple layers with different materials that have high thermal conductivity but low neutron absorption cross sections. By analyzing the temperature fluctuations across these layers due to the scattering of UCNs, we can effectively detect their presence without significantly absorbing them. We demonstrate through simulations that our multilevel surface detector offers improved sensitivity compared to conventional methods while maintaining a higher efficiency in detecting UCNs. This novel technique has significant potential in enhancing the capabilities of existing UCN experiments and enabling new research avenues in the field of ultracold neutron science.

Co-occurrent visual pattern makes aggregating contextual information a common
paradigm to enhance the pixel representation for semantic image segmentation.
The existing approaches focus on modeling the context from the perspective of
the whole image, i.e., aggregating the image-level contextual information.
Despite impressive, these methods weaken the significance of the pixel
representations of the same category, i.e., the semantic-level contextual
information. To address this, this paper proposes to augment the pixel
representations by aggregating the image-level and semantic-level contextual
information, respectively. First, an image-level context module is designed to
capture the contextual information for each pixel in the whole image. Second,
we aggregate the representations of the same category for each pixel where the
category regions are learned under the supervision of the ground-truth
segmentation. Third, we compute the similarities between each pixel
representation and the image-level contextual information, the semantic-level
contextual information, respectively. At last, a pixel representation is
augmented by weighted aggregating both the image-level contextual information
and the semantic-level contextual information with the similarities as the
weights. Integrating the image-level and semantic-level context allows this
paper to report state-of-the-art accuracy on four benchmarks, i.e., ADE20K,
LIP, COCOStuff and Cityscapes.

In a groundbreaking achievement, scientists have successfully taught a humanoid robot how to run. The robot, named "Atlas," has been able to learn and perform a range of movements, including jogging and sprinting, without any prior programming or human intervention.

The team behind the project, led by researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, used a machine learning algorithm called reinforcement learning to teach Atlas how to run. Reinforcement learning allows robots to learn through trial and error, receiving feedback in the form of rewards or penalties for their actions.

In the case of Atlas, the robot was tasked with moving forward as quickly as possible while maintaining its balance. The team provided Atlas with a reward signal that encouraged it to move faster, but also penalized it when it fell or deviated from a stable gait. Over time, the robot learned to adjust its movements to maximize its speed and stability, eventually developing a running motion that is remarkably similar to that of a human.

"This is a major milestone in robotics," said Dr. Pieter Abbeel, one of the lead researchers on the project. "For the first time, we've been able to teach a humanoid robot how to run without explicitly programming it. This opens up new possibilities for robots to learn complex tasks and adapt to changing environments."

The ability for robots to learn and adapt is particularly important in emergency situations, where pre-programmed instructions may not be sufficient. For example, during a natural disaster, a search and rescue robot could use its ability to learn and adapt to navigate unfamiliar terrain and locate survivors.

While Atlas still has some way to go before it can match the agility and endurance of a human runner, this breakthrough represents a significant step towards creating more advanced and capable robots. As the field of artificial intelligence continues to evolve, we can expect to see even more impressive feats of robotic mobility and dexterity in the years ahead.

The UK's Minister for Immigration, David Milburn, has spoken out in defense of the government's controversial new poster campaign aimed at reducing immigration.

The campaign, which features billboards with slogans such as "Is life here really worth living?", has been criticized by opposition parties and human rights groups who claim it is designed to create a negative image of immigrants and stir up anti-foreigner sentiment.

But speaking on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, Mr. Milburn insisted that the posters were necessary to address the issue of illegal immigration and to promote the benefits of returning home for those who have overstayed their visas.

"We are simply trying to encourage people who are here illegally to return home voluntarily," he said. "It's not about demonizing immigrants or suggesting they are not welcome. We want to make sure we have a fair and controlled system that works for everyone."

Mr. Milburn also rejected suggestions that the campaign was targeting specific ethnic minority groups, saying that the message was intended for anyone who had entered the country without proper documentation.

However, critics argue that the language used in the posters is divisive and could lead to increased discrimination against foreign nationals. Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper described the campaign as "dog whistle politics" and accused the government of using coded messages to appeal to voters' fears.

Human rights organization Amnesty International has also condemned the campaign, calling it a "shameful attempt to scapegoat migrants" and warning that it could contribute to a climate of hostility towards vulnerable communities.

Despite these concerns, Mr. Milburn maintained that the campaign was an important tool in tackling illegal immigration and would continue to run until further notice. He added that the government was committed to creating a fair and balanced approach to immigration policy, but that this required taking tough action against those who flouted the rules.

Alexey Andreyevich Rodin (Russian: Алексе́й Андре́евич Ро́дин; 14 March [O.S. 2 March] 1840 – 19 November [O.S. 7 November] 1917) was a Russian mathematician who made significant contributions to the fields of geometry and trigonometry. He is best known for his work on the theory of triangles, particularly for his proof of the Pythagorean theorem.

Born in Moscow, Russia, Rodin attended the Moscow State University, where he studied mathematics under the tutelage of Dmitri Mendeleev. After graduating from the university in 1861, he worked as a teacher and later as a professor at the same institution. In 1871, he became a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Rodin's most notable work, "The Foundations of Geometry" was published in 1902 and became a widely used textbook on geometry in Russia. In addition to his work on the Pythagorean theorem, he also made significant contributions to the development of trigonometry, including the creation of a new table of trigonometric functions.

Rodin was awarded the Imperial Russian Academy of Sciences' Gold Medal for his contributions to mathematics. He died in Moscow in 1917 at the age of 77.

Roasted Chiles and Corn Bread Recipe:

Ingredients: 
-1 cup all-purpose flour
-3 tablespoons granulated sugar
-2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
-1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
-2 large eggs, beaten
-1 cup milk
-1/2 cup melted butter or vegetable oil
-2 cups roasted red chilies, peeled, seeded and diced
-1 cup corn kernels
-1/4 cup chopped green onions 
-1/4 cup shredded cheese (cheddar or cotija work great)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit (190C). Grease an 8x8 inch baking square with cooking spray or butter. You can also line the bottom of the pan with parchment paper for easy removal.

2. In a medium bowl, mix together the dry ingredients: flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cayenne pepper. Set aside.

3. In another bowl, whisk together wet ingredients: beaten eggs, milk and melted butter or oil. Add in the mixture from step two and stir until well combined. Be careful not to overmix. The batter should be lumpy.

4. Fold in the roasted chilies, corn kernels, green onions, and shredded cheese into the wet mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.

5. Pour the batter into prepared pan and smooth out top with a spatula. Bake for about 35 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean (it might have some moisture since it’s a moist bread but it shouldn’t be raw). Allow cornbread to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

Enjoy this delicious and healthy roasted chile cornbread!

A vast number of people are using the internet to provide assistance following the devastating effects of the tsunami disaster by donating funds through various websites. Several prominent platforms like Google, Yahoo, Ebay, and Amazon have created easy-to-access pages featuring links that direct individuals to reputable organizations offering aid and relief services. In response, an organization called the Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC), formed by 12 leading charities, has established a dedicated website to collect donations, urging people to contribute online whenever possible, as this method allows for faster processing and quicker delivery of aid. The DEC website has already secured nearly £8 million in donations, with over 11,000 transactions occurring within a single hour. To facilitate the high volume of donations, telecommunications company BT took charge of secure payment processing and provided additional logistical support for phone and online appeals, setting up a call center at its London headquarters. Major companies are also contributing by modifying their homepages to feature links to reputable aid-giving organizations, including Oxfam, Doctors Without Borders, and Network for Good. Notably, Google has added a prominent link to its homepage guiding users to a comprehensive list of websites where donations can be made. Furthermore, online retailer Amazon has displayed a prominent notice allowing users to make direct donations to the American Red Cross, which will be utilized for relief efforts.

The search engine Ask Jeeves has announced a new advertising service that aims to revitalize online advertising. The new service, called "Ask Jeeves Direct Answer Ads," aims to provide a more engaging and effective way for businesses to reach their target audience.

Unlike traditional online ads that rely on banners and pop-ups, Ask Jeeves' new service will provide users with direct answers to their search queries, featuring relevant products and services. For example, if a user searches for "best camera for travel," a popup window will appear with information on top cameras for travel, along with links to relevant websites.

According to Ask Jeeves, their new service will be more effective than traditional online advertising methods because it provides a more personalized and useful experience for users. Additionally, the service will use advanced targeting and analytics tools to help businesses track the performance of their ads and make data-driven decisions.

The new service is part of a broader shift in the online advertising industry towards more personalized and relevant advertising methods. Companies like Google and Facebook have already made significant strides in this area, with targeted ads based on users' search history and social media activity.

Ask Jeeves' new service is expected to launch later this year, and the company hopes it will help them compete with larger players in the online advertising market.

Going into the theater, I was under the impression that this was a silly James Franco and Seth Rogen movie that made fun of The Room, a legendary bad movie. That's not what the Disaster Artist is at all. Instead, it celebrates The Room. It celebrates Tommy Wiseau, Greg Sestero, their passion, and their pursuit of a dream.

Sure, The Disaster Artist comments on how The Room bombed terribly; it had to acknowledge this. It comments on the utter lack of acting talent that Tommy and Greg possessed; it had to acknowledge this too. But it handles these details with such delicacy and care that I never felt that it was putting down the characters. Actually, it seemed that the film admired them. Even when the world told them to quit, they never gave up on themselves or each other. The message is surprisingly inspiring.

The movie becomes something more than mere mockery because of the way it handles the relationship between Tommy and Greg with such care and affection. The two genuinely liked each other and saw each other in ways that no one else did. Greg certainly did not understand all of Tommy's methods and decisions, but he understood Tommy's good intentions. Establishing this buddy connection is crucial later in the movie.

After Tommy writes The Room and they begin filming, Tommy expresses his idiosyncrasies in full force. While the film crew sees him as a confusing weirdo, we know there's something more. Despite his utter incompetence in directing and acting and all aspects of filmmaking, we still root him. And we still root for Greg, ever the supportive friend. Tommy makes absurd and confounding choices that don't make sense to Greg and they don't make sense to anyone else either. Even one of Tommy's explanations was simply "people do crazy things." Still, Greg remains loyal.

With as strange as Wiseau behaves, capturing his eccentricities would clearly prove challenging. Give James Franco credit for capturing Wiseau's weirdness in character without ever devolving into derisive mockery. Franco captures his gait, stiff shoulders, hunched posture, indeterminable and inconsistent accent, and his laugh. Watching The Room and hearing Tommy Wiseau laugh, I thought that it sounded completely fake. I chalked it up to another instance of poor acting. But after seeing Wiseau in interviews, I realized that it was his real laugh. To him, the laugh wasn't poor acting because that's what he thinks a genuine laugh sounds like.

Seeing and hearing Wiseau behaving as himself explains a lot about his behavior in The Room. He's just an interesting and very unusual guy. His acting and the acting of others in his movie is still atrocious, but it shifts from startlingly and confusingly bad to understandably bad. And more importantly, seeing the real Tommy makes his movie all the more fun.

You don't need to see The Room to enjoy The Disaster Artist. Would it help? Sure. Seeing The Room first makes many of the inside jokes made in The Disaster Artist funnier and gives a clearer sense of how confoundingly weird the movie truly is. Words cannot do it justice. To understand, you have to see The Room for yourself. I recommend seeing both.

2 cups Oats
1-1/4 cup Flour
1/2 teaspoons Baking Soda
1/2 teaspoons Salt
3/4 cups Butterscotch Chips
1 cup Unsalted Butter, Browned And Cooled
1 cup Brown Sugar
1 whole Egg
2 teaspoons Vanilla
1 cup Walnuts, Chopped
1/2 teaspoons Sea Salt
1 Tablespoon Milk, For Drizzle
1/4 cups Butterscotch Chips, For Drizzle
In a medium saucepan or skillet, heat over medium heat and brown butter. Allow to cool slightly - or place in fridge unti the butter sets, about 20 minutes. Prepare other ingredients while cooling. Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a 13x9 inch baking dish with non stick spray, then line with parchment paper, and spray again with non stick spray to adhere to the bottom of the pan. In a bowl, whisk together the oats, flour, baking soda and salt. Set aside. In another bowl, whisk together egg, vanilla, and brown sugar. Pour in the flour/oat mixture and combine. Add in butterscotch chips, and chopped walnuts. Pour mixture into the baking dish, press in to evenly distribute through the dish. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out with just a few crumbs on it. When done, set on a cooling rack. For glaze, in a microwave safe bowl or cup, melt together remaining butterscotch chips, brown sugar, and milk. Heat in increments to ensure the butterscotch chips do not scorch. Stir to form a glaze. Drizzle over the top of the cooling bars. Sprinkle with sea salt. Cool completely, then slice and serve.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art
performance for automatic medical image segmentation. However, they have not
demonstrated sufficiently accurate and robust results for clinical use. In
addition, they are limited by the lack of image-specific adaptation and the
lack of generalizability to previously unseen object classes. To address these
problems, we propose a novel deep learning-based framework for interactive
segmentation by incorporating CNNs into a bounding box and scribble-based
segmentation pipeline. We propose image-specific fine-tuning to make a CNN
model adaptive to a specific test image, which can be either unsupervised
(without additional user interactions) or supervised (with additional
scribbles). We also propose a weighted loss function considering network and
interaction-based uncertainty for the fine-tuning. We applied this framework to
two applications: 2D segmentation of multiple organs from fetal MR slices,
where only two types of these organs were annotated for training; and 3D
segmentation of brain tumor core (excluding edema) and whole brain tumor
(including edema) from different MR sequences, where only tumor cores in one MR
sequence were annotated for training. Experimental results show that 1) our
model is more robust to segment previously unseen objects than state-of-the-art
CNNs; 2) image-specific fine-tuning with the proposed weighted loss function
significantly improves segmentation accuracy; and 3) our method leads to
accurate results with fewer user interactions and less user time than
traditional interactive segmentation methods.

Premiership footballer and record company boss Kevin Campbell has gained a court injunction stopping R&B singer Mark Morrison from releasing an album.
The Everton striker signed Morrison to his fledging 2 Wikid Records label and claims he spent thousands of pounds producing his album Innocent Man. Now he is attempting to prevent Morrison releasing the album on Monday through another label. But Morrison vowed to ignore the order, saying "no judge is gonna stop me".
Morrison, who is now as well known for his brushes with the law than his music career, rose to fame with the 1996 single Return of the Mack.
But the Leicester singer has struggled to repeat its success following two spells in jail. One was for hiring a stand-in to complete his community service for possession of a stun gun and three-months following a nightclub fracas. He signed to Mr Campbell's label a year ago and has released one single, with the label saying the album was due for release on 24 January. But Mr Campbell said he learned that Morrison planned to release the album through Jet Star, which is advertising it on its website. Mr Campbell said: "I'm glad we were granted the injunction but I'm completely gutted that we have had to go that far. "Mark Morrison was given everything he asked for by 2 Wikid but it seems that he couldn't help but return to his old ways.
"I've worked hard to realise my ambition in football but had hoped that my future career would be in the music business. "I have always dreamt of starting a record label but now Mark Morrison has spoilt that dream for me. There is no loyalty in this business - just greed."
But Morrison is determined the album will be released on Monday. He said: "The injunction is ludicrous. "I signed a new deal with a new record company because I was not getting the support I needed from 2 Wikid. "I was with that label for a year and in that time released just one record, which was not properly promoted. He added: "The whole world is waiting for this album and it will come out on December 27. No injunction or judge will stop it. The Mack will return." The case is set to be heard in the High Court on 20 December.

Boris Johnson, Britain's prime minister since 2019, has announced that he will step down from his position in June after leading the country through several tumultuous years including Brexit and COVID-19 pandemic. In a brief statement issued by 10 Downing Street on Friday morning, Boris Johnson said: "I have always understood politics to be about serving people – first as their member of parliament then later as Prime Minister - but now I want to serve our great nation differently." 

Confirming speculation that had been swirling around him for weeks, Mr Johnson did not specify what his future plans might hold beyond retiring from frontline political life, simply saying it was time 'to give someone else': an opportunity'. His decision to retire comes just before local elections this May, which were seen as testing ground national mood ahead general election next year, with poll suggesting party could face crushing defeat if PM remains at helm.

The European Union has made good on its threat to scrap EU software patents, and in its place will promote an open, free and universal digital society.

In June 2011 it emerged that many technology companies were unhappy with how the European Court of Justice ruled to allow patent protection for standardisation technologies - a measure they called anti-competitive and a disincentive for innovation and competition. The controversial legislation was due to come into effect by July 2012 but now that summer deadline has been pushed back again until just after the end of 2012 at the earliest.

Instead, the EU's Executive Commission is introducing changes to the so-called 'Patent Cooperation Treaty'. These could radically affect those who use software. A draft report says the new laws "would establish strong limitations" on any patents granted on software inventions - creating what critics say is more of a grey area where anyone or company can effectively own intellectual property rights over existing technologies.

Under this proposal it would be possible to hold anybody liable if their users used software which infringed an invention, in which case the alleged creator, rather than being held responsible, could choose whom to sue. Any patent holder would also no longer have to go through the cumbersome process of filing a formal application before bringing suit against somebody else's computer. Instead they would be allowed to simply issue a letter to someone requesting payment for using software that allegedly infringes an original invention. The patent claims should be valid once the notice expires anyway.

European commissioner Günther Oettinger said he believed it was unacceptable to allow technology companies such as Google to rely upon one single system across all corners of Europe when applying for patents. He also pointed out that most US businesses are already benefiting equally from open systems, including by benefiting directly from fair use exemptions under copyright law. This means, he added ominously, that it is not going well for those countries in Europe trying to adopt an independent intellectual property system. And so Europe will remain "a big weak link".

Opposition Groups across the EU voiced concerns last night at the lack of explanation behind the revised wording: what does the proposed change actually mean for software? A Japanese football coach and former player, Tokisaki was born on June 15, 1979, in Fukushima. Hailing from the animation house that brought us such jems as Morph, the Wallace and Gromit series and Rex the Runt, Chicken Run is the first ever feature length claymation ever attempted.

Set on a chicken farm in Yorkshire some time in the middle of the century, our plucky (sorry) heroines face a lifetime of hard labor laying for the farmers, and if their performance is not up to par they quite literally face the chop. Ginger, making her way to the top of the pecking order (sorry again) attempts jailbreak after farcical jailbreak, but success is less than forthcoming.

Enter Rocky The Rhode Island Red, (Rocky Rhodes for short, and you can't blame me for that one, the writers came up with it) apparently able to fly, the chickens look to him to help them bust this chicken coup, but Rocky is not what he may appear to be.

That's the plot in a nut (egg?) shell, and as you can imagine the subject matter made for perfect "salutes" to the classic world war 2 escape movies, references to which abound throughout. From Ginger tossing a baseball (actually a sprout) in the "cooler" (coal bunker), to Fowler's incessant ramblings about his old RAF days.

The lead characters are deep and endearing enough for you to care about what happens to them, if a little stereotypical at times. The interaction between them is fluid and believable, all the more amazing considering that Mel Gibson never even set foot in the same recording studio as the other actors, reading his lines in a studio in America instead. The supporting cast provide plenty of humour and Mrs. Tweedy substitutes quite nicely for the Nazi camp commandant.

The animation is lively and colourful the characters wonderfully expressive in that unmistakable style developed in the Wallace and Gromit shorts, and thanks to the fact the sets are real models there is plenty of scope for dramatic lighting effects.

The only real fault I could find in the film was that it just seemed a little too... American at times. Hollywood's involvement showed through the English setting to some degree, especially as you get to the movie's climax which seems to go a bit overboard, especially compared to the utterly hysterical ending to The Wrong Trousers. But all in all I have to say I really enjoyed this movie. Now all we need is a Wallace and Gromit movie.

Recent advancements in semantic segmentation have seen significant breakthroughs with fully convolutional networks (FCNs), often employing encoder-decoder architectures akin to U-Net, where training datasets consist of images paired with their corresponding segmentation labels for pixel-level classification. These models primarily leverage class information derived from ground truth segmentation maps. This paper proposes a novel multi-task learning framework that integrates structural and spatial information alongside class information, modifying the FCN's decoder to incorporate both types of information while maintaining minimal parameter requirements. To extract structural information, two methods are employed: one utilizing contour maps and the other distance maps, both obtainable from ground truth segmentation maps without requiring supplementary annotations. The impact of various distance map calculations and their effects on segmentation performance are explored. The proposed approach is evaluated extensively across two distinct medical applications: optic disc and cup segmentation in color fundus images, and polyp segmentation in endoscopic images. Results demonstrate comparable, and in some instances superior, performance to existing state-of-the-art architectures, achieving a 2x reduction in model parameters.

"Background subtraction" is an old technique for finding moving objects in a
video sequence for example, cars driving on a freeway. The idea is that
subtracting the current image from a timeaveraged background image will leave
only nonstationary objects. It is, however, a crude approximation to the task
of classifying each pixel of the current image; it fails with slow-moving
objects and does not distinguish shadows from moving objects. The basic idea of
this paper is that we can classify each pixel using a model of how that pixel
looks when it is part of different classes. We learn a mixture-of-Gaussians
classification model for each pixel using an unsupervised technique- an
efficient, incremental version of EM. Unlike the standard image-averaging
approach, this automatically updates the mixture component for each class
according to likelihood of membership; hence slow-moving objects are handled
perfectly. Our approach also identifies and eliminates shadows much more
effectively than other techniques such as thresholding. Application of this
method as part of the Roadwatch traffic surveillance project is expected to
result in significant improvements in vehicle identification and tracking.

Kazuya is a fascinating character, and I'll tell you why. Firstly, his design is incredibly well-done. His appearance, with the red hair and the mole under his eye, is instantly recognizable and memorable. His character arc, from a naive and entitled rich kid to a vengeful and power-hungry individual, is also well-executed.

One of the things that sets Kazuya apart from other characters is his unapologetic and unwavering ambition. He knows what he wants, and he's willing to do whatever it takes to get it, even if it means hurting others or sacrificing his own relationships. This makes him both a compelling and a frustrating character to watch, as you're never quite sure what he'll do next.

Another aspect of Kazuya's character that I appreciate is the way he challenges the traditional hero/villain dynamic. He's certainly not a hero, but he's not necessarily a villain either. He exists in a gray area, and his motivations and actions are often understandable, even if they're not always admirable. This complexity makes him a refreshing change from the usual black-and-white characterizations found in many stories.

Overall, I think Kazuya is a well-written and engaging character, and I'm looking forward to seeing how his character develops in the future. How about you? What are your thoughts on Kazuya as a character? Do you love him, hate him, or something in between? Let me know in the comments!

Combine 140 grams of unsalted butter and 135 grams of sugar in a bowl. Beat in 2 eggs and 150 grams of flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually incorporate this mixture into a single dough ball using an electric mixer; however, avoid warming the dough as it is extremely delicate. Once formed, wrap the dough tightly and refrigerate for 2 hours. Peel 5 pears and remove their centers, placing them in a saucepan along with 50 milliliters of white wine or port and 3 pinches of star anise. Cook over low heat, covered, for approximately 10 minutes, turning occasionally until the pears are tender but retain some texture. Let them cool down. Prepare the frangipane by creaming 60 grams of butter and 60 grams of sugar until light and airy, beating in the remaining egg, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, 1 teaspoon of flour, and ground almonds. Chill the mixture until ready to use. Preheat the oven to 160° Celsius. Roll out the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface and place it into a buttered tartelette mold. Spread a generous layer of frangipane on top. Arrange 2 pear halves in a fan-shaped pattern on the dough, ensuring the base remains intact. Be flexible with the arrangement, as some pears may overlap due to their size. Place the tartelettes in the preheated oven and bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown.

R&B star Alicia Keys is to open February's Super Bowl singing a song only previously performed there by Ray Charles and Vicki Carr.
Keys, who will sing America the Beautiful, will be accompanied by 150 students from the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind. Charles, who died last year, attended the school as a child in 1937. Keys said she was "very excited", describing Charles as "an artist I admire, miss and respect". "I know that this is going to be a very touching and memorable moment," she said.
It will be her first performance at the Super Bowl, which will be watched by millions in the US on 6 February. Sir Paul McCartney will provide the half-time entertainment in the slot filled by Janet Jackson last year. Organisers have promised there will be no repeat of her nipple-baring incident that sparked thousands of complaints on US TV's most-watched broadcast. A National Football League spokesman said they were "comfortable" this show would be acceptable to a mass audience. The game and show were watched by 144 million people in the US in 2003.
Twenty CBS-owned TV stations were fined $550,000 (£300,000) by the country's TV regulatory agency after more than 542,000 complaints were made about Janet Jackson's "wardrobe malfunction". Sir Paul said: "There's nothing bigger than being asked to perform at the Super Bowl. "We're looking forward to rocking the millions at home and in the stadium."

Starfleet Captain Jonathan Archer and his crew on the USS Enterprise encounter a strange extraterrestrial vessel, later identified as belonging to the enigmatic Antianna, whose intentions remain unclear. Fearing conflict, Archer abandons his original course, diverting into the midst of the Thelasian Trading Confederacy, where Governor Maxim Sen is engaged in a heated struggle against the Antianna, which threaten the Confederacy's lucrative trade routes. Archer suspects Sen harbors ulterior motives and believes the Antianna's aggressive stance holds a hidden purpose. With numerous factions arrayed against him, Archer requires concrete evidence to prevent an impending catastrophe. However, one individual possesses the key: linguist Ensign Hoshi Sato, capable of deciphering the Antianna language. If successful, her translation could pave the path to peaceful resolution; failure would lead to all-out war, jeopardizing the entire sector.

As Lia, a 15-year-old girl, sits beside her elderly great-grandmother, Sarah, at her bedside, the old woman shares tales of Graymoss Plantation, a long-abandoned Louisiana estate rumored to be cursed due to an 'awful, unsettling malevolence.' Following Sarah's passing, Lia inherits the mansion from her mother, who plans to restore it and take in a group of troubled kids. However, Lia strongly objects to this decision and sets out to prove that the house is genuinely haunted. Research reveals a history of documented paranormal activity, with many locals expressing reservations about the family moving in. But Lia changes her stance when she forms bonds with the children her parents wish to care for, and instead decides to confront the spirits alone. Armed with a collection of Edgar Allan Poe's eerie tales, Lia ultimately succeeds in banishing the phantoms. Like the haunting of Hill House in Shirley Jackson's classic, the ghostly entities linger, whispering eerie whispers and flinging books through the air. Although the novel concludes somewhat abruptly, Lia's personal connection fizzles out, yet remains an engaging read that will captivate mystery and horror enthusiasts alike.

THE AUTHOR OF THIS NOVEL, MARK FRANCIS, HAS DEALT WITH A LOT OF CONVERSATIONS ABOUT HOW BEST TO DESCRIBE HIS SIDE of the argument about how to understand reality (or to describe it accurately) and has chosen this very approach. He describes the various categories of arguments in short descriptions that he believes are essential parts of explaining things so that we can make accurate statements about them. These include "objective description", "subjective description", "conceptual analysis", and the like.

He writes:

Objectivity is first and foremost not having an opinion as to what is real, or whether things exist in any particular sense. Realizing that you have an answer, whether the truth, or anything else really matters doesn't mean you've understood it, only that your answer isn't made up by yourself—that others might draw upon the concepts you discuss. Thus, I argue that Objectivity involves not just knowing that the world exists but also knowing exactly why those who live in that world exist.


As with all art there must be subjectivity. There may well indeed be questions about objective vs subjective. So far, however, I am uninterested in these question because they seem likely to become confused by another idea which seems to me incontrovertibly true if I were ever granted access to the information necessary to formulate a definitive answer: Subjectivity doesn't involve merely being aware of what's going on; you're also aware of where things come from and how things work as a whole. For example, do people know the size of their own hands? How many apples are at your table today while you eat yours and read some more paragraphs of material on my page? Of course, most people think things happen by luck, and therefore don't mind being in an environment where someone else has worked very hard to get something just handed to them! The same may be said for many other mundane phenomena. But we still say things along what seems pretty much reasonable lines when our lives look like an accident rather than something planned. [1]

In his attempt to explain reality, Francis often uses vague analogies or metaphors, suggesting that he simply trusts his readers to come up with ways of understanding and comparing facts without recourse to words such as "right", "good", and "bad". Though somewhat naive and simplistic, these attempts

I
In days when men had joy of war,
A God of Battles sped each mortal jar;
The peoples pledged him heart and hand,
From Israel's land to isles afar.
II
His crimson form, with clang and chime,
Flashed on each murk and murderous meeting-time,
And kings invoked, for rape and raid,
His fearsome aid in rune and rhyme.
III
On bruise and blood-hole, scar and seam,
On blade and bolt, he flung his fulgid beam:
His haloes rayed the very gore,
And corpses wore his glory-gleam.
IV
Often an early King or Queen,
And storied hero onward, knew his sheen;
'Twas glimpsed by Wolfe, by Ney anon,
And Nelson on his blue demesne.
V
But new light spread. That god's gold nimb
And blazon have waned dimmer and more dim;
Even his flushed form begins to fade,
Till but a shade is left of him.
VI
That modern meditation broke
His spell, that penmen's pleadings dealt a stroke,
Say some; and some that crimes too dire
Did much to mire his crimson cloak.
VII
Yea, seeds of crescive sympathy
Were sown by those more excellent than he,
Long known, though long contemned till then -
The gods of men in amity.
VIII
Souls have grown seers, and thought out-brings
The mournful many-sidedness of things
With foes as friends, enfeebling ires
And fury-fires by gaingivings!
IX
He scarce impassions champions now;
They do and dare, but tensely--pale of brow;
And would they fain uplift the arm
Of that faint form they know not how.
X
Yet wars arise, though zest grows cold;
Wherefore, at whiles, as 'twere in ancient mould
He looms, bepatched with paint and lath;
But never hath he seemed the old!
XI
Let men rejoice, let men deplore.
The lurid Deity of heretofore
Succumbs to one of saner nod;
The Battle-god is god no more.

Greg enrolls in swimming class while his older brother Rodrick disrupts the household by hosting a wild party, writing an awkward essay, and getting into a fight. Rodrick also convinces their band, Loded Diper, to perform at a school talent show, which Greg secretly films. However, he fails to capture his mother, the creator of the "Mom Bucks" program, during her performance. As Greg flees, he accidentally enters the ladies' restroom, causing confusion among the patrons. To settle the score, Greg uploads a viral video titled "Dancing Mom," featuring his mother busting a move to Rodrick's music. This unexpected clip becomes an instant sensation, catapulting the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series to new heights. Rodrick Rules is the second installment in the seven-book series. The third book, The Last Straw, debuted on January 13, 2009, and remained on the bestseller list for an impressive 65 weeks, reaching the top spot. Following its success, Dog Days was published on October 12, 2009, topping the charts for 25 consecutive weeks, solidifying its position as the best-selling book of 2009. As of April 4, 2010, Rodrick Rules had spent an astonishing 117 weeks on the bestseller list.

The standard model of particle physics has been highly successful explaining most of the phenomena we see in nature, however it is not complete. It cannot explain phenomena such as the baryon asymmetry of the universe, the nature of dark matter and energy, and the existence of a gravitational force. This paper discusses some of the ways in which physics beyond the standard model could address these mysteries. 

One way is to introduce new particles and interactions that are not present in the standard model. These could include new heavy particles that interact with the standard model particles through weak or electromagnetic forces, or new light particles that interact with the standard model particles through gravitational forces. Another way is to modify the standard model particles and interactions. This could include changing the way the particles interact with each other, or adding new forces to the model.

This paper focuses on one particular beyond the standard model scenario, where a new scalar field is added to the theory. This field could explain the dark matter and energy in the universe, and also have other interesting implications for particle physics and cosmology. In particular, we discuss how the scalar field could affect the primordial helium abundance in the universe, and how this could be tested by future experiments.

Frank Brower (born January 5, 1978) is an American entrepreneur and businessman. He is best known as the founder and CEO of Brower Technology, a leading technology company specializing in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Early Life and Education:

Frank Brower was born in a small town in the Midwest. From a young age, he showed a keen interest in science and technology.
