Ingredients:

- 1 medium-sized butternut squash (about 2 pounds)
- 2 tablespoons of olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 cup of freshly grated Parmesan cheese
- 2 cups of whole milk
- 3 large eggs
- 1/4 cup of all-purpose flour
- 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg
- 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs
- Butter for greasing the baking dish

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). 

2. Cut the butternut squash in half lengthwise and remove the seeds. 

3. Brush the cut sides of the squash with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. 

4. Place the squash halves cut side down on a baking sheet and roast in the oven for about 45 minutes, or until the squash is tender and can be easily pierced with a fork.

5. Remove the squash from the oven and let it cool. Once it's cool enough to handle, scoop out the flesh and discard the skin.

6. In a large bowl, combine the squash flesh, Parmesan cheese, milk, eggs, flour, and nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper to taste. 

7. Use a blender or food processor to puree the mixture until smooth.

8. Grease a baking dish with butter and sprinkle the bottom with breadcrumbs.

9. Pour the squash mixture into the prepared baking dish and smooth the top with a spatula.

10. Bake in the preheated oven for about 45 minutes, or until the pudding is set and the top is golden brown.

11. Remove the pudding from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.

12. Serve the Baked Squash and Parmesan Cheese Pudding warm, garnished with a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese and a drizzle of olive oil, if desired.

Enjoy this delicious and comforting dish!

Salted Chocolate and Caramel Bark Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups of semi-sweet chocolate chips
- 3 tablespoons of unsalted butter
- 1 can of dulce de leche
- 1/4 teaspoon of salt
- 1 cup of chopped nuts (optional)
- 1 cup of dried fruits (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit, and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

2. In a microwave-safe bowl or in a small saucepan on the stove, melt the chocolate chips and butter together, stirring frequently until smooth.

3. Pour the melted chocolate onto the prepared baking sheet and spread it out into an even layer.

4. In a separate bowl, mix together the dulce de leche and salt until well combined.

5. Pour the dulce de leche mixture over the chocolate, spreading it out evenly to cover the entire surface.

6. If desired, add chopped nuts and dried fruits to the top of the caramel mixture, pressing them down slightly so they stick to the caramel.

7. Place the baking sheet in the oven and bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the nuts are golden brown and the caramel is bubbly.

8. Allow the caramel bark to cool completely before breaking it into pieces and serving.

Optional: You can also add a layer of white chocolate on top of the dark chocolate before adding the nuts and dried fruits, for added contrast and flavor. Simply melt the white chocolate in the same way as the dark chocolate, and pour it over the cooled dark chocolate before adding the toppings.

Shirley McBay (born 1935) is an American mathematician, educator, and advocate for minority education in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). She is best known for her work as the Dean for Student Affairs at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and as the founder of the Quality Education for Minorities (QEM) Network.

== Early Life and Education ==

Shirley McBay was born in 1935 in Bainbridge, Georgia. She attended Spelman College, a historically black college in Atlanta, Georgia, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Mathematics in 1957. She then went on to earn a Master's degree in Mathematics from Atlanta University in 1959. In 1966, she became the first African American woman to earn a Ph.D. in Mathematics from the University of Georgia.

== Career ==

After earning her Ph.D., McBay taught at Spelman College for several years before joining the faculty at MIT in 1972. At MIT, she served as the Dean for Student Affairs from 1980 to 1990. During her tenure, she worked to increase the representation of women and minorities in STEM fields.

In 1990, McBay founded the Quality Education for Minorities (QEM) Network, a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the education of minorities in the United States. Through the QEM Network, McBay has worked to increase minority participation in STEM fields and to improve the quality of education in minority-serving institutions.

== Awards and Recognition ==

McBay has received numerous awards and recognition for her work in education and advocacy. In 1990, she was awarded the Arthur M. Bueche Award by the National Academy of Engineering for her contributions to science and technology policy. In 2000, she was honored with the Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring.

== Legacy ==

Shirley McBay's work has had a significant impact on the representation of minorities in STEM fields. Through her work at MIT and the QEM Network, she has helped to increase the number of minority students pursuing careers in STEM and has worked to improve the quality of education in minority-serving institutions. Her efforts have paved the way for future generations of minority students in STEM.

At the start of the nineteenth century a castle was built on the Heiligenberg. Grand Duchess Wilhelmine of Hesse-Darmstadt and her son, Prince Alexander of Hesse-Darmstadt, added an extension designed by Georg Moller in 1862–1867 . Alexander (1823–1888), third son of Grand Duke Louis II of Hesse-Darmstadt, from 1852 onwards mainly lived in Darmstadt or at the Schloss Heiligenberg, at least when he was not on campaign. On 28 October 1851 he entered a morganatic marriage with countess Julia Hauke, a lady in waiting to his sister, Tsarina Maria Alexandrovna of Russia. In a variation of Ebert's Hat Problem involving three individuals and three different colors, participants make simultaneous guesses about their respective hat colors based on the information provided by others' choices. A winning outcome occurs when at least one person correctly identifies their hat color without anyone incorrectly guessing. This research focuses on optimizing the likelihood of success in Ebert's Hat Problem with varying color probabilities, specifically the asymmetric scenario. By leveraging the concept of adequate sets, which remains unaffected by the specific probability distributions, our approach enables more efficient computation compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, it allows for a more nuanced exploration of the asymmetric case.

A next generation DVD technology backed by Sony has received a major boost.
Film giant Disney says it will produce its future DVDs using Sony's Blu-ray Disc technology, but has not ruled out a rival format developed by Toshiba. The two competing DVD formats, Blu-ray developed by Sony and others, and Toshiba's HD-DVD, have been courting top film studios for several months. The next generation of DVDs promises very high quality pictures and sound, as well as a lot of data. Both technologies use a blue laser to write information. It has a shorter wavelength so more data can be stored. Disney is the latest studio to announce which technology it is backing in a format battle which mirrors the 1980s Betamax versus VHS war. Sony lost out to JVC in that fight.
The current battle for Hollywood's hearts and minds is a crucial one because high-definition films will bring in billions of revenue and the studios would prefer to use one standard. Last month, Paramount, Universal and Warner Brothers said they were opting for the Toshiba and NEC-backed format, HD-DVD high-definition discs.
Those studios currently produce about 45% of DVD content. Sony Pictures Entertainment and MGM Studios have already staked their allegiance with the Blu-ray Disc Association, whose members also include technology companies Dell, Samsung and Matsushita. Twentieth Century Fox is still to announce which technology it will be supporting. If Fox decided to go with Blu-ray too, it would mean the format would have a 47% share of DVD content. Disney said its films would be available on the Blu-ray format when DVD players for the standard went on sale on North America and Japan, expected in 2006. Universal is to start producing films on the HD-DVD format in 2005, and Paramount will start releasing titles using the standard in 2006. Toshiba expects sales of HD-DVDs to reach 300bn yen ($2.9bn, £1.5bn) by 2010.

The sea is calm to-night.
The tide is full, the moon lies fair
Upon the straits; on the French coast the light
Gleams and is gone; the cliffs of England stand;
Glimmering and vast, out in the tranquil bay.
Come to the window, sweet is the night-air!
Only, from the long line of spray
Where the sea meets the moon-blanched land,
Listen! you hear the grating roar
Of pebbles which the waves draw back, and fling,
At their return, up the high strand,
Begin, and cease, and then again begin,
With tremulous cadence slow, and bring
The eternal note of sadness in.
Sophocles long ago
Heard it on the A gaean, and it brought
Into his mind the turbid ebb and flow
Of human misery; we
Find also in the sound a thought,
Hearing it by this distant northern sea.
The Sea of Faith
Was once, too, at the full, and round earth's shore
Lay like the folds of a bright girdle furled.
But now I only hear
Its melancholy, long, withdrawing roar,
Retreating, to the breath
Of the night-wind, down the vast edges drear
And naked shingles of the world.
Ah, love, let us be true
To one another! for the world, which seems
To lie before us like a land of dreams,
So various, so beautiful, so new,
Hath really neither joy, nor love, nor light,
Nor certitude, nor peace, nor help for pain;
And we are here as on a darkling plain
Swept with confused alarms of struggle and flight,
Where ignorant armies clash by night.

Ingredients:
1 pound pears, peeled, cored, and sliced
1/4 cup white sugar
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
6 tablespoons butter
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/2 cup white sugar
1 egg
1/2 cup milk
1/4 cup blue cheese, crumbled

Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
2. In a large bowl, combine pears, 1/4 cup sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg. Melt butter in a 9x13 inch baking dish. Add pears, and toss to coat.
3. Bake pears for 15 minutes.
4. Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and 1/2 cup sugar. In a small bowl, whisk together egg and milk. Stir milk mixture into flour mixture until just moistened.
5. Drop dough by spoonfuls over pears. Sprinkle with blue cheese.
6. Bake shortcakes for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.

I am surprised by the streets of Chicago
when the palm of winter grips them with snow
as if to forgive the city’s mistakes
and give it a canvas that’s new, white, and clean–
its fingers, the branches on all of the trees
kneading the air that blows in from the lake.
I’ve never lived next to the pulse of the lake
(until I set foot down the side of Chicago)
breathing in through the streets and out through the trees
welcoming the cool of the wet, numbing snow.
It lets my mind slip into thinking it’s clean
as if to personally forgive my mistakes.
“But what have you done to forgive your mistakes? ”
Did I ask this? Or is that the voice of the lake?
Some days, not even does it appear clean,
worn down from its tall standing neighbor, Chicago.
It scrapes at the sky, asking it for more snow
to stick to and freeze the trunks of the trees.
If I were a branch on one of these trees
incapable of making a single mistake,
I’d grab at the sky as it shook out the snow
and grow my roots thick till they tasted the lake.
But I wouldn’t bend to the force of Chicago
that’s constantly keeping me from being clean.
And what does it mean to try to be clean?
I don’t understand the stillness of the trees
when they’re being attacked by the size of Chicago
as if to glorify the city’s mistakes
that glisten like stars at night on the lake
before it all froze and was covered with snow.
Ah! To imagine how long there’s been snow.
How can something this old still feel so clean
and dance through the wind that swoops in from the lake?
Is it the kneading by the spiny branches on trees
trusting that there will be no more mistakes
that leaves these the only pure thing in Chicago?
Here comes the snow that seeks out the trees
Am I now clean? Where are my mistakes?
Chicago belongs where it lay with the lake.

Our proposed framework addresses the challenge of segmenting generic objects across both static images and dynamic videos by generating detailed pixel-level masks for all 'object-like' regions, including those from unseen object categories. The US has petitioned the World Trade Organization to examine the EU's customs tariffs, which the US claims are discriminatory and impede international trade. The EU's internal bodies acknowledge the inconsistencies in their customs policies but have not addressed them, primarily affecting smaller and medium-sized US enterprises. Following the EU's expansion to 25 member states in May, the US lodged the complaint after negotiations failed to yield a resolution. This move coincided with the US and EU temporarily shelving their disagreement over aircraft subsidies to manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing. EU Trade Commissioner Peter Mandelson stated that both parties agreed to resume discussions on the aircraft subsidy issue, leading to WTO filings in the previous autumn. In explaining its request for a WTO panel to address customs barriers, the US Trade Representative's office cited the need to address these issues early in the EU's enlargement process, particularly amidst the integration of ten new eastern European nations in May. With trade between the US and the 25-member EU totaling $155.2 billion in 2003, the US argued that the lack of a unified EU customs system and inadequate procedures for swift review hinder US exports, especially for smaller and mid-sized businesses. However, an EU representative in Washington dismissed the US complaint, labeling it "very weak" and pointing out the absence of concrete evidence showing US companies are being unfairly harmed. The WTO's dispute settlement panel may take several months to deliver its findings.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have recently seen tremendous success in
various computer vision tasks. However, their application to problems with high
dimensional input and output, such as high-resolution image and video
segmentation or 3D medical imaging, has been limited by various factors.
Primarily, in the training stage, it is necessary to store network activations
for back propagation. In these settings, the memory requirements associated
with storing activations can exceed what is feasible with current hardware,
especially for problems in 3D. Motivated by the propagation of signals over
physical networks, that are governed by the hyperbolic Telegraph equation, in
this work we introduce a fully conservative hyperbolic network for problems
with high dimensional input and output. We introduce a coarsening operation
that allows completely reversible CNNs by using a learnable Discrete Wavelet
Transform and its inverse to both coarsen and interpolate the network state and
change the number of channels. We show that fully reversible networks are able
to achieve results comparable to the state of the art in 4D time-lapse hyper
spectral image segmentation and full 3D video segmentation, with a much lower
memory footprint that is a constant independent of the network depth. We also
extend the use of such networks to Variational Auto Encoders with high
resolution input and output.

Here's a heaping tablespoon of sea salt for boiling, along with one pound of imported orecchiette pasta. For the vegetables, chop one and a half pounds of broccoli rabe into 1-inch pieces. Heat three tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. 6 ounces feta cheese, crumbled
4 ounces cream cheese
1 egg, beaten
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
1 tablespoon chopped fresh dill or 1 teaspoon dried dill
8 sheets packaged phyllo dough
1/2 cup butter
Defrost the phyllo dough and return the remainder to the freezer. Butter a cookie sheet. Melt the butter and remove from the heat. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Mix the feta and cream cheese with the egg, parsley, and dill and set aside. Layout one sheet of phyllo dough on a counter. (Keep the remaining dough covered with a slightly damp towel to prevent its drying out.) Brush the sheet of dough with some melted butter. Cut it the short way into 5 strips, about 3x10 inches each. Place 1-1/2 teaspoons of the filling at one end of each strip. Roll the strips into cylinders about 1/2 inch in diameter. Continue until all of the dough has been cut, filled, and rolled. Arrange 2 to 3 cylinder per person on the cookie sheet and brush them with more butter. (Freeze the rest of the cylinders, unbaked, for use at another time.) Bake for about 10 minutes, or until the cylinders are well browned and very flaky. Bureks, frozen unbaked, can go directly from the freezer into a preheated 375-degree F oven to make an instant hors d'oeuvre.

Here's a 2-pound London broil steak, along with some fresh bay leaves, an onion, two whole tomatoes, one celery stalk, salt, 1 ¼ cups of olive oil, some finely chopped green bell peppers, 2 cloves of garlic, another bay leaf, a pinch of dried oregano, a quarter teaspoon of ground cumin, ½ ounce of tomato sauce, a pinch of sugar, ¼ teaspoon of white wine vinegar, half a cup of stock made from cooking meat, a pinch of salt, and ¼ cup of red wine. Place all these ingredients in a large pot and pour in cold water. Bring it to a rolling boil, skim off the scum, then reduce heat and let it simmer for about an hour or until the meat becomes tender. Remove the meat, let it cool down, shred it, and set it aside. Strain the remaining liquid and save it to use as part of the sauce later; you can also use it to make a comforting soup. For the Tomato Sauce for Ropa Vieja: Heat some oil in a large pan, sauté the onion and green pepper until they're soft. Then add the garlic, another bay leaf, the dried oregano, and the cumin, and let them cook for five more minutes. Next, combine the canned tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, the reserved stock, salt, and red wine. Add this mixture to the pan and stir everything together until it boils, then lower the heat and let it simmer for about thirty minutes, stirring occasionally. Now, put the shredded meat into a large baking dish, pour the sauce over it, and mix it well. Cover it and let it cook for twenty to thirty minutes, stirring every now and then. Serve it over white rice alongside very ripe, fried plantains if available.

Laser-induced magnetization precession of a thick Pt/Co/Pt film with
perpendicular interface anisotropy was studied using time resolved
magneto-optical Kerr effect. Although the demagnetization energy dominates the
interface anisotropy for the Co thickness considered, and the Co layer can be
characterized by an effective easy-plane anisotropy, we found that an
additional $\pi$ shift in the initial phase for the magnetization precession is
needed to describe the measured data using only the effective easy-plane
anisotropy. The additional $\pi$ phase is rendered by the dependence on the
phonon temperature of the interface anisotropy, in contrast to the dependence
on the electron temperature of the demagnetization energy. Our observation that
the precession phase is affected by both the electron and phonon temperature
warrants a detailed knowledge about the forms of anisotropy present in the
system under investigation for a complete description of laser-induced
magnetization precession.

Segmentation challenges arise significantly when objects of interest are partially occluded,
background clutter is present, and strong noise is also involved. To address this issue,
a new approach is presented that leverages "weak" shape priors. In this proposed method,
an active contour is constrained to reach a configuration where its parameters' probability
densities closely match those derived from model densities trained on sample data.
Numerical tests reveal that the shape modeling can be considered "weak," as it only slightly
influences the segmentation process, allowing data-driven forces to dominate. Meanwhile,
the priors impose sufficient constraints to guide the segmentation's convergence without
requiring large amounts of training data, resulting in more accurate outcomes than PCA-based
regularization techniques. These advantages are demonstrated through a series of experiments.

Black trees against an orange sky,
Trees that the wind shook terribly,
Like a harsh spume along the road,
Quavering up like withered arms,
Writhing like streams, like twisted charms
Of hot lead flung in snow. Below
The iron ice stung like a goad,
Slashing the torn shoes from my feet,
And all the air was bitter sleet.
And all the land was cramped with snow,
Steel-strong and fierce and glimmering wan,
Like pale plains of obsidian.
-- And yet I strove -- and I was fire
And ice -- and fire and ice were one
In one vast hunger of desire.
A dim desire, of pleasant places,
And lush fields in the summer sun,
And logs aflame, and walls, and faces,
-- And wine, and old ambrosial talk,
A golden ball in fountains dancing,
And unforgotten hands. (Ah, God,
I trod them down where I have trod,
And they remain, and they remain,
Etched in unutterable pain,
Loved lips and faces now apart,
That once were closer than my heart --
In agony, in agony,
And horribly a part of me. . . .
For Lethe is for no man set,
And in Hell may no man forget.)
And there were flowers, and jugs, bright-glancing,
And old Italian swords -- and looks,
A moment's glance of fire, of fire,
Spiring, leaping, flaming higher,
Into the intense, the cloudless blue,
Until two souls were one, and flame,
And very flesh, and yet the same!
As if all springs were crushed anew
Into one globed drop of dew!
But for the most I thought of heat,
Desiring greatly. . . . Hot white sand
The lazy body lies at rest in,
Or sun-dried, scented grass to nest in,
And fires, innumerable fires,
Great fagots hurling golden gyres
Of sparks far up, and the red heart
In sea-coals, crashing as they part
To tiny flares, and kindling snapping,
Bunched sticks that burst their string and wrapping
And fall like jackstraws; green and blue
The evil flames of driftwood too,
And heavy, sullen lumps of coke
With still, fierce heat and ugly smoke. . . .
. . . And then the vision of his face,
And theirs, all theirs, came like a sword,
Thrice, to the heart -- and as I fell
I thought I saw a light before.
I woke. My hands were blue and sore,
Torn on the ice. I scarcely felt
The frozen sleet begin to melt
Upon my face as I breathed deeper,
But lay there warmly, like a sleeper
Who shifts his arm once, and moans low,
And then sinks back to night. Slow, slow,
And still as Death, came Sleep and Death
And looked at me with quiet breath.
Unbending figures, black and stark
Against the intense deeps of the dark.
Tall and like trees. Like sweet and fire
Rest crept and crept along my veins,
Gently. And there were no more pains. . . .
Was it not better so to lie?
The fight was done. Even gods tire
Of fighting. . . . My way was the wrong.
Now I should drift and drift along
To endless quiet, golden peace . . .
And let the tortured body cease.
And then a light winked like an eye.
. . . And very many miles away
A girl stood at a warm, lit door,
Holding a lamp. Ray upon ray
It cloaked the snow with perfect light.
And where she was there was no night
Nor could be, ever. God is sure,
And in his hands are things secure.
It is not given me to trace
The lovely laughter of that face,
Like a clear brook most full of light,
Or olives swaying on a height,
So silver they have wings, almost;
Like a great word once known and lost
And meaning all things. Nor her voice
A happy sound where larks rejoice,
Her body, that great loveliness,
The tender fashion of her dress,
I may not paint them.
These I see,
Blazing through all eternity,
A fire-winged sign, a glorious tree!
She stood there, and at once I knew
The bitter thing that I must do.
There could be no surrender now;
Though Sleep and Death were whispering low.
My way was wrong. So. Would it mend
If I shrank back before the end?
And sank to death and cowardice?
No, the last lees must be drained up,
Base wine from an ignoble cup;
(Yet not so base as sleek content
When I had shrunk from punishment)
The wretched body strain anew!
Life was a storm to wander through.
I took the wrong way. Good and well,
At least my feet sought out not Hell!
Though night were one consuming flame
I must go on for my base aim,
And so, perhaps, make evil grow
To something clean by agony . . .
And reach that light upon the snow . . .
And touch her dress at last . . .
So, so,
I crawled. I could not speak or see
Save dimly. The ice glared like fire,
A long bright Hell of choking cold,
And each vein was a tautened wire,
Throbbing with torture -- and I crawled.
My hands were wounds.
So I attained
The second Hell. The snow was stained
I thought, and shook my head at it
How red it was! Black tree-roots clutched
And tore -- and soon the snow was smutched
Anew; and I lurched babbling on,
And then fell down to rest a bit,
And came upon another Hell . . .
Loose stones that ice made terrible,
That rolled and gashed men as they fell.
I stumbled, slipped . . . and all was gone
That I had gained. Once more I lay
Before the long bright Hell of ice.
And still the light was far away.
There was red mist before my eyes
Or I could tell you how I went
Across the swaying firmament,
A glittering torture of cold stars,
And how I fought in Titan wars . . .
And died . . . and lived again upon
The rack . . . and how the horses strain
When their red task is nearly done. . . .
I only know that there was Pain,
Infinite and eternal Pain.
And that I fell -- and rose again.
So she was walking in the road.
And I stood upright like a man,
Once, and fell blind, and heard her cry . . .
And then there came long agony.
There was no pain when I awoke,
No pain at all. Rest, like a goad,
Spurred my eyes open -- and light broke
Upon them like a million swords:
And she was there. There are no words.
Heaven is for a moment's span.
And ever.
So I spoke and said,
"My honor stands up unbetrayed,
And I have seen you. Dear . . ."
Sharp pain
Closed like a cloak. . . .
I moaned and died.
Here, even here, these things remain.
I shall draw nearer to her side.
Oh dear and laughing, lost to me,
Hidden in grey Eternity,
I shall attain, with burning feet,
To you and to the mercy-seat!
The ages crumble down like dust,
Dark roses, deviously thrust
And scattered in sweet wine -- but I,
I shall lift up to you my cry,
And kiss your wet lips presently
Beneath the ever-living Tree.
This in my heart I keep for goad!
Somewhere, in Heaven she walks that road.
Somewhere . . . in Heaven . . . she walks . . . that . . . road. . . .

Drang nach Osten (German for "drive to the east") was an ideology promoted by certain German and Austrian political and military figures in the 19th century, which emphasized Germany's need to expand its territory towards the east through military conquest. This concept became particularly influential under the Third Reich, leading to aggressive expansionist policies that ultimately led to World War II.

The term itself originated in the 1840s with the writings of German nationalist leader Fritz Müller, who argued for a united Germany to actively pursue territorial conquests in order to become a major world power. His ideas were echoed by others including Otto von Bismarck, Adolf Hitler, and other proponents of Nazi Germany's aggressive expansionist policies.

In the view of these individuals, German unification was not enough and the country needed more land and resources to become truly great. This drive for expansion culminated in the Anschluss of Austria into the Reich in 1938 and the subsequent invasion of Poland in September 1939, which marked the beginning of World War II.

The Drang nach Osten ideology has been widely criticized as it contributed to the persecution and holocaust of millions of people, particularly Jews and Slavs. It also continues to be a controversial subject in modern-day Germany, with debates about whether the nation should take responsibility for its past actions and acknowledge the ongoing impact of its history on Europe and beyond.

Constance Eaton Hamilton (1862–1945) was a British-Canadian government official and activist. After activism supporting refugees and women in Winnipeg, she moved to Toronto and continued to support causes such as women's suffrage, becoming president of the Equal Franchise League of Toronto. She was elected for a one-year term on the  Toronto City Council in the 1920 elections, becoming the first female member of Toronto City Council and the first woman in Ontario to hold elected office at either the federal, provincial, or municipal level. After two terms  she resigned to continue her work campaigning for immigrant settlement and refugee issues, and for equal rights. In 1979, the Toronto city council established the Constance E. Hamilton Award on the Status of Women. Early life and education
She was born in Yorkshire, England in 1862 to Dr George Fowler Bodington (1829-1902) and Caroline Mary Eaton (1825-1873). Early she studied with private tutors. Fluent in German, she attended the Conservatory of Music in Leipzig, Germany and became a skilled pianist. She also worked as a part-time farmer for parts of her early life.  Hamilton immigrated to Canada with her family in 1887 and settled in Vancouver. The following year she met and married Lauchlan Hamilton, an older businessman.

WIS, a dual NBC/CW-affiliated TV station licensed to Columbia, South Carolina, is owned by Gray Television. Its studios are situated on Bull and Gervais Streets in downtown Columbia, while its transmitter lies on Rush Road, southeast of I-20, in rural southwestern Kershaw County. The station can be accessed on Charter Spectrum channel 3 in both standard and high-definition formats. Established on November 7, 1953, WIS initially broadcast a University of South Carolina versus University of North Carolina football match as its inaugural program. Originally owned by the Broadcasting Company of the South, a subsidiary of the Liberty Life Insurance Company, which also operated WIS radio (560 AM), the station began operation under Charles Batson's leadership, who served as its president and general manager until his retirement in 1983. WIS holds the distinction of being the fourth television station to launch in South Carolina, surpassing WCOS-TV, which closed down in 1956, and WNOK-TV, which relocated to channel 19 in 1961 and became WLTX. As one of the longest-running stations in the state, WIS ranks third only to WCSC-TV in Charleston and WNOK/WLTX.

We primarily investigate the stability of iterated polynomials and linear transformations that maintain strong q-log-convexity of polynomials. Specifically, we examine the properties of the linear transformation y_n(q), which is defined as the sum of terms T_{n,k}*x_k(q) for k ranging from 0 to n, where [T_{n,k}]_{n,k≥0} is a collection of non-negative numbers. Our work provides conditions for these linear transformations to preserve strong q-log-convexity or log-convexity. Furthermore, we demonstrate how several specific linear transformations, including Stirling transformations of various types, Jacobi-Stirling transformations, Legendre-Stirling transformations, central factorial transformations, and others, uniformly preserve these convexities. Additionally, we verify a conjecture by Lin and Zeng and build upon previous results by Chen et al. and Zhu regarding strong q-log-convexity of polynomials, as well as those by Liu and Wang concerning transformations maintaining log-convexity. By exploring the relationship between stability and q-log-convexity, we provide new insights into the behavior of iterated polynomials. Using the concept of interlacing of zeros, we establish criteria for the stability of iterated Sturm sequences and q-log-convexity of polynomials. This leads to the derivation of the stability of certain iterated Eulerian polynomials of types A and B, along with their q-analogs. Moreover, we show that the generating functions of alternating runs of types A and B, as well as longest alternating subsequences and up-down runs of permutations, form q-log-convex sequences.

The story revolves around Stevens, an devoted English butler bound to serve Lord Darlington through a series of flashbacks. The narrative commences with Stevens receiving a letter from an old colleague, revealing hints of unhappiness in her marital life, prompting him to contemplate reevaluating his long-held devotion to Lord Darlington. Meanwhile, his new employer, Mr Farraday, invites Stevens to embark on a well-deserved vacation by lending him his vehicle, sparking introspection about his unwavering dedication to Lord Darlington and his complicated past relationships. China plans to maintain its stringent credit controls throughout 2005, aiming to curb the country's rapidly expanding economy, according to reports from state media. Initially implemented in the first half of the year, these measures were designed to mitigate the risks associated with swift growth, particularly concerns about escalating prices and undue strain on the country's fragile banking system. Despite the fast-paced growth rate of 9.1%, China's economy has maintained its momentum for over a year now. The surge in manufacturing production has led to substantial increases in energy consumption, contributing to higher global oil prices for most of the year. From a theoretical perspective, the government aims for a 7% growth target; however, it maintains that such an overshoot does not necessarily indicate a hard landing – a situation where the economy becomes overbalanced. With its currency pegged at 8.28 to the US dollar, steadily declining, China's exports remain competitive in global markets, despite resisting international calls to reevaluate its monetary policy. Notably, the current credit controls appear to have started yielding results, as industrial production increased by 15.7% in the period leading up to October, albeit a decrease from the 23% rise seen in February, while inflation decreased to 4.3%. Meanwhile, retail sales continue to flourish.

Conservative Party leader Michael Howard announced plans to reduce the number of Members of Parliament by roughly one-fifth if his party comes to power, as part of their proposed "smaller government bill". This initiative aims to minimize government intervention in citizens' lives. The proposal also involves reducing the number of government special advisors. Additionally, a referendum will be held in Wales to determine whether to abolish the Welsh Assembly. The proposed changes are expected to occur within five years of the Conservatives winning the general election.

The exact number of MPs to be reduced depends on the outcome of the Welsh referendum, potentially leading to approximately 120 fewer representatives from the current 659. If Wales decides to maintain its Assembly, it may face additional losses. Both parties intend to decrease the number of civil servants at Whitehall, with Labour planning for an 80,000 reduction and the Conservatives aiming for nearly 100,000. Shadow Commons leader Oliver Heald stated that this move aligns with their goal of eliminating excessive state interference in personal lives through smaller government operations.

Howard argued that these reforms address the disparity between the number of Scottish and Welsh MPs compared to those from England. He noted the average constituency population in England (around 70,000) is significantly higher than in Wales (59,000), Scotland (53,000), and Northern Ireland (66,000). Under the revised system, the number of Welsh MPs would be adjusted to match the fairness of the UK-wide representation. Howard emphasized the need for swift implementation, suggesting the changes could be introduced immediately or during the upcoming election.

A new method for classifying cardiac pathology is proposed, leveraging an innovative technique to extract image-derived features that describe the heart's shape and movement. A unique semi-supervised learning process harnesses both abundant unsegmented images and limited manually segmented images from experts to produce pixel-level apparent flow between consecutive frames in a 3D+time MRI imaging sequence. By merging this apparent flow map with cardiac segmentation masks, a localized apparent flow representing myocardium and ventricular cavity movements is generated, resulting in time-series representations of myocardial segment dimensions - radius and thickness. These motion-based features provide reliable and interpretable markers of abnormal cardiac motion. To further refine these motion features, shape-related characteristics are incorporated into a classification framework, enabling the use of just nine input parameters. This streamlined approach yields a straightforward, comprehensible, and versatile model for disease diagnosis. Our model achieved 95% accuracy on the ACDC dataset and 94% on the test set, matching the performance of existing state-of-the-art methods. Comparative analysis with other models highlights several key strengths of our methodology.

I'm 25 years old. I have no children. So why am I praising a 'kid's movie' which nobody saw? Because I have never seen a film pack the emotional wallop 'The Iron Giant' provided.

The film's plot is similar to 'E.T.' - a young boy meets an alien robot from outer space, who is stranded on earth, and runs afoul of paranoid government agents. Not to knock the Spielberg film, but what makes 'The Iron Giant' the better film is that the young boy is the teacher. It is he who has to teach the Giant about the beauty of life, the difference between good and evil, and choices we have to make. The Iron Giant, it turns out, is a weapon, who has to struggle against his own nature. The film has an obvious (and timely) gun control message, but its real message is about the choice we make when dealing with other people. We can use our powers for good or lash out at everyone around us.

I dare not give away the climax. All I will say is that it features a sacrifice absolutely breaktaking and emotionally shattering (albeit somewhat blunted by the ending). The animation is gorgeous, Michael Kamen's score is perfect, and the film beautifully evokes the 1950s.

Sadly, poor marketing kept audiences away in droves. All I can say is, to heck with the box office gross. Despite Warner's appearant desire to pretend the film never existed, the word is getting around about what a magical film this is, and I have no doubt it will join 'It's a Wonderful Life' as a film which bombed in theatres but became a classic over the years. See it now, so you can say you discovered it before everyone else did.

Over the past few years it has been demonstrated that "coarse timesteppers"
establish a link between traditional numerical analysis and microscopic/
stochastic simulation. The underlying assumption of the associated
lift-run-restrict-estimate procedure is that macroscopic models exist and close
in terms of a few governing moments of microscopically evolving distributions,
but they are unavailable in closed form. This leads to a system identification
based computational approach that sidesteps the necessity of deriving explicit
closures. Two-level codes are constructed; the outer code performs macroscopic,
continuum level numerical tasks, while the inner code estimates -through
appropriately initialized bursts of microscopic simulation- the quantities
required for continuum numerics. Such quantities include residuals, time
derivatives, and the action of coarse slow Jacobians. We demonstrate how these
coarse timesteppers can be applied to perform equation-free computations of a
kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of E. coli chemotaxis. Coarse-grained
contraction mappings, system level stability analysis as well as acceleration
of the direct simulation, are enabled through this computational multiscale
enabling technology.

The Football Association has filed charges against both Liverpool and Millwall over disturbances at their Carling Cup match on October 26. Millwall, which suffered a 3-0 defeat, faces accusations of racist behavior by its supporters. The incident began when seats were torn apart, and four individuals were removed from the stadium. A spectator with disabilities sustained an injury near the field, prompting the deployment of riot police to manage the situation. Liverpool's supporters attributed the trouble to chants referencing the Hillsborough tragedy, in which 96 fans perished in 1989. However, Millwall chairman Theo Paphitis has refuted this claim, stating that CCTV footage indicates a Liverpool supporter attacked a Millwall fan in the west stand as the trigger for the violence. Despite this, Millwall has been charged with two FA rule breaches: failing to stop fans from engaging in discriminatory behavior and allowing spectators to throw objects onto the field. In contrast, Liverpool is being charged with only one breach for failing to regulate their own fans' aggressive conduct. Both teams have until December 23 to respond to the charges.

12 ounces flank steak, trimmed of excess fat and sinew
1 tablespoon peeled, minced fresh ginger
1 1/2 teaspoons soy sauce
1 teaspoon cornstarch
1 teaspoon peanut or vegetable oil
1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons oyster sauce
2 tablespoons Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
2 tablespoons peanut or vegetable oil
1 1/2 cups sugar snap peas (about 7 ounces), strings removed
1 cup very thinly sliced carrots (about 2 small)
4 medium scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup pickled ginger slices (about 1 ounce), coarsely chopped if large
Basic Steamed White Rice, for serving
Cut the flank steak with the grain into 2-inch-wide strips, then cut each strip against the grain into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Place the beef and the remaining ingredients in a medium bowl and stir to evenly coat the meat; set aside. Place the oyster sauce and Shaoxing wine or sherry in a small bowl and stir to combine; set aside. Heat a 14-inch flat-bottomed wok over high heat until a bead of water vaporizes when dropped in the pan. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of the oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the reserved beef in an even layer. Cook undisturbed until the beef begins to sear, about 1 minute. Then, using a metal spatula, stir-fry for 30 seconds until the beef is lightly browned but not cooked through. Transfer to a plate. Drizzle the remaining tablespoon of oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the sugar snaps and carrots. Stir-fry until just warmed through, about 1 minute. Return the beef and any accumulated juices to the wok along with the reserved oyster sauce mixture, green onions, and pickled ginger. Stir-fry until the beef is just cooked through and the pickled ginger is well distributed, about 30 to 60 seconds. Serve with steamed rice.

Dinosaurs and amusement parks collide in Jurassic World. As a fan, I felt compelled to witness this spectacle. The opening sets high expectations, only to disappoint in its latter stages. The thrilling action sequences, particularly those involving the enclosure housing a vulnerable young visitor, are enjoyable. However, the final act devolves into absurdity.

Chris Pratt shines as Owen Grady, the charming and fearless raptor trainer, bringing a likable charm reminiscent of Indiana Jones. Bryce Dallas Howard portrays Claire Dearing, the strict park administrator, whose initial disagreements with Owen eventually unfold in predictable fashion. Her character development is aided by her two nephews, who serve as plot devices.

Vincent D'Onofrio appears as Hoskins, a ruthless military representative aiming to exploit velociraptors for military purposes. His performance is convincing, though his sinister intentions feel contrived and lack coherence. Director Colin Trevorrow aimed to depict realistic dinosaur behavior, instead opting for mindless carnage. This approach results in gruesome, unprovoked violence against innocent bystanders, prioritizing entertainment over logic.

A notable example of this excess can be seen in a prolonged and senseless killing sequence, which feels more like a twisted cartoon than a legitimate dramatic moment. This gratuitous violence is devoid of consequences or resolution, leaving viewers feeling disengaged.

As we reach the conclusion, it's advisable to set aside critical thinking. While the first installment demonstrated potential for intelligent storytelling alongside dinosaurs, the sequel fails to deliver a coherent narrative.

Phases of matter are conventionally characterized by order parameters
describing the type and degree of order in a system. For example, crystals
consist of spatially ordered arrays of atoms, an order that is lost as the
crystal melts. Like- wise in ferromagnets, the magnetic moments of the
constituent particles align only below the Curie temperature, TC. These two
examples reflect two classes of phase transitions: the melting of a crystal is
a first-order phase transition (the crystalline order vanishes abruptly) and
the onset of magnetism is a second- order phase transition (the magnetization
increases continuously from zero as the temperature falls below TC). Such
magnetism is robust in systems with localized magnetic particles, and yet rare
in model itinerant systems where the particles are free to move about. Here for
the first time, we explore the itinerant magnetic phases present in a spin-1
spin-orbit coupled atomic Bose gas; in this system, itinerant ferromagnetic
order is stabilized by the spin-orbit coupling, vanishing in its absence. We
first located a second-order phase transition that continuously stiffens until,
at a tricritical point, it transforms into a first- order transition (with
observed width as small as h x 4 Hz). We then studied the long-lived metastable
states associated with the first-order transition. These measurements are all
in agreement with theory.

1 cup coarsely chopped fresh Italian parsley

3/4 pound fusilli pasta
1 cup hickory smoke chips, soaked in water 30 minutes, drained
2 large ears fresh corn, husked
2 large zucchini, trimmed, halved lengthwise
1 large red onion, sliced into 3 large rounds
Blend parsley, vinegar and garlic in processor until parsley is finely chopped, scraping down sides of bowl twice. With machine running, gradually add 1/2 cup olive oil. Season vinaigrette to taste with salt and pepper. Cook pasta in large pot of boiling salted water until just tender but still firm to bite, stirring occasionally. Drain pasta. Rinse under cold water and drain again. Transfer to large bowl. Mix in 2 tablespoons vinaigrette. Prepare barbecue (medium heat). Place smoke chips in 8x6-inch foil packet with open top. Set packet atop coals about 5 minutes before grilling. Brush corn, zucchini and onion with remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Add corn kernels, zucchini and onion to pasta in large bowl. Mix in enough vinaigrette to coat. Season to taste with salt and pepper. (Can be prepared 8 hours ahead. Cover and refrigerate. Bring to room temperature before serving.)

British film director Sir Alan Parker has been made an officer in the Order of Arts and Letters, one of France's highest cultural honours.
Sir Alan received his decoration in Paris on Wednesday from French Culture Minister Renaud Donnedieu de Vabres. "You have explored the possibilities of film with an immense talent," Mr de Vabres said as he presented the award. Parker praised French films, saying: "Hollywood, which created modern cinema, uses it only as a commodity." He told the minister: "I am honoured to be thus distinguished by France, the flag carrier of cinema throughout the world." Sir Alan's films include Oscar-winning Fame plus Midnight Express and The Commitments.
A founding member of the Director's Guild of Great Britain, he is a former chairman of the UK Film Council and on the board of the British Film Institute. "Through your work and your campaigns, you have shown us how the artist occupies an essential place in our contemporary society," Mr de Vabres said. "Through your dreams which you show us, through the links that you weave, you question the world through the mirror of your work." He also cited the director's 2003 film The Life of David Gale, in which Kevin Spacey played a man on Death Row, as proof of his "veritable artistic commitment against the death sentence".

Men said at vespers: 'All is well!'
In one wild night the city fell;
Fell shrines of prayer and marts of gain
Before the fiery hurricane.
On threescore spires had sunset shone,
Where ghastly sunrise looked on none.
Men clasped each other's hands, and said
'The City of the West is dead!'
Brave hearts who fought, in slow retreat,
The fiends of fire from street to street,
Turned, powerless, to the blinding glare,
The dumb defiance of despair.
A sudden impulse thrilled each wire
That signalled round that sea of fire;
Swift words of cheer, warm heart-throbs came;
In tears of pity died the flame!
From East, from West, from South and North,
The messages of hope shot forth,
And, underneath the severing wave,
The world, full-handed, reached to save.
Fair seemed the old; but fairer still
The new, the dreary void shall fill
With dearer homes than those o'erthrown,
For love shall lay each corner-stone.
Rise, stricken city! from thee throw
The ashen sackcloth of thy woe;
And build, as to Amphion's strain,
To songs of cheer thy walls again!
How shrivelled in thy hot distress
The primal sin of selfishness!
How instant rose, to take thy part,
The angel in the human heart!
Ah! not in vain the flames that tossed
Above thy dreadful holocaust;
The Christ again has preached through thee
The Gospel of Humanity!
Then lift once more thy towers on high,
And fret with spires the western sky,
To tell that God is yet with us,
And love is still miraculous!

In biological cells and novel diagnostic devices biochemical receptors need
to be sensitive to extremely small concentration changes of signaling
molecules. The accuracy of such molecular signaling is ultimately limited by
the counting noise imposed by the thermal diffusion of molecules. Many
macromolecules and organelles transiently bind to molecular motors and are then
actively transported. We here show that a random albeit directed delivery of
signaling molecules to within a typical diffusion distance to the receptor
reduces the correlation time of the counting noise, effecting an improved
sensing precision. The conditions for this active focusing are indeed
compatible with observations in living cells. Our results are relevant for a
better understanding of molecular cellular signaling and the design of novel
diagnostic devices.

Analyzing an electron microscopy dataset involves identifying individual neurons and determining the connections between them, which is often a labor-intensive process. Historically, there has been limited focus on automating the identification of actual synapses between neurons due to the complexity of this task. Several factors contribute to this disparity, including the need to first accurately identify neuron shapes and the time-consuming nature of manual tracing. Furthermore, relying solely on the size of the contact area between neurons is insufficient for determining connections.

However, recent advancements have revealed that merely relying on contact area is not a reliable method for predicting synaptic connections. Additionally, as progress in segmentation has improved, annotating synapses has become an increasingly significant portion of the overall reconstruction time. To address this issue, researchers have developed algorithms capable of detecting both pre-synaptic and postsynaptic neurons independently. Specifically, pre-synaptic structures are identified using a deep learning model, while postsynaptic partners are detected using a neural network conditioned on local segmentation results.

This approach represents a significant breakthrough as it minimizes the need for extensive training data, leverages recent advances in image segmentation directly, and provides a comprehensive solution for polyadic synapse detection. Moreover, novel evaluation metrics are introduced to assess the algorithm's performance on larger-than-usual datasets, demonstrating that fully automated predictions can effectively characterize connectivity.

Ingredients:
- 1 block of firm tofu
- 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro
- 1/4 cup of chopped scallions
- 2 cloves of minced garlic
- 1 tablespoon of soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil
- 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon of sesame oil
- 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper
- 6 egg roll wrappers
- 1 avocado
- Salt

Instructions:
1. Drain the tofu and cut it into small cubes.
2. In a pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and add the minced garlic.

10. Fold the wrapper over the tofu mixture and tuck in the sides.
11. Roll the egg roll tightly and seal the end with a little water.
12. Heat a pan with vegetable oil over medium heat and add the egg rolls.
13. Cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown.

Let D be a bounded domain in n-dimensional Eucledian space with a smooth
boundary. We indicate appropriate Sobolev spaces of negative smoothness to
study the non-homogeneous Cauchy problem for an elliptic differential complex
{A_i} of first order operators. In particular, we describe traces on the
boundary of tangential part t_i (u) and normal part n_i(u) of a
(vector)-function u from the corresponding Sobolev space and give an adequate
formulation of the problem. If the Laplacians of the complex satisfy the
uniqueness condition in the small then we obtain necessary and sufficient
solvability conditions of the problem and produce formulae for its exact and
approximate solutions. For the Cauchy problem in the Lebesgue spaces L^2(D) we
construct the approximate and exact solutions to the Cauchy problem with
maximal possible regularity. Moreover, using Hilbert space methods, we
construct Carleman's formulae for a (vector-) function u from the Sobolev space
H^1(D) by its Cauchy data t_i (u) on a subset S on the boundary of the domain D
and the values of A_i u in D modulo the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Some
instructive examples for elliptic complexes of operators with constant
coefficients are considered.

To prepare this rich dessert, start by melting 4 ounces of high-quality dark chocolate in a double boiler over simmering water. Once smooth, let it cool for 10 minutes before setting aside. In a separate bowl, cream together 3/4 cup of sugar, 6 tablespoons of unsalted butter, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract using an electric mixer. Gradually incorporate 6 large egg yolks one at a time, ensuring thorough mixing after each addition. Then, combine the cooled chocolate, followed by 1/2 cup of finely ground poppy seeds. For the meringue topping, whip 6 large egg whites in a different bowl until they reach stiff peaks without becoming too dry. Fold in half of the egg whites into the chocolate mixture, then fold the remaining egg whites into the first batch, combining them seamlessly. Transfer the mixture to a greased 9-inch springform pan, smoothing the top evenly. Bake at 350°F until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, approximately 45 minutes. Allow the cake to cool completely before refrigerating it overnight. The wind blew steady from the East;
For many days hot grew the weather,
About the time of our Lady's Feast.
For many days we rode together,
Yet met we neither friend nor foe;
Hotter and clearer grew the weather,
Steadily did the East wind blow.
We saw the trees in the hot, bright weather,
Clear-cut, with shadows very black,
As freely we rode on together
With helms unlaced and bridles slack.
And often, as we rode together,
We, looking down the green-bank'd stream,
Saw flowers in the sunny weather,
And saw the bubble-making bream.
And in the night lay down together,
And hung above our heads the rood,
Or watch'd night-long in the dewy weather,
The while the moon did watch the wood.
Our spears stood bright and thick together,
Straight out the banners stream'd behind,
As we gallop'd on in the sunny weather,
With faces turn'd towards the wind.
Down sank our threescore spears together,
As thick we saw the pagans ride;
His eager face in the clear fresh weather,
Shone out that last time by my side.
Up the sweep of the bridge we dash'd together,
It rock'd to the crash of the meeting spears,
Down rain'd the buds of the dear spring weather,
The elm-tree flowers fell like tears.
There, as we roll'd and writhed together,
I threw my arms above my head,
For close by my side, in the lovely weather,
I saw him reel and fall back dead.
I and the slayer met together,
He waited the death-stroke there in his place,
With thoughts of death, in the lovely weather,

Madly I fought as we fought together;
In vain: the little Christian band
The pagans drown'd, as in stormy weather
The river drowns low-lying land.
They bound my blood-stain'd hands together,
They bound his corpse to nod by my side:
Then on we rode, in the bright March weather,
With clash of cymbals did we ride.
We ride no more, no more together;
My prison-bars are thick and strong,
I take no heed of any weather,
The sweet Saints grant I live not long.

I've had this experience before. For me it was sort of a psychological block on getting the music going in a direction that didn't fit the lyrics, so the music was locked into a certain rhythm/melody that I knew was "wrong" for the lyrics, but I couldn't break out of it... sometimes you just have to walk away for a while and come back to it later. Sometimes it means the melody/rhythm you're writing simply isn't right for the lyrics, and you have to scrap it and start over from scratch.

As others have said, it can be helpful to jam on the chords and see if anything new presents itself, or to start singing random notes or lyrics over the chords (exactly what you were doing), until something clicks.

For others, it can help to talk/sing the lyrics aloud as if you're having a conversation, and then sing/speak the tones/rhythms of your speech back into a melody.

Sometimes when I'm really stuck in this situation, I'll reduce the lyrics to just a few key words, or even a single word, and use that as the seed for the melody. I find that once I have a good melody, I can usually modify it to fit the actual lyrics, if I need to.

The Alden staRRcar, short for "Self-Transport Road and Rail Car", was a personal rapid transit (PRT) system designed by William Alden in the 1960s. It originally envisioned small electrically powered cars suitable for short distance trips at low speed within urban areas, which could optionally merge onto tracks that would provide power and guidance for high-speed travel over longer inter-city distances. It was one of the earliest dual-mode vehicles to be proposed, and one of the earliest to be actually built. Over its lifetime the design changed dramatically, originally a four-person vehicle with dual-mode operation but eventually emerging as a much larger people mover for 20 people. In this form, Boeing Vertol was awarded a construction contract in 1970 to build a demonstration system in Morgantown, West Virginia. A smaller system was also built by their licensee, Kobe Steel, and installed at the Expo '75 on Okinawa (as well as the more advanced CVS). The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system first opened for service in 1975, and with the exception of a closure for a major expansion, has remained in service since then.

This paper introduces Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRW-Net) for semantic image segmentation as a combination of convolutional neural networks, random walks on graphs and spectral graph theory. The basic idea is to extend the receptive field of a neural network's convolutional layer at a minimal cost. Given a CNN, CRW-Net extends the receptive field by one convolutional layer which has random connections to the original CNN's convolutional layers. The randomness comes from the random choice of edges in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs). To solve the issue of overfitting in GCN-based models, We proposed a loss function called graph spectral loss. We empirically show that the proposed method can improve segmentation performance when it is combined with fully connected CRF on PASCAL VOC 2012 (segmentation accuracy 71.2\%), VOCS (segmentation accuracy 77.1\%) and COCO-Stuff (segmentation accuracy 51.2\%). Our proposed method achieved the state-of-the-art performance on COCO-Stuff, outperformed the previous best result by more than 3\%.

The above text was extracted from a page on the arxiv.org website (https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06107). I've seen researchers reference arxiv.org, but I've always wondered how people use this resource. Do the papers get cited on Google Scholar? If not, what is the primary use case for authors to release papers on arxiv.org?

A: ArXiv is not a publication venue; it is an archive.  They have an agreement that once an author publishes on the archive, he/she will not post the work elsewhere for at least a month, which is why you see one-month "first notice of use."  That protects the author in case somebody sees the work, then publishes something on it earlier.

A: The primary use of arxiv is to provide a quick way for researchers to distribute their work to a large audience before peer review. Once posted, the paper can be immediately cited, discussed, etc., while the researchers work on tweaking / fixing their paper.
For example, if an author finds a minor error in their arXiv posted paper, they can make the corrections and repost it

Recent advancements in medical image segmentation have largely relied on Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, which have demonstrated satisfactory results over the last decade. Nevertheless, these models suffer from limitations due to their intrinsic biases in convolutional architectures, which fail to grasp long-range dependencies within images. In contrast, emerging Transformer-based architectures, leveraging self-attention mechanisms, have successfully captured complex relationships and learned rich representations. Inspired by these developments, our work seeks to investigate the potential of applying Transformer-based networks to medical image segmentation tasks. Notably, most existing Transformer-based approaches for visual applications necessitate substantial datasets for proper training. Conversely, medical imaging datasets exhibit relatively limited sizes compared to their visual counterparts, hindering efficient training of Transformers for medical purposes. Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornmeal
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 package (2 1/4 teaspoons) active dry yeast
- 1 cup warm water (110°F)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 cup pizza sauce
- 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1/2 cup sliced pepperoni
- 1/4 cup sliced black olives (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced green bell peppers (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced red onions (optional)
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Fresh basil leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, salt, and sugar. In a separate small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until it becomes frothy.

2. Pour the yeast mixture and olive oil into the dry ingredients. Stir until a dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour. If it's too dry, add a little more water. Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.

3. Grease a deep-dish pizza pan or a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Press the dough into the pan, making sure to cover the bottom and sides evenly. Let the dough rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes until it doubles in size.

4. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Once the dough has risen, spread the pizza sauce evenly over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges. Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce.

5. Arrange the pepperoni slices on top of the cheese. If desired, add black olives, green bell peppers, and red onions as additional toppings. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the toppings.

6. Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is bubbly and slightly browned.

7. Remove the pizza from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh basil leaves if desired. Slice and serve hot.

Deep learning techniques for 3D brain vessel image segmentation have not been
as successful as in the segmentation of other organs and tissues. This can be
explained by two factors. First, deep learning techniques tend to show poor
performances at the segmentation of relatively small objects compared to the
size of the full image. Second, due to the complexity of vascular trees and the
small size of vessels, it is challenging to obtain the amount of annotated
training data typically needed by deep learning methods. To address these
problems, we propose a novel annotation-efficient deep learning vessel
segmentation framework. The framework avoids pixel-wise annotations, only
requiring weak patch-level labels to discriminate between vessel and non-vessel
2D patches in the training set, in a setup similar to the CAPTCHAs used to
differentiate humans from bots in web applications. The user-provided weak
annotations are used for two tasks: 1) to synthesize pixel-wise pseudo-labels
for vessels and background in each patch, which are used to train a
segmentation network, and 2) to train a classifier network. The classifier
network allows to generate additional weak patch labels, further reducing the
annotation burden, and it acts as a noise filter for poor quality images. We
use this framework for the segmentation of the cerebrovascular tree in
Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Images (SWI). The
results show that the framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, while
reducing the annotation time by ~77% w.r.t. learning-based segmentation methods
using pixel-wise labels for training.

A key figure in introducing this innovative approach, which emphasized both teamwork and creativity, Michels relied on players like Johan Cruyff and Johan Neeskens, allowing them to seamlessly transition between positions. Cruyff was instrumental in organizing attacks and playing imaginative football, taking advantage of the fluid team dynamic. Michels' contributions were acknowledged just days after undergoing heart surgery, with KNVB officials hailing him as one of their greatest coaches. Throughout his career, Michels worked at various clubs, including Barcelona, Cologne, and Leverkusen, earning recognition for his achievements, including being named FIFA's Coach of the Century in 1999. General Sir John Gordon Noel Wilton,  (22 November 1910 – 10 May 1981) was a senior commander in the Australian Army. He served as Chief of the General Staff (CGS), the Army's professional head, from 1963 until 1966, and as Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (CCOSC), forerunner of the role of Australia's Chief of the Defence Force, from 1966 until 1970. His eight-year tenure as senior officer of first the Army and then the Australian military spanned almost the entire period of the nation's involvement in the Vietnam War. Born in Sydney, Wilton entered the Royal Military College, Duntroon, in 1927. Owing to lack of opportunity in the Australian military at the time, he took a commission in the British Army following his graduation in 1930. He spent most of the remainder of the decade with the Royal Artillery in India. Wilton returned to Australia on the eve of World War II and was commissioned into the Royal Australian Artillery. He saw action with the 7th Division in Syria and the 3rd Division in New Guinea, earning a mention in despatches in the former campaign and the Distinguished Service Order in the latter.  Finishing the war a temporary colonel, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1947. Wilton was posted to Korea in 1953 to take command of the 28th Commonwealth Brigade, leading it in its final action of the war in July. He was raised to Commander of the Order of the British Empire and awarded the US Legion of Merit for his performance in Korea.

Bradley Sinopoli (born April 14, 1988) is a former Canadian football wide receiver who played for nine years in the Canadian Football League (CFL). It consists of 152 classes with 300k images collected from ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) and Pascal VOC 2012 datasets. Each class has two domains: synthetic rendered images and real world photos. We investigate the lexicographically smallest word composed entirely of non-negative integers. This word often acts as a fixed point under uniform transformations or is closely tied to such transformations. Consider, for instance, the smallest 7/4-power-free word, which is also a fixed point of a 50847-uniform transformation. Our goal is to analyze the structure of the smallest a/b-power-free word for three distinct classes of fractions a/b as well as identify unusual cases that deviate from these patterns. To achieve this, we create an algorithm for verifying power-freeness under specific types of transformations for both numerical fractions and symbols representing those fractions symbolically. Furthermore, we link the concept to words over finite alphabets, showing that the smallest 27/23-power-free word corresponds to a word consisting only of the digits 0, 1, and 2, and that this sequence of digits forms a 353-automatic sequence.

The four defendants were the masterminds behind a popular peer-to-peer file-sharing website called "MegaUpload," which allowed users to store and share files, including copyrighted content such as movies, TV shows, music, and software, without permission from the copyright holders. The site was shut down by the FBI in 2012 following an investigation that revealed the massive scale of copyright infringement taking place on the site. 

The jury found that the defendants were aware of the widespread copyright infringement taking place on MegaUpload but took no meaningful action to prevent it. In a statement, the U.S. Attorney's Office said that the defendants "made a profit by encouraging, promoting, and assisting the widespread distribution of copyrighted materials without the permission of the copyright owners." 

The four defendants face a maximum sentence of five years in prison and significant financial penalties for their role in operating MegaUpload. The sentencing hearing is scheduled for later this year.

Existing image segmentation methods primarily rely on global contextual information to improve pixel representations, focusing on the entire image at once.
However, these approaches often neglect the importance of pixel-level contextual information, which can be derived from semantic segmentation.
To address this limitation, our approach combines image-level and semantic-level contextual information to enhance pixel representations.
We develop an image-level context module that captures contextual information for each pixel across the entire image, and then aggregate pixel-level representations based on learned categories under true segmentation masks.
Next, we calculate similarities between individual pixel representations and both image-level and semantic-level contextual information.
Finally, we combine these contextual elements using weights determined by their respective similarities, resulting in improved pixel representations.
By integrating image-level and semantic-level contexts, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, including ADE20K, LIP, COCOStuff, and Cityscapes.

Both What's the 411? and her 1994 album My Life are featured on the Rolling Stones 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list, and the latter on Time magazine's All-Time 100 Albums. Chips (1940–1946) was a trained sentry dog for United States Army, and reputedly the most decorated war dog from World War II. Chips was a German Shepherd-Collie-Husky mix owned by Edward J. Wren of Pleasantville, New York. During the war, private citizens like Wren donated their dogs for duty. Chips shipped out to the War Dog Training Center, Front Royal, Virginia, in 1942 for training as a sentry dog. He served with the 3rd Infantry Division in North Africa, Sicily, Italy, France and Germany.  His handler was Pvt. John P. Rowell.  Chips served as a sentry dog for the Roosevelt-Churchill conference in 1943. Later that year, during the invasion of Sicily, Chips and his handler were pinned down on the beach by an Italian machine-gun team.  Chips broke from his handler and jumped into the pillbox, attacking the gunners. The four crewmen were forced to leave the pillbox and surrendered to US troops. In the fight, he sustained a scalp wound and powder burns.  Later that day, he helped take ten Italians prisoner.

Deep learning methods have achieved promising performance in many areas, but
they are still struggling with noisy-labeled images during the training
process. Considering that the annotation quality indispensably relies on great
expertise, the problem is even more crucial in the medical image domain. How to
eliminate the disturbance from noisy labels for segmentation tasks without
further annotations is still a significant challenge. In this paper, we
introduce our label quality evaluation strategy for deep neural networks
automatically assessing the quality of each label, which is not explicitly
provided, and training on clean-annotated ones. We propose a solution for
network automatically evaluating the relative quality of the labels in the
training set and using good ones to tune the network parameters. We also design
an overfitting control module to let the network maximally learn from the
precise annotations during the training process. Experiments on the public
biomedical image segmentation dataset have proved the method outperforms
baseline methods and retains both high accuracy and good generalization at
different noise levels.

While deep convolutional neural networks have made significant strides in medical image processing and analysis, their reliance on extensive annotation data poses a challenge due to the requirement for specialized expertise and limited availability of annotated samples. This limitation is particularly prevalent in clinical settings where annotating medical images can be labor-intensive. To address this issue, we present a novel approach to few-shot medical image segmentation that empowers models to adapt rapidly to new, unseen classes with minimal training data. Our solution involves constructing an episodic deep convolutional network, which incorporates a novel global correlation module inspired by the spatial regularity inherent in medical images. This module facilitates the exchange of information between a reference (support) image and a target (query) image, enhancing overall performance. Furthermore, we introduce a discriminability-enhanced embedding technique to promote clustering within feature domains of the same organ while maintaining distinctiveness among different organs. Experimental results from ablation studies confirm the efficacy of our global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Subsequent evaluations on abdominal images from both computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities showcase our proposed model's outstanding performance, outperforming existing methods in these scenarios.

There is an escalating demand for sign language recognition technology, particularly among the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. Despite limited research efforts, only a few initiatives focus on developing automatic systems that can accurately identify sign language from video inputs, often using color-coded gloves and other tools. The existing approaches rely heavily on data preprocessing, which involves separating the data used for training from the data intended for recognition. Recognizing sign language sequences poses significant challenges due to the vast range of hand shapes and movements involved. To address this issue, this paper proposes an innovative method combining image segmentation and restoration using topological derivatives to enhance recognition accuracy. The quality of the restored images is evaluated both subjectively and objectively to compare various techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating image restoration before segmentation substantially improves hand detection accuracy and allows for better differentiation between distinct hand postures and the surrounding environment. Ultimately, this research aims to contribute to the development of automated sign language recognition systems designed primarily for social welfare purposes.
